\section{A clean return source program}\label{smc:ct:sec:wrapper}

Let $R$ be a source satisfying Section~\ref{smc:ct:sec:interface}. Form two disjoint copies of its states and one new state,
\[
Q_{\cl}=\{\Fq q:q\in Q\}\;\dot\cup\;\{\Bq q:q\in Q\}\;\dot\cup\;\{H\}.
\]
For each instruction $q\xrightarrow{\mathrm{op}}q'$, introduce
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ct:eq:copies}
\Fq q\xrightarrow{\mathrm{op}}\Fq {q'},
\qquad
\Bq {q'}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{op}^{-1}}\Bq q.
\end{equation}
The inverse exchanges increments with decrements, retains the counter index, and leaves both kinds of test and no-op unchanged. Add just two bridges:
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ct:eq:bridges}
\Fq {q_h}\xrightarrow{\NOP}\Bq {q_h},
\qquad
\Bq {q_0}\xrightarrow{\NOP}H.
\end{equation}
The new initial state is $\Fq {q_0}$ and the sole designated terminal state is $H$. In particular the two copies of $q_h$ are ordinary, nonterminal states for the CA compiler.

\begin{lemma}[Preservation of reversible syntax]\label{smc:ct:lem:syntax}
The program $R_{\cl}$ defined by~\eqref{smc:ct:eq:copies}--\eqref{smc:ct:eq:bridges} is separated, deterministic, and reversible. Its initial state has no incoming instruction and $H$ has no outgoing instruction.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The forward copy retains each original incoming and outgoing group. In the backward copy, outgoing groups are the inverses of original incoming groups, and incoming groups are inverses of original outgoing groups. A singleton arithmetic instruction remains singleton. A test group remains the same pair of disjoint tests on the same unchanged counter. Thus reversal preserves the syntactic conditions.

The first bridge uses an empty outgoing side at $\Fq {q_h}$ and an empty incoming side at $\Bq {q_h}$; both are empty because $q_h$ had no outgoing instruction. The second uses the empty outgoing side at $\Bq {q_0}$, by freshness~\eqref{smc:ct:eq:fresh}, and the fresh incoming side at $H$. Each added group is a legal singleton no-op. No other side is changed. The claimed entry and exit properties follow immediately.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Restoration and first source halt]\label{smc:ct:thm:restore}
Suppose the original run from $(q_0,N_0)$ first reaches $q_h$ after $h$ instructions. Write its sections as $(q_t,N_t)$, $0\le t\le h$, with $q_h$ also denoting its final state. Then the wrapped run is exactly
\begin{align*}
&(\Fq {q_0},N_0),\ldots,(\Fq {q_h},N_h),\\
&(\Bq {q_h},N_h),(\Bq {q_{h-1}},N_{h-1}),\ldots,(\Bq {q_0},N_0),(H,N_0).
\end{align*}
It first reaches $H$ after $2h+2$ instructions and restores the whole raw integer, including its cofactor. If the original run does not reach $q_h$, the wrapped run does not reach $H$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Before the first bridge, the forward copy executes exactly the original instructions. The bridge is available precisely at $\Fq {q_h}$ and preserves $N_h$. Every reversed arithmetic instruction is enabled on the actual preceding output: the inverse of an increment is a decrement on a number just multiplied by the relevant prime, and the inverse of a decrement is an always-enabled increment. Each inverse test sees the same unchanged raw number. These operations restore the previous raw value exactly. Backward uniqueness gives no alternative predecessor branch.

Inducting in reverse order reconstructs $(q_{h-1},N_{h-1}),\ldots,(q_0,N_0)$. The original initial state cannot occur at a positive source time, because no instruction targets it. Therefore the second bridge cannot be encountered prematurely. It preserves $N_0$ and changes only the state to $H$. The count is $h+1+h+1=2h+2$. The invariant cofactor in~\eqref{smc:ct:eq:raw} is unchanged by every operation and is restored along with both valuations.

If the original run is infinite, its forward copy is infinite and never takes the first bridge. If it is stuck nonfinally, the forward copy is stuck at that same section. Neither case reaches a backward-copy state or $H$. When $h=0$, the hypotheses imply $q_0=q_h$ is isolated; the run consists of the two bridges and the same proof applies.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Why the fresh entry condition matters}\label{smc:ct:sec:fresh}

Consider the separated reversible source
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ct:eq:badfresh}
q_0\xrightarrow{\ZERO_0}q_1,\qquad
q_1\xrightarrow{\INC_0}q_0,\qquad
q_0\xrightarrow{\POS_0}q_h.
\end{equation}
From $N_0=1$ its trace is $(q_0,1),(q_1,1),(q_0,2),(q_h,2)$. A backward copy first arrives at $\Bq {q_0}$ with $N=2$, before undoing the increment. An unconditional exit there would restore the wrong input. It also conflicts syntactically with the inverse decrement already leaving $\Bq {q_0}$. The implementation rejects this source. Rejecting only an incoming instruction enabled on the current input would be insufficient.

Nor can an arbitrary reversible source be freshened merely by prepending a no-op into its old initial state: that new incoming motion may conflict with existing incoming instructions. The source-existence dependency must genuinely supply the needed normal form. Morita and Imai~\cite{moritaimai}, Proposition 3.4, give universal reversible two-counter simulation, and Lemma 3.5 supplies a simulator with no instruction entering its initial state while preserving reversibility. Apply these results after choosing one universal source problem. The finite counts below start after this normalization; no bound on its overhead is claimed. A terminal halt may be enforced by deleting outgoing instructions from the designated halt state, preserving first-halt behavior and the separated conditions.

\subsection{Relation to classical uncomputation}

Forward computation followed by inverse execution to clear temporary information is a classical idea. Bennett's 1973 construction~\cite{bennett} restores the input after retaining the desired output and clearing intermediate information. Here the source is already reversible, so its inverse execution needs no new history tape. A terminal control label records success while both counter values are restored. This report claims neither novelty nor priority for the forward-and-reverse idea; it proves the particular source syntax, finite geometry, exact target, and resource consequences needed for this CA.

\section{Exact configurations and the sharp threshold}\label{smc:ct:sec:exact}

Apply the inherited compiler to $R_{\cl}$ with $H$ as its designated final state, and abbreviate its CA to $A$. Set
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ct:eq:pair}
x_N=C_{R_{\cl}}(\Fq {q_0},N),\qquad y_N=C_{R_{\cl}}(H,N).
\end{equation}
Both descriptions are computed directly from the supplied $N$. They have identical absolute support and differ only in the controller state inside the weight-two left symbol.

\begin{theorem}[Whole-configuration equivalence]\label{smc:ct:thm:equiv}
For every positive raw input $N$,
\[
\bigl(\exists t\in\NN:\ A^t(x_N)=y_N\bigr)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
R\text{ reaches }q_h\text{ from }(q_0,N).
\]
On a first source halt at $h$, the target is first reached at the end of cleaned source instruction $2h+2$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
On a halt, Theorem~\ref{smc:ct:thm:restore} gives the canonical section $(H,N)$ after the indicated number of source instructions. Proposition~\ref{smc:ct:prop:interface} resets the finite registers at every section. The right marker has stayed at zero and the left pair returns to $-12N$. There are exactly the three prescribed channels and vacuum elsewhere, so the resulting object is the entire target in~\eqref{smc:ct:eq:pair}, not just a matching halt symbol.

Before this section, Theorem~\ref{smc:ct:thm:restore} lists all canonical source states, none equal to $H$. Intermediate macro stages have different stage or shuttle types and cannot equal the clean stage-zero target. The prescribed-row simulation therefore rules out an earlier hit.

For a nonhalting source, an infinite forward execution continues through its intended macros without an $H$ section. A finite stuck execution takes the explicit escape continuation: the escaping channel moves forever away and never reassembles a clean pair. These are complete descriptions of both possible nonhalting continuations, not finite-prefix checks. No arbitrary completion row supplies a later false target. The equivalence follows.
\end{proof}

The theorem concerns the first exact hit. It makes no assertion that the target is stationary, that it occurs only once, or that the subsequent orbit remains a simulated source run. Completion may determine post-hit behavior. None of those later facts is needed for reachability.

\begin{corollary}[One fixed rule]\label{smc:ct:cor:onerule}
Fix a universal reversible fresh-entry source as above. Then exact-pair reachability for its fixed cleaned CA is undecidable on the computable family~\eqref{smc:ct:eq:pair}. Exact-pair reachability is recursively enumerable: direct simulation semidecides a hit.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Encode an instance of the fixed source's halting problem into its initial counter values, then into $N$ and the pair $(x_N,y_N)$. Both endpoints are computed without the halt time or output values. A decision procedure for this restricted CA reachability family would decide source halting by Theorem~\ref{smc:ct:thm:equiv}. Direct CA simulation enumerates finite times and checks finite configuration equality, proving the semidecision statement. With a standard many-one complete halting source, the same reduction gives recursively enumerable completeness.
\end{proof}

This supplies a fixed rule, not a variable rule supplied alongside each input. It does not supply one fixed target for every $N$. The dependence of $y_N$ on $N$ is explicit and is part of the reduction.

\subsection{Why mass two cannot do the same}

\wtag\ [Source~15 summarizes here, ``from the companion proof'', the mass-two decision argument: finite walker maps, the near/far threshold $2r$, the $|Q_2|+2r|Q_1|^2$ near shapes, the translating recurrent tail, exact target tests at every phase and at all later translates, and polynomial bit complexity for a fixed rule. That is Theorem~\ref{smc:sl:thm:two} of Part~IV, proved there, and Section~\ref{smc:tm:sec:lower} of source~14; the summary is not reprinted.]

Combining this decision theorem with Theorem~\ref{smc:ct:thm:equiv} proves the mass threshold in Theorem~\ref{smc:ct:thm:main}. The assumptions exclude zero-weight active computation and signed mass cancellation. A prescribed finite ring has a finite mass sector and is decidable by orbit search, so it is a different problem.

\section{Radius one and the exact clock}\label{smc:ct:sec:clock}

\subsection{The first target time}

Let $\Theta$ be the native microtime of the original forward source trace and $N_h$ its final raw value. Reversal exchanges an increment $N\to N'$ with a decrement $N'\to N$. Table~\ref{smc:ct:tab:clock} gives
\[
108N+96N'+8=96N'+108N+8.
\]
The decrement/increment pair has the same symmetry. Inverse tests and no-ops leave the raw value unchanged and have the same duration. Hence the reversed half takes exactly $\Theta$, in reverse order of macro durations. The two bridges cost $192N_h+8$ and $192N_0+8$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact first-target clock]\label{smc:ct:thm:clock}
If the original first halt is after $h$ source instructions, the native CA first reaches its exact target at
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ct:eq:cleanclock}
T_{\cl}=2\Theta+192(N_h+N_0)+16.
\end{equation}
For $h=0$ this is $384N_0+16$, with both no-op bridges retained.
\end{theorem}

This is logical inverse execution using forward CA time and different finite controller types. It is not the microscopic inverse orbit under $A^{-1}$, and need not reverse particle worldlines. The time identity follows from the explicit macro formulas, not from global reversibility by itself.

\subsection{Four-site spatial blocking}

Group old sites $4k,4k+1,4k+2,4k+3$ into blocked site $k$. Every old channel gets an offset $0,1,2,3$. This is a conjugacy of full shifts, with weight equal to the sum of the four old weights. A native radius-four update and its radius-four inverse become radius-one updates because the four-site block needs only itself and its two neighboring blocks.

The native right marker stays at blocked coordinate zero, offset zero. Since $-12N=-4(3N)$, the left pair is at blocked coordinate $-3N$, also offset zero. Conjugacy preserves exact equality at every tick, and therefore preserves the first-hit time $T_{\cl}$. No extra particle or background is added.

\subsection{Four-phase internal dilation}

The alternative radius-one construction keeps native coordinates and gives every channel four phase copies. A native velocity in $[-4,4]$ is spread over four single-cell submoves; the local collision permutation acts once per four-phase cycle. On synchronized phase-zero configurations, four new ticks implement one native tick. Each individual step remains a full-space bijection, including on configurations outside the synchronized encoded sector, as established by the inherited phase construction.

The target uses phase-zero channels. At every time all three encoded tokens have phase $t\bmod4$, so an off-section time cannot equal that nonempty target. At time $4t$, its state equals the native state after $t$ ticks under the phase-zero encoding. The first exact target is consequently at $4T_{\cl}$, with the same coordinates $-12N$ and $0$. Both radius-one alternatives have four times the native number of channel types. Spatial blocking preserves the clock; internal dilation preserves the native coordinate convention. \wtag\ [The two constructions are source~14's Theorems~\ref{smc:tm:thm:blocking} and~\ref{smc:tm:thm:slowdown}, applied to the wrapped source.]

Radius zero cannot support the stated undecidable exact-pair problem: sites neither move nor communicate, and a finite-support configuration has a finite orbit of independent finite-state updates. Thus radius one also attains the smallest possible radius for this result.

Let the normalized original source have $q=|Q|$ states, $J$ instructions, instruction-register modulus $m=J+1$, and $d$ arithmetic instructions. Let $B$ be its residue-expanded branch count: a zero test at prime three contributes two branches, and each other instruction contributes one. The wrapper does not simplify or remove unreachable states.

K_{\mathrm{types}}&=96q'm'+6q'd'+2d'+6q'+2314,\label{smc:ct:eq:types}\\

Both radius-one alternatives use $4K_{\mathrm{types}}$ channels. Equation~\eqref{smc:ct:eq:completed} is not a flattened count of blocked local rows: spatial blocking uses a composed finite description. The counts are constructive upper descriptions for this generator, not smallest-alphabet or optimal-overhead theorems. They do not assign a numerical universal alphabet size, because no expanded universal normalized source is supplied here.

\section{Compact quadratic certificates}\label{smc:ct:sec:certificate}

The finite source horizon $h$ is an external parameter. The certificate is a polynomial over natural numbers whose zeros encode first halt of the original source at that horizon. Reusing this certificate avoids independently guessing the inverse computation. We give the original encoding and the precise sense in which its witness determines a full cleaned witness.

\subsection{Forward branch forms and exactness}

Expand zero tests at prime $p$ into residues $r\in\{1,\ldots,p-1\}$. For every step $0\le t<h$ and branch $1\le j\le B$, use natural variables $e_{tj}$ and $u_{tj}$. The affine forms in Table~\ref{smc:ct:tab:branches} describe an old raw value $A_j$, a new raw value $C_j$, and duration $D_j$. Fix an injective integer coding of states; let $s_j$ and $t_j$ be branch $j$'s source and target codes. They may coincide for a self-loop.

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccc@{}}
\toprule
Branch & $A_j(e,u)$ & $C_j(e,u)$ & $D_j(e,u)$\\
\midrule
$\INC$ at $p$ & $e+u$ & $p(e+u)$ & $108A_j+96C_j+8e$\\
$\DEC$ at $p$ & $p(e+u)$ & $e+u$ & $96A_j+108C_j+8e$\\
$\POS$ at $p$ & $p(e+u)$ & $p(e+u)$ & $192A_j+8e$\\
$\ZERO$ at $p$, residue $r$ & $pu+re$ & $pu+re$ & $192A_j+8e$\\
$\NOP$ & $e+u$ & $e+u$ & $192A_j+8e$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{All forms vanish when $e=u=0$. At $e=1$, natural $u$ enforces the exact enabled arithmetic or residue class.}\label{smc:ct:tab:branches}
\end{table}

Define the affine sums, separately at every $t$,
\[
E_t=\sum_j e_{tj},\quad U_t=\sum_j A_j(e_{tj},u_{tj}),\quad
V_t=\sum_j C_j(e_{tj},u_{tj}),
\]
\[
S_t=\sum_j s_j e_{tj},\quad Q_t=\sum_j t_j e_{tj},\quad
\Theta=\sum_{t,j}D_j(e_{tj},u_{tj}).
\]
Set $V_{-1}=N_0$ and $Q_{-1}=\operatorname{code}(q_0)$. These are affine interfaces, not new variables. The core polynomial is
\begin{align}
P_h={}&\sum_{t=0}^{h-1}\bigl[(E_t-1)^2+(S_t-Q_{t-1})^2+(U_t-V_{t-1})^2\bigr]\notag\\
&+(Q_{h-1}-\operatorname{code}(q_h))^2
+\sum_{t=0}^{h-1}\sum_{j=1}^{B}(E_t-e_{tj})(e_{tj}+u_{tj}).\label{smc:ct:eq:poly}
\end{align}
It has degree at most two. Every summand is nonnegative on the full natural orthant, since $E_t-e_{tj}=\sum_{k\ne j}e_{tk}\ge0$. \wtag\ [Table~\ref{smc:ct:tab:branches} and~\eqref{smc:ct:eq:poly} are source~14's branch table and certificate~\eqref{smc:tm:eq:certificate}, with $q_h$ for $q_f$; the gate is discussed in the note after Theorem~\ref{smc:tm:thm:certificate}.]

\begin{lemma}[Forward zero fibers]\label{smc:ct:lem:forwardzero}
For fixed input coordinates, $P_h$ has a natural zero exactly when the original run first halts at horizon $h$. If a zero exists, its full forward witness is unique. Its affine endpoints are $N_0$, $N_h=V_{h-1}$, and $\Theta$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}[\wtag\ Pointer]
This is source~14's Theorem~\ref{smc:tm:thm:certificate}, for the same polynomial. Source~15's proof repeats source~14's (the square $(E_t-1)^2$ and natural selectors force one-hot selection, every inactive product forces its offset to zero, the active offset is $N-1$, $N/p-1$ or $(N-r)/p$, the terminal square forces a first halt, and $h=0$ leaves only the constant halt square); it is not reprinted.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The compact clean certificate and roles of coordinates}

Use the forward polynomial unchanged and replace its exposed physical-time form by~\eqref{smc:ct:eq:cleanclock}. By Theorems~\ref{smc:ct:thm:restore} and~\ref{smc:ct:thm:equiv}, its zero already proves the exact cleaned target and determines every source section in both halves. The fixed compiler then determines every intervening CA microconfiguration. This is a certificate for the specified encoded source computation, not a general certificate for arbitrary CA trajectories.

To impose a supplied exact microtime $T$, add just
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ct:eq:timesquare}
\bigl(\kappa[2\Theta+192(N_h+N_0)+16]-T\bigr)^2,\qquad
\kappa=\begin{cases}1&\text{native or spatial},\\4&\text{phase}.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
For fixed $T$ this adds no variable. To expose time as a free output coordinate, introduce one natural $T$ and the same square; it is uniquely determined in each accepted input fiber. The target raw value is the already existing input expression $N_0$. Its restoration needs neither a separately guessed output value nor another endpoint square.

The exact core ledger is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ct:eq:compactledger}
2Bh\ \text{natural variables},\qquad 3h+1\ \text{affine-square slots},\qquad Bh\ \text{affine-product slots}.
\end{equation}
These are unsimplified emitted slots; a degenerate term may vanish identically. By comparison, applying the original exporter directly to the cleaned program at horizon $2h+2$ would give
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ct:eq:naiveledger}
8(B+1)(h+1)\ \text{core variables},\qquad 6h+7\ \text{squares},\qquad
4(B+1)(h+1)\ \text{products}.
\end{equation}
The smaller ledger is justified by source composition and the zero-fiber lift below, not by dropping constraints from an arbitrary reverse run.

\subsection{Input modes and their paid costs}

A fixed positive raw input is a constant. A free raw input uses $N_0=x+1$ with one genuine natural input coordinate $x$ and no loader square. Fixed counters $(a,b)$ can be encoded externally by the computable constant $2^a3^b$.

For an explicitly bounded counter interface, fix bounds $0\le a\le A$ and $0\le b\le C$. Introduce $K=(A+1)(C+1)$ natural selectors $\lambda_{ij}$ and three squares
\[
\left(\sum\lambda_{ij}-1\right)^2,\quad
\left(a-\sum i\lambda_{ij}\right)^2,\quad
\left(b-\sum j\lambda_{ij}\right)^2.
\]
Use $N_0=\sum 2^i3^j\lambda_{ij}$ by affine substitution. The selectors are uniquely one-hot on accepted inputs. Every genuinely free $a$ or $b$ is an additional input coordinate; fixed values are constants. This finite table is not an unbounded exponentiation gadget.

Let $r$ count genuine input coordinates, $k$ loader selectors, $\ell\in\{0,3\}$ loader squares, $s\in\{0,1\}$ a free time output, and $\epsilon\in\{0,1\}$ whether a time equality is included. The full compact ledger is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ct:eq:fullledger}
\begin{aligned}
\text{natural variables}&=2Bh+r+k+s,\\
\text{affine squares}&=3h+1+\ell+\epsilon,\\
\text{affine products}&=Bh,\qquad \text{degree}\le2.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
For $h=0$, the time form is $384N_0+16$ before any phase scaling, and all optional input and time costs are still charged.

\subsection{An affine lift to the full cleaned witness}\label{smc:ct:sec:lift}

Index original expanded branches by $j=0,\ldots,B-1$ for this subsection. In the full cleaned exporter, branches $j$ are the forward copies, $B+j$ are their inverse copies, and $2B,2B+1$ are the bridges. Its steps are indexed $0,\ldots,2h+1$. Denote its branch variables by $\widetilde e_{s,k},\widetilde u_{s,k}$.

The following affine substitution $L$ maps compact witnesses to full ones:
\begin{align}
\widetilde e_{t,j}&=e_{t,j},&\widetilde u_{t,j}&=u_{t,j},&&0\le t<h,\label{smc:ct:eq:liftF}\\
\widetilde e_{2h-t,B+j}&=e_{t,j},&\widetilde u_{2h-t,B+j}&=u_{t,j},&&0\le t<h,\label{smc:ct:eq:liftB}\\
\widetilde e_{h,2B}&=1,&\widetilde u_{h,2B}&=N_h-1,\label{smc:ct:eq:liftbridge1}\\
\widetilde e_{2h+1,2B+1}&=1,&\widetilde u_{2h+1,2B+1}&=N_0-1.\label{smc:ct:eq:liftbridge2}
\end{align}
Every unlisted full-core coordinate is zero. Preserve all genuine input coordinates, loader selectors, and any time output. Coordinate names are merely labels: rename them consistently if a user-specified public name collides with a larger full-core variable name.

\begin{theorem}[Affine bijection of natural zero fibers]\label{smc:ct:thm:lift}
With the same fixed source, horizon, input interface, and optional time condition, $L$ restricts to a bijection from compact natural zeros to natural zeros of the full cleaned-source certificate at horizon $2h+2$. Projection onto its original forward variables and public coordinates is its inverse, after any consistent renaming.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Start with a compact zero. Lemma~\ref{smc:ct:lem:forwardzero} gives a genuine forward trace and positive endpoints $N_0,N_h$. Thus the two bridge magnitudes in~\eqref{smc:ct:eq:liftbridge1}--\eqref{smc:ct:eq:liftbridge2} are natural, and every coordinate of $L$ is natural.

For an original increment, $N=e+u$ and $N'=p(e+u)$. Its inverse decrement on $N'$ uses exactly the same $e,u$, so exchanges the old and new affine raw values. An original decrement has the same property with increment as its inverse. Tests and no-ops have unchanged raw values and retain the same parameters, including the zero-test residue. Consequently~\eqref{smc:ct:eq:liftB} realizes the unique inverse trace step by step. The bridge rows are no-ops at $N_h$ and $N_0$. All unselected coordinates are zero, so their inactive products vanish. The source and raw interface squares match the concatenated trace, and the full terminal state is $H$.

The unchanged loader satisfies its original three squares when present. Summing the full duration forms gives~\eqref{smc:ct:eq:cleanclock}; hence any time endpoint square also agrees. The lifted assignment is therefore a full natural zero.

Conversely, the forward-certificate exactness theorem applied to the full cleaned exporter turns any of its natural zeros into a first-halt cleaned execution of length $2h+2$. The only route to $H$ traverses a forward first halt, both bridges, and the unique inverse trace. If that forward length is $k$, Theorem~\ref{smc:ct:thm:restore} gives total length $2k+2$, so $k=h$. Projecting to the first $h$ rows and original public coordinates gives a compact zero; the clock identity supplies its time condition. Full witness uniqueness at fixed input forces all remaining rows to be precisely~\eqref{smc:ct:eq:liftB}--\eqref{smc:ct:eq:liftbridge2}. Thus the two maps are inverses on zero fibers.
\end{proof}

The restriction to zero fibers is essential. The bridge expression $N_h-1$ can be negative at a general natural assignment that is not a compact zero. The claim is not a map of the entire natural orthant, nor an identity of the two polynomial values off their zero sets. The natural domain is also essential for the original encoding: fractional branch magnitudes can bypass discrete divisibility or residue guards. No assertion for nonnegative rational or real solutions is made. \wtag\ [The programme's review~\cite{reviewthreemass} exhibits both limitations exactly: for a one-step increment at $N_0=1$ and the off-zero assignment $e=u=0$, the compact polynomial has value~3, its lift has value~18 and a bridge coordinate $-1$; and a one-step prime-two zero test at $N_0=2$ has the nonnegative rational zero $e=1$, $u=1/2$ of source~14's Section~\ref{smc:tm:sec:certificate}. It records them as documented limitations, not defects, and checks 45 compact-to-full natural zero-fibre bijections.]

Finally, this is a family indexed by externally fixed $h$. Eventual halting is a union over all finite horizons. Merely replacing $h$ by a variable does not give a fixed-arity unbounded-time quadratic polynomial, and fixed-horizon uniqueness does not imply a finite-fold unbounded-time representation.

\section{Validation and reproducibility}\label{smc:ct:sec:validation}

\subsection{What the implementations check}

The cleanup exporter validates structural freshness, builds the forward/inverse source table, composes the original polynomial, and exposes the cleaned clock. A separate checker reconstructs the wrapped program and affine outputs instead of trusting these claims in the exported JSON. It invokes the unchanged independent forward checker and validates the natural witness, optional literal polynomial expansion, and full resource ledger. Its decoded cleaned trace is compared with actual source execution and literal lattice evolution.

The producer tests exercise all primitive operations, both nonzero prime-three residues, guarded branch/merge behavior, a mixed chain with unequal original endpoint values, $h=0$, immediate and delayed stalls, a growing nonhalting prefix, raw cofactors, loader interfaces, invalid freshness, clock symmetry, and maliciously altered certificates. Successful lattice checks compare the entire target and every canonical section, test conservation and inverses, and require prescribed pair rows through the first hit. Selected cases execute all native, spatial, and phase ticks.

The independent lattice harness separately builds the wrapper, executes source instructions, recognizes the full canonical configurations, and steps the generated collision and stream maps without calling the compiler's ordinary step or ready helpers. Its certificate audit exercises valid interfaces and rejects deliberate mutations. The separate lift audit compares explicit forward/reverse variable reuse with the full cleaned exporter and its frozen independent checker.

\paragraph{Finite evidence and theorem evidence.}
Finite tests verify concrete implementations and boundary cases. The all-input restoration and nonhalting exclusion follow from the proofs, the full-space reversible behavior from the compiler, and undecidability from the classical source dependency. No finite collection of successful traces proves universality, and a growing finite prefix does not alone prove nonhalting. The archive records each test's actual scope rather than conflating these forms of evidence.

\paragraph{Replay summary.} The completed release receipt records the exact test counts and subject hashes. The independently checked lattice sample comprises 14 small sources and 35 runs, including 26 successful cleanups and nine stuck inputs. It covers 111\,712 native ticks, 9\,456 spatial ticks, and 37\,824 phase ticks. The independent certificate pass checks 61 valid model/interface cases, rejects 174 mutations and 19 malformed syntax or API cases, and enumerates 1\,536 natural assignments for prime-three zero-test branches. The producer checks 77 affine-lift cases; the independent lift audit checks 24 cases and 96 public-coordinate naming-collision regressions. The producer lattice suite covers 45 halting runs, 21 stalls, 197\,374 native ticks, 21\,120 spatial ticks, and 84\,480 phase ticks; it also checks 140 clock-symmetry cases. Normal and optimized Python runs are recorded separately.

\subsection{Portable replay and source provenance}

The portable archive includes this standalone editable LaTeX source and PDF, the cleanup code and independent checker, literal examples, the five exact frozen Python dependencies, independent audit harnesses, receipts, and build/replay scripts. Python replay uses only the standard library. PDF rebuild uses a conventional TeX installation and the packages declared at the top of the source. No third-party paper PDFs are redistributed.

All package files are covered by a SHA-256 manifest except the manifest itself. A verifier checks both hashes and the expected file set. The archive safety check rejects absolute paths, parent traversal, duplicate members, and symbolic links. Fresh replay is performed from an extracted copy rather than from the source working directory. Temporary generated outputs remain outside the sealed file set. The final PDF is rendered and every page is visually checked.

The provenance ledger records hashes for the five frozen dependencies, the exact extension sources, source-audit scripts, and the companion report that establishes inherited results. Independent harnesses are made portable only by changing dependency/output path selection; that adaptation is recorded explicitly and the adapted copies are rerun. Receipts identify which subject code was actually tested. References link to primary publications; packaging does not silently substitute a different local-rule generator.

\section{Boundaries and precise next questions}\label{smc:ct:sec:questions}

The construction settles the mass threshold for exact-pair reachability in the stated weighted model. It also settles radius one as a sufficient radius with three conserved mass units. Several stronger or more concrete claims remain distinct.
\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{smc:ct:q:universal} \textbf{A fully expanded universal instance.} Instantiate a particular universal reversible two-counter table with fresh entry and terminal halt, provide its input encoder, and freeze the resulting cleaned local rule. This would yield an exact universal alphabet and row count. The small examples in this archive do not perform that instantiation. (\wtag\ Compare source~14's Question~\ref{smc:tm:q:source} and Part~IV's first question; all three are open.) (\wtag\ Added 3 October 2026, batch~82: answered in part outside this report, as the note at Question~\ref{smc:tm:q:source} says; the cleaned universal rule of this automaton is not frozen.)
\item\label{smc:ct:q:fixedtarget} \textbf{One target independent of the input.} Determine whether a suitable fixed reversible weighted CA can have undecidable reachability to one chosen finite configuration from a computable input family. The present restoration construction gives $y_N$, not a single $y$. Injectivity and the backward orbit of a fixed target must be handled explicitly; no claim of impossibility follows from this report.
\item\label{smc:ct:q:overhead} \textbf{Smaller finite-state overhead.} Reduce the duplicate state space, residue clock, or two bridge costs while retaining global reversibility and exact scratch cleanup. Compare improvements using the same target convention and all resource ledgers. A faster logical inverse cannot be assumed to reverse microscopic paths. (\wtag\ Compare source~14's Question~\ref{smc:tm:q:overhead}.)
\item\label{smc:ct:q:mass} \textbf{The integer-state mass convention.} Find the corresponding sharp reversible threshold when each cell state's integer value is its conserved mass. Equal-weight channel types used here cannot be transferred by relabeling. This is a different model-specific question. (\wtag\ Compare source~14's Question~\ref{smc:tm:q:mass}, answered in part by Part~\ref{smc:su:part}, as the note there says.) (\wtag\ Added 3 October 2026, batch~82: answered outside this report, five, as the note at Question~\ref{smc:tm:q:mass} says.)
\item\label{smc:ct:q:unbounded} \textbf{A costed unbounded-time certificate.} Compose this frontend with an explicit fixed-arity Diophantine encoding of unbounded computation, and state degree, variable costs, and the resulting fiber properties. The fixed-horizon affine lift alone supplies no finite-fold or single-fold unbounded-time conclusion. (\wtag\ Compare source~14's Question~\ref{smc:tm:q:unbounded}.) (\wtag\ Added 3 October 2026: answered for fixed eligible sources by Part~\ref{smc:uc:part}, which composes this frontend with the research tree's residue-history interface: exact degrees 2344 and~1192, ledgers of 604, 479, 477 and~480 operations (603, 478, 476 and~479 folded, 608, 483, 481 and~484 canonical) and 60, 58, 58 and~58 positive witnesses for four nonuniversal fixtures, and infinite witness fibres, also after canonicalization of the outer history (Theorems~\ref{smc:uc:thm:fibers} and~\ref{smc:ch:thm:infinite}). The emitted representations are not finite-fold. Part~VIII does not address Questions~\ref{smc:ct:q:universal} and~\ref{smc:ct:q:fixedtarget}.)
\item\label{smc:ct:q:mechanized} \textbf{Mechanized compiler composition.} Formalize the separated syntax, inverse source transform, prescribed collision routes, and zero-fiber correspondence in one proof system. The key interfaces to preserve are exact absolute configurations, natural domains, and the distinction between source steps and CA ticks.
\end{enumerate}

There is close geometric prior art. Brandt, Portmann and Uitto~\cite{brandt2020} use three finite-state agents, a prime-exponent gap, and reflected-shuttle arithmetic. The companion report \textup{[source~14, Section~\ref{smc:tm:sec:limits}]} compares those mechanisms with the global reversible CA and its cleanup obligations. The extension here does not claim a literature-wide priority result or a new general principle of uncomputation. Its conclusion is the explicit exact-target strengthening, under the model and dependencies stated above.
