\section{Scope and relation to the earlier reports}\label{smc:bp:sec:scope}
Report 30 established quantitative geometry for promised conservative cellular automata of fixed mass at most four and supplied a weighted planar realization~\textup{[source~20, Part~\ref{smc:zd:part}]}. The present report supplies a binary realization directly. Every occupied site has weight one, and the selected orbit contains exactly four occupied sites at every time. The proof of this example is self-contained and does not require a general orbit-classification theorem.
\wtag\ [Its counts are exact instances of source~20's Theorems~\ref{smc:og:thm:geometry} and~\ref{smc:og:thm:timing} (an expanding shuttle of rank two, with leading coefficient $1/2$) and, after the vertical shift, of Theorem~\ref{smc:og:thm:drift} (linear box order with a square-root deficit, as in source~20's Theorem~\ref{smc:og:thm:exactdrift}).]

The starting mechanism is the one-dimensional binary shuttle in Report 12, Section 7 \textup{[Section~\ref{smc:fm:sec:binary} here, rule~\eqref{smc:fm:eq:binary}]}, ``An explicit binary expanding shuttle''~\textup{[source~17, Part~\ref{smc:su:part}]}. Its replacements, up to translation, are
\[
\{0,1\}\mapsto\{1,2\},\quad
\{0,2\}\mapsto\{-1,1\},\quad
\{0,1,3\}\mapsto\{-1,1,4\},\quad
\{0,2,4\}\mapsto\{0,3,4\}.
\]
We keep both moving-pair replacements and all four input shapes. At the right bounce, only the outgoing right marker moves up one row. At the left bounce, the entire output triple moves up one row. These two transverse changes make successive sweeps occupy successive rows. Thus the four horizontal patterns are not presented as new patterns. The quadratic section clock is inherited from the same flight lengths; the planar visited set and vertical-drift geometry are proved below.

Report 13 distinguishes local or fixed-formula certificates from more general timed constructions~\textup{[source~18, Part~\ref{smc:su:part}]}. We preserve that distinction. The quartic in Section~\ref{smc:bp:sec:quartic} describes \emph{one local transition}, with a literal expanded polynomial and exact resource ledger. It is not an unbounded orbit tableau. Report 30's \textup{[source~20's Corollary~\ref{smc:og:cor:original-target}]} separate complete-target theorem is discussed only in Section~\ref{smc:bp:sec:limits}; it does not follow from the local quartic.

Throughout, $k\ge7$ is an integer, $\NN=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$, and a ``natural witness'' means a tuple of nonnegative integers. The notation $O_k(1)$ permits a bound depending on the fixed initial gap $k$. Spatial counts count distinct lattice sites ever occupied, not visits, particles with multiplicity, or space-time events.

\section{The exact component rule}\label{smc:bp:sec:rule}
Identify a binary configuration with its occupied set $S\subseteq\Z^2$, which may be infinite. Join distinct occupied sites whenever their Chebyshev distance is at most two. A connected component that is a translate of an input $A$ in Table~\ref{smc:bp:tab:rule} is replaced by the corresponding translate of $B$. All other components remain unchanged. Only translates are recognized; neither reflections nor rotations are implicitly included. Call the resulting map $G$.

\begin{table}[htbp]\centering
\begin{tabular}{cll}\toprule
Rule & Input $A$ & Output $B$\\\midrule
$E$ & $\{(0,0),(1,0)\}$ & $\{(1,0),(2,0)\}$\\
$W$ & $\{(0,0),(2,0)\}$ & $\{(-1,0),(1,0)\}$\\
$R$ & $\{(0,0),(1,0),(3,0)\}$ & $\{(-1,0),(1,0),(4,1)\}$\\
$L$ & $\{(0,0),(2,0),(4,0)\}$ & $\{(0,1),(3,1),(4,1)\}$\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{The four exact component replacements. A surrounding empty halo is part of recognition, not an optional condition.}\label{smc:bp:tab:rule}
\end{table}

\begin{lemma}[Recognition and bounded matching]\label{smc:bp:lem:matching}
The component prescription is unambiguous. On every finite or infinite configuration it gives a bijection from old occupied sites to new occupied sites whose displacements have max norm at most one. In particular, outputs from different components do not overlap.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Each input shape is connected in the distance-two graph. An exact translate has a unique anchor, namely its minimum $x$ coordinate and common $y$ coordinate. The pair shapes have different gaps; the triple shapes have different gap lists. Therefore distinct rules cannot recognize the same component. Isolated sites, nonhorizontal components, larger components, and infinite components are unrecognized and stay fixed.

Use the following source-to-target bijections within recognized components:
\begin{align*}
E:&\quad(0,0)\mapsto(1,0),\quad(1,0)\mapsto(2,0),\\
W:&\quad(0,0)\mapsto(-1,0),\quad(2,0)\mapsto(1,0),\\
R:&\quad(0,0)\mapsto(-1,0),\quad(1,0)\mapsto(1,0),\quad(3,0)\mapsto(4,1),\\
L:&\quad(0,0)\mapsto(0,1),\quad(2,0)\mapsto(3,1),\quad(4,0)\mapsto(4,1).
\end{align*}
Use the identity on every frozen component. Every displacement has norm at most one. Distinct components have all mutual distances at least three. If matched outputs from two components coincided, their source sites would have distance at most two by the triangle inequality, a contradiction. This includes a recognized component next to a frozen finite or infinite component. Outputs within each component are distinct by the displayed bijection. The combined matching is therefore a bijection onto the new occupied set.
\end{proof}

For finite $S$, the lemma proves exact particle conservation. For infinite $S$, it proves a well-defined bounded-displacement matching without subtracting infinite cardinalities. Two output components may join after a step; the next step simply recognizes or freezes the newly formed component. Such joining does not invalidate the one-step argument.

\begin{figure}[htbp]\centering
\includegraphics[width=.99\linewidth]{figures/21-planar-shuttle-rule.pdf}
\caption{Exact primitive replacements and the source-to-target matching. Gray grid points are unoccupied reference sites. The two transverse bounce changes are visible in $R$ and $L$. The required empty radius-two halo around each input is not drawn.}\label{smc:bp:fig:rule}
\end{figure}

\section{Locality on the full shift}\label{smc:bp:sec:locality}
For a translated input $A+a$, define its halo and recognition predicate by
\[
H(A+a)=(A+a)+[-2,2]^2,\qquad
P_{A,a}(S)\Longleftrightarrow S\cap H(A+a)=A+a,
\]
where intervals denote integer lattice intervals. This finite predicate is equivalent to saying that $A+a$ is exactly an occupied connected component. Indeed, the shape is connected, and the first site of any occupied path leaving it must lie in its halo. Conversely, an empty surrounding halo excludes every such path. This works on infinite configurations as well: a fragment of a larger or infinite component cannot be falsely rewritten because a window truncates the rest.

To evaluate the new bit at $z$, consider only anchors for which $z$ is in a primitive input or output. If the old bit is zero, a successful predicate turns it on exactly when the corresponding replacement creates $z$. If the old bit is one, a successful predicate turns it off exactly when the replacement removes $z$. Otherwise the bit is preserved. Lemma~\ref{smc:bp:lem:matching} ensures that these local decisions agree with the component prescription on the entire binary full shift.

For every candidate and each input site $p$, one has $\inorm{p-z}\le4$. Its halo is therefore within radius six of $z$. More precisely, the changed-site cylinders read only
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:rectG}
D_G=[-6,6]\times[-3,2],\qquad |D_G|=78.
\end{equation}
The central unchanged bit lies in the same rectangle. All formulas commute with translations. No input shape is recognized in the vacuum, so $G$ is quiescent. This proves the upper radius bound on all $2^{169}$ square radius-six windows without enumerating them. Section~\ref{smc:bp:sec:degree} proves that the smaller 78-cell dependency rectangle is exact.

Let $\tau$ be vertical translation by $(0,1)$, with $\tau S=S+(0,1)$, and set
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:F}
F=\tau\circ G.
\end{equation}
Translation equivariance gives $F^t(S)=\tau^tG^t(S)$. Evaluating $F$ at $z$ evaluates $G$ at $z-(0,1)$, so its read rectangle is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:rectF}
D_F=[-6,6]\times[-4,1].
\end{equation}
Thus $F$ also has radius at most six, fixes the vacuum, and preserves every finite mass. Although the component matching for $G$ moves sites by at most one, no such displacement bound is needed to reprove conservation after the global translation.

\section{Four particles and the exact section clock}\label{smc:bp:sec:orbit}
Start from
\[
S_0=\{(0,0),(3,0),(4,0),(k,0)\},\qquad k\ge7.
\]
Put
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:clock}
T_n=n^2+(2k-11)n\qquad(n\in\NN).
\end{equation}
\begin{theorem}[Complete phase description]\label{smc:bp:thm:orbit}
For every $n\ge0$,
\[
G^{T_n}(S_0)=\{(0,n),(3,n),(4,n),(k+n,n)\}.
\]
Writing $d=k+n$, the cycle $[T_n,T_{n+1})$ consists of these two inclusive phase lists:
\begin{align}
G^{T_n+j}(S_0)&=\{(0,n),(3+j,n),(4+j,n),(d,n)\},
&&0\le j\le d-6,\label{smc:bp:eq:ephase}\\
G^{T_n+d-5+q}(S_0)&=\{(0,n),(d-4-q,n),(d-2-q,n),(d+1,n+1)\},
&&0\le q\le d-6.\label{smc:bp:eq:wphase}
\end{align}
In particular, each displayed support contains four distinct particles.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
At the section, the adjacent pair is isolated from both markers. For $j<d-6$, its separation from each marker is at least three, so $E$ advances it by one. At $j=d-6$, the right component is exactly the $R$ triple $\{d-3,d-2,d\}$ in row $n$; the left marker is separated because $d-3\ge4$. The next state is the $q=0$ state of~\eqref{smc:bp:eq:wphase}.

The returning gap-two pair is separated from the lifted marker by three columns: $(d+1)-(d-2)=3$. A row difference of one does not reduce this max-norm distance. The separation only grows during the return. For $q<d-6$, the pair's leftmost site is at least three, so $W$ applies and decreases both horizontal coordinates by one. At $q=d-6$, the lower component is the exact $L$ triple $\{0,2,4\}$, separated from the upper marker by at least $d-3\ge4$. One $L$ step gives the next section.

The duration is $(d-6)+1+(d-6)+1=2d-10$. Summing these durations for $d=k,k+1,\ldots,k+n-1$ gives~\eqref{smc:bp:eq:clock}. This proves induction from $n=0$ \textup{[read: this completes the induction on $n$]}. The endpoints in the two lists cover exactly $2d-10$ states and exclude the next section; they remain valid for $k=7$.
\end{proof}
\wtag\ [Theorem~\ref{smc:bp:thm:orbit} is the planar lift of source~17's Proposition~\ref{smc:fm:prop:hits}: the four input shapes, the two moving pairs, the cycle of $2d-10$ steps and the clock are source~17's, and so are the steps of the proof; only the transverse lifts of the right marker and of the left-bounce output are new, as source~21 says above.]

\begin{figure}[htbp]\centering
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{figures/21-planar-shuttle-orbits.pdf}
\caption{Actual simulation of the component rule from $k=7$. Left: the first eight completed rows visited by $G$, simulated through $T_8$, with the two missing families marked by open circles. Right: every occupied site of $F$ through time 96, colored by the four particles using the bounded matching. The drifted traces have no repeated site. Both panels are generated from the rule, not drawn from the count formulas.}\label{smc:bp:fig:orbits}
\end{figure}

\section{Visited sites and first arrivals}\label{smc:bp:sec:visits}
\begin{theorem}[The wedge and its two missing lines]\label{smc:bp:thm:visited}
The complete stationary-frame visited set is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:visited}
V_k=\{(0,n):n\ge0\}\ \cup\ \{(x,n):n\ge0,\ 2\le x\le k+n-2\}\ \cup\ \{(k+n,n):n\ge0\}.
\end{equation}
It is the integer wedge $n\ge0$, $0\le x\le k+n$ with precisely the two families $x=1$ and $x=k+n-1$ removed.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
On row $n$, the east phase visits $[3,k+n-2]$ and the west phase additionally reaches $2$. It never reaches $1$. The markers occupy $0$ and $k+n$. The right marker may first occupy its row during the preceding cycle, but no extra sites result. Future cycles use higher rows. Hence the union is exactly~\eqref{smc:bp:eq:visited}.
\end{proof}

Let $\theta_k(x,n)$ be the first time $G^t(S_0)$ occupies $(x,n)$, and leave it undefined at an unvisited site. For $n\ge1$, put $d=k+n$. Then the exact disjoint branches are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:first}
\theta_k(x,n)=
\begin{cases}
T_n,&x\in\{0,3,4\},\\
T_n+2d-11,&x=2,\\
T_n+x-4,&5\le x\le d-2,\\
T_n-(d-6),&x=d.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
The same formula holds on row zero except that $\theta_k(k,0)=0$. For the right-marker branch, its creation time is $T_{n-1}+d-6$, and $T_n-T_{n-1}=2d-12$, giving the displayed value. The interior branch is the leading east-moving member's first visit. The site $2$ first appears in the last pre-$L$ return state, whose relative time is $d-5+d-6=2d-11$. These branches partition every visited row even at the smallest gap. They establish piecewise-quadratic first-arrival data directly, without using a certificate compiler.

\section{Exact centered counts and stationary inverse}\label{smc:bp:sec:Gcount}
For integer $N\ge0$, define
\[
C_{G,k}(N)=\#(V_k\cap[-N,N]^2),\qquad
R_{G,k}(M)=\min\{N\in\NN:C_{G,k}(N)\ge M\},\quad M\in\NN.
\]
\begin{theorem}[Stationary count and complete inverse]\label{smc:bp:thm:Gcount}
One has
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:Gcount}
C_{G,k}(N)=
\begin{cases}
1,&N=0,\\
N(N+1),&1\le N\le k-2,\\
\dfrac{N^2+(2k-1)N-k^2+3k-4}{2},&N\ge k-1.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
The exact generalized inverse is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:Ginverse}
R_{G,k}(M)=
\begin{cases}
0,&0\le M\le1,\\
\left\lceil\dfrac{\sqrt{1+4M}-1}{2}\right\rceil,
&2\le M\le(k-2)(k-1),\\[5pt]
\left\lceil\dfrac{\sqrt{8M+8k^2-16k+17}-(2k-1)}{2}\right\rceil,
&M>(k-2)(k-1).
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
Thus $C_{G,k}(N)=\frac12N^2+(k-\frac12)N+O_k(1)$ and
$R_{G,k}(M)=\sqrt{2M}-k+\frac12+O_k(1)$. \wtag\ [The terms $-k+\frac12$ are absorbed by $O_k(1)$; more precisely $R_{G,k}(M)=\sqrt{2M}-k+\frac12+\vartheta_M+o(1)$ with $0\le\vartheta_M<1$, the ceiling's rounding.]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
All visited coordinates are nonnegative. For $1\le N\le k-2$, every included row contributes exactly $N$ sites: $0$ and $2,\ldots,N$. At $N=0$ only the origin contributes.

For $N\ge k$, the full wedge contributes
\[
(N+1)^2-\frac{(N-k)(N-k+1)}2.
\]
Subtract the $N+1$ holes on $x=1$ and the $N-k+2$ holes on $x=k+n-1$. Simplification gives the final branch. At $N=k-1$, the complete square loses $N+1$ sites on $x=1$ and one upper-edge hole; $N(N+1)-1$ agrees with that branch. Omitting either family of holes would produce the wrong polynomial.

The count is strictly increasing, and solving the corresponding quadratic inequality gives the two ceiling formulas. The threshold in~\eqref{smc:bp:eq:Ginverse} places the last inverse in the last count branch. The asymptotics follow by expanding its positive root; integer rounding contributes a bounded error.
\end{proof}

\section{Vertical drift and four disjoint traces}\label{smc:bp:sec:drift}
For each time $t$, let $n(t)$ be the unique integer satisfying $T_{n(t)}\le t<T_{n(t)+1}$. Call the left marker and two matched moving particles the three bulk trajectories. Their $F$ height is
\[
h(t)=t+n(t).
\]
The right marker has $G$ row $r(t)\in\{n(t),n(t)+1\}$, so its $F$ position is $(k+r(t),v(t))$, where $v(t)=t+r(t)$. The functions $n(t)$ and $r(t)$ are nondecreasing, so $h(t)$ and $v(t)$ are strictly increasing.

\begin{lemma}[Disjointness of all four traces]\label{smc:bp:lem:traces}
Each particle's $F$ trace has no self-intersection, and the four traces are pairwise disjoint. Every time contributes four new sites to the all-time visited set.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The strictly increasing heights exclude self-repetition. All three bulk sites at a given time have the same height and distinct horizontal coordinates. Their heights agree across two times only when the times agree, so the three bulk traces are pairwise disjoint.

Suppose a marker site at time $t$ equals a bulk site at time $u$. Write $r=r(t)$ and $n=n(u)$. Every bulk horizontal coordinate is at most $k+n-2$, while the marker coordinate is $k+r$. Equality forces $n\ge r+2$. Height equality gives $u=t+r-n\le t-2$. Monotonicity then implies $n(u)\le n(t)\le r(t)=r$, contradicting $n\ge r+2$. Thus no marker site lies on a bulk trace.
\end{proof}

The three bulk trajectories have one site at every nonnegative height except the skipped levels
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:a}
a_n=T_n+n-1=n^2+(2k-10)n-1,\qquad n\ge1.
\end{equation}
Indeed $n(t)$ rises by one at $T_n$, so $h$ jumps by two there. The right marker rises to row $n+1$ at
\[
\rho_n=T_n+k+n-5.
\]
It therefore skips precisely
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:b}
b_n=\rho_n+n=n^2+(2k-9)n+k-5,\qquad n\ge0.
\end{equation}
Both sequences are strictly increasing. They interlace: $b_0<a_1$, and for $n\ge1$,
\[
a_n<b_n<a_{n+1},\qquad
b_n-a_n=n+k-4,\qquad a_{n+1}-b_n=n+k-5.
\]
No height is skipped by both the bulk and marker families. Notice that ``four new sites per time'' alone does not count sites in a spatial box: the four sites may enter that box at different heights and horizontal positions.

\section{The exact drift count and its inverse}\label{smc:bp:sec:Fcount}
Write $V_{F,k}=\bigcup_{t\ge0}F^t(S_0)$ and define $C_{F,k}(N)$ and $R_{F,k}(M)$ by the same centered-box and generalized-inverse conventions.

\begin{lemma}[The horizontal cutoff]\label{smc:bp:lem:cutoff}
Every $F$-visited site $(x,y)$ satisfies $0\le x\le\max(k+1,y)$ and $y\ge0$. Consequently, for $N\ge k+1$, horizontal truncation removes no visited site of height at most $N$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For bulk sites in rounds $n=0,1$, $x\le k+n-2\le k-1$. For $n\ge2$, $T_n\ge T_2=4k-18\ge k-2$, and hence $x\le k+n-2\le T_n+n\le y$.

For the right marker, rows $r\le1$ give $x=k+r\le k+1$. When $r\ge2$, its first time in that row is $\rho_{r-1}=T_{r-1}+k+r-6$, so
\[
y-x\ge T_{r-1}+r-6\ge T_1-4=2k-14\ge0.
\]
All coordinates are nonnegative by the phase formulas and the drift. The first lifted marker has $x=k+1$, so the claimed threshold cannot simply be replaced by $N\ge k$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Floor-root count and inverse]\label{smc:bp:thm:Fcount}
For every integer $N\ge k+1$, let $\alpha=2k-10$ and $\beta=2k-9$. Then
\begin{align}
A_k(N)&=\#\{n\ge1:a_n\le N\}
=\left\lfloor\frac{\sqrt{\alpha^2+4(N+1)}-\alpha}{2}\right\rfloor,\label{smc:bp:eq:A}\\
B_k(N)&=\#\{n\ge0:b_n\le N\}
=1+\left\lfloor\frac{\sqrt{\beta^2+4(N-k+5)}-\beta}{2}\right\rfloor,\label{smc:bp:eq:B}\\
C_{F,k}(N)&=4(N+1)-3A_k(N)-B_k(N)\label{smc:bp:eq:Fcount}\\
&=4N-4\sqrt N+O_k(1).\nonumber
\end{align}
As $M\to\infty$,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:Finverse}
R_{F,k}(M)=\frac M4+\sqrt{\frac M4}+O_k(1).
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Lemma~\ref{smc:bp:lem:cutoff} reduces the box count to a height count. The three disjoint bulk traces each omit $A_k(N)$ of the $N+1$ heights, and the marker trace omits $B_k(N)$. Lemma~\ref{smc:bp:lem:traces} allows these counts to be added without overlap. Solving the two quadratic inequalities gives~\eqref{smc:bp:eq:A}--\eqref{smc:bp:eq:B}; the stated cutoff ensures that their expressions are nonnegative. Each is $\sqrt N+O_k(1)$.

For the inverse, set $m=M/4$ and $u=m+\sqrt m$. Then $u-\sqrt u=m+O(1)$. Rounding $u$ to an integer changes the count by $O_k(1)$. Beyond the transient, increasing $N$ by one adds four sites at a nonskipped height, one at a bulk skip, or three at a marker skip. The interlacing excludes a simultaneous skip. Thus an $O_k(1)$ count discrepancy can be corrected by $O_k(1)$ further radius, proving~\eqref{smc:bp:eq:Finverse}.
\end{proof}

For completeness, the finite transient also has an exact formula requiring no limiting convention:
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:transient}
C_{F,k}(N)=\sum_{t=0}^N\#\{(x,y)\in G^t(S_0):x\le N,\ t+y\le N\}\qquad(N\ge0).
\end{equation}
All coordinates are nonnegative and the traces are disjoint; times $t>N$ have height greater than $N$. Thus~\eqref{smc:bp:eq:transient} follows directly and can use the complete phase formulas. Together with~\eqref{smc:bp:eq:Fcount}, it gives an exact algorithm for every inverse value: check the finite transient, then find the least integer satisfying the monotone floor inequality. The implementation evaluates roots with integer square roots, including exact-square boundaries, rather than floating-point approximations.

\section{Exact Boolean degree and all essential inputs}\label{smc:bp:sec:degree}
For input shape $A$ at anchor $a$, define the exact-component indicator
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:indicator}
M_{A,a}(c)=\prod_{p\in A+a}c_p\prod_{q\in H(A+a)\setminus(A+a)}(1-c_q).
\end{equation}
On binary inputs it equals one precisely for an isolated recognized component. The local rule is the following real multilinear polynomial on binary inputs:
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:poly}
g_z(c)=c_z+
\sum_{(A,B)}\ \sum_{b\in B\setminus A}M_{A,z-b}(c)
-\sum_{(A,B)}\ \sum_{a\in A\setminus B}M_{A,z-a}(c).
\end{equation}
Its validity on the whole Boolean cube follows from exact recognition and disjoint outputs, not merely from checking the selected orbit. There are respectively $2,4,4,6$ signed translated indicators of types $E,W,R,L$. Each halo is a rectangle of height five and width $6,7,8,9$, respectively. The indicator degrees are consequently $30,35,40,45$.

Summing~\eqref{smc:bp:eq:poly} over sites gives a second finite-input conservation proof: each translated-indicator sum is unchanged by the offset, and $|B\setminus A|=|A\setminus B|$. Only finitely many indicators can be nonzero on a finite support, so these sum rearrangements are legitimate.

\begin{theorem}[Exact degree and exact dependency set]\label{smc:bp:thm:degree}
The unique real multilinear polynomial for the local Boolean rule has degree exactly 45. Every cell of $D_G$ is essential and no other cell is; $F$ has exactly the translated dependency set $D_F$. Both specified rules therefore have exact centered Chebyshev radius six.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The polynomial~\eqref{smc:bp:eq:poly} is multilinear because each indicator uses every input bit at most once. The six $L$ indicators have distinct rectangular halos of size 45. Each has three occupied factors and 42 complementary factors, so its degree-45 top coefficient is $(-1)^{42}=1$, multiplied by the birth or removal sign. Their top monomials are distinct and cannot cancel one another; every other indicator has degree at most 40. This proves exact degree 45 by uniqueness of multilinear interpolation on the Boolean cube.

For the three births, the $L$ halos have horizontal intervals $[-2,6]$, $[-5,3]$, $[-6,2]$ and vertical interval $[-3,1]$. For the three removals, the horizontal intervals are $[-2,6]$, $[-4,4]$, $[-6,2]$ and the vertical interval is $[-2,2]$. Their union is exactly $D_G$. Every one of its 78 variables therefore occurs in a nonzero degree-45 monomial.

If a Boolean function were independent of one such variable, the difference between the polynomial's one and zero restrictions would vanish on the Boolean cube. Uniqueness of multilinear interpolation would force this derivative polynomial to vanish identically, contradicting the nonzero monomial containing that variable. Thus all 78 variables are essential. Section~\ref{smc:bp:sec:locality} excludes any other dependency. Translating the evaluation point gives $D_F$ and its essentiality. Both rectangles contain a horizontal coordinate of absolute value six, which proves the exact centered radius.
\end{proof}

The release also supplies an explicit finite witness for each cell: two configurations differing at that cell only, with different central outputs. The file \file{essential-input-witnesses.json} in \file{scientific/audit/} records all 78 pairs. They are checked with both the direct component simulator and the independently encoded cylinder evaluator. Translating both inputs down one row gives the corresponding $F$ witness. This is a concrete flip-witness confirmation independent of relying on the top-monomial argument. Exact radius here is a property of these two rules, not a least-radius claim over all possible binary constructions.

\section{A literal one step quartic with unique auxiliaries}\label{smc:bp:sec:quartic}
Enumerate the 78 cells of $D_G$ in row-major order, increasing $y$ and then $x$, and add one external output variable $y_{\rm out}$. There are 79 external variables. For each of the sixteen indicators, use its own unshared multiplication chain, listing occupied factors first and complementary factors afterward. Within each group use row-major order. Start the chain with its first external occupied factor. At every subsequent factor introduce one new auxiliary $z$ and one residual
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:gates}
z-uv\quad\hbox{or}\quad z-u(1-v),
\end{equation}
where $u$ is the preceding chain value and $v$ is the next external input. Indicator order and all variable indices are recorded canonically in the certificate.

There are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:aux}
2\cdot29+4\cdot34+4\cdot39+6\cdot44=614
\end{equation}
auxiliaries and the same number of gate residuals. Add the 78 bit residuals $c_i(c_i-1)$ and the output residual
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bp:eq:outres}
y_{\rm out}-c_{(0,0)}-\sum_{\rm births}z_{\rm last}+\sum_{\rm removals}z_{\rm last}.
\end{equation}
Let $P$ be the sum of squares of these $614+78+1=693$ residuals. The circuit gives an ordinary integer polynomial, not a compressed truth predicate or a symbolic placeholder for an unspecified computation.
\wtag\ [Arithmetizing a Boolean circuit by bit equations and product gates is the standard device of Part~IV's gate residuals (Section~\ref{smc:sl:sec:presburger-quartic}); the counts 614, 693 and 3403 are source~21's own.]

\begin{theorem}[The local zero set and canonical witnesses]\label{smc:bp:thm:quartic}
The total degree of $P$ is exactly four. For any fixed external input-output tuple, its natural auxiliary fiber has exactly one element if that tuple is a valid binary local transition, and has no element otherwise. The same statement holds when the auxiliaries range over all real numbers.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Every residual has degree at most two, so $P$ has degree at most four. The squares of bit residuals supply positive fourth-power monomials of the external input variables, which cannot be canceled by the other squared residuals here; hence the degree is exactly four.

Since $P$ is a sum of real squares, $P=0$ is equivalent to simultaneous vanishing of every residual. The bit residuals force each external input into $\{0,1\}$. Each acyclic chain equation then forces its next auxiliary uniquely, starting from an external input. All forced values are themselves zero or one. Finally~\eqref{smc:bp:eq:outres} forces the output to equal~\eqref{smc:bp:eq:poly}, hence the actual binary local output. Conversely, for a valid transition these forced chain values make every residual zero.

Therefore the unique real auxiliary tuple is natural, and invalid external tuples have no real or natural auxiliary solution. This argument proves uniqueness by the specific deterministic chain structure. It is not an inference from finite perturbation tests or from decidability.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The exact algebra ledger}
There are $2\cdot1+4\cdot1+4\cdot2+6\cdot2=26$ plain-product gates, each with two residual monomials, and $2\cdot28+4\cdot33+4\cdot37+6\cdot42=588$ complementary-factor gates, each with three. The bit residuals each have two monomials and the output residual has 18. Thus the uncollected ledgers are
\begin{align*}
\text{residual-monomial occurrences}&=26\cdot2+588\cdot3+78\cdot2+18=1990,\\
\text{ordered square-expansion occurrences}&=26\cdot4+588\cdot9+78\cdot4+18^2=6032.
\end{align*}
Collecting equal monomials in the literal exported polynomial gives Table~\ref{smc:bp:tab:ledger}. The last three values were independently reconstructed and compared exactly, not assumed from the circuit description.

\begin{table}[htbp]\centering
\begin{tabular}{lr}\toprule
Resource & Exact value\\\midrule
External input bits & 78\\
External variables including output & 79\\
Canonical natural auxiliaries & 614\\
Total variables & 693\\
Squared residuals & 693\\
Residual-monomial occurrences & 1990\\
Ordered square-expansion occurrences & 6032\\
Distinct collected monomials & 3403\\

Total degree & 4\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Literal resource ledger for the deliberately unshared one-step circuit. No auxiliary-minimality claim is made.}\label{smc:bp:tab:ledger}
\end{table}

The machine-readable \file{scientific/local-quartic-certificate.json} contains all 3403 collected terms, the full variable order, all 614 gates, all 693 residuals, and all sixteen indicators. A monomial is a list of variable indices with repetitions representing powers; coefficients are exact integers. The independent artifact reader re-expands squared residuals using unordered pairs and compares the resulting sparse polynomial exactly. A second reconstruction begins from the geometric primitive replacements and independently rebuilds indicators, gates, residuals, and every coefficient. Thus the expanded artifact is checked against both its circuit and its intended geometry.

\section{Verification and portable reproduction}\label{smc:bp:sec:verification}
The release separates proofs from executable evidence. The reviewed source proofs \file{PROOF.md} and \file{LOCAL_ALGEBRA.md} are preserved under \file{scientific/}. This report supplies a connected mathematical presentation. Independent reviews and explicit flip witnesses accompany the source files. No finite regression is offered as an enumeration of all full-shift configurations.

\subsection{Independent routes and finite coverage}
The direct simulator \file{component_rule.py} builds occupied components and applies the four replacements. The pointwise evaluator \file{local_rule.py} imports neither that simulator nor its rule dictionary; it encodes the sixteen occupied-and-empty cylinders independently and exports exact integer masks. Both $G$ and $F$ are evaluated.

The primary suite checks all 4096 supports in a $4\times3$ rectangle, all 8192 supports in a 13-site line, arbitrary exterior contexts, one-site halo interference, interacting active and malformed templates, births over a full-radius candidate region, large translations, exact orbit phases, first arrivals, both box counts, disjoint traces, and integer-root boundary cases. Its deterministic receipt reports 76680 direct orbit phase steps, 46980 first-arrival checks, and 53601 drift count checks. These are finite checks of the displayed formulas, not substitutes for the all-input proofs.

The quartic artifact reader checks 350 binary local fixtures and their incorrect binary outputs. At the vacuum witness it tests all 614 upward unit perturbations, one per auxiliary. It also compares the sparse identity at 60 nonbinary integer points and obtains all 78 essentiality witnesses. These tests do not exhaust all auxiliary perturbations on all inputs; uniqueness is proved in Theorem~\ref{smc:bp:thm:quartic}. Independent component, drift, cross-implementation, and geometry-to-quartic reconstruction checks provide separate routes. Every scientific test used by the release replay uses explicit exception checks, so optimization does not disable its checks. Normal and \file{-O} runs must agree with the exact expected receipts, including JSON value types.

\subsection{Integrity before execution and isolated outputs}
The portable verifier first compares the exact required payload file set and independently pinned SHA-256 values before executing any packaged scientific code. It then runs in fresh external copies. Adjacent-output scripts are executed only in those copies. Expected receipts are compared recursively with exact types, so a Boolean is not accepted in place of an integer. The verifier checks that release bytes, file modes, and modification times are unchanged after the run. The release checksum list and archive checksum provide an additional external integrity layer; executing the verifier still presumes trust in that bootstrap file.

The README supplies exact commands and requirements. Scientific replay needs Python 3.10 or later and only the standard library. PDF rebuild needs \file{pdflatex} and the listed TeX packages; figure regeneration additionally needs Matplotlib. Supplied vector PDF figures allow a report rebuild without Matplotlib. Build products and replay receipts belong outside the release. Bounded tamper regressions test changed code, missing required files, altered certificate content, and strict typed comparisons; they do not run the scientific suite on tampered payloads.

The portable package contains no Python bytecode caches, private absolute paths, third-party source caches, or files from earlier releases. Those earlier releases are cited, not modified. The exact source and receipt lineage is recorded in \file{verification/source-lineage.json}.

\section{Consequences limits and next questions}\label{smc:bp:sec:limits}
This example realizes two distinct counting regimes with an ordinary binary mass-four orbit: a quadratic stationary-frame wedge count with sharp coefficient $1/2$, and a linear drifted count with a square-root deficit of coefficient four. The deficit records skipped heights of four disjoint traces, rather than weighted-site multiplicities. The two removed wedge lines and the finite horizontal cutoff are essential to the exact formulas.

The construction proves existence for the specified initial family, not a classification of arbitrary malformed orbits. Malformed inputs are covered by the conservation and locality proof; they are not claimed to enter a shuttle. Neither $G$ nor $F$ is asserted reversible or universal. No smallest mass, smallest radius among constructions, minimal number of essential cells, optimal Boolean degree, or optimal auxiliary count is asserted.

The local quartic relates 78 input bits to one next-step output. Its unique real auxiliary tuple follows from acyclic multiplication chains and bit equations. It does not imply an unbounded-time finite-fold representation for arbitrary recursively enumerable sets. Report 30 separately proves that, for a fixed promised conservative CA and fixed mass-at-most-four input, untimed reachability of a canonical \emph{complete configuration} has an effective ordinary quartic with one natural witness tuple, optionally including first occurrence time~\textup{[source~20, Part~\ref{smc:zd:part}]}. That theorem uses the full classified timed charts and whole-orbit injectivity in the expanding case. Its hypotheses include this example, but its general certificate is not the 614-auxiliary local polynomial here. Site or partial-pattern recurrence cannot be substituted for complete-target injectivity, and no real-witness conclusion is inherited from that theorem.

Natural next questions remain tightly connected to this construction:
\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{smc:bp:q:radius} Can a binary planar four-particle wedge be realized with a smaller centered radius or fewer essential cells while retaining a transparent all-input conservation proof? (\wtag\ Open. Compare source~17's Question~\ref{smc:fm:q:radius} for the one-dimensional rule, which stays open too.)
\item\label{smc:bp:q:shared} Can shared products reduce the 614 local auxiliaries without introducing noncanonical inactive values, and what exact collected polynomial results?
\item\label{smc:bp:q:bounces} Which changes to the two transverse bounces preserve four-trace disjointness after drift, and which change the coefficient of the square-root deficit?
\end{enumerate}
These are questions, not claims settled by the present finite checks or by the existing general classification.

Four complete native or spatially blocked circuits have respectively 604, 479, 477 and 480 arithmetic operations, 60, 58, 58 and 58 positive witnesses, and exact degrees 2344, 1192, 1192 and 1192. Each includes twenty comparison squares and the entire finalizer. The original four-phase variant pays one additional multiplication. A separately audited constant-folded schedule reduces both native and phase-four totals to 603, 478, 476 and 479, with unchanged witness counts and degrees. Exact degrees have deterministic modular leading-component certificates. Both directions of the first-target interpretation follow from explicitly identified inherited theorems. Every accepted nonempty fiber has infinitely many positive witnesses, as every sufficiently large dyadic height admits a fresh native extension. The four fixtures themselves halt in one or two source steps and are nonuniversal demonstrations. No arbitrary c.e. ordinary-input loader, universal numerical bound, optimality claim, rational-zero theorem or materialized full positive Pell witness is supplied. Initially halted sources have separate four-gate, witness-free quadratic certificates.
\end{quote}

\section{Result and scope}\label{smc:uc:sec:result}
Throughout, $\NN=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ and every existential coordinate of a nonempty packet belongs to $\Np$. Fix a reversible separated two-counter source $R$ whose entry $q_0$ has no incoming instruction and whose terminal halt $q_h$ has no outgoing instruction. For the nonempty construction assume $q_0\ne q_h$. The raw initial payload is $N_0=x+1$, with $x\in\NN$; its prime-two and prime-three valuations encode the two counters. Factors coprime to six are part of the payload and are preserved.

The inherited three-mass compiler uses a finite alphabet of Boolean channel subsets, with mass equal to the number of occupied channels and vacuum of mass zero. The resulting cellular automaton (CA) preserves total mass three on the configurations here. This is a weighted finite-alphabet model, not the model in which an integer state label itself equals its mass.

\begin{theorem}[Fixed-source clean-time composition]\label{smc:uc:thm:main}
Assume the inherited complete raw-history/native theorem and the inherited exact clean-target CA theorem described in Section~\ref{smc:uc:sec:dependencies}. For an eligible fixed source $R$, the construction below gives an integer polynomial $Q_R(x,U;z,\theta)$ with no external history horizon, such that for every $x,U\in\NN$,
\[
\exists (z,\theta)\in\Np^{d_R+1}\quad Q_R(x,U;z,\theta)=0
\]
if and only if the cleaned CA first reaches its exact canonical whole-configuration target at time $U$ from its canonical input at raw payload $x+1$. The terminal payload $F$ is a retained coordinate of $z$ and
\[
U=2\theta+192(F+x+1)+16.
\]
Spatial blocking preserves this time. The four-phase construction replaces the right side by four times the entire expression. The dimension depends on the fixed source, not its runtime.
\end{theorem}

This is a composition theorem with explicit dependencies. The portable packet emits the construction completely for these four fixed sources:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}llll@{}}\toprule
Fixture & Literal source & Accepted raw inputs & Steps\\\midrule
INC2;DEC2 & $s\xrightarrow{\mathrm{INC2}}a\xrightarrow{\mathrm{DEC2}}h$ & all $N_0>0$ & 2\\
ZERO3 & $s\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ZERO3}}h$ & $3\nmid N_0$ & 1\\
NOP & $s\xrightarrow{\mathrm{NOP}}h$ & all $N_0>0$ & 1\\
POSITIVE3 & $s\xrightarrow{\mathrm{POSITIVE3}}h$ & $3\mid N_0$ & 1\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
A disabled test is a nonfinal stuck state. Each fixture has singleton incoming and outgoing instruction groups, fresh entry and terminal halt. Its generic certificate has no horizon parameter, but these short executions do not demonstrate a long or universal execution. Their simple accepted relations could have much smaller specialized descriptions; the measured costs concern the fully retained generic compiler, not minimal representations.

The present unbounded packet differs from Reports 19--20 \textup{[Parts~IV and~V of \path{five-particle-binary-automata}, on the binary five-particle automaton]}: those reports concern finite-horizon CA schemas and canonical natural witness tuples. Here the native positive witnesses have unbounded height freedom, and accepted nonempty fibers are provably infinite.

\section{The clean source and exact physical target}\label{smc:uc:sec:clean}
\wtag\ [This section restates source~15's clean return wrapper and exact target for the reader: the wrapper and its restoration theorem are Section~\ref{smc:ct:sec:wrapper} and Theorem~\ref{smc:ct:thm:restore}, the freshness discussion is Section~\ref{smc:ct:sec:fresh}, the target is Theorem~\ref{smc:ct:thm:equiv}, and the clock identity~\eqref{smc:uc:eq:clean} is Theorem~\ref{smc:ct:thm:clock}, in which source~15 writes $\Theta$ for $\theta$, $N_h$ for $F$ and $T_{\cl}$ for $\Tclean$. It is printed in full as source~22's own account; no novelty is claimed for it.]
\subsection{Forward and reverse source traces}\label{smc:uc:sec:traces}
Construct $R_{\mathrm{clean}}$ with controls $\mathrm F:q$, $\mathrm B:q$ for each source control $q$, and a new sole halt $H$. Copy every source instruction forward, copy its inverse backward, and add
\[
\mathrm F:q_h\xrightarrow{\mathrm{NOP}}\mathrm B:q_h,
\qquad
\mathrm B:q_0\xrightarrow{\mathrm{NOP}}H.
\]
INC and positive-only DEC exchange; ZERO, POSITIVE and NOP are self-inverse. In the backward copy, incoming and outgoing source groups interchange. Singleton arithmetic groups remain singletons, and a complementary pair of tests remains disjoint. Terminality makes the first bridge legal; entry freshness makes the second bridge legal.

Suppose the original first-halting trace has $\ell$ instructions and payloads $N_0,\ldots,N_\ell=F$. The cleaned trace is its forward copy, the halt bridge, its uniquely determined inverse trace, and the entry bridge. Each reverse step restores its actual forward input. No original instruction enters $q_0$, so the reverse copy cannot reach $\mathrm B:q_0$ prematurely. Thus the first $H$ occurs after $2\ell+2$ source instructions and restores the entire integer $N_0$, including its coprime cofactor. A nonhalting or nonfinal stuck forward run never reaches the first bridge.

Freshness is a genuine hypothesis. An arbitrary source cannot be made eligible merely by prepending a NOP: it can conflict with existing incoming groups. If $q_0$ recurs in the original trace, an unguarded reverse exit at $\mathrm B:q_0$ could leave before the input is restored. The packet includes a rejecting regression for such a nonfresh source.

\subsection{Geometry and first target}\label{smc:uc:sec:geometry}
At a canonical native section, the fixed right marker is at absolute coordinate $0$, and the clean stage-zero controller with its stationary shuttle is at $-12N_0$. All other channels and sites are vacuum. The input controller is $\mathrm F:q_0$; the exact target replaces it by $H$ at the same positions. Equality includes the entire finite configuration, not just an observed control label or a translate.

The inherited section theorem excludes an earlier target at a macro boundary or inside a macro. A stuck source follows its prescribed shuttle escape and cannot form that target. Arbitrary completion rows are not used before the first target or along these nonhalting and stuck continuations. No claim is made about later target recurrences or stationary posthalt behavior.

Blocking four sites gives radius one, moves the left pair to $-3N_0$ with offset zero, and preserves every time. The alternative four-phase radius-one simulator keeps the native positions; its exact target is phase zero. Its first time is four times the native time, since off-section phases cannot equal this target. Both preserve mass three without a background.

\subsection{The clock identity}\label{smc:uc:sec:clockid}
A forward step $N\to N'$ has native duration
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\mathrm{INC}:&108N+96N'+8,\\
\mathrm{DEC}:&96N+108N'+8,\\
\mathrm{ZERO},\mathrm{POSITIVE},\mathrm{NOP}:&192N+8\quad(N'=N).
\end{array}
\]
Interchanging $N,N'$ and inverting the instruction preserves the duration. If $\theta$ is the forward duration, the reverse half also takes $\theta$. The two NOP bridges take $192F+8$ and $192N_0+8$. Therefore
\begin{equation}\label{smc:uc:eq:clean}
\Tclean=2\theta+192(F+N_0)+16
       =2\theta+192(F+x+1)+16.
\end{equation}
This is forward execution of a logically reversed source with different control states. It does not follow from microscopic CA reversibility alone.

\section{The complete polynomial and both directions}\label{smc:uc:sec:polynomial}
The only exact raw coordinate $y$ occurs in the final output-copy residual $F-y$. It occurs in neither the raw core nor the other nineteen comparisons. The differently named native auxiliary \file{native__y_aux} is retained. Replace every occurrence of the raw natural time $t$ by a fresh positive coordinate $\theta$, including its occurrence in the height and clock row. Drop only $F=y$, retain positive $F$ and its encoded endpoint, and append~\eqref{smc:uc:eq:clean}.

Let $E_1,\ldots,E_{19}$ be the retained residuals after the time substitution, with $F$ among $z$. The complete emitted polynomial is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:uc:eq:sos}
Q_R(x,U;z,\theta)
 =\sum_{i=1}^{19}E_i(x,z,\theta)^2
  +\bigl(2\theta+192(F+x+1)+16-U\bigr)^2.
\end{equation}
Equivalently, as an identity of integer polynomials on all tuples,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:uc:eq:identity}
Q_R(x,U;z,\theta)=P_R(x,F,\theta;z)
             +\bigl(2\theta+192(F+x+1)+16-U\bigr)^2.
\end{equation}
The old last square is identically zero after the explicit substitution $y=F$. This identity does not compare the polynomials while leaving $y$ independently free. For phase four, multiply the entire clean affine expression by four inside the new square.

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{smc:uc:thm:main}]
For soundness, an integer zero of~\eqref{smc:uc:eq:sos} makes every residual zero, since a sum of real squares is zero only when each square is zero. Set the forgotten natural coordinate $y=F$ and the original natural time $t=\theta$. Positivity makes both substitutions admissible. This reconstructs a zero of the complete inherited raw certificate, hence an actual first-halting source trace with its exact terminal payload and native time. The clean-wrapper theorem and~\eqref{smc:uc:eq:clean} give its first exact whole-configuration target at the requested $U$.

Conversely, if the cleaned CA first reaches its target, the inherited clean theorem gives an original first halt. Its $F$ is positive and its $\theta$ is positive because the source starts away from halt and every genuine instruction has positive duration. The raw theorem supplies positive witnesses at $y=F,t=\theta$. These witnesses satisfy the nineteen retained rows, while~\eqref{smc:uc:eq:clean} supplies the twentieth. Thus~\eqref{smc:uc:eq:sos} vanishes. The spatial and phase statements follow from their inherited section correspondence.
\end{proof}

Promoting $t$ directly to a positive variable costs one witness and no arithmetic gate; a separate $W-1$ shift is unnecessary for nonempty runs. No reverse history packet, reverse native witnesses, new selector lane, hidden external horizon or unpaid exponentiation is introduced. Removing $F$ itself would invalidate the positive target port and the halt-bridge duration; removing chronological or native rows is also unjustified.

\section{Retained chronology and nonwrapping time}\label{smc:uc:sec:chronology}
\wtag\ [This section restates, for the circuit with $t$ replaced by $\theta$, the residue-history proof~\cite{residuehistory} and the exact-clock argument of the pinned interface and of its independent review~\cite{threemassraw}, with the radix $Ch^2$ in place of the former linear one; it is printed in full as source~22's own account.]
\subsection{Pretyping and the actual history}\label{smc:uc:sec:pretyping}
The general encoded source configuration is $n=K(N-1)+q$. Here $K=5$ and $m=6K=30$. The residue fixes the control and payload modulo six. The source becomes a total positive residue-affine map
\[
f(mq+s)=a_s q+d_s,\qquad q\geq0,\quad1\leq s\leq m,
\]
with integer $a_s\geq0,d_s>0$. Missing guards, the halt control, trap and unused labels go to a permanent rejecting trap with unchanged payload. A nonempty orbit ending at the original halt is consequently a genuine first-halting source orbit.

In the general construction choose a source-dependent dyadic $C$ at least the inherited radix multiplier and $2384m+2$. For the four fixtures $C=131072$ suffices. For the packet's height $h$, distinct from its source step count $\ell$, retain
\[
h=n_0+n_f+\theta+\eta,\qquad B=Ch^2,\qquad C=131072,
\qquad\eta>0.
\]
Write selector hats as $\widehat E_s=E_s+1$, quotient hat as $\widehat W=W+1$, and exceptional-slope hats as $\widehat Z_a=Z_a+1$. Set
\[
J=\sum_s E_s,\quad P=(B-1)J+1,\quad
G_a=\sum_{s:a_s=a}E_s,\quad R_h=(h-1)J.
\]
The two retained outer equations are
\begin{align}
J+(W+1)+\sum_a(Z_a+1)+\beta&=P,\qquad\beta>0,\label{smc:uc:eq:global}\\
B\mathcal N+n_0&=\mathcal C+Pn_f,\label{smc:uc:eq:transport}
\end{align}
where the paid chronological words are
\[
\mathcal C=mW+\sum_s sE_s,\qquad
\mathcal N=a_0W+\sum_a(a-a_0)Z_a+\sum_s d_sE_s.
\]
Negative slope differences are allowed in this algebraic expression; nonnegativity is not presumed before typing.

Equation~\eqref{smc:uc:eq:global} first excludes $J=0$: then $P=1$ while $W+1+\beta\geq2$. It bounds $W,Z_a,J<P$, with $E_s,G_a\leq J$. The selector, class and range AND lanes are
\[
(E_s,J,E_s),\qquad (W,(B-1)G_a,Z_a),\qquad (W,R_h,W).
\]
All lane coefficients lie in $[0,P)$. Concatenate them in base $P$ to ports $H_*,M_*,A_*$. If $L=m+g+1$ and $v$ is the least power of two at least $L$, then
\[
0\leq H_*,M_*,A_*<P^L\leq P^v<Q_*=BP^v.
\]
These bounds are obtained before assuming a history or digit typing. The sixteen retained native comparisons, on the paid padded ports
\[
16H_*+12,\quad16M_*+10,\quad16A_*+8,\quad16Q_*,
\]
give the prescribed-scale native AND theorem. They force $Q_*$ dyadic and $H_*\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}M_*=A_*$. Hence $B,P$ are dyadic, and so is the integer $h$, since $B=Ch^2$ and $C$ is dyadic.

The identity $P-1=(B-1)J$ now forces $P=B^\ell$ for an integer $\ell\geq1$: writing $B=2^b,P=2^p$ and reducing $p$ modulo $b$ proves $b\mid p$. Thus $J=1+B+\cdots+B^{\ell-1}$. Selectors are subsets of these unit positions. Their sum is $J$; the bound $m<B$ prevents a carry, so exactly one residue is selected at each time. The range lane gives quotient digits $0\leq q_i<h$, and class lanes select their correct subsets. The words in~\eqref{smc:uc:eq:transport} consequently have genuine positive base-$B$ digits. Their bounds and the endpoint bounds yield
\[
n_0=\mathcal C_0,\qquad
\mathcal C_{i+1}=\mathcal N_i,\qquad
\mathcal N_{\ell-1}=n_f.
\]
This is actual chronological transport, not an unordered flow or a bare endpoint comparison. The inherited proof supplies the exact digit bounds; replacing its former linear radix by $Ch^2$ preserves them because the new radix dominates the old multiplier times $h$.

\subsection{Why the clock congruence is exact}\label{smc:uc:sec:nowrapclock}
Each current encoded configuration lies in $[1,mh]$. No current configuration repeats in a deterministic first-halting orbit: repetition would force a cycle and exclude the later first halt. Therefore
\[
1\leq\ell\leq mh.
\]
Each current payload satisfies $N\leq6h$, and every genuine native tick satisfies
\[
0<\tau\leq396N+8\leq2384h.
\]
It follows that
\begin{equation}\label{smc:uc:eq:nowrap}
\sum_{i<\ell}\tau_i\leq2384mh^2<Ch^2-1=B-1,
\end{equation}
since $C\geq2384m+2$. Independently the positive height identity gives $0<\theta<h<B-1$.

The paid affine packed clock $\mathcal C_\tau=\sum_i\tau_iB^i$ uses exactly the same selected-quotient and selector hats. Its retained comparison is
\[
\mathcal C_\tau=(B-1)(\widehat k-1)+\theta,\qquad\widehat k>0.
\]
Reducing modulo $B-1$ gives $\sum_i\tau_i\equiv\theta\pmod{B-1}$. Both numbers lie in $[0,B-2]$ by~\eqref{smc:uc:eq:nowrap}; hence they are equal. Hiding $\theta$ existentially changes none of these paid guards. The new cleanup square is applied only after exact native time is established.

This argument requires first-halt rejecting totalization. It does not apply automatically to arbitrary endpoints that permit looping after an earlier acceptance. Nor is a bounded sample of nonhalting behavior proof of nonhalting.

\section{Every accepted nonempty witness fiber is infinite}\label{smc:uc:sec:fibers}
\begin{theorem}[Infinite positive fibers]\label{smc:uc:thm:fibers}
For any accepted fixed pair $(x,U)$ of an emitted nonempty native, spatial or phase-four circuit, its complete positive witness fiber is infinite. Rejected fibers are empty. This assertion excludes the separate initially halted circuits.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Fix the actual first-halting source trace, its payload $F$, native time $\theta$, encoded endpoints $n_0,n_f$, length $\ell\geq1$ and residue quotients $q_i$. For every sufficiently large dyadic integer
\[
h>\max\{n_0+n_f+\theta,q_0,\ldots,q_{\ell-1}\},
\]
set $\eta=h-n_0-n_f-\theta>0$, $B=Ch^2$, $P=B^\ell$ and $J=1+B+\cdots+B^{\ell-1}$. Pack the same residue indicators, quotients and selected quotients in this new base. Zero words have positive hat one and are allowed.

Let $g\leq m-1$ be the number of exceptional slope classes. They are disjoint, so $\sum_aZ_a\leq W\leq(h-1)J$. The exact remaining global slack is
\begin{align*}
\beta&=P-J-(W+1)-\sum_a(Z_a+1)\\
     &=(B-2)J-W-\sum_aZ_a-g\\
     &\geq(B-2h)J-g>0.
\end{align*}
For the last inequality, the new radix satisfies $B\geq K_0h$, where the inherited dyadic multiplier $K_0$ is at least $4$ and $m+1$; also $h\geq3$ and $J\geq1$. Thus $(B-2h)J\geq(K_0-2)hJ>g$. These are strict positive supplied slacks, not merely nonnegative residuals.

All actual lane equalities hold. Selector words are at most $J$, quotient and selected-quotient words are at most $(h-1)J<P$, class masks are at most $(B-1)J=P-1$, and the range mask is below $P$. Therefore the concatenated ports are below the dyadic prescribed scale $Q_*=BP^v$. Their padded positive versions are strictly below $16Q_*$. The inherited prescribed-scale completeness theorem supplies fresh positive native witnesses at every such scale. No old native tuple is assumed to remain valid when $h$ changes.

Chronological transport is the actual fixed path, and
\[
\widehat k=1+\frac{\mathcal C_\tau-\theta}{B-1}\in\Np,
\]
since $\mathcal C_\tau-\theta=\sum_i\tau_i(B^i-1)$ is a nonnegative multiple of $B-1$. For $\ell=1$ the quotient is zero and the hat is one. The terminal payload and cleanup equation preserve the same fixed external $(x,U)$. Thus every permitted height extends to a full positive zero.

There are infinitely many such dyadic heights; distinct heights give distinct retained $\eta$. The resulting complete tuples are distinct regardless of native multiplicity at a fixed scale.
\end{proof}
The result is an all-height consequence of the inherited completeness theorem. The checker verifies 54 larger-height outer extensions as implementation evidence; it does not numerically construct huge full native/Pell witnesses. A deterministic source trace and unique reverse lift therefore coexist with infinitely many arithmetic witnesses. These emitted representations are not finite-fold, without implying any multiplicity limitation for a different representation of the same simple relation.

This theorem shows that for the present coding it does not. Source~23 (Theorems~\ref{smc:ch:thm:projection} and~\ref{smc:ch:thm:infinite}) shows that infinitude survives even at the least admissible height.]

\section{Complete arithmetic ledgers and exact degrees}\label{smc:uc:sec:ledgers}
\subsection{Literal cost model}\label{smc:uc:sec:costmodel}
Each binary $+$, $-$ or $\times$ gate costs one operation. Constant multiplications and squarings count as multiplications; the integer literals are explicitly listed in each ledger. This model does not synthesize those constants from a restricted initial constant set. There is no gate for exponentiation, division, bitwise AND or an unspecified predicate. Powers such as $P^v$ are realized by their fixed squaring chains. Bitwise AND appears only in the semantic checker of the native encoding, not as a free polynomial gate.

The new affine bridge consists of these six paid gates:
\[
F+x,\quad F+x+1,\quad192(F+x+1),\quad2\theta,
\quad192(F+x+1)+2\theta,\quad192(F+x+1)+2\theta+16.
\]
They cost $2M+4A$, where $A$ includes addition and subtraction. Deleting the old $F=y$ square and its accumulation removes $1M+2A$; adding the clean-time square and its accumulation restores $1M+2A$. Every final twenty-row SOS uses twenty subtractions, twenty squarings and nineteen additions: $20M+39A=59$ gates.

\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrrrrr@{}}\toprule
Fixture & Raw core & $M$ & $A$ & Total & Witnesses & Degree\\\midrule
INC2;DEC2 & 539 & 239 & 365 & 604 & 60 & 2344\\
ZERO3 & 414 & 184 & 295 & 479 & 58 & 1192\\
NOP & 412 & 182 & 295 & 477 & 58 & 1192\\
POSITIVE3 & 415 & 189 & 291 & 480 & 58 & 1192\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
These totals include the core, six bridge gates and the full finalizer. Each has two natural parameters $x,U$ and twenty comparisons. Spatial blocking uses precisely the same polynomials. Phase four adds one multiplication by literal four before the final clean comparison, giving totals $605,480,478,481$ with the same $A$, witnesses and degrees.

respectively, since $192+16=208$ and $4\cdot208=832$. In either model, compute $F+x$, the first scalar product, the $\theta$ product, their sum, and the final constant addition. \subsection{Witnesses and literal inheritance}\label{smc:uc:sec:witnesses}
The witnesses are the raw positive list followed by \file{theta_positive}: twenty-two native coordinates, thirty selector hats, one quotient hat, $g$ selected-quotient hats, two slacks, $F$, the shifted clock quotient and $\theta$. Thus the count is $58+g$, with $g=2$ for INC2;DEC2 and zero for the other fixtures. The exact gate and coordinate names are in every JSON circuit and matching textual DAG.

The independent auditor checks 3560 inherited-gate identities across all eight nonempty variants. Every raw core gate is unchanged except the operand substitution $t\mapsto\theta$. It checks all 152 retained comparison-pair identities and the complete twenty-row finalizers. The complete ancestor set of the output equals all declared gates and ports: there are no undeclared operands, forward references, dead charged gates or dead supplied coordinates.

\subsection{Deterministic exact degree certificates}\label{smc:uc:sec:degree}
The claimed degrees are exact total polynomial degrees in all supplied coordinates, before restricting to the zero set or quantifying witnesses. Give each coordinate $v_i$ degree one and each integer literal degree zero. Propagate a formal bound $d$ by addition of bounds at multiplication and maximum at addition or subtraction. Simultaneously evaluate the degree-$d$ homogeneous component under the integer ray
\[
v_i=(i+2)z,\qquad i=0,1,\ldots,
\]
using the exact emitted order \file{parameters + auxiliaries}, modulo $p=1000003$.

At a sum or difference of bound $d$, an operand contributes its stored coefficient only if its formal bound equals $d$. At a product, multiply the stored top coefficients. A zero coefficient never lowers the bound: cancellation on this chosen ray cannot justify discarding lower components for subsequent operations. Induction on the gate list proves both the degree upper bound and the claimed component evaluation. A nonzero output value modulo $p$ implies a genuinely nonzero integer homogeneous component, so the lower bound matches the upper bound. Primality is not needed for this nonzero-modulus implication.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrr@{}}\toprule
Circuit family & Degree & Top value modulo $1000003$\\\midrule
INC2;DEC2 native and phase four & 2344 & 135347\\
ZERO3 NOP POSITIVE3 native and phase four & 1192 & 977370\\
Initially halted native & 2 & 585225\\
Initially halted phase four & 2 & 418734\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The full weight map and every per-gate degree/top row are in the JSON artifacts. Two independently implemented data-only checkers recompute the certificates. Nonempty traces contain two zero-top entries, and an explicit cancellation regression verifies retention of their bounds. Equality of the high-degree native and phase-four coefficients is consistent with changing only a degree-one time residual. No degree claim is a lower bound on circuit size or on the intrinsic complexity of the represented relation.

\section{Initially halted sources and raw input limits}\label{smc:uc:sec:halted}
\subsection{The separate zero step circuit}\label{smc:uc:sec:zerostep}
If $q_0=q_h$, freshness and terminality make it isolated. The cleaned trace consists of two NOP bridges, with $\theta=0$ and $F=N_0$. Hence
\[
\Tclean=384N_0+16=384x+400.
\]
The separate polynomial is
\[
(384x+400-U)^2,
\]
with four gates, $2M+2A$, one comparison, zero witnesses and degree two. Its phase-four counterpart is $(1536x+1600-U)^2$, with the same ledger by constant folding. Neither is forced through the positive-time nonempty packet. At an accepted external pair the witness fiber is the singleton empty tuple, so the infinite-fiber theorem does not apply.

\subsection{All input clock sanity checks}\label{smc:uc:sec:sanity}
On accepted paths of the four fixtures, $F=N_0$. Direct source arithmetic gives
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll@{}}\toprule
Fixture & Native forward duration $\theta$ & Clean duration\\\midrule
INC2;DEC2 & $600N_0+16$ & $1584x+1632$\\
NOP & $192N_0+8$ & $768x+800$\\
ZERO3 when $3\nmid x+1$ & $192N_0+8$ & $768x+800$\\
POSITIVE3 when $3\mid x+1$ & $192N_0+8$ & $768x+800$\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
All phase-four durations are multiplied by four. The generic circuits deliberately retain $F$, rather than specializing these coincidences away. For example a fresh singleton INC2 source has $F=2N_0$, $\theta=300N_0+8$, and clean time $1176N_0+32$. Additional wrapper tests cover this unequal-payload behavior and coprime factors five and seven, without claiming a full emitted generic circuit count for these extra sources.

A fake ZERO3 halt at $N_0=3$ and fake POSITIVE3 halt at $N_0=1$ fail the retained chronological endpoint row: their totalized successors are the rejecting trap, not halt. This construction removes no selector and no encoded halt endpoint, and does not pass through a weakened fixed-horizon selector interface.

\subsection{What the raw coordinate cannot represent}\label{smc:uc:sec:rawlimits}
Write $N_0=2^a3^bc$, with $\gcd(c,6)=1$. Scaling the raw payload by a positive factor coprime to six preserves guards and the control sequence, and scales the payload throughout. For each corresponding tick,
\[
\tau(cN)-8=c\bigl(\tau(N)-8\bigr).
\]
When output and time are existentially hidden, halting thus depends only on $\nu_2(x+1),\nu_3(x+1)$. In particular $x=0$ and $4$ cannot be distinguished for halting; among positive coordinates, neither can $x=4$ and $6$. This excludes interpreting the raw $x+1$ interface as an arbitrary c.e. ordinary-input loader.

The general fixed-source theorem is compatible with encoded input contracts, but a numerical universal claim would require a concrete fixed universal separated reversible source table, its proved ordinary-input or decoder interface, and a fully charged emission and audit. None is supplied here. The inherited clean theorem's abstract computable reduction is not such a paid loader.

All zero-set interpretations require natural external coordinates and strictly positive integer witnesses. Real SOS nonnegativity does not extend the native theorem to rational or real witnesses. The target depends on the input; no fixed universal target, stationary halt, arbitrary later recurrence, optimality or new universal operation bound is asserted.

\section{Independent checks and reproducible delivery}\label{smc:uc:sec:checks}
\subsection{What was checked}\label{smc:uc:sec:checked}
The new emitter authenticates the pinned raw JSON, parses its literal arithmetic, verifies the old finalizers and emits complete clean circuits. It does not execute the upstream author scripts. The independent literal auditor checks all ten JSON circuits and all eight text DAGs: 4092 gates, 162 comparison rows, inheritance, closure, liveness, literal constants, counts, degree certificates and complete SOS output identity.

The literal auditor also checks 120 signed assignments, 320 modular assignments and 606 exact or adjacent-time zero-step evaluations. These are finite arithmetic identities. No implication from modular SOS zero to individual modular residual zero is used. Eight deliberately corrupted circuit copies are rejected: omitted witness, undeclared operand, changed inherited gate, deleted comparison, wrong cleanup constant, extra dead gate, undercounted ledger and false degree.

A separate semantic checker records:
\begin{itemize}
\item 19200 residue-state and clock evaluations, including rejecting controls;
\item 576 accepted full outer packed histories, with all four outer equations and the actual joined AND checked;
\item 576 each of strict no-wrap and coprime-scaled trace checks;
\item 192 false prime-three halts rejected by chronological transport;
\item 576 rejections each for clean-time, native-time and final-payload mutations;
\item 384 complete signed/modular SOS evaluations and 390 zero-step exact evaluations;
\item 29 additional physical-wrapper checks, including 13 unequal-payload cases, and one nonfresh-entry rejection;
\item 54 larger-height outer extensions at unchanged input and clean time.
\end{itemize}
Native and phase-four cases are counted separately. These are not hundreds of distinct source programs. Bounded tests and all-tuple arithmetic identities support implementation correctness; the inherited theorems and the proofs above establish the unbounded semantic interpretation.

\textbf{No complete positive native/Pell zero tuple has been numerically materialized.} Outer-history witnesses stop at the native interface. Signed or modular evaluations of the entire DAG are not evaluations at a full positive satisfying native witness. The package preserves this distinction explicitly in its receipts.

The release contains this editable \file{report21.tex}, its rendered \file{report21.pdf}, the unchanged mathematical freeze under \file{reproducibility/}, the separate constant-folded alternatives under \file{folded-clocks/}, and standard-library integrity and replay tools. From the release root:

python -B replay.py --output /tmp/new-report21-replay

The output directory must be new and outside the release. The assertion-dependent secondary degree checker runs normally and is explicitly required to reject optimized execution; the full independent circuit auditor recomputes every degree certificate successfully in both modes. The distributed PDF is already built and is not needed for arithmetic replay.

The release manifest enumerates every delivered payload file by exact relative path, byte length and SHA-256. Its checker rejects missing files, extra files or directories, symlinks, nonregular objects, duplicate JSON keys, noncanonical paths, altered pins and altered bytes, including under Python optimization. A companion digest protects the manifest's bytes against accidental change. These are consistency checks, not a digital signature; authenticity requires a separately trusted archive digest. All pages of the final PDF were rendered and visually reviewed; its text and mathematical claims were independently reviewed against the frozen source. The packaged quality and replay receipts distinguish those review results from foundational theorem dependencies. \section{The two results and their common scope}\label{smc:ch:sec:main}
We use $\NN=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ and $\Np=\{1,2,\ldots\}$. External coordinates are natural integers. Every supplied witness coordinate in a nonempty circuit is strictly positive. Computed arithmetic registers may be signed; they are not extra witnesses.

Fix an eligible deterministic reversible separated source $R$, using INC2, INC3, enabled DEC2 and DEC3, ZERO2, ZERO3, POSITIVE2, POSITIVE3 and NOP. Its entry $q_0$ has no incoming instruction, its designated halt $q_h$ has no outgoing instruction, and initially $q_0\ne q_h$. Eligibility means that the inherited complete raw residue-history/native interface and exact clean-target wrapper apply. It does not assert a free fresh-entry transformation for every reversible program.

The positive raw input is $N_0=x+1$. The valuations at two and three encode the counters, and the cofactor coprime to six remains part of the payload. Disabled guards are nonfinal stuck states. The cleaned cellular automaton (CA) has total mass three on the configurations considered, using a finite alphabet of Boolean channel subsets whose mass is the number of occupied channels. This is not the convention that a state's integer label equals its mass.

Let $Q_R(x,U;w)$ denote the complete five-gate-folded clean-clock polynomial of Report 21 \textup{[source~22, Section~\ref{smc:uc:sec:folded}; as a polynomial it equals source~22's $Q_R$ of~\eqref{smc:uc:eq:sos}, whose circuits it computes with one gate fewer, and its witness tuple $w$ is source~22's $(z,\theta)$]}. For a nonempty first-halting source history let $F$ be its final raw payload and $\theta>0$ its forward physical native duration. Native and spatially blocked time satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ch:eq:clean}
U=2\theta+192(F+x+1)+16.
\end{equation}
The phase-four time is four times the whole right side. The exact target restores the entire raw input and the prescribed absolute marker/controller geometry; phase four has a phase-zero target. The semantic claim is a first-hit claim about this whole finite configuration, not a claim about arbitrary microscopic states or later recurrence.

\begin{theorem}[Canonical outer history and infinite full fibers]\label{smc:ch:thm:combined}
Assume the inherited native completeness, residue-history and clean-target theorems described in Section~\ref{smc:ch:sec:sources}. Set
\[
S=n_{\rm initial}+n_{\rm target}+\theta,\qquad h=S+\eta,
\]
where $\eta$ is the existing positive height slack. Add $\kappa\in\Np$ and define
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ch:eq:poly}
\Qcan(x,U;w,\kappa)
=Q_R(x,U;w)+(\eta+\kappa-S-1)^2.
\end{equation}
Then for each $x,U\in\NN$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item A positive zero exists exactly when the inherited cleaned CA first reaches its specified target at $U$ in the chosen clock model.
\item At an accepted pair, $h$ is the least power of two strictly greater than $S$, and every supplied outer coordinate is unique.
\item Projection onto the twenty-two native coordinates is a bijection onto the entire positive native extension fiber at its uniquely fixed padded ports and prescribed scale.
\item Every such nonempty full fiber is infinite. Starting from any one witness, only native $j,o,y_{\rm aux}$ need vary; all supplied outer coordinates and the other nineteen native coordinates can stay fixed.
\end{enumerate}
The initially halted, witness-free construction is separate and excluded from items 2--4.
\end{theorem}

Equation~\eqref{smc:ch:eq:poly} is an identity of integer polynomials on all tuples. Items 2--4 are statements about accepted positive fibers. In particular the fiberwise inverse in item 3 inserts fixed outer constants; it is not an all-input polynomial procedure for discovering a halting trace or a global polynomial coordinate change from old witnesses to new witnesses.

The outer-canonical packet alone does not decide native cardinality. Its statement of that limitation is retained in the archive. The separate fixed-scale theorem in Section~\ref{smc:ch:sec:infinity} supplies the additional fact needed for item 4. Report 21's infinite-fiber conclusion \textup{[Theorem~\ref{smc:uc:thm:fibers}]} remains correct; the new result shows that enlarging height is not necessary for infinitude.
