\section{Why the physical clock pays for the canonical height}\label{smc:ch:sec:height}
\subsection{Encoded states and exact instruction durations}\label{smc:ch:sec:durations}
Assign controls in $\{1,\ldots,K\}$, including a rejecting trap, and put $m=6K$. Encode a positive raw payload and control by
\[
n=K(N-1)+q,\qquad 1\le q\le K.
\]
Missing guards, original halt, trap and unused labels transition to the trap with unchanged payload, and the trap never exits. Thus a nonempty path ending at the original halt represents its first genuine halt. The retained residue-affine table is
\[
f(mz+r)=a_rz+d_r,\qquad 1\le r\le m,\ z\ge0,\ a_r\ge0,\ d_r\ge1.
\]
For a current encoded configuration,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ch:eq:quot}
\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{6K}\right\rfloor
=\left\lfloor\frac{N-1}{6}\right\rfloor.
\end{equation}
Indeed, writing $N-1=6a+b$, $0\le b\le5$, leaves remainder $Kb+q-1$ between zero and $6K-1$.

The literal native tick durations, measured at the current payload, are
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lc@{}}\toprule
Enabled instruction & Native duration $\tau$\\\midrule
INC2 & $300N+8$\\
INC3 & $396N+8$\\
DEC2 & $150N+8$\\
DEC3 & $132N+8$\\
ZERO POSITIVE NOP & $192N+8$\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Therefore, in any genuine nonempty first-halting trace with $\theta=\sum_i\tau_i$,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ch:eq:bound}
z_i=\left\lfloor\frac{N_i-1}{6}\right\rfloor<N_i\le\tau_i\le\theta.
\end{equation}
The weaker uniform inequality $\tau_i\ge132N_i+8$ is enough. The argument does not require monotone payloads or an endpoint bound on intermediate growth. A large temporary payload costs physical time at the very step where it appears.

With
\[
n_{\rm initial}=Kx+q_0,\quad
n_{\rm target}=K(F-1)+q_h,\quad
S=n_{\rm initial}+n_{\rm target}+\theta,
\]
every $h>S$ already exceeds every true quotient. This is the completeness point that an arbitrary endpoint-only canonical-height proposal would lack.

\subsection{The strict dyadic interval}\label{smc:ch:sec:dyadic}
\begin{lemma}\label{smc:ch:lem:dyadic}
For $S\in\Np$, $h=S+\eta$, and $\eta,\kappa\in\Np$, the new comparison $\eta+\kappa=S+1$ is equivalent to
\[
S<h\le2S,\qquad \eta=h-S,\qquad \kappa=2S+1-h.
\]
Exactly one power of two lies in $(S,2S]$, the least one strictly greater than $S$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The two inequalities are precisely positivity of the displayed slacks. If $2^a\le S<2^{a+1}$, then $2^{a+1}\in(S,2S]$ and adjacent powers lie outside. When $S=2^a$, the chosen height is $2S$, with $\eta=S$ and $\kappa=1$; the inadmissible choice $h=S$ would make $\eta=0$.
\end{proof}

The old radix is $B=Ch^2$, where $C$ is a fixed dyadic integer satisfying
\[
C\ge L,\qquad C\ge2384m+2,\qquad
L\ge\max\{4,m+1,1+\max_r(a_r+d_r)\},
\]
and $L$ is dyadic. The native theorem forces $B$ and the length power $P$ to be dyadic. Since $C$ is dyadic and $h$ is a positive integer, $B=Ch^2$ dyadic forces $h$ dyadic: an odd prime divisor of $h$ would divide $B$. The new row is not an independent dyadicity oracle. In the emitted fixtures $K=5$, $m=30$, $C=131072$.

\section{Soundness and exact canonical completeness}\label{smc:ch:sec:completeness}
\subsection{The old no-wrap argument remains necessary}\label{smc:ch:sec:oldnowrap}
\wtag\ [This subsection restates source~22's argument of Section~\ref{smc:uc:sec:nowrapclock} (with $t$ for source~22's $\ell$, $C_\tau$ for its $\mathcal C_\tau$ and $\widehat c_\tau$ for its $\widehat k$); it is printed as source~23's account of why that argument is still needed.]
A positive integer zero of~\eqref{smc:ch:eq:poly} annihilates all old comparison squares and the new square. Old soundness supplies the first-halting history, $F$ and its clock. Lemma~\ref{smc:ch:lem:dyadic} then forces the stated height. No old comparison is deleted.

For clarity, the inherited exact-clock proof does not obtain the clock merely from a congruence. Before digit typing, its global equation implies $J\ge1$, $P\ge B$ and that all lane coefficients lie in $[0,P)$. The native block establishes actual packed AND and dyadic $B,P$. Then
\[
P-1=(B-1)J
\]
forces $P=B^t$, $J=1+B+\cdots+B^{t-1}$ for $t\ge1$. Selector lanes type one residue per time and the range mask $(h-1)J$ types $0\le z_i<h$. Chronological transport gives the deterministic orbit from the initial endpoint to the halt, with each current encoded state in $[1,mh]$.

A current state cannot repeat before a deterministic first halt, so $t\le mh$. Its payload satisfies $N_i\le6h$, giving $\tau_i\le396N_i+8\le2384h$. Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ch:eq:nowrap}
0<\sum_i\tau_i\le2384mh^2<Ch^2-1=B-1.
\end{equation}
Independently $0<\theta<h<B-1$. If $C_\tau=\sum_i\tau_iB^i$ is the typed clock word, the retained paid comparison is
\[
C_\tau=(B-1)(\widehat c_\tau-1)+\theta.
\]
Reduction modulo $B-1$ gives $\sum_i\tau_i\equiv\theta$, and the strict interval bounds give equality. First-halt totalization is essential here. The new cap neither replaces the proof nor permits loops or posthalt continuation.

\subsection{Positive witnesses at the exact selected height}\label{smc:ch:sec:exactheight}
Conversely take the genuine first-halting trace and its $\theta=\sum_i\tau_i$. Choose the unique dyadic $h\in(S,2S]$, set $\eta=h-S$, $\kappa=2S+1-h$, and use~\eqref{smc:ch:eq:bound} to fit all true quotient digits. Set
\[
B=Ch^2,\qquad P=B^t,\qquad J=\sum_{i=0}^{t-1}B^i.
\]
Pack the chronological selector words $E_r$, quotient word $W$ and selected-quotient words $Z_a$ for the $g$ exceptional slope classes. Their supplied hats are $E_r+1,W+1,Z_a+1$. Zero words therefore have positive hat one and are allowed.

Disjoint exceptional classes give $\sum_a Z_a\le W\le(h-1)J$. The global comparison fixes the remaining slack as
\begin{align}
\beta&=P-J-(W+1)-\sum_a(Z_a+1)\notag\\
&=(B-2)J-W-\sum_a Z_a-g\notag\\
&\ge(B-2h)J-g\ge(L-2)hJ-g>0.\label{smc:ch:eq:beta}
\end{align}
For the final strict bound use $L\ge4$, $L\ge m+1$, $g\le m-1$, $h\ge3$ and $J\ge1$. The physical nonempty setting has $S>2$, so its selected height satisfies the required lower bound.

All scalar AND lane coefficients lie in $[0,P)$. Selectors and class selectors are at most $J$; $W$ and every $Z_a$ are at most $(h-1)J<P$; class masks are at most $(B-1)J=P-1$. Let $\ell=m+g+1$ be the number of lanes and $v$ the least power of two at least $\ell$. For the joined words $H,M,A$,
\[
0\le H,M,A<P^\ell\le P^v<Q_{\rm native}=BP^v.
\]
The genuine AND holds lane by lane. The actual native ports and scale are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ch:eq:ports}
\mathsf a=16H+12,\quad \mathsf b=16M+10,\quad
\mathsf c=16A+8,\quad q=16Q_{\rm native}.
\end{equation}
The three ports are positive and below $q$, $q$ is dyadic, and the low padding satisfies $12\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}10=8$. Prescribed-scale completeness supplies all twenty-two positive native coordinates at this exact scale. It is neither necessary nor generally correct to reuse a native tuple from another height.

Finally
\[
\widehat c_\tau=1+\frac{C_\tau-\theta}{B-1}\in\Np,
\]
since $C_\tau-\theta=\sum_i\tau_i(B^i-1)$ is a nonnegative multiple of $B-1$. For one step this hat equals one. Transport, physical time, clean time and the new cap all hold, so every one of the twenty-one comparisons vanishes. This proves completeness at the canonical height, rather than at an unspecified sufficiently large height.

\section{The precise canonical object}\label{smc:ch:sec:projection}
Fix an accepted $(x,U)$ and clock model. Determinism and first-halt semantics fix the entire trace, its length $t$, final payload $F$, native duration $\theta$, and every residue and quotient. These fix the endpoints and $S$, hence $h,\eta,\kappa$, then $B,P,J$, every packed word and hat. Equation~\eqref{smc:ch:eq:beta} fixes $\beta$ and the clock comparison fixes $\widehat c_\tau$. All outer registers and the padded ports~\eqref{smc:ch:eq:ports} are fixed as well.

The supplied outer coordinates are the selector hats, quotient hat, exceptional selected-quotient hats, $\eta,\beta,F,\widehat c_\tau,\theta,\kappa$. In these fixtures their number is $39$ for INC2;DEC2 and $37$ for the other three. Quantities $S,h,B,P,J$ are computed registers, not additional coordinates.

Write $o(x,U)$ for this unique outer tuple and $\mathcal E(\mathsf a,\mathsf b,\mathsf c,q)\subseteq\Np^{22}$ for the set of \emph{all} positive native assignments satisfying the complete sixteen-comparison block at the fixed boundary. The native coordinate order, with the literal prefix \file{native__} understood, is
\[
\begin{gathered}
F_0,F_1,F_2,a,c,d,f,h,i,j,k,o,r,s,w,\\
\tau,\eta,\zeta,\mathit{ga},y_{\rm aux},\mathit{odd\_half},\mathit{bound\_beta}.
\end{gathered}
\]
Native $h,\eta,\tau$ are different coordinates from the outer height, outer slack and physical clock. Native $F_3$ and $q$ are computed ports, not supplied coordinates.

\begin{theorem}[Entire-fiber projection]\label{smc:ch:thm:projection}
Projection that retains the twenty-two native coordinates is a bijection
\[
\{(w,\kappa)>0:\Qcan(x,U;w,\kappa)=0\}
\longrightarrow\mathcal E(\mathsf a,\mathsf b,\mathsf c,q).
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
A complete zero satisfies the native block at the fixed outer boundary, so projection is well defined. If two witnesses project to the same native tuple, their outer tuples both equal $o(x,U)$; this proves injectivity. Conversely, adjoin $o(x,U)$ to \emph{any} member of $\mathcal E$. The sixteen native comparisons hold by definition, and the five nonnative comparisons depend only on the fixed outer data and external ports. All twenty-one comparisons therefore hold. This proves surjectivity onto the entire native fiber, not merely a selected family of native extensions.
\end{proof}

The comparison-independence statement is checked transitively on all eight complete emitted DAGs; no native witness enters an outer comparison through a hidden intermediate. All native gate rows, the ordered coordinate list and the sixteen comparison pairs are retained literally from the folded parents.

This is accepted-fiber canonicality. It does not give a total polynomial function $(x,U)\mapsto o(x,U)$, nor an all-tuple polynomial normalization map from an old witness to a new witness. The extra square restricts the old zero set's outer projection, even though the old-polynomial portion remains identical on all tuples.

\section{Infinitely many native extensions at fixed scale}\label{smc:ch:sec:infinity}
\subsection{The two affected equations}\label{smc:ch:sec:affected}
Fix the four ports~\eqref{smc:ch:eq:ports} and any positive native solution. All symbols in this section except the four ports refer to native coordinates. Define
\[
p=2r+1,\qquad \rho=ic^2,\qquad D=\rho^2-1,\qquad
u=jc-p=of-c,\qquad y=y_{\rm aux}.
\]
We write $\rho$ instead of $R$ to avoid confusing this auxiliary integer with the fixed source program. The exact native comparisons involving $j,o,y$ are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ch:eq:nativechanged}
u=jc-p=of-c,\qquad \rho^2(u^2-y^2)=1-y^2.
\end{equation}
The second is equivalently $(\rho u)^2-Dy^2=1$. The distinct unchanged auxiliary norm is
\[
\rho^2=(a^2+4a+3)(f^2-1).
\]
It remains valid because all its supplied coordinates are fixed.

Positivity is available directly from the source equations. Since $q\ge16$ and $s=2\mathit{odd\_half}+1\ge3$, let $E=(wq)(sq)>0$. The retained equations give
\[
k=r+1+hE>r+1,\qquad c=(sq)k+\eta>48(r+1)>p.
\]
As $j\ge1$, $u\ge c-p>0$. Also $\rho=ic^2>1$, so $D>0$. The optional nonsquare fact $(\rho-1)^2<D<\rho^2$ is true but not needed below. No deep classification of the auxiliary Pell index is used to establish these inequalities.

The only direct gate uses of the three changing coordinates are $of=o\cdot f$, $jc=j\cdot c$, and $\mathit{aux\_y2}=y^2$. Their transitive comparison descendants are exactly native comparisons 13 and 14, numbered from one. These are full comparisons 15 and 16. All other fourteen native comparisons and all five outer comparisons are independent of them. Derived gate values along those paths may change; the claim fixes the other \emph{supplied coordinates}, not every arithmetic register.

\subsection{A congruence preserving norm family}\label{smc:ch:sec:family}
\begin{theorem}[Fixed-scale native infinitude]\label{smc:ch:thm:infinite}
Every nonempty positive fiber of this prescribed native block is infinite. From any positive seed, the other nineteen supplied native coordinates can remain unchanged.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Put $M_0=\rho cf$ and
\[
B_0=\begin{pmatrix}\rho&D\\1&\rho\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\binom{V_0}{Y_0}=\binom{\rho u}{y}.
\]
The determinant of $B_0$ is $\rho^2-D=1$, so its reduction modulo $M_0$ belongs to the finite group $\mathrm{GL}_2(\Z/M_0\Z)$. Let $L_0\ge1$ be its order. A completely specified alternative is $L_0=(M_0^4)!$: there are at most $M_0^4$ residue matrices, so the order is at most $M_0^4$ and divides this factorial. The order is not claimed to divide $M_0^4$ itself.

For every $n\ge0$ define
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ch:eq:family}
\binom{V_n}{Y_n}=B_0^{nL_0}\binom{V_0}{Y_0},\qquad
u_n=\frac{V_n}{\rho},\qquad
j_n=\frac{u_n+p}{c},\qquad
o_n=\frac{u_n+c}{f}.
\end{equation}
Set $y_{{\rm aux},n}=Y_n$ and leave all other native coordinates unchanged.

Since $B_0^{nL_0}\equiv I\pmod{M_0}$,
\[
V_n\equiv\rho u\pmod{\rho cf}.
\]
Thus $u_n$ is an integer and $u_n\equiv u\pmod{cf}$. The seed identities $u+p=jc$ and $u+c=of$ then make $j_n,o_n$ integers. No coprimality assumption on $c,f$ is required.

For arbitrary $V,Y$,
\begin{align*}
(\rho V+DY)^2-D(V+\rho Y)^2
&=(\rho^2-D)(V^2-DY^2)\\
&=V^2-DY^2.
\end{align*}
Therefore the seed norm $V_0^2-DY_0^2=1$ is preserved. Substituting $V_n=\rho u_n$ gives exactly
\[
\rho^2(u_n^2-Y_n^2)=1-Y_n^2,
\qquad j_nc-p=u_n=o_nf-c.
\]
These are both changed comparisons in~\eqref{smc:ch:eq:nativechanged}. The other fourteen native comparisons keep their seed values by the dependency statement above.

Finally $V_0,Y_0>0$ and one multiplication by $B_0$ sends a positive vector to
\[
V'=\rho V+DY>V,\qquad Y'=V+\rho Y>Y.
\]
Since $L_0\ge1$, $V_n,Y_n$ strictly increase with $n$. All reconstructed coordinates are positive, and distinct $n$ give distinct $Y_n$. This yields infinitely many positive native tuples at the same ports and scale.
\end{proof}

These matrix powers and the factorial describe witnesses mathematically. They introduce no new circuit gates, comparisons or existential coordinates. The result is seed-relative: it does not assert that inadmissible ports possess a seed. At a valid canonical boundary, the inherited prescribed-scale theorem supplies one; Theorem~\ref{smc:ch:thm:projection} lifts the whole resulting family to the complete canonical circuit.

The family need not enumerate the entire native fiber. It proves a cardinality lower bound sufficient here. The pinned auxiliary-index notes already retain noncanonical indices and exhibit related congruence behavior \cite{pellparity,pellsigns}; the present matrix argument needs no novel index-classification or divisibility theorem.

It is printed as Part~III of the collection's report \path{fixed-universal-polynomials} (Theorem \texttt{fup:nf:thm:class}), which implies Theorem~\ref{smc:ch:thm:infinite}: there a seed also has infinitely many native extensions, with the seventeen fixed coordinates among the nineteen that the matrix family keeps fixed. \section{Literal circuits and full operation ledgers}\label{smc:ch:sec:ledger}
\subsection{Four fixtures in two clock models}\label{smc:ch:sec:fixtures}
The archive emits eight complete nonempty circuits and two unchanged zero-step circuits. The fixed sources are \wtag\ [those of source~22, whose table in Section~\ref{smc:uc:sec:result} is the same as source~23's and is printed once: INC2;DEC2, $s\xrightarrow{\mathrm{INC2}}a\xrightarrow{\mathrm{DEC2}}h$, accepting all $N_0>0$ in two steps; and ZERO3, NOP and POSITIVE3, $s\to h$ in one step, accepting $3\nmid N_0$, all $N_0$ and $3\mid N_0$ respectively].
They are nonuniversal demonstrations of the generic unbounded mechanism. The generic eligible-source proof does not mean that a literal circuit for every eligible source, or a long universal computation, has been emitted. These simple accepted relations admit smaller specialized descriptions; no minimality claim is made.

An operation is one binary multiplication, addition or subtraction in the literal straight-line DAG. Reuse is allowed; integer constants are literal; signs in intermediate registers are unrestricted. Every comparison's subtraction and square, and every final accumulation, are charged. Both native/spatial and phase-four models have the same complete ledger:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrrrrrr@{}}\toprule
Fixture & $M$ & $A$ & Total & Outer & Native & All & Degree\\\midrule
INC2;DEC2 & 240 & 368 & 608 & 39 & 22 & 61 & 2344\\
ZERO3 & 185 & 298 & 483 & 37 & 22 & 59 & 1192\\
NOP & 183 & 298 & 481 & 37 & 22 & 59 & 1192\\
POSITIVE3 & 190 & 294 & 484 & 37 & 22 & 59 & 1192\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Here $A$ includes additions and subtractions; Outer, Native and All count supplied positive coordinates. Every nonempty circuit has two natural external ports, twenty-one comparisons and the complete $62$-gate SOS finalizer. Across both clock models this is $4112$ nonempty gates; the two zero-step circuits bring the delivered total to $4120$.

\subsection{Materializing S without a hidden free gate}\label{smc:ch:sec:materialize}
The folded parent's graph did not already contain $S$. Its height schedule was
\[
d=n_{\rm initial}+n_{\rm target},\qquad
b=d+\eta,\qquad h=b+\theta.
\]
In each of the eight actual parent DAGs, $b$, named \file{bridge_height_without_time}, has exactly one consumer, the height addition, and occurs in no comparison. Replace the last two additions by
\[
S=d+\theta,\qquad h=S+\eta.
\]
The same two gates now materialize $S$; associativity preserves $h$ on every integer tuple. The single-consumer graph condition ensures every other old register and all twenty old residual polynomials remain unchanged. This is a checked graph reassociation, not an assumption that a useful affine register is free.

Two additional producers compute $\eta+\kappa$ and $S+1$. Rebuild the entire finalizer from all twenty-one comparisons: twenty-one residual subtractions, twenty-one self-products and twenty accumulation additions give
\[
21M+41A=62\text{ operations}.
\]
The parent's twenty-row finalizer cost $20M+39A=59$. Thus the fully paid net change is $1M+4A=5$ gates and one positive coordinate. The folded-parent totals were $603,478,476,479$, producing the displayed $608,483,481,484$.

The resulting output satisfies~\eqref{smc:ch:eq:poly} on arbitrary signed integer assignments, including away from the old zero set. The natural ports and all old coordinate positions retain their order; $\kappa$ is appended. The folded time bridge stays
\[
192(F+x)+2\theta+208\quad\text{or}\quad768(F+x)+8\theta+832.
\]
In both models the canonical $S$ uses forward native $\theta$, never the phase-four time or a source-step count.

\subsection{Exact polynomial degree}\label{smc:ch:sec:degree}
Degree means total degree of the complete output polynomial in all supplied ports and witnesses, before restricting to zeros. Formal upper bounds propagate by maximum at addition/subtraction and sum at multiplication. Along the integer ray $v_i=(i+2)z$, with $v_i$ ordered as parameters followed by auxiliaries, propagate coefficients at those formal bounds modulo $1000003$. A vanishing leading coefficient never lowers its stored bound.

The nonzero output coefficients at the formal upper bounds are $135347$ at degree $2344$ for INC2;DEC2 and $977370$ at degree $1192$ for each other fixture. Thus the lower and upper bounds match. The appended coordinate leaves old weights unchanged, reassociation preserves old polynomials, and the new square has only degree two. Independently computed full univariate specializations agree with the certificates, including all gate coefficients. These degrees are properties of the emitted polynomials; they are not lower bounds on every representation of the same accepted relation.

\section{Boundary cases and limits}\label{smc:ch:sec:limits}
\subsection{Initially halted and rejected inputs}\label{smc:ch:sec:halted}
\wtag\ [The zero-step polynomials are source~22's, Section~\ref{smc:uc:sec:zerostep}, unchanged.]
If $q_0=q_h$, freshness and terminality make the control isolated. The cleaned computation consists of two NOP bridges, $\theta=0$ and $F=x+1$. The separate polynomials are
\[
(384x+400-U)^2,\qquad(1536x+1600-U)^2.
\]
Each has four operations, $2M+2A$, one comparison, no witnesses and exact degree two. The files are byte-identical to the frozen originals. An accepted zero-step pair has the single empty witness tuple. It has no twenty-two-coordinate native fiber, and is not covered by the nonempty infinitude conclusion.

For stuck or nonhalting inputs the old positive fiber is empty, so adding a square cannot create a zero. Rejecting totalization and inherited soundness, rather than a bounded simulation prefix, justify the unbounded statement. Wrong requested clean times remain rejected; in phase four a time not divisible by four cannot satisfy the clean-time row. Quotient words equal to zero are valid via hat one, including the one-step clock quotient hat.

\subsection{Sanity checks on all accepted fixture inputs}\label{smc:ch:sec:sanity}
Let $N_0=x+1$. On the accepted paths of these four fixtures $F=N_0$: \wtag\ [the table is source~22's, in Section~\ref{smc:uc:sec:sanity}, printed once: forward native time $600N_0+16$ and native clean time $1584x+1632$ for INC2;DEC2, and $192N_0+8$ and $768x+800$ for NOP, for ZERO3 if $3\nmid N_0$ and for POSITIVE3 if $3\mid N_0$].
Phase-four times are four times these values. The generic circuits retain $F$ and its paid ports rather than specializing the equal-input/output coincidence away.

\subsection{What does not follow}\label{smc:ch:sec:notfollow}
\wtag\ [The first paragraph repeats source~22's Section~\ref{smc:uc:sec:rawlimits}.]
The raw input contract still preserves cofactors coprime to six. Writing $N_0=2^a3^bc$ with $\gcd(c,6)=1$, such scaling preserves guards and source control sequence; each corresponding duration obeys $\tau(cN)-8=c(\tau(N)-8)$. When output and time are hidden, halting depends only on the two valuations. For example $x=0$ and $x=4$ cannot be distinguished for halting by this raw interface. It is not a paid arbitrary ordinary-input/program loader.

No general finite-fold MRDP impossibility follows from an infinite fiber in this particular representation. Nor does deterministic computation force uniqueness of arithmetical auxiliaries. The established conclusions are exactly unique outer history, a fixed-port native-fiber bijection, and infinitely many remaining native extensions. No rational or real zero-set theorem, arbitrary signed-witness interpretation, fixed universal target, stationary halt, later-recurrence theorem, minimal circuit bound, or new universal numerical operation bound is asserted.

The matrix formula is explicit relative to a positive seed, but neither this report nor its finite replay materializes a complete positive native Pell seed. Existence comes from the inherited completeness theorem; infinitude then follows from the mathematical matrix argument.

\section{Independent evidence and portable replay}\label{smc:ch:sec:replay}
\subsection{Mathematical checks and finite evidence}\label{smc:ch:sec:evidence}
The outer packet has independent proof and complete-circuit audits. Its circuit audit checks the exact inherited graph, liveness, coordinate order, all-tuple extra-square identity, complete ledgers, degree and zero-step identity. It records $96$ signed and $256$ modular identity evaluations and $29$ rejected circuit corruptions. Finite modular evaluations are supplemental arithmetic tests; no inference from a modular SOS zero to separate modular residual zeros is made.

The independent outer semantic checker records, among other tests:
\begin{itemize}
\item $32768$ scalar strict-next-dyadic cases, including $16$ exact dyadic boundaries;
\item $6656$ residue/control quotient identities and $1749$ enabled primitive duration bounds;
\item $3072$ accepted full \emph{outer} histories, comprising $1536$ parent and $1536$ canonical candidates;
\item $1536$ larger-height repackings that retain the old outer constraints and AND but fail the new cap;
\item $1024$ false-halt rejections, $9216$ wrong-clean-time rejections and $3072$ cap-slack mutation rejections;
\item $60$ accepted all-zero quotient-word histories and $390$ exact zero-step evaluations.
\end{itemize}
These are tests across the four small fixtures and both models, not counts of distinct universal programs. Accepted outer histories check positive outer slacks, padded native-port bounds, genuine joined AND and strict no-wrap. They do not construct complete positive native zeros.

The fixed-scale audit separately checks the source inequalities, the exact two affected native comparisons, the full transitive dependency graph and the norm/congruence proof. Its local numerical family examples exercise only the auxiliary recurrence system. They are deliberately labeled as such, not as complete positive native witnesses. The combined release checker connects the native coordinate order and dependencies directly to the eight actual canonical DAGs.

Normal and optimized Python runs are reported separately. Passing under \file{python -O} is not, by itself, proof that assertions executed; the delivered replay records the actual coverage and uses explicit failures for release-integrity checks. Neither finite test totals nor the optimized interpreter replace the general proofs in Sections~\ref{smc:ch:sec:height}--\ref{smc:ch:sec:infinity}.

\subsection{Package and reproduction contract}\label{smc:ch:sec:package}
The portable archive includes this LaTeX source and PDF, exact complete arithmetic JSON/text DAGs, the two theorem packets, pinned inherited data and prose, independent checkers, original/delivered provenance, and a release-level exact inventory. All computation is local standard-library Python; public source URLs are provenance links and are not needed for replay.

The principal directories are \file{canonical-height/}, \file{native-fibers/} and \file{inherited-source/}. The outer packet includes authenticated base/folded reference data. The release inventory rejects missing, changed and extra files, unexpected directories, hidden extras and symlinks; its negative tests also exercise malformed manifests and tampered pinned dependencies. A checksum is an integrity check, not a digital signature: archive authenticity requires a trusted separately obtained digest.

From an extracted release directory, the documented entry points are
\begin{lstlisting}
python -B verify_release.py
python -B release_checks.py
python -B replay.py --output ../report22-replay
\end{lstlisting}
Choose a new output directory outside the sealed release. The replay must not write generated receipts, bytecode or build products into the sealed inventory. Optional PDF rebuilding uses \file{build.sh}, writes temporary TeX files outside the package, and replaces only the PDF; it is therefore an intentional release edit and requires resealing if retained.

The final delivery process includes a fresh ZIP extraction, read-only normal and optimized replay from that extracted tree, adversarial inventory checks, independent article review, PDF text/build checks and visual inspection of every page. Separate machine-readable receipts record the exact executed checks and outcome. Replaying the mathematical packet authenticates and recomputes its data; it does not claim to solve an unbounded witness search.

\phantomsection\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Source 24: A sharp reversible four particle timing threshold}
\noindent{\large\bfseries Source 24 (batch-91 manuscript 01): A sharp reversible four particle timing threshold}\par
\noindent ``Report 49'', 4 October 2026. \wtag\ From the archive \path{A_Sharp_Reversible_Four_Particle_Timing_Threshold_Package.zip} (main file \path{Research_Report49/manuscript/report49.tex}, 14-page PDF; neither is shipped). Its labels carry the prefix \texttt{smc:rt:}, and its sections are Sections~\ref{smc:ix:rt:sec:statement}--\ref{smc:rt:app:provenance} here; its appendix is printed as the last of them. Statements keep their numbering by section, and equations are numbered by section. Its abstract follows.
\begin{quote}\small
We specify a one-dimensional, binary, globally reversible, number-conserving cellular automaton of radius at most $90$. From the four-particle input $\{0,5,6,d\}$, $d\ge13$, the exact word $\word$ at the fixed coordinates $[0,6]$ occurs precisely at times $k^2+(2d-23)k$, $k\in\NN$. Six literal endpoint swaps, protected by isolation and prospective raw-key preservation, define the automaton on the entire binary full shift. We prove reversibility also for malformed and infinite configurations and derive every intermediate state of the clock orbit. An explicitly credited adaptation of the inherited mass-at-most-three argument proves that every fixed-input exact anchored observation below four particles is eventually periodic. Thus four is the least particle count for this timing phenomenon, also when global reversibility is required. The relation has the elementary quartic certificate $[k^2+(2x+3)k-t]^2=0$, with empty or singleton fibers over $\NN$ and over $\Q_{\ge0}$, but not an exact interpretation over $\R_{\ge0}$. This is a reversible realization and a sharp timing result, not a universality, arithmetic-record, or literature-priority claim.
\end{quote}
\noindent\textbf{Conventions.} $\NN=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. Intervals of sites are inclusive integer intervals. Composition $BA$ means apply $A$ first. A finite set denotes the binary configuration with exactly those occupied sites.

\section{Statement and scope}\label{smc:ix:rt:sec:statement}
A binary cellular automaton (CA) is a deterministic, time-independent, translation-equivariant map $F:\{0,1\}^{\Z}\to\{0,1\}^{\Z}$ whose output at a site depends on a fixed finite neighborhood. Radius $R$ means the neighborhood is contained in $[-R,R]$. The vacuum is the all-zero configuration. We use finite number conservation:
\[
 |\supp F(c)|=|\supp c|\qquad\text{for every finite-support }c.
\]
This is the standard convention used in Morita's definition of an RNCCA~\cite{morita2012}. Global reversibility here means a two-sided inverse on \emph{all} bi-infinite binary configurations, not merely on an invariant family of finite inputs.

For a word $w\in\{0,1\}^{m+1}$ anchored at $a$, define
\[
 H(F,c;w,a)=\{t\in\NN:(F^t(c))_{a+i}=w_i\ (0\le i\le m)\}.
\]
Zeros are part of the observation. The configuration may contain other particles outside the observed interval. A set $H\subseteq\NN$ is eventually periodic if some $T\ge0$, $P\ge1$ satisfy $t\in H\iff t+P\in H$ for every $t\ge T$.

\begin{theorem}[Sharp reversible timing threshold]\label{smc:rt:thm:main}
There exists a fixed binary number-conserving CA $F$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ and its inverse are CAs of radius at most $90$ on $\{0,1\}^{\Z}$.
\item For every $d\ge13$, with $C_d=\{0,5,6,d\}$,
\[
 H(F,C_d;\word,0)=\{k^2+(2d-23)k:k\in\NN\}.
\]
This set is infinite and not eventually periodic.
\item For every binary number-conserving CA $G$, every finite input with at most three occupied sites, and every fixed exact anchored finite word, the occurrence-time set is effectively eventually periodic.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently four is the least particle count permitting a non-eventually-periodic occurrence-time set in this model, both without a reversibility restriction and with global reversibility required.
\end{theorem}

The lower-bound argument in item 3 is inherited, not newly claimed: Section~\ref{smc:rt:sec:lower} gives a self-contained binary, per-input adaptation of the stronger weighted uniform timed-semilinearity theorem in the inspected source \textup{[source~16, Theorem~\ref{smc:su:thm:main}]}. The generic guarded-swap mechanism likewise comes from the repository's parallel-particle review~\cite{reviewparallel}. The contribution examined here is the six-row reversible clock, its exact anchored timing, and the resulting sharp threshold within this model.

\wtag\ [Without item~1 the theorem is already in this report: item~3 is the binary case of source~16's Corollary~\ref{smc:su:cor:decision}, since a binary automaton has the single weight-one symbol~$1$ (its last sentence: occurrence times of a fixed observation from a fixed input of mass at most three are effectively eventually periodic), and source~17's noninjective radius-six rule realizes item~2's phenomenon with the hits $k^2+(2d-11)k$ from $\{0,3,4,d\}$ (Proposition~\ref{smc:fm:prop:hits}). The threshold four without reversibility thus follows from sources~16 and~17. New here is that the upper example is globally reversible. In one dimension the least particle count for binary \emph{universality}, reversible or not, is five (Reports~14 and~15, Part~I of \path{five-particle-binary-automata}; Section~\ref{smc:tm:sec:frontquestions}); the timing threshold four is a different and smaller threshold, and the two are compatible because source~17's four-mass decision theorem covers this rule (Section~\ref{smc:rt:sec:related}).]

\section{The literal local rule}\label{smc:rt:sec:rule}
In each of two blocks, a row consists of two distinct finite endpoints $E_0,E_1$ and a read interval $W$ containing them. Table~\ref{smc:rt:tab:rows} is the complete row data; no unlisted legal-state convention is imposed.
\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.22}
\begin{tabular}{ccccc}
\toprule Block & Row & $E_0$ & $E_1$ & $W$\\\midrule
$A$ & $\row{AR}$ & $\{0,1\}$ & $\{0,2\}$ & $[-4,6]$\\
$A$ & $\row{AL}$ & $\{0,4\}$ & $\{0,3\}$ & $[-4,8]$\\
$A$ & $\row{AC}$ & $\{0,1,6\}$ & $\{-1,2,7\}$ & $[-5,8]$\\\midrule
$B$ & $\row{BR}$ & $\{0,2\}$ & $\{1,2\}$ & $[-4,6]$\\
$B$ & $\row{BL}$ & $\{0,3\}$ & $\{-1,3\}$ & $[-5,7]$\\
$B$ & $\row{BC}$ & $\{-5,0,3\}$ & $\{-5,0,1\}$ & $[-5,8]$\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{The complete six-row specification of source~24's rule. Coordinates are offsets from the row's anchor; every unspecified site in its read interval must be zero.}\label{smc:rt:tab:rows}
\end{table}

A \emph{raw key} is a pair $\kappa=(\text{row},x)$, where $x\in\Z$ is an anchor. For configuration $c$, the key is present exactly when
\[
 \supp(c)\cap(x+W)=x+E_0\quad\text{or}\quad x+E_1.
\]
The key does \emph{not} include the endpoint side. This omission is essential: swapping an endpoint must preserve the key rather than replace it with a differently named key. Let $K_A(c)$ and $K_B(c)$ denote the raw-key sets for the respective blocks.

For a present key $\kappa$, let $S_\kappa c$ replace the occupied endpoint with the other endpoint and leave every other site unchanged. Set
\[
 b=7,\qquad r=8,\qquad H=2(b+r)=30.
\]
For a fixed block, select $\kappa=(\text{row},x)$ precisely when both conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{Isolation:} no other raw key has anchor within distance $30$ of $x$. Another row at the same anchor counts as another key.
\item \textbf{Prospective preservation:} after the hypothetical swap, the raw-key set with anchors in $[x-15,x+15]$ is exactly the same as before it.
\end{enumerate}
All selected swaps act simultaneously. Keys failing either test do nothing; sites in no selected write support retain their state. Finally define $F=B\circ A$.

This is a finite local algorithm, including on malformed input. In particular, prospectivity must search for \emph{new} keys after the hypothetical swap, not merely test whether previously present keys survive. The next section proves that simultaneous writes are unambiguous and local.

\section{Full shift reversibility}\label{smc:rt:sec:fullshift}
We give the complete guarded-swap proof, including preservation of rejected keys. It uses no particle-count bound.

\wtag\ [Second route. Lemma~\ref{smc:rt:lem:guard} is the prospective-isolation lemma of Report~26, Lemma \texttt{fpa:pi:lem:parallel} of \path{five-particle-binary-automata} (Part~VI there), with the same isolation distance $H=2(b+r)$ and the same radius bound $3(b+r)$; that report applies it to a binary five-particle compiler. Source~24 credits the mechanism to the programme's review of Reports~26--28~\cite{reviewparallel} and gives the proof again for its own row format, in which a key does not record its endpoint side. The proof is printed because it is self-contained; no novelty is claimed for the lemma.]

\begin{lemma}[Prospective isolation]\label{smc:rt:lem:guard}
Consider a finite family of endpoint swaps with distinct, nonempty endpoints of equal weight. Every endpoint is contained in its own read window; all writes lie in $[-b,b]$ and all reads in $[-r,r]$, where $r\ge b$. Suppose each swap exchanges the two sides of its own raw-key predicate. Select a raw key at $x$ by isolation within $H=2(b+r)$ and preservation of all raw keys within $b+r$ under its hypothetical swap. The parallel block $T$ is a translation-equivariant full-shift involution of radius at most $3(b+r)$. It fixes vacuum and conserves particle number on finite configurations.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Write $K(c)$ for all raw keys in the block. A hypothetical write at $x$ can change a raw predicate at $y$ only if the radius-$b$ write window and radius-$r$ read window meet, so only if $|x-y|\le b+r$. Therefore the local prospective test $P_\kappa(c)$ is equivalent to the global equality
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rt:eq:globalkeys}
 K(S_\kappa c)=K(c).
\end{equation}
This equality is about key identity, not endpoint side.

Two selected anchors have distance greater than $H$. Their write windows are disjoint. Moreover, a single raw-predicate read window cannot meet two selected write windows: if it met those at $x$ and $y$, then $|x-y|\le2(b+r)=H$, a contradiction. Every raw predicate therefore sees either no write or exactly the change produced by one selected hypothetical swap. In the latter case \eqref{smc:rt:eq:globalkeys} preserves its truth value. Thus
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rt:eq:parallelkeys}
 K(Tc)=K(c)
\end{equation}
for arbitrary finite or infinite $c$.

Isolation consequently has the same truth value before and after $T$. To check selection itself, the prospective test at a present key anchored at $x$ depends only on
\[
 [x-(b+2r),x+(b+2r)]:
\]
its tested anchors are within $b+r$ and their reads extend another $r$. Any \emph{other selected} key at $y$ has $|x-y|>H$, because its own isolation test sees the raw key at $x$, whether or not $x$ is selected. Its radius-$b$ write window misses this entire comparison window.

If $\kappa$ is selected, its own swap exchanges the two configurations whose raw sets are compared in \eqref{smc:rt:eq:globalkeys}; the other selected writes cannot affect that comparison. Hence its prospective test remains true. If $\kappa$ is isolated but prospectively rejected, no own write occurs and no other selected write reaches the comparison window; it remains rejected. If it is nonisolated, it remains nonisolated by \eqref{smc:rt:eq:parallelkeys}, hence rejected. Indeed, the same window argument preserves its prospective status too. No new raw key appears by \eqref{smc:rt:eq:parallelkeys}. The entire selected-key set is therefore unchanged. A second block application performs the same disjoint endpoint involutions and returns $c$.

For locality at an output site $z$, only anchors within $b$ of $z$ can write there. At any such anchor, isolation reads radius $H+r$, and prospectivity reads radius $b+2r$. Thus an adequate output radius is
\[
 b+\max\{H+r,b+2r\}=3(b+r).
\]
All conditions use relative coordinates, so the rule is translation-equivariant. Nonempty endpoints imply no key on vacuum and only finitely many present keys on finite support. Disjoint equal-weight swaps then preserve the finite particle count. The proof and the involution identity apply without a finite-support assumption.
\end{proof}

In Table~\ref{smc:rt:tab:rows}, the endpoint sizes agree row by row, the endpoints lie inside their read intervals, their supports lie in $[-7,7]$, and the read intervals lie in $[-8,8]$. Exact replacement exchanges the two own-key alternatives. Lemma~\ref{smc:rt:lem:guard} gives
\[
 A^2=B^2=\mathrm{id},\qquad F^{-1}=A\circ B,
\]
on the full shift, and radii at most $45$ for each block and $90$ for $F$ and $F^{-1}$. These are certified upper bounds, not minimal-radius claims. Although a time step factors into two blocks, the same fixed composite rule is used at every time; this is not a spatially partitioned or time-alternating model with an extra hidden clock state.

\subsection{Why isolation alone is insufficient}\label{smc:ix:rt:sec:isolation}
Take
\[
 X=\{-8,-5,0,1\},\qquad Y=\{-8,-5,0,2\}.
\]
The only $A$-key of $X$ is $(\row{AR},0)$. Its hypothetical swap yields $Y$, which has both $(\row{AR},0)$ and $(\row{AC},-7)$. Thus the actual rule rejects the swap. An isolation-only variant sends $X$ to $Y$ and fixes $Y$, and is therefore noninjective.

The example also tests simultaneous accepted and rejected keys: add $\{70,71\}$ to $X$. The key at $0$ is still isolated but prospectively rejected; $(\row{AR},70)$ is selected. The actual output is $X\cup\{70,72\}$, and both statuses are preserved. This is a concrete malformed-input check, not an assumption that malformed configurations are all fixed.

\wtag\ [Report~26 gives a counterexample of the same kind for its own rule family, on a binary ring of period~12 (Section \texttt{fpa:pi:sec:lemma} of \path{five-particle-binary-automata}); the example above is source~24's own, for its six rows.]

\section{The complete four particle orbit}\label{smc:rt:sec:orbit}
For $D\ge13$, write
\[
 C_D=\{0,5,6,D\},\qquad L_D=2D-22.
\]
\begin{proposition}[Every intermediate state]\label{smc:rt:prop:orbit}
For $0\le s<L_D$,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rt:eq:phases}
 F^s(C_D)=
 \begin{cases}
 \{0,5+s,6+s,D\},&0\le s\le D-11,\\
 \{0,2D-18-s,2D-14-s,D+1\},&D-10\le s\le2D-23.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
At the endpoint, $F^{L_D}(C_D)=C_{D+1}$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The two phase intervals are adjacent and disjoint and cover the whole cycle. We first compute all four possible kinds of complete step, retaining the intermediate half-step:
\begin{align}
 \{0,p,p+1,D\}
 &\xrightarrow{\row{AR}(p)}\{0,p,p+2,D\}
 \xrightarrow{\row{BR}(p)}\{0,p+1,p+2,D\},\label{smc:rt:eq:right}\\[-2pt]
 &\hspace{55mm}5\le p\le D-7;\notag\\[-10pt]
 \{0,D-6,D-5,D\}
 &\xrightarrow{\row{AC}(D-6)}\{0,D-7,D-4,D+1\}\notag\\
 &\xrightarrow{\row{BL}(D-7)}\{0,D-8,D-4,D+1\};\label{smc:rt:eq:rc}\\
 \{0,q,q+4,D+1\}
 &\xrightarrow{\row{AL}(q)}\{0,q,q+3,D+1\}
 \xrightarrow{\row{BL}(q)}\{0,q-1,q+3,D+1\},\label{smc:rt:eq:left}\\[-2pt]
 &\hspace{55mm}6\le q\le D-8;\notag\\[-10pt]
 \{0,5,9,D+1\}
 &\xrightarrow{\row{AL}(5)}\{0,5,8,D+1\}
 \xrightarrow{\row{BC}(5)}\{0,5,6,D+1\}.\label{smc:rt:eq:lc}
\end{align}
Equations~\eqref{smc:rt:eq:right} and \eqref{smc:rt:eq:left} are flights; \eqref{smc:rt:eq:rc} and \eqref{smc:rt:eq:lc} are the two contacts. At $D=13$, the left-flight range is empty and the left phase is the single state $s=3$. Thus the smallest allowed parameter is included.

It remains to prove that these proposed arrows are the actual guarded moves. At every displayed state and half-state exactly one particle pair has distance at most four; all other pairs have distance at least five. Every endpoint in Table~\ref{smc:rt:tab:rows} contains such a close pair. Consequently every raw key must use this unique pair.

For block $A$, gaps $1,2$ permit $\row{AR}$; the only competing endpoint with gap $1$ is the input of $\row{AC}$. It requires a third particle six sites to the right of the pair's left site, precisely where the $\row{AR}$ guard also reads. At right contact it creates $\row{AC}$ and excludes $\row{AR}$; during right flight the right marker is farther away. Gaps $4,3$ permit $\row{AL}$; the only competing gap-$3$ endpoint is the output of $\row{AC}$. Its third particle is eight sites right of the pair's left site, precisely inside the $\row{AL}$ guard. Thus on the reverse side of the contact it excludes $\row{AL}$. That marker distance does not occur in the free left-flight half-states.

For block $B$, gaps $2,1$ permit $\row{BR}$, with only the output of $\row{BC}$ competing at gap $1$. Gaps $3,4$ permit $\row{BL}$, with only the input of $\row{BC}$ competing at gap $3$. Both $\row{BC}$ endpoints require a third particle five sites left of the close pair's left site. That site is in the relevant $\row{BR}$ or $\row{BL}$ read interval, so the contact and free move cannot coexist. The marker occurs exactly at left contact or its reverse half-step. At the right contact the pair's left site is $D-7\ge6$, so the origin cannot accidentally trigger $\row{BC}$.

The unused origin at right contact is outside $[D-11,D+2]$, since $D\ge13$. The unused right marker at left contact is $D+1\ge14$, outside $[0,13]$. The displayed flight bounds likewise keep spectator particles out of the relevant read intervals. Hence each proposed half-step has exactly one raw key before and after its hypothetical swap, and it is the \emph{same row-anchor key}. Isolation and prospectivity both pass. These arrows prove \eqref{smc:rt:eq:phases} and its endpoint by induction.
\end{proof}

\begin{figure}[!ht]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.97\textwidth]{figures/24-reversible-clock-spacetime.pdf}
\caption{The first six cycles of source~24's clock from $C_{13}$, obtained by iterating the literal guarded rule, not by plotting the phase formula. Each square is one occupied site; time increases downward. Dashed lines mark exactly the seven observed hits $0,4,10,18,28,40,54$. The moving pair changes its separation from one to four at the right contact, and the right marker advances one site per cycle. The plotted coordinates and observations are saved as a CSV, and independently checked against \eqref{smc:rt:eq:phases}. \wtag\ [Shipped as \texttt{figures/24-reversible-clock-spacetime.pdf}; the CSV is \texttt{data/24-reversible-figures-clock-spacetime.csv}.]}\label{smc:rt:fig:clock}
\end{figure}

\section{Exact timing and an elementary quartic}\label{smc:rt:sec:timing}
At $s=0$ in \eqref{smc:rt:eq:phases}, the sites $0,5,6$ are occupied and sites $1,2,3,4$ are empty. During the right phase the adjacent pair is $\{5,6\}$ only when $s=0$. During the left phase the moving particles have separation four, while the other two particles occupy $0$ and $D+1\ge14$; hence the exact word cannot occur. This proves \emph{all-time exclusivity}, not just the existence of section returns.

Starting at $C_d$, the $k$th hit is the configuration $C_{d+k}$ at time
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rt:eq:times}
 t_k=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}L_{d+j}
 =\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}(2(d+j)-22)
 =k^2+(2d-23)k.
\end{equation}
The empty sum gives $t_0=0$. Successive gaps are
\[
 t_{k+1}-t_k=2k+2d-22,
\]
which tend to infinity. Every infinite eventually periodic subset of $\NN$ has bounded successive gaps: beyond its threshold, a nonempty periodic residue class supplies a point at least once per period. Thus \eqref{smc:rt:eq:times} is not eventually periodic. In one variable Presburger-definability is equivalent to eventual periodicity, so the hit set is not Presburger-definable~\cite{ginsburgspanier}.

\begin{remark}[\wtag\ Source~24's quartic is source~17's]\label{smc:rt:cor:quartic}
Source~24 states as its Corollary~4.1, \emph{Exact nonnegative rational fibers}: ``For $x,t\in\NN$, put $d=13+x$ and
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rt:eq:quartic}
 Q(x,t;k)=\bigl[k^2+(2x+3)k-t\bigr]^2.
\end{equation}
The polynomial has total degree four and a single natural witness coordinate $k$. Its zero fiber over $\NN$ is empty when $t$ is not a hit, and a singleton when $t$ is a hit. The zero fiber over $\Q_{\ge0}$ is exactly the same fiber.'' Its proof: ``The timing polynomial is strictly increasing for $k\ge0$: its consecutive differences are $2k+2x+4>0$. Its values on $\NN$ are exactly \eqref{smc:rt:eq:times}. Squaring introduces no additional zeros. If a rational $k$ is a root of the monic integer polynomial $k^2+(2x+3)k-t$, write $k=a/b$ in lowest terms with $b>0$. Multiplication by $b^2$ implies $b\mid a^2$, hence $b=1$. A nonnegative rational root is therefore natural. This is the elementary monic rational-root argument, not an inference from finite rational testing.''

This is the certificate $\mathcal P(x,t;k)$ of~\eqref{smc:fm:eq:quartic}, polynomial for polynomial: source~17 writes $d=7+x$ for its shuttle, whose hits $k^2+(2d-11)k$ become $k^2+(2x+3)k$, and source~24 writes $d=13+x$, whose hits $k^2+(2d-23)k$ become the same expression. The statement, the strict monotonicity, the monic rational-root argument and the failure over nonnegative reals (every natural $t$ has a nonnegative real root) are all in Section~\ref{smc:fm:sec:quartic}, where the result is printed, together with its least-degree note and the programme's confirmation~\cite{reviewlowmass}; source~24 says the certificate has ``the same arithmetic form'' as the earlier shuttle's. Only the automaton behind the polynomial differs: for source~24 it is globally reversible.
\end{remark}

The domain restrictions matter. At a genuine hit, the second root is $-k-(2x+3)$, so unrestricted integer or rational fibers are not singletons. Over nonnegative reals every $t\ge0$ has a nonnegative root; for example $x=0,t=1$ has the false witness $(\sqrt{13}-3)/2$, although $1$ is not a clock hit. Thus the certificate is not real-exact. It is a direct elementary encoding of this one timing relation, already of the same arithmetic form as the earlier nonreversible shuttle's certificate \textup{[\path{17-four-mass-BINARY-INDEPENDENT-AUDIT.md}; source~17, Section~\ref{smc:fm:sec:quartic}]}; no universal-polynomial degree, arity, or single-fold record is claimed. \wtag\ [No certificate with $(x,t)$ as its only external data is real-exact: Remark~\ref{smc:ix:rem:realtrace}.]

\subsection{A dense observation of the same orbit}\label{smc:ix:rt:sec:dense}
The complete orbit also illustrates why quadratic \emph{section times} do not force every finite-word hit set to be a union of quadratic sequences.
\begin{corollary}[A density one hit set]\label{smc:rt:cor:dense}
For $d\ge13$ and $t_k$ from \eqref{smc:rt:eq:times}, the exact word \texttt{100000} at $[0,5]$ has occurrence set
\[
 H(F,C_d;\texttt{100000},0)
 =\bigcup_{k\ge0}[t_k+1,t_{k+1}-2]\cap\NN.
\]
This set has natural density one and an infinite complement. It cannot be a finite union of eventually arithmetic progressions and positive-leading-coefficient quadratic polynomial sequences, even when the latter are restricted to eventual arithmetic progressions of their parameter.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
The origin is always occupied and sites $1,2,3,4$ are always empty in \eqref{smc:rt:eq:phases}. Site $5$ is occupied exactly at the first and last state of each cycle: $s=0$ in the right phase and $s=L_D-1$ in the left phase. Hence the only omitted times in cycle $k$ are $t_k$ and $t_{k+1}-1$, proving the interval formula. Since $t_k=k^2+O(k)$, there are only $O(\sqrt T)$ omissions through time $T$, but infinitely many altogether. Thus the density is one and the set is not cofinite.

A quadratic sequence with positive leading coefficient has only $O(\sqrt T)$ values in $[0,T]$, so any finite union of such sequences has density zero. A finite union of eventual arithmetic progressions is eventually periodic. If its union with a density-zero set has density one, that eventually periodic part must itself have density one, and therefore be cofinite. Its union would then be cofinite, contradicting the infinitely many omissions above.
\end{proof}
This is an elementary additional observation of the same proved orbit. It does not contradict the inherited fixed-input quadratic \emph{chart} description, which allows a second within-flight parameter and hence growing intervals of times; see Section~\ref{smc:rt:sec:related}.

\wtag\ [The ``inherited fixed-input quadratic chart description'' is source~18's Lemma~\ref{smc:tq:lem:interface}: in its charts the within-flight parameter $j$ ranges over an interval whose length grows with the cycle, which produces exactly such bands of times.]

\section{Why three particles cannot suffice}\label{smc:rt:sec:lower}
This section adapts the stationary-unit, no-split, finite-encounter argument from the inherited source \textup{[source~16]}, specifically its model and timed-evolution theorem at lines 5406--5459 and proof at lines 5464--5743 of the pinned source \wtag\ [Section~\ref{smc:su:sec:model} with Theorem~\ref{smc:su:thm:main} and Corollary~\ref{smc:su:cor:decision}, and Sections~\ref{smc:su:sec:frame}--\ref{smc:su:sec:observation}]. The source treats weighted alphabets with at most one weight-one label and establishes uniform Presburger evolution. We reprove only the binary, fixed-input statement needed here. This narrower presentation is included for logical completeness, not as a claim of a new lower-bound argument.

\wtag\ [Second route, step by step. The stationary frame below is that of Section~\ref{smc:su:sec:frame}; the no-split argument is Lemma~\ref{smc:su:lem:invariant}; the pair tail~\eqref{smc:rt:eq:pairtail} is Lemma~\ref{smc:su:lem:walker}; the core of diameter at most $4S$ and the exact evolution before it are Section~\ref{smc:su:sec:core} with Lemma~\ref{smc:su:lem:outside}; the first-entry interval~\eqref{smc:rt:eq:firstentry} is~\eqref{smc:su:eq:hit} of Lemma~\ref{smc:su:lem:first} verbatim; the return graph is Proposition~\ref{smc:su:prop:orbits}; and the observation step is Section~\ref{smc:su:sec:observation}. Source~24's version is shorter because it is binary and per input: it needs no uniform construction (Section~\ref{smc:su:sec:uniform}), and it concludes eventual periodicity of each observation directly. Source~19's Lemma~\ref{smc:zd:lem:triple} is the same fixed-input statement on $\Z^d$.]

\begin{theorem}[Inherited binary per-input bound]\label{smc:rt:thm:three}
Fix a one-dimensional binary, quiescent, number-conserving CA $G_0$ of finite radius. For every fixed finite-support input with at most three particles, the relation between time and its occupied output coordinates is effectively Presburger-definable. In particular, every fixed exact anchored finite-word occurrence set is effectively eventually periodic. Reversibility is unnecessary.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
We give the orbit decomposition and then the observation argument.

\paragraph{A stationary singleton frame.}
Conservation forces the successor of a single particle at $0$ to be a single particle at some $\delta$ with $|\delta|\le R$, where $R$ is a radius of $G_0$. Let $\tau_a$ denote translation to the right by $a$, and set
\[
 G=\tau_{-\delta}G_0,\qquad S=\max\{1,R+|\delta|\}.
\]
Every singleton is fixed by $G$, whose radius is at most $S$. Also $G_0^t=\tau_{\delta t}G^t$. The padding $S\ge1$ includes radius-zero rules.

Join occupied sites at distance at most $2S$ into components. Distinct components are more than $2S$ apart, so no radius-$S$ read neighborhood meets two of them. Quiescence and finite propagation imply exact one-step independence: their separately computed successor supports are disjoint and their union is the global successor.

\paragraph{A bounded pair cannot split into distant components.}
Suppose a two-particle configuration has diameter $d\le2S$, translated to $\{0,d\}$. If $d>S$, each original occupied site's neighborhood is exactly its isolated-singleton neighborhood, so both sites remain occupied. They already exhaust the conserved mass, and the pair is fixed. If $d\le S$, any new occupied output site must see both particles: a neighborhood seeing zero or just one would give the vacuum or stationary-singleton output there. Such a site lies in $[d-S,S]$, which also contains $0,d$ and has width $2S-d\le2S$. The successor pair thus still has diameter at most $2S$. Induction proves this bound at all times.

Normalize a bounded pair by putting its leftmost site at zero. There are only $2S$ possible normalized pair shapes. The next shape and the displacement of its leftmost site depend only on that shape. A repeated shape yields a computable finite transient and a translated periodic tail:
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rt:eq:pairtail}
 G^{\mu+r+np}(q)=\tau_{nD}q_{\mu+r}
 \quad(0\le r<p,\ n\ge0),
\end{equation}
for constants $\mu,p,D$ and finitely many explicit configurations. A pair initially farther than $2S$ apart consists of two fixed singletons. This settles zero, one, and two particles.

\paragraph{The finite three-particle encounter core.}
For mass three take the core to be the configurations of diameter at most $4S$. It has $\binom{4S}{2}$ normalized shapes. Every connected three-particle configuration is in the core, since its two adjacent gaps are at most $2S$. Outside the core there are therefore either three isolated fixed singleton components, or a bounded pair and one stationary singleton. A single step from the core has diameter at most $6S$ by finite propagation.

In the pair-plus-singleton case, let $z_k$ be the isolated pair orbit and let $b$ be the singleton's site. Until the first $k$ at which the span of $\supp(z_k)\cup\{b\}$ is at most $4S$, the actual orbit is exactly this union, also at the first such time if it exists. Indeed, if the singleton were within $2S$ of the pair, the pair's diameter bound $2S$ would put the whole span within $4S$. Before entry the two components are more than $2S$ apart, so one-step independence applies inductively. In particular, the counterfactual union is disjoint throughout the portion used.

First entry is effective. Inspect the finite transient in \eqref{smc:rt:eq:pairtail}. On a periodic phase the pair's leftmost site has the form $a+A_r+nD$ and its diameter is a constant $d_r\le2S$. Core entry on that phase is exactly
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rt:eq:firstentry}
 b-4S\le a+A_r+nD\le b+4S-d_r,\qquad n\in\NN.
\end{equation}
This is an integer interval problem. For $D=0$ it is always or never satisfied; for $D>0$ use the least nonnegative integer above the lower bound and test the upper bound; for $D<0$ reverse the inequalities. Comparing the finitely many phase and transient candidates determines the first entry or certifies no entry.

\paragraph{A finite return graph describes all intermediate times.}
For each normalized core shape, take one exact step. A core successor gives a return edge of duration one and a fixed spatial displacement. If the successor is outside, the preceding classification and first-entry procedure either give a later first return, with a fixed positive duration and displacement, or a completely described nonreturning orbit. These data depend only on the normalized starting shape, so this is a finite deterministic graph.

If a nonreturning edge occurs, the tail is fixed or is a stationary singleton plus an independent bounded pair with translated periodic tail. Otherwise a normalized core shape repeats. At two actual times $t_0<t_1$ we then have $G^{t_1}(c)=\tau_aG^{t_0}(c)$, and determinism and translation equivariance give
\[
 G^{t_1+n}(c)=\tau_aG^{t_0+n}(c)\qquad(n\ge0).
\]
This identity includes \emph{every intermediate time}, not just returns to the core. Thus, after a finite transient, the entire configuration is periodic up to one translation, or is an independent stationary singleton and a bounded translated-periodic pair.

\paragraph{Exact observations in the original frame.}
On each of finitely many time phases $t=T+r+nP$, every occupied coordinate has the form $a_j+n d_j$ in the stationary frame. In the original frame it becomes
\[
 a_j+\delta(T+r)+n(d_j+\delta P).
\]
All coefficients are fixed integers. Together with the finite transient, these formulas give a finite disjunction of linear existential formulas for time and occupied coordinates; particle ordering, if needed, can also be imposed by linear inequalities. Hence the timed relation is Presburger-definable.

For an exact word anchored at $z$, each required one means at least one of these at-most-three coordinates equals the corresponding site; each required zero means \emph{none} equals that site. On a fixed time phase, each equality of an affine coordinate to a fixed site is either always true, always false, or true at at most one integer $n$. Consequently the full observation is eventually constant on each phase. A finite union of those phase tails and finitely many exceptions is effectively eventually periodic. The interval computations, finite-state iterations, and finite equality tests above make the threshold and period computable. This proves the theorem without requiring the source's stronger uniform-in-input-position construction.
\end{proof}

Applying Theorem~\ref{smc:rt:thm:three} to the reversible subclass supplies the lower bound in Theorem~\ref{smc:rt:thm:main}; Sections~\ref{smc:rt:sec:fullshift}--\ref{smc:rt:sec:timing} supply the four-particle upper example. The lower bound relies on binary particles having a single internal type. It makes no assertion about several weight-one labels, signed weights, active zero-weight backgrounds, time-dependent rules, infinite-support inputs, or other dimensions.

\section{Relation to the existing results}\label{smc:rt:sec:related}
The scope separates three different questions: timing regularity, decidability of finite observations, and computational universality. The present example separates eventual periodicity from the other two: a simple decidable quadratic set can have unbounded gaps.

\paragraph{The earlier four-particle shuttle.}
The inspected repository audit of source 17 describes a different radius-six binary four-particle shuttle and explicitly proves that rule noninjective \textup{[\path{17-four-mass-BINARY-INDEPENDENT-AUDIT.md}; the rule~\eqref{smc:fm:eq:binary} and the note after Proposition~\ref{smc:fm:prop:rule}]}. Its arithmetic timing corollary already has the elementary squared-polynomial form used here. It does not supply global reversibility. The six-row rule above addresses that missing property using the inherited prospective-isolation mechanism~\cite{reviewparallel}. Its reversibility proof deliberately handles candidate births, rejected keys, and arbitrary full-shift configurations.

\paragraph{Low-particle work and universality.}
The inherited source records Kong's 2021 binary three-particle nonuniversality argument and its periodic-orbit decomposition \textup{[\cite{kongthesis}; source~16, Section~\ref{smc:su:sec:sources}]}. The source then gives the stronger weighted single-unit-label timed theorem used for our lower bound. We rely on the pinned source proof, reproduced in the binary specialization above; we do not attribute its full weighted or uniform conclusion to Kong.

The same inspected article records already available binary and globally reversible binary five-particle universality constructions in the repository's \emph{five-particle-binary-automata} collection, Reports 14 and 15, and its four-mass decidability theorem \textup{[\path{five-particle-binary-automata}, Part~I; source~17, Theorem~\ref{smc:fm:thm:main}; the dated note in Section~\ref{smc:su:sec:sources}]}. Those are separate results. We do not rerun their source programs or use their universality claims in a proof here. Four-particle nonperiodic timing is compatible with four-particle decidability, and the present rule is not claimed to compute universally. The inherited source 17 already proves fixed-input alternatives consisting of independent finite-phase objects, whole configurations periodic up to translation, or expanding shuttles with affine section gaps and anchors and positive-quadratic accumulated section times (lines 6269--6330 \wtag\ [Proposition~\ref{smc:fm:prop:normal} and Corollary~\ref{smc:fm:cor:spatial}]). Source 18 refines this to complete disjoint fixed-input timed charts with at most two natural parameters, affine domains, and degree-at-most-two coordinate and time polynomials \wtag\ [Lemma~\ref{smc:tq:lem:interface}]. These include within-flight time bands, not only isolated quadratic return sequences; Corollary~\ref{smc:rt:cor:dense} is consistent with that established description.

\paragraph{The standard multistate setting.}
Morita proves a universal 96-state, four-neighbor one-dimensional RNCCA by simulating a reversible partitioned CA~\cite{morita2012}. That primary result establishes the expressive power of reversible number conservation with many states; it does not give this binary fixed-four-particle timing statement. No literature-priority claim follows from the present source comparison. The radius bound $90$ is also not asserted optimal.

\wtag\ [Further context in this collection. Report~26 (Part~VI of \path{five-particle-binary-automata}) applies the same prospective-isolation lemma to make a binary five-particle universal compiler a product of two full-shift involutions; source~24 applies it to a four-particle clock, which is not universal. The programme's intake reads source~24 as ``a decidable quadratic timing set, not a universal substrate improvement''~\cite{reviewnewsignals}.]

\section{Independent checks and reproducibility}\label{smc:rt:sec:checks}
The unrestricted conclusions above are mathematical proofs, not mechanically formalized theorems. Finite computation checks the literal implementation and boundary arithmetic; it cannot replace the full-shift argument. The frozen independent audit records a final mathematical PASS and an additional complete UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer replay \textup{[\path{24-reversible-frozen-audit-AUDIT.md}]}.

\subsection{Three separately inspectable checkers}
The candidate checker was newly written from the stated rule. The independent sparse checker was separately written from the six rows and imports no candidate implementation. It discovers every possible raw key by aligning occupied sites with endpoint offsets, tests exact read windows, and rediscovers the complete raw-key set after hypothetical swaps. The independent C++ implementation uses rotated masks on 64-periodic words rather than sparse alignment code.

The independent audit records:
\begin{itemize}
\item All 540 potentially changing source-side, target-row, relative-anchor interactions, comprising 49,840 complete local assignments. Forty-eight assignments change a raw predicate, so prospective rejection is nonvacuous. At most 12 free bits occur in any interaction table.
\item Every step of 108 cycles, $D=13,\ldots,120$: 11,988 complete steps and unique selected raw keys at every half-step; plus 36 large-coordinate phase and contact tests through $D=10^{100}$.
\item A continuous 3,780-step orbit with exactly the 61 hits $k^2+3k$, $0\le k\le60$.
\item 4,736 arbitrary or malformed finite configurations, yielding 9,472 checked blocks: 4,179 changed blocks, 2,962 with multiple selected keys, and 21 with isolated prospectively rejected keys. Both inverse identities and translation covariance were checked.
\item All 262,144 binary words of width 18 embedded in period 64, and 252 additional two-island words: 524,792 checked blocks, including 80 isolated-rejection blocks and 216 multiple-selection blocks. Both inverse identities passed on every enumerated width-18 word.
\item The compact candidate-birth example and simultaneous accepted/rejected example; 42 large-integer quartic tests and 1,516,800 rational trials.
\end{itemize}
The periodic tests are exact induced tests on infinite periodic configurations. Period 64 is greater than $2H=60$, avoiding duplicate lifts in an isolation neighborhood, and greater than $2(b+r)=30$, separating the raw-predicate influence neighborhoods of copies of a hypothetical write. Consequently the ring prospective test agrees with the specified single-anchor test. The enumeration is \emph{not} all $2^{64}$ periodic words. Likewise the local interaction tables exhaust each pairwise raw-predicate interaction, not every radius-45 input neighborhood. These distinctions are part of the audit scope.

The C++ source uses explicit failure checks rather than assertions disabled by optimization. Its optimized and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer runs produced byte-identical JSON receipts. Python checks likewise use explicit failure tests. The recorded audit environment was Python 3.12.14 and Debian g++ 14.2.0.

\subsection{The offline release packet}
The archive includes the editable manuscript and PDF, figure and numerical trace, inspected checker sources, read-only frozen candidate and audit files, and SHA-256 manifests. The inherited article is preserved as inert evidence with its exact excerpt and provenance; it is never compiled, imported, or executed. No upstream executable, automation, or schedule is run.

The release helper \path{code/replay.py} first verifies the manifest, then copies only the inspected checker sources into a fresh temporary directory. All checker output and newly compiled binaries stay in that scratch directory. It compares deterministic results to the frozen receipts, ignoring only the recorded sparse checker's elapsed-time field. It also verifies the source hashes and excerpt identity, regenerates the numerical spacetime trace from the literal rule, and rebuilds this manuscript with shell escape disabled. No frozen input is overwritten and no network access is required. The optional sanitizer mode recompiles only the independently authored C++ checker with UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. See \path{README.txt} for exact commands and prerequisites.

SHA-256 manifests authenticate correspondence with the inspected packet once their digest is obtained through a trusted channel; they are integrity checks, not a claim of digital signatures or third-party certification. The independent audit's original manifest is retained separately. Figure~\ref{smc:rt:fig:clock} is supplementary illustration; its seven hit rows and every plotted occupied coordinate are reproduced by the checker-based trace generator.

\section{Further questions}\label{smc:ix:rt:sec:questions}
These are directions for investigation, not consequences claimed by this report.
\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{smc:ix:rt:q:radius} \textbf{Radius and guard efficiency.} Can the radius-$90$ reversible example be reduced substantially while retaining a transparent full-shift proof? The conservative bounds $b=7$, $r=8$, and global isolation $H=30$ are sufficient rather than optimized. Any reduction must still preserve rejected-key status and exclude candidate births. (\wtag\ Open. It is the reversible form of source~17's Question~\ref{smc:fm:q:radius}, whose noninjective binary example has radius six.)
\item\label{smc:ix:rt:q:uniform} \textbf{Uniform descriptions across initial inputs.} The inherited sources already give effective fixed-input four-particle orbit alternatives and quadratic phase charts. A different question is whether a suitable exact timed normal form can be made uniform in the initial particle positions, with precisely stated syntax and parameter bounds. The present family gives one uniform quadratic timing formula, but does not settle that general problem. No fixed-input classification is asserted open here. (\wtag\ Added 4 October 2026: answered conditionally by source~25, the same pipeline's next report but one, for the single-unit class at mass at most four: one finite chart family uniform in all ordered initial coordinates, with at most two evolution parameters and at most three gap quotients (Theorem~\ref{smc:ut:thm:uniform}), conditional on source~17's scattering data and source~18's fixed-input charts.)
\item\label{smc:ix:rt:q:criterion} \textbf{A useful criterion for safe parallel swaps.} Can prospectivity be replaced by a simpler finite syntactic criterion for suitable endpoint families, while retaining the full-shift conclusion? The compact counterexample above rules out isolation alone, but does not preclude stronger row-specific compatibility conditions.
\item\label{smc:ix:rt:q:formal} \textbf{Proof-assistant verification.} A formalization could connect the finite predicate algorithm to the global involution theorem, the exact orbit, and the inherited low-particle lower bound. Exhaustive local interaction records provide useful test data, but a full proof must also cover arbitrary infinite supports and all intermediate times.
\end{enumerate}
