\phantomsection\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Source 25: Uniform timed charts for four mass units}
\noindent{\large\bfseries Source 25 (batch-91 manuscript 03): Uniform timed charts for four mass units}\par
\noindent ``Report 51'', 4 October 2026. \wtag\ From the archive \path{Uniform_Timed_Charts_for_Four_Mass_Units_Package.zip} (main file \path{Research_Report51/manuscript/report51.tex}, 21-page PDF; neither is shipped). Its labels carry the prefix \texttt{smc:ut:}, and its sections are Sections~\ref{smc:ut:sec:statement}--\ref{smc:ut:app:provenance} here; its appendix is printed as the last of them. Its main theorem is conditional on source~17's scattering data and source~18's fixed-input chart theorem, which it imports from this article by line number (brackets translate the lines into labels); its obstruction uses source~24, which it calls ``Report~49''. Its abstract follows.
\begin{quote}\small
Fix a one-dimensional finite-radius conservative cellular automaton with a unique zero-weight vacuum, positive integer nonvacuum weights, and at most one weight-one symbol. Conditional on the pinned source-17 scattering mechanism and source-18 fixed-input chart theorem, we construct one finite effective family of complete timed-orbit charts, uniform in all ordered initial coordinates at total mass at most four. On finitely many disjoint Presburger input cells, at most two natural evolution parameters suffice; stationary-frame positions are affine and time has joint total degree at most two. Literal affine domains require at most three additional, uniquely determined initial-gap quotients, giving at most five natural chart parameters. The decisive step is a fully guarded symbolic contraction up to the first bounded ordinary reset, after which only fixed templates are added. This proves uniform untimed stationary-frame Presburger reachability. A copied-input, selector-safe compilation gives a finite-arity quartic with empty or singleton natural witness fibers for the uniform complete timed relation. Its witness count includes copies, quotients, selectors and slacks, and is not two or five. A shifted version of Report 49's [source~24's] reversible clock shows that original-frame untimed reachability can fail to be Presburger even from one fixed four-particle input. We give the full arithmetic construction, endpoint ownership proof, conditional dependency ledger and independent adversarial checks. No general compiler implementation, formal verification, or literature-priority claim is asserted.
\end{quote}
\noindent\textbf{Conventions.} $\NN=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. Coordinates are integers. Translation $\tau_a$ moves a configuration to the right by $a$. A complete configuration lists every occupied site and its label; all unlisted sites are vacuum. ``Affine'' allows rational coefficients until positive denominators are cleared.

\section{The uniform statement and its scope}\label{smc:ut:sec:statement}
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet with distinguished vacuum $0$. Let $w:A\to\NN$ have $w(0)=0$ and $w(a)>0$ for $a\ne0$. Let $F:A^{\Z}\to A^{\Z}$ be a deterministic, time-independent, translation-equivariant cellular automaton of finite radius $R$, with quiescent vacuum and
\[
 M(F(c))=M(c),\qquad M(c)=\sum_{i\in\Z}w(c_i)
\]
for every finite-support configuration $c$. There is at most one symbol of weight one; labels of higher weights need not be unique. Fix a tuple $\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$ of nonzero input labels with total weight at most four. An input is determined by $\mathbf x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in\Z^m$, $x_1<\cdots<x_m$, with these labels in order. Thus $m\le4$. Empty input is allowed.

\wtag\ [This is the model of source~16 (Section~\ref{smc:su:sec:model}) and source~17 (Section~\ref{smc:fm:sec:model}) at mass at most four.]

If a unit symbol $u$ exists, conservation implies that an isolated $u$ becomes exactly one $u$, displaced by some $\delta\in[-R,R]$. Put
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:frame}
 G=\tau_{-\delta}F,\qquad S=\max\{1,R+|\delta|\}.
\end{equation}
Then $G$ has radius at most $S$ and fixes every isolated $u$. If no unit exists, put $G=F$, $\delta=0$ and $S=\max\{1,R\}$. In either case $F^t=\tau_{\delta t}G^t$.

\begin{theorem}[Conditional uniform timed chart theorem]\label{smc:ut:thm:uniform}
Assume the finite scattering data of source 17 and the complete fixed-input chart theorem of source 18, in the precise forms stated in Section~\ref{smc:ut:sec:imports}. For fixed $F$ and $\mathbf a$, one can effectively construct a finite family, independent of the magnitudes of $\mathbf x$, with these properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The ordered input space is partitioned into finitely many disjoint cells defined by integer-affine equalities and inequalities and fixed-modulus congruences in the initial gaps $g_i=x_{i+1}-x_i$.
\item On each input cell, a chart has a fixed ordered output-label tuple and at most two additional natural evolution parameters $\mathbf z$. Its remaining domain constraints are rational-affine equalities and inequalities in $(\mathbf x,\mathbf z)$. Its time $T(\mathbf x,\mathbf z)$ is a rational polynomial of total degree at most two jointly in all these variables. Every occupied coordinate $V_j(\mathbf x,\mathbf z)$ in the $G$ frame is affine. All outputs are integral on the domain.
\item For each fixed valid input $\mathbf x$, the disjoint union of the chart domains maps bijectively to the complete timed orbit
\[
 \{(t,G^t(c_{\mathbf a,\mathbf x})):t\in\NN\}.
\]
The bijection includes uniqueness of the chart and its natural parameters, not merely coverage by finitely many formulas.
\end{enumerate}
A literal integer-affine-domain version is obtained by adding at most $m-1\le3$ uniquely input-determined natural gap quotients, hence at most $m+1\le5$ natural chart parameters for nonempty input. The empty input has a one-clock vacuum chart.
\end{theorem}

The word \emph{uniform} is essential: the same finite family handles arbitrarily large input gaps. Source 18 by itself fixes the entire initial configuration and permits an input-dependent finite history to be materialized. That alone does not imply this theorem. Here all preprocessing depends only on the fixed rule, radius, weights and input-label case. No practical complexity or coefficient-size bound is claimed.

\wtag\ [The two imports are source~17's Lemmas~\ref{smc:fm:lem:safe}, \ref{smc:fm:lem:counter} and~\ref{smc:fm:lem:dispatch} with Proposition~\ref{smc:fm:prop:normal}, and source~18's Theorem~\ref{smc:tq:thm:main} with Lemma~\ref{smc:tq:lem:interface}. Source~18 is itself conditional on Proposition~\ref{smc:fm:prop:normal}, so Theorem~\ref{smc:ut:thm:uniform} rests on source~17 twice; source~17's proofs have been reviewed by the programme~\cite{reviewlowmass}, source~18's chart and compiler argument passed a scoped intake conditional on source~17's normal form (\path{review_timed_four_mass_source18_intake.md}, commit \texttt{39f398985})~\cite{reviewsourceeighteen}, and the intake of source~25~\cite{reviewnewsignals} does not certify either import. The theorem answers source~17's Question~\ref{smc:fm:q:uniform} and the uniform half of its Question~\ref{smc:fm:q:normalform} under these conditions, and the corresponding remarks in Section~\ref{smc:zd:sec:frontquestions}; source~18's statement that it gives no bound uniform over inputs remains true of source~18. With the uniform family the timed relation is still not Presburger: source~17's binary shuttle already excludes that for one fixed input (Proposition~\ref{smc:fm:prop:hits}).]

\begin{corollary}\label{smc:ut:cor:consequences}
Under the same assumptions, complete untimed reachability in the stationary frame is uniformly Presburger-definable in input and output coordinates. In the original frame, complete timed outputs have degree at most two. For each fixed input-label and output-label case, the uniform complete timed relation has an integer polynomial of degree at most four with exactly one natural witness tuple at a member and none otherwise, using canonical natural pairs for signed external coordinates.
\end{corollary}

The Presburger conclusion concerns \emph{untimed stationary-frame} outputs. The timed relation is not claimed Presburger, and Proposition~\ref{smc:ut:prop:obstruction} shows that original-frame untimed reachability can genuinely fail to be Presburger. The single-fold statement concerns natural witnesses and keeps time external; it is not a generic rational- or real-witness theorem. No theorem here covers several weight-one types, signed weights, an active zero-weight background, infinite support, higher dimensions, or nonuniform rules.

\section{Imported finite dynamics and the dependency boundary}\label{smc:ut:sec:imports}
The inert, pinned combined article \textup{[sources~16, 17 and~18 of this report, at blob \texttt{ec10c7a5}]} is included in the release. Its source numbering is internal to that article: source 16 is \emph{Three mass units with a single unit symbol}; source 17 is \emph{Four mass units and exact reachability}; source 18 is \emph{Canonical quartic certificates for timed four mass orbits}. The article's repository blob and exact content hash are recorded in Section~\ref{smc:ut:app:provenance}. The following are the imported dynamical ingredients, not newly claimed classifications.

\wtag\ [Restatement. This section restates source~16's Sections~\ref{smc:su:sec:frame}--\ref{smc:su:sec:orbits}, source~17's Sections~\ref{smc:fm:sec:packets}--\ref{smc:fm:sec:scattering} and source~18's chart interface, in places word for word; brackets name each counterpart. It is printed because it fixes the exact form in which source~25 uses them and adds two explicit bounds (the remark that the section mechanism applies at every current gap $D>N$, and the inequality after~\eqref{smc:ut:eq:flightcontact}); no novelty is claimed for it.]

\subsection{Independent components and the no split packet lemma}
Join occupied sites at distance at most $2S$. If distinct components are farther than $2S$ apart, no radius-$S$ read neighborhood sees both. Quiescence and finite propagation imply exact one-step independence; the separately evolved output supports are disjoint and their union is the actual successor.

Source 16 proves that a mass-two packet of diameter at most $2S$ never exceeds that diameter under $G$ \wtag\ [Lemma~\ref{smc:su:lem:invariant}]. The short argument also explains why a coarse finite-speed estimate would be insufficient. A single weight-two label has its next support within a width-$2S$ interval. For two units at $0,d$, $1\le d\le2S$, if $d>S$, each original site sees precisely its isolated-unit neighborhood. Both units remain, exhausting all mass. If $d\le S$, a new nonzero site must see both units: seeing zero or just one would give the vacuum or stationary-singleton output there. Every new site is in $[d-S,S]$, which also contains $0,d$ and has width at most $2S$. Induction proves the claim.

There are finitely many normalized mass-two shapes: the weight-two labels and two units with separation $1,\ldots,2S$. Each has a finite deterministic shape orbit and a computable finite-phase description
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:packet}
 G^{\mu+r+pk}(q)=\tau_{k\eta}q_r,\qquad
 0\le r<p,\quad k\in\NN,
\end{equation}
with fixed integers $\mu,p,\eta$ and explicitly known phase configurations. A bounded pair cannot emit one independent fragment and retain another across distinct $2S$ components. \wtag\ [This is~\eqref{smc:fm:eq:profile} of source~17's Lemma~\ref{smc:fm:lem:two}, and source~16's Lemma~\ref{smc:su:lem:walker}.]

Source 16 also supplies the finite mass-three core of diameter at most $4S$, its first-return computation and complete fixed-input profiles \wtag\ [Section~\ref{smc:su:sec:core} and Proposition~\ref{smc:su:prop:orbits}; source~17's Lemma~\ref{smc:fm:lem:three}]. A core return repeats a normalized configuration; determinism then repeats the \emph{whole} intervening orbit up to translation, rather than merely its section points. These data yield, for each connected mass-three seed, a fixed prefix followed by a compact translated-periodic configuration or by a stationary unit and an independently receding mass-two packet. Zero packet drift is absorbed into the compact case.

\subsection{The noncircular seed library and safety constants}
Let $\mathcal E$ be the finite family of normalized connected mass-three seeds, each of diameter at most $4S$. A seed may carry a finite analytical tag recording the target unit's coordinate at entry; this is not a physical label or extra memory in the automaton. For every seed select the complete finite prefix and eventual compact or emission outcome supplied above. Prolong an emission prefix until the nonzero-drift packet stays farther than $2S$ from its residual unit in every future phase.

Choose a single integer $B\ge4S$ bounding the absolute coordinates, relative to the seed's left edge, of every occupied site throughout every chosen prefix and every initial-period representative. Include each residual marker. Compact phase diameters and emitted head-to-marker offsets are then at most $2B$. Source 17 fixes
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:thresholds}
 N=4B+12S,\qquad W=N+2B.
\end{equation}
The seeds defining $B$ are the original span-$4S$ seeds. They are not all shapes of span $W$, and $B$ does not depend on the arbitrary gap being analyzed. This noncircular choice is part of the uniformity input. \wtag\ [Section~\ref{smc:fm:sec:library}; \eqref{smc:ut:eq:thresholds} is~\eqref{smc:fm:eq:thresholds}.]

A seed translated to left edge $a$, together with a fourth unit at $b$, is safely independent throughout its complete fixed prefix whenever $|b-a|>B+2S$. For an outside-$W$ connected-seed-plus-unit input, its seed diameter gives
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:safeseed}
 |b-a|>W-4S>B+2S.
\end{equation}
A compact outcome can then have a very long flight. Its first actual proximity to the fourth unit, if any, has total diameter at most $2B+2S<W$. It therefore either escapes independently or enters a bounded full encounter. It is never replaced by a purported constant-time scattering reaction. \wtag\ [Lemma~\ref{smc:fm:lem:safe} and the paragraph after it.]

\subsection{The large gap section interface}
An \emph{ordinary} mass-four state has complete diameter at most $W$. A \emph{live emission section} has two stationary units at $L<R$, gap $D=R-L>N$, and one bounded mass-two head at a prescribed finite-phase launch offset from one marker, drifting toward the other. Its finite control records the launch side, packet phase and type, and finite seed tags.

The geometric ordinary and live sets can overlap. At a designated emission checkpoint, use the live tag whenever $D>N$, even if the span is at most $W$. At other dispatch states apply the ordinary span test first. Once entered, a live step retains its tag through the next designated emission or explicit reset. Accordingly, \emph{first ordinary reset} below means the first ordinary dispatch under this convention, not the first incidental intermediate time of span at most $W$. \wtag\ [This is source~17's representation convention, Section~\ref{smc:fm:sec:scattering}.]

After adjoining a fixed gap residue to the control, a continuing live edge has fixed data
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:edge}
 D'=D+c_q,\qquad L'=L+e_q,\qquad h_q(D)=\alpha_qD+\beta_q,
\end{equation}
with $c_q,e_q\in\Z$, $\alpha_q>0$ rational, and an integer positive duration on its admissible residue. Every intermediate flight phase and local-prefix state is retained. The source construction applies at \emph{every current} gap $D>N$, not just beyond an unrecorded input-dependent threshold. \wtag\ [\eqref{smc:ut:eq:edge} is~\eqref{smc:fm:eq:counter} of Lemma~\ref{smc:fm:lem:counter}, whose ``sufficiently large gap'' is the bound $D>N$ of~\eqref{smc:fm:eq:thresholds}, as source~17 says there.]

Here are the source bounds behind that assertion. At contact with target marker $b$, the seed's left edge $a'$ satisfies $|a'-b|\le4S$. The other marker $p$ then obeys
\[
 |p-a'|\ge D-4S>N-4S>B+2S.
\]
The entire seed prefix is safe. The new residual marker moves from $b$ by at most $4S+B$, and $D>N>B+4S$ prevents marker order reversal. Thus both gap and anchor change by fixed additive constants.

For the flight, reflect if necessary so the packet drift $\eta>0$. Let its phase-$r$ left edge relative to the launch marker be $h_r+\eta k$ and its width be $d_r\le2S$. First proximity in that phase is exactly
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:flightcontact}
 D-2S-d_r\le h_r+\eta k\le D+2S.
\end{equation}
The hull test is exact here because a width-$2S$ mass-two support has no gap between the radius-$2S$ neighborhoods of its occupied sites. The launch bound $|h_r|\le2B$ gives
\[
 D-2S-d_r-h_r>N-4S-2B=2B+8S>0.
\]
No hidden negative period count or new transient occurs. On each $D\bmod\eta$, candidate counts are $D/\eta$ plus fixed offsets, and candidate times have the same leading coefficient $p/\eta$. Eligibility and the earliest phase depend only on this residue. Finite propagation prevents crossing the target without proximity. These facts give the finite control and affine duration in \eqref{smc:ut:eq:edge}. \wtag\ [\eqref{smc:ut:eq:flightcontact} is~\eqref{smc:fm:eq:contact}, with source~17's drift $d$ written $\eta$; the displayed lower bound makes explicit source~17's statement that $D>N$ ensures nonnegative candidate counts.]

The noncontinuing alternatives are retained: an outward head escapes independently; an inward emission with next gap at most $N$ has span at most $N+2B=W$; a compact outcome either escapes or reaches an ordinary configuration after its separately accelerated flight. The large-gap mechanism does not retain a second independent gap through a compact reset.

\subsection{Exactly what the fixed templates supply}
For \emph{each fixed} complete input, source 18 converts source 17's normal form into finitely many disjoint half-open charts, with at most two natural parameters, integer-affine domains, quadratic time, affine stationary-frame positions, and complete timed-orbit bijectivity \wtag\ [Lemma~\ref{smc:tq:lem:interface}, Section~\ref{smc:tq:sec:partition}]. It may explicitly materialize a large finite history depending on that fixed input. We use this only for the finitely many normalized ordinary shapes of span at most $W$, after the first ordinary reset. The new uniform deduction is initial symbolic dispatch plus symbolic live-cycle contraction and additive reset composition. Neither the fixed-input theorem alone nor a collection of separately computed input orbits would justify that deduction.

\section{A uniform first contact calculation}\label{smc:ut:sec:contact}
\begin{lemma}[First contact on finitely many input cells]\label{smc:ut:lem:contact}
Consider finitely many fixed finite-phase objects with anchors affine in the external input coordinates. Their independent counterfactual motion has a finite disjoint input partition on which either no monitored proximity ever occurs or the first proximity time and all occupied positions at that time are affine. Every earlier complete configuration has half-open affine charts using at most one natural evolution parameter. All residue divisors are fixed constants.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Take a common fixed transient $\mu$ and common phase period $P$. At elapsed time $\mu+r+Pk$, each occupied site has a form
\[
 a_v(\mathbf x)+b_{v,r}+d_{v,r}k,\qquad 0\le r<P,\quad k\in\NN,
\]
where the phase constants and drifts are fixed. For any monitored pair of occupied sites, proximity at most $2S$ is exactly
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:interval}
 -2S\le A(\mathbf x)+d k\le2S.
\end{equation}
A finite union over site pairs is necessary for compact shapes with holes. A hull-only test for an arbitrary compact mass-three phase is not valid.

If $d=0$, the earliest phase count is $k=0$ when $|A(\mathbf x)|\le2S$ and no candidate exists otherwise. If $d>0$, the earliest possible candidate is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:ceil}
 k_* = \max\left\{0,\left\lceil\frac{-2S-A(\mathbf x)}{d}\right\rceil\right\};
\end{equation}
it is retained only if the upper inequality in \eqref{smc:ut:eq:interval} holds there. For $d<0$, replace $(A,d)$ by $(-A,-d)$. Split the numerator modulo the positive fixed divisor, then split the maximum at zero. The resulting count and candidate time are affine, with affine eligibility tests. Each transient time is one further constant-time candidate with affine eligibility.

Among the finitely many eligible candidates, choose the least actual time, breaking ties by a fixed index. Comparisons between affine candidate times remain affine. This gives disjoint input cells, including a cell with no candidate. Ties select an arithmetic description only: the actual configuration retains \emph{all} simultaneous physical contacts.

The precontact chart in phase $r$ has guard
\[
 0\le\mu+r+Pk<h(\mathbf x),
\]
where $h$ is the selected first-contact elapsed time. In a no-contact cell omit the upper bound. The finite transient is handled separately. All guards and positions are affine. Before the first proximity, the objects are farther than $2S$ apart, so one-step independence holds. The preceding independent step therefore also gives the actual complete configuration \emph{at} first contact, with disjoint occupied sites. The next piece owns that endpoint; the precontact piece does not.

If entry time and anchors already depend affinely on $\mathbf x$, add the entry time and substitute the anchors. This does not change degree. Every ceiling divides by a fixed integer, never by a variable gap. Rational-affine integrality and congruence pullbacks are treated explicitly in Section~\ref{smc:ut:sec:quotients}.
\end{proof}

\wtag\ [For one fixed input this is the first-entry computation of source~16 (Lemma~\ref{smc:su:lem:first}, interval~\eqref{smc:su:eq:hit}) and of source~17 (Lemma~\ref{smc:fm:lem:safe}); the lemma makes it uniform in the input by the residue splitting of~\eqref{smc:ut:eq:ceil}. The warning against hull tests for compact shapes complements~\eqref{smc:fm:eq:contact}, where the hull test is exact because the moving object is a mass-two packet.]

\section{Uniform initial dispatch}\label{smc:ut:sec:dispatch}
Partition the initial coordinates by $2S$-component structure, labels and bounded internal gaps. A component of mass $b$ has at most $b$ occupied sites and diameter at most $2S(b-1)$. Its normalized shape therefore lies in a fixed finite list, chosen with affine equality and inequality tests.

At total mass four, the component mass partitions and their dispatch are exhaustive.
\begin{description}[style=nextline]
\item[$4$] The initial complete configuration has diameter at most $6S<W$ and is ordinary.
\item[$1+1+1+1$] All components are stationary units under $G$ and the complete configuration is fixed.
\item[$2+2$] Apply Lemma~\ref{smc:ut:lem:contact} to the two packet profiles. If no contact occurs, their synchronized motion is a terminal independent profile. At first contact, the two widths at most $2S$ and the contact distance at most $2S$ give complete span at most $6S<W$, hence an ordinary state.
\item[$3+1$] If already ordinary, dispatch there. Otherwise \eqref{smc:ut:eq:safeseed} ensures the seed's complete fixed prefix is independent of the fourth unit. An emission yields an independent outward tail or a live section, with the small-gap branch ordinary. A compact outcome is followed by Lemma~\ref{smc:ut:lem:contact} until escape or ordinary first contact. That flight can be arbitrarily long in the original input gap.
\item[$2+1+1$] Apply Lemma~\ref{smc:ut:lem:contact} to the packet and both units. A simultaneous contact connects all four masses, so its span is at most $6S$. A single contact yields a connected mass-three seed plus the remaining unit. This is either ordinary or safely distant and follows the $3+1$ case. Arithmetic tie-breaking must not discard the simultaneous-contact branch.
\end{description}

\wtag\ [These are the five mass partitions of source~17's Lemma~\ref{smc:fm:lem:dispatch}, now dispatched uniformly in the input coordinates.]

Every path has a bounded number of symbolic stages: at most one first packet contact, one fixed seed prefix, and one compact flight. This bound depends on the component cases, not on any initial gap. At a designated inward emission checkpoint apply the live-tag convention of Section~\ref{smc:ut:sec:imports}. Every necessary comparison involves affine positions. Consequently each initial cell ends in an independent terminal profile, an ordinary state, or a live section with entry time, anchor and gap affine in $\mathbf x$. All earlier times already have half-open affine-output charts with at most one evolution parameter.

An independent terminal profile uses a \emph{common} phase period and one common clock. Assigning a separate free clock to each object would describe configurations that never coexist. Once phases are synchronized, all object positions are affine in the same natural period count.

\subsection{Mass at most three}
With a unit symbol, source 16's finite normalized core of span at most $4S$ supplies the same construction. Before first core entry there are independent finite-phase packets and units. The first-contact or first-core-entry arithmetic is affine after residue refinement. Once a bounded core shape is selected, its full fixed template has affine time and positions. A repeated normalized core shape repeats the complete intervening orbit up to translation. Thus no four-mass shuttle or quadratic live-cycle clock is needed at these masses.

\wtag\ [At mass at most three, source~16's Theorem~\ref{smc:su:thm:main} already gives a uniform Presburger timed relation, which is stronger; this subsection only fits that case into the chart format.]

\subsection{The case without a unit symbol}
Every occupied site then has weight at least two, so at mass at most four there are at most two occupied sites. A separated two-site input must have weights $2+2$. An isolated weight-two site cannot split: its successor must be one weight-two site. Its label and bounded one-step displacement form a finite-state walker with eventual finite-phase motion. A weight-three singleton also cannot split; a weight-four singleton \emph{can} split, and is not silently treated as a walker.

Take all complete configurations of diameter at most $2S$, including singletons, as a finite normalized core. Outside it there are precisely two independent weight-two walkers. Lemma~\ref{smc:ut:lem:contact} describes their first proximity uniformly in the input gap. From each fixed core shape, take one exact step and compute the next core return or an independent escaping profile. Each return has a fixed positive elapsed time and translation increment. The finite deterministic graph of normalized core states either escapes or repeats. Repetition gives a complete translated-periodic template, including intermediate states. This handles possible weight-four splits and proves uniform affine charts without introducing fictitious unit markers. Vacuum has empty support and $t=z$, $z\in\NN$; padding $S\ge1$ handles radius zero without division by zero.

\section{Finite control and every live cycle endpoint}\label{smc:ut:sec:cycles}
Absorb $D$ modulo a common fixed modulus into live control $q$. Include all emission drifts, duration denominators and residues needed by compact-outcome contacts. The unguarded large-gap continuation map is now deterministic on a finite set. Its actual use is subject to $D>N$ at the current section and $D'>N$ for the next live section.

Follow control until a terminal branch, a failed small-gap guard or a repeated control. Before a repeat there are only finitely many edges. Their gap and anchor updates and accumulated times are affine in the entry data. A compact outcome uses the first-contact lemma and either escapes or resets. These are finite affine branches. If control repeats, the intervening cycle word is fixed. Because control includes residues, the net gap change is a multiple of the control modulus, so its residue itinerary repeats.

Let the cycle have $p$ edges indexed $i=0,\ldots,p-1$. Write the fixed gap and anchor increments as $\gamma_i,\varepsilon_i$, and put
\begin{align}
 c_0&=0,&c_s&=\sum_{i<s}\gamma_i,&c_p&=\Delta,\nonumber\\
 e_0&=0,&e_s&=\sum_{i<s}\varepsilon_i,&e_p&=E,\label{smc:ut:eq:offsets}\\
 b&=\min_{0\le s\le p}c_s.&&&&\nonumber
\end{align}
For cycle-entry gap $d$ and left marker $\ell$, edge $s$ in cycle $n$ starts with
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:sections}
 D_{n,s}=d+n\Delta+c_s,\qquad L_{n,s}=\ell+nE+e_s.
\end{equation}

\begin{lemma}[Complete endpoint guard]\label{smc:ut:lem:guard}
Cycle $n$ is completed live-to-live exactly when
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:guard}
 d+n\Delta+c_s>N\quad(0\le s\le p),
 \quad\text{equivalently}\quad d+n\Delta+b>N.
\end{equation}
This condition includes the final endpoint as well as every interior endpoint.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
At each live section, the fixed edge data apply whenever the current gap exceeds $N$. If the next endpoint also exceeds $N$, the designated inward emission remains live. Induction over the cycle therefore proves sufficiency. If any endpoint first fails, its arriving edge has been traversed, but its terminal launch is an ordinary reset. The cycle is then not completed live-to-live. This proves necessity and explains why its final endpoint cannot be omitted.
\end{proof}

If $\Delta\ge0$ and $d+b>N$, every later cycle is valid. If $d+b\le N$, the first cycle fails, and a finite affine split chooses its first failed endpoint. The case $\Delta=0$ is not replaced by an input-uniform fixed period: the physical period can be $A d+\beta$ and depends on the arbitrary entry gap. Its clock must retain the product $nd$.

\begin{lemma}[Exact symbolic contraction]\label{smc:ut:lem:contract}
Suppose $\Delta=-a<0$. The number of wholly completed live-to-live cycles before the failed cycle is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:K}
 K=\max\left\{0,\left\lceil\frac{d+b-N}{a}\right\rceil\right\}.
\end{equation}
On a finite sign and residue refinement of the input cells, $K$ is affine in $\mathbf x$. The first failed endpoint $s\in\{1,\ldots,p\}$ is uniquely selected by the affine guards
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:failure}
 d-Ka+c_r>N\quad(0\le r<s),\qquad d-Ka+c_s\le N.
\end{equation}
Its complete normalized launch shape belongs to a fixed finite ordinary family, and its anchor is affine in $\mathbf x$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
By \eqref{smc:ut:eq:guard}, cycle $n$ completes precisely when $an<d+b-N$. Counting the natural integers satisfying this strict inequality yields \eqref{smc:ut:eq:K}, including $K=0$ and exact divisibility. If $K>0$, the final-endpoint guard for cycle $K-1$ proves that cycle $K$ starts live. If $K=0$, that is the entry hypothesis. Some endpoint in the next cycle fails, so its first failure is indeed in $1,\ldots,p$. The edge arriving there is traversed under a live start, and the endpoint belongs to the reset rather than to a live successor.

For $v=d+b-N>0$, fix $v\equiv r\pmod a$, $0\le r<a$. Then
\[
 K=(v-r)/a+\mathbf1_{r>0};
\]
for $v\le0$, $K=0$. Every divisor is fixed, hence these are affine input formulas after the finite refinement. No new free reset-count witness is needed.

At failure, the preceding gap is an integer greater than $N$ and the last fixed decrement $\gamma_{s-1}$ crosses $N$. The endpoint gap is thus at least $N+1+\gamma_{s-1}$ and at most $N$; source 17 additionally preserves positive marker order. The launch span is at most $W$. Finitely many normalized shapes suffice, selected by affine equalities. By \eqref{smc:ut:eq:sections}, its anchor is $\ell+KE+e_s$, affine after substitution.
\end{proof}

\wtag\ [For one fixed input, source~17's Proposition~\ref{smc:fm:prop:normal} needs only the expanding case $\Delta>0$ of a repeated control, since a contracting cycle reaches an ordinary state after finitely many cycles; uniformly in the input that number $K$ is unbounded, and Lemma~\ref{smc:ut:lem:contract} computes it symbolically. Note that $b$ in~\eqref{smc:ut:eq:offsets} is the least partial gap change, not a coordinate as in Section~\ref{smc:ut:sec:imports}.]

\section{Quadratic clocks and all intermediate times}\label{smc:ut:sec:clocks}
Write the edge duration at gap $z$ as $h_i(z)=\alpha_i z+\beta_i$, and define
\begin{align}
 A&=\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}\alpha_i,&
 C&=\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}(\alpha_i c_i+\beta_i),\nonumber\\
 A_s&=\sum_{i<s}\alpha_i,&
 C_s&=\sum_{i<s}(\alpha_i c_i+\beta_i).\label{smc:ut:eq:clockconstants}
\end{align}
We use $C$ here so as not to confuse this cycle constant with the safety bound $B$. A full cycle entered at gap $z$ lasts $Az+C$. If its initial global time is $T_*$, the start time of edge $s$ in cycle $n$ is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:clock}
 S_s(n)=T_*+n(Ad+C)+\frac{A\Delta n(n-1)}2
                  +A_s(d+n\Delta)+C_s.
\end{equation}
Indeed the preceding cycles have durations $A(d+j\Delta)+C$, $0\le j<n$, and the preceding edges of cycle $n$ contribute the final two terms. Formula \eqref{smc:ut:eq:clock} also holds at $s=p$, the endpoint of a whole word.

\wtag\ [At $s=0$ this is source~17's section clock~\eqref{smc:fm:eq:time}, $T_n=T_0+A'\frac{n(n-1)}2+C'n$, with $A'=A\Delta$ and $C'=Ad+C$: the letters $A$ and $C$ differ between the two sources. Here the entry gap $d$ is an affine function of the input, which produces the bilinear term $nd$.]

Initial dispatch and the finite control preperiod make $T_*,d,\ell$ affine in the input coordinates on each cell. Hence \eqref{smc:ut:eq:clock} has joint total degree at most two in $(\mathbf x,n)$. Its non-affine terms are $nd$ and $n(n-1)$; no coefficient depending on $\mathbf x$ multiplies $n^2$. In particular $\Delta=0$ retains the generally bilinear term $nAd$.

\subsection{Flight and local prefix charts}
At edge $s$, let the packet period be $P_s$ and the affine flight duration be $f_s(z)$, with any fixed edge offsets absorbed. For each phase $0\le r<P_s$, use $n,j\in\NN$ and
\begin{align}
 t&=S_s(n)+r+P_sj,\label{smc:ut:eq:flightchart}\\
 0&\le r+P_sj<f_s(d+n\Delta).\nonumber
\end{align}
Every occupied stationary-frame coordinate is affine in $(\mathbf x,n,j)$. Fixed scattering-prefix phase $v$ has time
\[
 t=S_s(n)+f_s(d+n\Delta)+v
\]
and affine positions in $(\mathbf x,n)$. A finite refinement fixes labels and phase choices. The flight and prefix own consecutive half-open intervals; the endpoint launch belongs to the next piece. The two natural parameters have distinct meanings: cycle number and within-flight period quotient.

For complete contracting cycles impose $0\le n<K(\mathbf x)$. This is an affine guard after the residue refinement. In the final partial cycle substitute $n=K(\mathbf x)$, select $s$ by \eqref{smc:ut:eq:failure}, and retain every edge before its first failed endpoint, including the entire arriving edge strictly before its endpoint. At most $j$ remains free on these charts. Substitution of an affine $K$ into a quadratic time preserves total degree two; coordinates stay affine.

For a failing first nonnegative cycle use $n=0$. For a valid nonnegative cycle let $n$ be unbounded. A noncontinuing terminal or compact branch occurs in the finite control preperiod; a repeated deterministic continuing control cannot later acquire a new outcome except through a failed gap guard.

The reset timestamp at endpoint $s$ is $S_s(K)$, a quadratic input function. One must \emph{not} put a nonlinear guard $t<Q(\mathbf x)$ into a chart domain. Chronology is enforced by the affine cycle bounds and affine within-phase bounds above; time is a quadratic \emph{output}. Positive actual edge durations and Euclidean division inside each packet period then give unique ownership of every pre-reset time.

\subsection{Sorting and labels}
The finitely many indexed occupied sites may change spatial order between phases or input cells. Refine a chart by each candidate permutation $\pi$, adding
\[
 V_{\pi(j+1)}-V_{\pi(j)}-1\ge0.
\]
Stationary-frame differences are affine, so these are affine constraints after denominator clearing. Actual occupied sites are distinct, and exactly one strict permutation passes. Labels follow their sites; repeated labels do not create additional accepted orders. The same ordering applies in the original frame because the common shift $\delta t$ cancels in every difference.

\wtag\ [For one fixed input the flight charts and the sorting refinement are source~18's (\eqref{smc:tq:eq:flight} and~\eqref{smc:tq:eq:sorting}); here the cycle number and the within-flight quotient keep their meaning, and the input enters affinely.]

\section{The first ordinary reset removes unbounded geometry}\label{smc:ut:sec:reset}
\begin{proposition}[Additive template composition]\label{smc:ut:prop:reset}
Suppose a disjoint input cell reaches its first ordinary state, under the designated live-tag convention, at time $Q(\mathbf x)$ with left anchor $a(\mathbf x)$. Refine it to fix the normalized complete shape $o$. If $Q$ is quadratic and $a$ affine, then its entire suffix has charts of the form
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:composition}
 t=Q(\mathbf x)+t_o(\mathbf z),\qquad
 V_j=a(\mathbf x)+v_{o,j}(\mathbf z),
\end{equation}
with at most two natural evolution parameters, affine domains, quadratic time, and affine stationary-frame positions.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
There are finitely many normalized complete configurations of mass at most four and diameter at most $W$. Precompute the source-18 fixed-input chart family for each such $o$, in the stationary-frame rule $G$. Translation equivariance and determinism say that the suffix from the actual reset is exactly the translate by $a(\mathbf x)$ of the orbit from $o$, with time shifted by $Q(\mathbf x)$. This gives \eqref{smc:ut:eq:composition}.

This operation adds two quadratic expressions; it does not insert the quadratic arrival time as a variable argument of another quadratic clock. The template domain depends only on its own evolution parameters; combine it with the affine input cell. The normalized shape has erased every unbounded relative geometric coordinate. Only the affine anchor and quadratic elapsed time survive. No cycle-count parameter from the initial contraction persists as an independent witness.

The fixed template may contain a huge explicitly materialized prefix. Its size depends on $G$ and one of finitely many bounded shapes, not on the arbitrary original gaps. Thus this finite preprocessing is compatible with input uniformity. The reset time itself belongs to the template at relative time zero, and all pre-reset charts exclude it.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{smc:ut:thm:uniform}, except for the quotient syntax]
Initial dispatch covers every possible component case and all intervening times. It reaches a terminal independent profile, a bounded ordinary state, or a live section. The finite-control preperiod and cycle construction cover every live excursion until its first reset, or forever if it remains live. Compact exits use the first-contact construction, so they leave no unaccounted long flight. A first ordinary reset invokes Proposition~\ref{smc:ut:prop:reset}, which covers the entire remaining orbit without symbolically concatenating later input-dependent excursions.

Every branch choice is a finite affine or fixed-residue refinement. Earliest-contact tie-breaking, the first failed endpoint, half-open stage boundaries, cycle counts, synchronized phases and Euclidean within-flight quotients give exactly one description per physical time for each fixed input. Sorting preserves uniqueness. Small masses and the no-unit case were handled in Section~\ref{smc:ut:sec:dispatch}. The family is finite because the rule, phase libraries, controls, cycles and ordinary shapes are finite. The only unbounded free evolution coordinates used are the cycle number and within-flight quotient, or the at-most-two parameters of a fixed suffix template. Formulae \eqref{smc:ut:eq:clock} and \eqref{smc:ut:eq:composition} give the asserted degree bounds.

The bijection is \emph{fiberwise in the input}. Forgetting the input itself need not leave an injective parametrization: a noninjective rule can merge different initial configurations. This is not an additional global injectivity claim.
\end{proof}

\section{Input residues and the honest parameter ledger}\label{smc:ut:sec:quotients}
All residue tests arise from relative coordinates; a common translation of the input leaves them unchanged. An integral affine combination of input positions invariant under such translations can be rewritten as an affine combination of the gaps $\mathbf g=(g_1,\ldots,g_{m-1})$.

One must pull rational-affine residues back \emph{before} choosing the final modulus. If $(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf g+c)/d$ is integer-valued on the current cell, with $d>0$, its residue $\rho\bmod M$ is equivalent there to
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:pullback}
 \mathbf a\cdot\mathbf g+c\equiv d\rho\pmod{dM}.
\end{equation}
The modulus is $dM$, not merely $\operatorname{lcm}(d,M)$. For example, the parity of $D/2$ requires $D\bmod4$ on even $D$; $D\bmod2$ cannot distinguish $D=2$ from $D=4$.

Only finitely many branches, fixed divisors, cycles, normalized resets and fixed templates occur. Therefore finitely many integer-affine input congruences suffice. Choose a common positive multiple $H$ of their pulled-back moduli. For every gap residue vector $0\le r_i<H$, introduce the equations
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:quotientlift}
 x_{i+1}-x_i=Hu_i+r_i,\qquad u_i\in\NN,\quad 1\le i<m.
\end{equation}
Since $g_i\ge1$, these quotients are natural; if $r_i=0$, ordered input forces $u_i\ge1$. Each input has exactly one residue vector and exactly one quotient vector. After these substitutions and positive denominator clearing, every remaining domain constraint is integer-affine. This completes the syntax part of Theorem~\ref{smc:ut:thm:uniform}.

\begin{table}[ht]
\centering\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{p{0.47\linewidth}cc}
\toprule
Quantity for one nonempty-input chart & Bound & Role\\\midrule
Free evolution parameters & $2$ & Cycle and phase, or template\\
Canonical initial-gap quotients & $m-1\le3$ & Unique from input\\
Total natural affine-chart parameters & $m+1\le5$ & Sum of the preceding rows\\
Private signed-input copies for quartic & $2m\le8$ & Selected chart only\\

\end{table}

Dropping the time output leaves a finite union of affine-domain affine-output relations, with fixed congruences or their canonical affine lifts. Existential projection over natural parameters is Presburger-definable. This gives the first assertion of Corollary~\ref{smc:ut:cor:consequences}; the classical connection with effective semilinearity is due to Ginsburg and Spanier~\cite{ginsburgspanier}. Fixed finite-pattern tests, including required zeros, and translation queries can also be formed within Presburger arithmetic from these complete stationary-frame configurations. The argument does not make a quadratic time graph Presburger, and forgetting time can destroy the timed chart's single-fold property.

Finally, original-frame coordinates are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:original}
 Y_j=V_j+\delta T.
\end{equation}
They have total degree at most two. This is sufficient for the quartic compiler below, but is not an untimed original-frame Presburger deduction.

\subsection{A genuine original frame obstruction}\label{smc:ut:sec:obstruction}
The frame restriction is substantive. The following direct corollary uses the already audited reversible clock of Report 49 \textup{[source~24, Proposition~\ref{smc:rt:prop:orbit}]}; it does not depend on the conditional uniform-chart imports.

\begin{proposition}[Non Presburger absolute untimed reachability]\label{smc:ut:prop:obstruction}
There is a globally reversible conservative binary CA $F$, with $F$ and $F^{-1}$ of radius at most $91$, whose forward untimed set of complete outputs from the single fixed input $\{0,5,6,13\}$ is not Presburger-definable in its four sorted absolute occupied coordinates. Its stationary-singleton frame has a Presburger-definable untimed orbit from that input.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Call the radius-at-most-$90$ clock in Report 49 $G$ (that report calls it $F$). For $D\ge13$, put $C_D=\{0,5,6,D\}$ and $L_D=2D-22$. The report's complete-orbit proposition gives
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:priorclock}
 G^s(C_D)=
 \begin{cases}
 \{0,5+s,6+s,D\},&0\le s\le D-11,\\
 \{0,2D-18-s,2D-14-s,D+1\},&D-10\le s\le2D-23,
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
and $G^{L_D}(C_D)=C_{D+1}$. \wtag\ [\eqref{smc:ut:eq:priorclock} is~\eqref{smc:rt:eq:phases}, repeated with source~24's $F$ written $G$.] The displayed coordinates are strictly increasing in each range and their minimum is always zero. An isolated singleton is fixed, since every literal rule endpoint requires at least two particles.

Set $F=\tau_1\circ G$. Translation commutes with $G$, so $F^t=\tau_t\circ G^t$ and $F^{-1}=G^{-1}\circ\tau_{-1}$. Both maps have radius at most $91$, preserve particle number and are inverse on the full shift. The singleton drift of $F$ is $1$, so its stationary frame is precisely $G$.

From $C_{13}$, cycle $k$ starts at $t_k=k^2+3k$ and has gap $D=13+k$. Let $\mathcal R_F\subseteq\Z^4$ be the complete forward untimed output set, in sorted coordinates. Its minimum coordinate at physical time $t$ is $t$. Intersect $\mathcal R_F$ with the affine slice
\[
 y_2-y_1=5,\qquad y_3-y_1=6.
\]
The right phase of \eqref{smc:ut:eq:priorclock} meets this slice exactly at $s=0$. The left phase has middle-pair separation four and cannot meet a slice requiring separation one. The full phase bounds and sorting exclude spectator substitutions, including at the smallest gap $D=13$. Thus the exact intersection is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:obstructionslice}
 \{(t_k,t_k+5,t_k+6,t_k+13+k):k\in\NN\}.
\end{equation}
If $\mathcal R_F$ were Presburger, intersection with this slice and projection onto $y_1$ would make $\{k^2+3k:k\in\NN\}$ Presburger. A unary Presburger subset of $\NN$ is eventually periodic~\cite{ginsburgspanier}. Here successive gaps $2k+4$ tend to infinity: an eventual period $P\ge1$ would put $t_k+P$ strictly between consecutive terms for sufficiently large $k$, a contradiction.

By contrast the complete stationary-frame untimed orbit is explicitly
\begin{align*}
 \mathcal R_G={}&\{(0,p,p+1,D):D\ge13,\ 5\le p\le D-6\}\\
 &\quad\cup\{(0,q,q+4,E):E\ge14,\ 5\le q\le E-9\}.
\end{align*}
These are precisely the two phase ranges with $D=13+k$, and their union is Presburger. This proves both claims.
\end{proof}

Report 49's \textup{[source~24's]} inherited binary theorem also proves that complete original-frame timed evolution is Presburger for every fixed input of at most three particles \wtag\ [Theorem~\ref{smc:rt:thm:three}; for weighted single-unit rules, source~16's Theorem~\ref{smc:su:thm:main}]. Projecting away time preserves Presburger definability. Thus four is the least particle count for failure of fixed-input original-frame untimed reachability in the binary conservative model, including its globally reversible subclass. This sharpness deduction uses that explicitly credited lower-bound theorem in addition to the clock orbit.

The failure already holds for one fixed anchored input, so a uniform original-frame untimed relation cannot always be Presburger either: specializing its input coordinates would give $\mathcal R_F$. These statements concern forward time and absolute coordinates. Quotienting outputs by arbitrary translation removes this particular obstruction. The remaining classification question is which additional rules or drift conditions preserve original-frame untimed regularity.

\wtag\ [Relation to Part~VII, which source~25 does not cite. Source~20's Theorem~\ref{smc:og:thm:drift} states that a nonzero drift can destroy semilinearity in the original frame, and its explicit weighted radius-six planar automata have original-frame visited site sets that are not semilinear (Proposition~\ref{smc:og:prop:nonsemilinear}, Theorem~\ref{smc:og:thm:exactdrift}); source~21 realizes the planar drift regime by a binary rule. A non-Presburger original-frame phenomenon of a fixed four-mass input was therefore known in this report in dimension two. Proposition~\ref{smc:ut:prop:obstruction} differs in three respects: it is one-dimensional, its rule is binary and globally reversible, and the non-Presburger set is the set of complete outputs (a relation in $\Z^4$), not a set of visited sites. Its argument, a drift of one site per step added to a clock whose stationary orbit is Presburger, is the one-dimensional, reversible instance of the mechanism of Theorem~\ref{smc:og:thm:drift}. In one dimension the obstruction is also close to source~17's remark (Question~\ref{smc:fm:q:normalform}) that ``the binary shuttle rules out Presburger arithmetic'' for original-frame timed relations; the new point is that it survives forgetting the time.]

\section{A selector safe uniform quartic}\label{smc:ut:sec:quartic}
We now give the complete algebraic construction. This is a uniform adaptation of source 18's fixed-input compiler, not the unmodified use of that compiler on external-variable coefficients.

\wtag\ [Source~18's compiler is Section~\ref{smc:tq:sec:compiler} with Proposition~\ref{smc:tq:prop:compiler}: selectors, constant lifting~\eqref{smc:tq:eq:lift}, pooled output denominators and natural slacks, and its signed external pairs are Section~\ref{smc:tq:sec:signed}. It was already noted as a second route to Part~I's Theorem~\ref{smc:cg:thm:quarticunion} (Section~\ref{smc:zd:sec:relation}). The new ingredient here is the private copy of the external input~\eqref{smc:ut:eq:copies}, gated with the other private variables, which keeps the degree at four when chart formulas are quadratic in the input.]

Fix an ordered output-label tuple $\mathbf b=(b_1,\ldots,b_\ell)$. Keep only the charts with that tuple and use original-frame outputs \eqref{smc:ut:eq:original}, or stationary-frame outputs if that is the desired relation. There are $J$ retained charts. If $J=0$, the constant polynomial $1$ with no witnesses represents the empty relation. Assume $J\ge1$ and nonempty input for the following ledger; vacuum is treated by its one-clock chart.

\subsection{Canonical external coordinates and private input copies}
Encode each signed external input coordinate uniquely as
\[
 x_i=x_i^+-x_i^-,\qquad x_i^+,x_i^-\in\NN,\qquad x_i^+x_i^-=0.
\]
Use the same canonical convention for external output coordinates $y_j=y_j^+-y_j^-$. Time $t$ remains a natural external variable. These are external encodings, not freely chosen difference-pair witnesses.

For each chart $h$, introduce a natural selector $e_h$, private natural copies $X_{hi}^+,X_{hi}^-$, its natural gap quotients $\mathbf u_h$, its $k_h\le2$ natural evolution coordinates $\mathbf z_h$, and later one natural slack per inequality. The copy residuals are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:copies}
 R_{hi}^{\pm}=X_{hi}^{\pm}-e_hx_i^{\pm}.
\end{equation}
They are quadratic in all variables. Replace every occurrence of $x_i$ within chart $h$ by $X_{hi}^+-X_{hi}^-$. Denote its private vector before slacks by $v_h=(X_h^+,X_h^-,\mathbf u_h,\mathbf z_h)$. Now its domain forms $A_{hr}(v_h)\ge0$, $H_{hs}(v_h)=0$ are affine and its time/coordinate outputs $P_{hq}(v_h)$ are quadratic polynomials with genuinely numerical coefficients.

Clear the positive denominator of each domain form \emph{before} introducing a natural slack. An inequality such as $(n-1)/2\ge0$ requires the integral form $n-1\ge0$, not a natural slack equated to a potentially half-integral left-hand side. Include the quotient equations \eqref{smc:ut:eq:quotientlift}, input order tests and all chart guards among the domain forms. The private quotient variables are determined by the selected external input, not free additional choices at a polynomial zero.

\subsection{Constant lifting, gates and pooled outputs}
For a polynomial in the private variables of chart $h$, define
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:lift}
 \Lift_h f=f(v_h)-f(0)+e_h f(0).
\end{equation}
Only the numerical constant is multiplied by the selector. With $E=\sum_h e_h$, introduce natural slacks $s_{hr}$ and set
\begin{align}
 R_0&=E-1,\nonumber\\
 R_{hr}^{\ge}&=\Lift_h A_{hr}-s_{hr},&
 R_{hs}^{=}&=\Lift_h H_{hs},\label{smc:ut:eq:domainres}\\
 Z_h&=\sum_i(X_{hi}^++X_{hi}^-)+\sum_i u_{hi}
                  +\sum_j z_{hj}+\sum_r s_{hr},\nonumber\\
 R_h^{\mathrm{off}}&=(1-e_h)Z_h.\label{smc:ut:eq:gate}
\end{align}
Let $Y_0=t$ and $Y_q=y_q^+-y_q^-$ for $1\le q\le\ell$. Choose one positive common denominator $L_q$ for the \emph{pooled} rational output expression in coordinate $q$, and set
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:outputs}
 R_q^{\mathrm{out}}=L_q\left(Y_q-\sum_{h=1}^J\Lift_hP_{hq}\right),
 \qquad 0\le q\le\ell.
\end{equation}
Clearing each chart separately and then summing the separately rescaled values would change the relation. For outputs $z_1/2$ and $z_2/3$, the pooled equation is $6Y-3z_1-2z_2=0$, not $Y-z_1-z_2=0$.

Define the integer polynomial
\begin{align}\label{smc:ut:eq:quartic}
 \mathcal C={}&R_0^2+\sum_{h,i,\pm}(R_{hi}^{\pm})^2
       +\sum_{h,r}(R_{hr}^{\ge})^2+\sum_{h,s}(R_{hs}^{=})^2\nonumber\\
       &+\sum_{q=0}^{\ell}(R_q^{\mathrm{out}})^2
       +\sum_h(R_h^{\mathrm{off}})^2.
\end{align}
Every residual has total degree at most two; hence $\deg\mathcal C\le4$. It is a literal sum of squares, globally nonnegative on real values, although its exactness assertion below concerns natural witnesses only.

\begin{proposition}[Empty or singleton natural fibers]\label{smc:ut:prop:quartic}
For valid canonical external input and output pairs, the natural zero fiber of \eqref{smc:ut:eq:quartic} is in bijection with the chart points mapping from that external input to that complete timed output. It is therefore empty or a singleton, and is a singleton exactly for the desired uniform timed relation.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
At a zero every squared residual vanishes. $R_0=0$ and natural selectors imply that exactly one selector is $1$ and the others are $0$, without extra Boolean equations. On an inactive chart, \eqref{smc:ut:eq:gate} gives $Z_h=0$. Since every summand is natural, all its private copies, quotients, evolution parameters and slacks vanish individually. Its lifted domain and output forms consequently vanish.

On the active chart, \eqref{smc:ut:eq:copies} sets the private copies equal to the fixed canonical external coordinates. Constant lifting returns the original forms. The surviving domain equations say exactly $A_{hr}=s_{hr}\ge0$ and $H_{hs}=0$, and the pooled outputs say $Y_q=P_{hq}$. The quotient equations determine their unique natural values. By Theorem~\ref{smc:ut:thm:uniform}, there is exactly one admissible selected chart point if the complete timed output is reached, and none otherwise. Each active slack is the uniquely determined integer $A_{hr}$.

Conversely, a chart point fixes its selector, copies, quotients, evolution parameters and slacks uniquely; set all other private coordinates to zero. This is a zero of \eqref{smc:ut:eq:quartic}, and the two constructions are inverse. Naturality is indispensable: signed private coordinates could cancel in $Z_h$, and arbitrary signed difference-pair witnesses would admit multiple representations.
\end{proof}

If noncanonical external natural pairs must be rejected rather than excluded by the interface, append the squared quadratic residuals
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:canonical}
 (x_i^+x_i^-)^2\quad(1\le i\le m),\qquad
 (y_j^+y_j^-)^2\quad(1\le j\le\ell).
\end{equation}
They add no witnesses and preserve degree four. Invalid ordering or incompatible labels is rejected by the retained chart guards or by the empty family. Finitely many label cases may alternatively be combined using a tagged, padded external encoding; we make no optimized arity claim for that optional packaging.

\subsection{Why private copies are necessary}
Source 18's constant lift is degree-safe when the entire input is fixed. Applying it directly to $f(\mathbf x,\mathbf z)$ can fail: $f(\mathbf x,0)$ may be quadratic in the external input. The naive term $e_hx^2$ has degree three, and its squared output residual can have degree six. Private copies convert such a term to $X_h^2$; the copying equation $X_h-e_hx$ has degree two, so its square has degree four. Including the copies in the inactive gate makes this repair exact rather than merely degree-preserving.

For a concrete two-chart arithmetic fixture, let $x\in\NN$ be external and take the private natural vector
\[
 (e_0,e_1,X_0,X_1,u_0,u_1,n_0,n_1)\in\NN^8.
\]
Use the residuals
\begin{align*}
 &e_0+e_1-1,\quad X_0-e_0x,\quad X_1-e_1x,\\
 &X_0-2u_0,\quad X_1-2u_1-e_1,\\
 &(1-e_0)(X_0+u_0+n_0),\quad (1-e_1)(X_1+u_1+n_1),\\
 &t-(X_0^2+X_0n_0+n_0^2+X_1^2+X_1n_1+n_1^2+e_1),\\
 &v-(X_0+n_0+X_1-n_1).
\end{align*}
The charts select even or odd input with a unique parity quotient and use a genuinely quadratic external-input term after copying. Their sum of squares has total degree four. The naive alternative $[t-(xn+n^2+ex^2)]^2$ has total degree six. This fixture checks the algebraic architecture only; it is not claimed to be the orbit chart of a particular cellular automaton.

\subsection{The full witness and residual ledger}
Let $I$ be the total number of inequalities and $H_0$ the total number of equalities across retained charts, after denominator clearing. Equalities include all quotient equations. The number of natural witnesses is exactly
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:witnessledger}
\begin{split}
 W_{\rm nat}&=J+\sum_{h=1}^J\bigl(2m+(m-1)+k_h\bigr)+I\\
             &=3mJ+\sum_hk_h+I\le(3m+2)J+I.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Here the first $J$ are selectors. Each nonempty-input chart has at most $3m+1\le13$ private variables before selector and slacks. The displayed sum-of-squares construction has
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ut:eq:residualledger}
 1+2mJ+I+H_0+(\ell+1)+J
\end{equation}
squared residual slots, with a further $m+\ell$ if \eqref{smc:ut:eq:canonical} is included. Zero or redundant residuals may be removed, but these are the explicit unoptimized counts. The total is fixed for the rule and label cases, independent of input gap sizes and requested time. It need not be small. This completes Corollary~\ref{smc:ut:cor:consequences}.

\wtag\ [The programme's intake confirms the reading of this ledger: ``$\le2$ evolution parameters is not $\le2$ total Diophantine witnesses; a per-chart pre-slack bound is $3m+1\le13$'', and there is no ``optimized numerical gate ledger''~\cite{reviewnewsignals}. The quartic is for one fixed rule and one pair of label cases, so the project's universal operation bounds~\cite{repo} are untouched.]

\section{Adversarial boundaries and verification}\label{smc:ut:sec:verification}
The frozen proof note received a scoped structural PASS; a separate adversarial audit then examined the imported source arguments, uniform initial dispatch, every cycle endpoint, template composition, congruence pullback and the copied-input compiler \textup{[\path{25-uniform-frozen-science-PROOF-NOTE.md} with \path{25-uniform-frozen-science-REVIEW.md}; \path{25-uniform-frozen-audit-AUDIT.md}]}. Both conclusions are conditional on the stated pinned dynamics and fixed-template theorem. Mathematical proofs carry the unrestricted claims; finite computations validate explicit arithmetic fixtures.

\subsection{Failures of tempting shortcuts}
The following examples were retained as negative controls.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Omitting the final endpoint.} With $N=10$, initial gap $12$ and cycle word $(-3)$, the start is live but the endpoint gap is $9$. A start-only check wrongly accepts a whole live-to-live cycle.
\item \textbf{Checking only start and finish.} With $N=10$, initial gap $13$ and increments $(-5,+6)$, the start and final gap $14$ are live and net drift is positive, but the interior gap is $8$. Positive net drift alone does not give an infinite live cycle.
\item \textbf{Replacing a strict count by the wrong rounding.} Completed cycles satisfy $an<v$. If $v>0$ is a multiple of $a$, $\lfloor v/a\rfloor+1$ overcounts; the correct count is $\lceil v/a\rceil$.
\item \textbf{A hull test for arbitrary compact shapes.} For support $\{0,20,21\}$, probe $10$ and proximity radius $2$, the probe is inside the expanded hull but is farther than $2$ from every occupied site. The general first-contact calculation must use occupied-site pairs.
\item \textbf{An insufficient congruence modulus.} On even $D$, knowing $D\bmod2$ does not determine whether $D/2$ is even. Pulling back a modulus through a denominator requires the product in \eqref{smc:ut:eq:pullback}.
\item \textbf{Uncopied external quadratic terms.} The naive selector-times-$x^2$ lift creates an actual sextic squared residual. Copying inputs, and gating all copies, is necessary for this quartic architecture.
\item \textbf{A false fixed period at zero gap drift.} $\Delta=0$ does not remove the input dependence from $n(Ad+C)$. Deleting $nd$ destroys uniform timing even though section geometry has constant gap.
\end{enumerate}
These refute weakened arguments, not the stated theorem. The arithmetic section examples do not assert realizability of every abstract increment word by a CA.

\subsection{Fresh arithmetic checks and their limits}
The frozen candidate checker uses only Python's standard library, exact integers and rational arithmetic. It recorded:
\begin{itemize}
\item 26,733 first-contact interval cases, including zero and signed drift
\item 69,800 direct contracting-cycle comparisons across 1,396 words
\item 105 large-integer contraction cases with gaps through $10^{100}$
\item 1,538 nonnegative-cycle guard cases and 225 directional degree checks
\end{itemize}
The separate audit checker uses Python and SymPy. Its direct section oracle advances one edge and every elapsed time; the independently constructed charts use the closed clock and accelerated reset formula. It recorded:
\begin{itemize}
\item 7,020 abstract section/input cases and 7,353,761 timed phase descriptions, with no missing or duplicate time
\item 3,242 bounded-reset cases, including additive composition with a fixed prefix and periodic reset template
\item 2,196 synchronized first-contact cases with multiple phases, multiple site pairs, and signed or zero drift
\item 703,125 natural witness tuples in finite boxes for the copied-input two-chart quartic, plus symbolic degrees four and six for the repaired and naive constructions
\item 10,374 denominator-inside-congruence comparisons and explicit rejection of incomplete endpoint, hull and modulus variants
\end{itemize}
The independent manuscript review also checked the explicit signed-input copying, quotient and residual ledgers with separate algebra fixtures. A separate literal-row check of the Report 49 consequence compared 10,301 complete states through 100 cycles, ending at time 10,300, and found exactly the 101 predicted section hits. It imports no clock implementation; the all-time obstruction follows from the proof above.

The witness boxes test their finite ranges only; they do not prove all-natural-fiber uniqueness. The section words are abstract arithmetic fixtures, not a generated library of CA rules. Neither checker implements the general rule-to-chart construction. These limits are recorded in the frozen receipts and retained in the release.

\subsection{An isolated reproducibility packet}
The release contains the editable TeX, rendered PDF, byte-preserved frozen proof and audit packets, the pinned inherited article as inert text, and new release helpers. The replay helper verifies all frozen hashes, copies only the inspected fresh arithmetic checkers into new scratch directories, runs them with Python assertions enabled, and compares their deterministic receipts exactly. It does not execute the inherited article, upstream programs, saved schedules, or any general CA compiler. All checker output is directed to the copied scratch files, leaving frozen evidence unchanged.

The PDF helper copies only this manuscript into a new external build directory, uses installed TeX with shell escape disabled, and fixes the source date and PDF metadata for deterministic rebuilding. The archive helper uses a fixed member order, timestamps and permissions. The release manifest verifies content correspondence; hashes are not digital signatures or third-party certification. Exact commands, prerequisites and path-safety rules appear in the release README. Mathematical audit scope and release integrity are distinct checks.

\section{Relation to earlier work and further questions}\label{smc:ut:sec:questions}
The source dependency is deliberately narrower than a claim that this report independently establishes a new low-mass CA classification. Source 16 already supplies uniform timed Presburger behavior through mass three. Source 17 supplies four-mass decidability and its finite-control, single-gap scattering construction. Source 18 already supplies complete fixed-input quadratic charts and their natural-single-fold quartic compiler. The additional deduction here is one uniform family across arbitrary initial positions, with the exact residue and quotient syntax, first-reset argument and copied-input repair made explicit.

The inherited source credits Kong's 2021 thesis for a binary three-particle nonuniversality precursor~\cite{kongthesis}. This is historical context, not an attribution of the present weighted uniform theorem to that thesis. The fresh university PDF retrieval for this report was rate-limited; the detailed precursor attribution follows the inspected pinned source and scope note. Morita's primary 2012 construction gives a universal 96-state four-neighbor reversible number-conserving CA by a multistate simulation~\cite{morita2012}; it does not settle this fixed-four-mass unique-unit-label timing statement. No priority conclusion follows from the literature comparison or from a failed search for a matching theorem.

Meaningful remaining questions include the following.
\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{smc:ix:ut:q:conditional} \textbf{Remove the conditional packaging.} Can the entire finite-library construction, source-18 template theorem and present uniform deduction be joined into one independently formalized result, with the live-tag convention and all intermediate-time ownership represented explicitly?
\item\label{smc:ix:ut:q:implement} \textbf{Implement the effective construction.} A rule-to-chart implementation would need to enumerate actual seeds, produce validated period and contact data, track congruence pullbacks, emit guarded cycle charts and verify fixed templates. Arithmetic fixture checkers do not perform these tasks. What certificate interface makes such preprocessing independently checkable without trusting the generator? (\wtag\ The same gap is source~17's Question~\ref{smc:fm:q:complexity}, source~18's further directions (Section~\ref{smc:tq:sec:checks}) and source~19's Question~\ref{smc:zd:q:compiler}.)
\item\label{smc:ix:ut:q:optimize} \textbf{Optimize auxiliary variables and modulus size.} The at-most-three input quotient cost is transparent but not proved minimal. Can literal raw-coordinate affine domains use fewer total natural auxiliaries for this class? Which geometric or arithmetic restrictions allow a smaller common modulus or copied-input ledger?
\item\label{smc:ix:ut:q:frame} \textbf{Characterize original frame regularity.} Proposition~\ref{smc:ut:prop:obstruction} settles the existence of a genuine non-Presburger obstruction, already for a reversible binary four-particle rule and one fixed input. Which additional conditions on the rule, phase drifts or observation encoding ensure original-frame untimed Presburger reachability? (\wtag\ For planar weighted rules, source~20 already exhibits nonsemilinear original-frame site sets under drift (Theorem~\ref{smc:og:thm:exactdrift}); the existence of an obstruction is new here only in one dimension and for reversible rules. The characterization is open.)
\item\label{smc:ix:ut:q:real} \textbf{Separate natural from real exactness.} The generic compiler is exact over natural witnesses only. Which restricted chart families have enough integrality structure to force all nonnegative rational or real zeros to represent physical integer-time states, and what extra conditions are genuinely necessary? (\wtag\ Source~18's four-witness binary certificate is one such family: it is exact for nonnegative real witnesses (Corollary~\ref{smc:tq:cor:uniform}).)
\item\label{smc:ix:ut:q:quantify} \textbf{Quantify preprocessing.} Effectiveness gives no useful bound on chart count, phase periods, coefficients or the materialized prefixes of bounded templates. Explicit rule-dependent complexity bounds would clarify when the construction is practical. They must account for fixed but potentially enormous reset-template histories.
\end{enumerate}
None of these questions reopens the already imported fixed-input chart theorem. Nor is the general two-total-variable raw-affine claim asserted as a consequence of the present proof.

\[
 \{Q_i(n)+p_ij:\ n\ge n_i,\ n\equiv\rho_i,\ l_i(n)\le j\le u_i(n),\ j\equiv\sigma_i\},
\]
with $Q_i$ a rational quadratic that is integral on its domain, $l_i,u_i$ rational affine and the congruences of fixed moduli, together with finitely many exceptions and an eventually periodic set. \emph{Sketch given:} in an expanding orbit with zero drift every anchored test, including each required zero, is a Boolean combination of affine conditions on the chart parameters $(n,j)$ of source~18's Lemma~\ref{smc:tq:lem:interface}; split into disjoint cases, refine residues and take the eventually dominant affine bounds; finitely many exceptional cycles give finite intervals. \begin{remark}[\wtag\ No polynomial certificate of a time-only clock relation is exact over nonnegative reals]\label{smc:ix:rem:realtrace}
Let $T\subseteq\NN^m$ and let $P(\mathbf v,\mathbf w)$ be a real polynomial with $n$ witnesses such that, for every $\mathbf v\in\NN^m$, $P(\mathbf v,\mathbf w)=0$ has a solution $\mathbf w\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^n$ exactly when $\mathbf v\in T$. Then $S=\{\mathbf v\in\mathbb R^m:\exists\mathbf w\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^n,\ P(\mathbf v,\mathbf w)=0\}$ is semialgebraic by the Tarski--Seidenberg theorem, and $T=S\cap\NN^m$. Conversely every such trace is represented: a basic set $\{f=0,\ g_1>0,\ldots,g_r>0\}$ is the projection of the zeros of $f^2+\sum_i(g_iw_i^2-1)^2$, a finite union is the projection of the zeros of the product of these polynomials in disjoint witnesses, and a real witness $w$ is written $a-b$ with $a,b\ge0$.

For $m=1$ a semialgebraic subset of $\mathbb R$ is a finite union of points and intervals, so its trace on $\NN$ is finite or cofinite. Fix $x\in\NN$ in the hit relation $t=k^2+(2x+3)k$ of~\eqref{smc:rt:eq:times} with $d=13+x$. Its section $\{k^2+(2x+3)k:k\in\NN\}$ is infinite and misses $t_k+1$ for every $k$, because consecutive hits differ by $2k+2x+4\ge4$. So no polynomial certificate $P(x,t;\mathbf w)$, of any degree and with any number of witnesses, is exact for nonnegative real witnesses with $(x,t)$ as its only external data. This is sharper than the false witness $(\sqrt{13}-3)/2$ printed after Remark~\ref{smc:rt:cor:quartic}, which refutes real exactness for one certificate only. The same argument applies to the set of Corollary~\ref{smc:rt:cor:dense} (infinite, with infinite complement) and to source~17's hits (Proposition~\ref{smc:fm:prop:hits}). Over $\mathbb Q_{\ge0}$ the obstruction disappears, since a projection over rational witnesses need not be semialgebraic, and source~24's quartic is exact there (Remark~\ref{smc:rt:cor:quartic}).
\end{remark}
