Its bibliography entries are this report's~\cite{accumulations}, \cite{owpositivity}, \cite{smcreadme56} and~\cite{reviewsignal}. Its abstract follows.
\begin{quote}\small
Fix a rational, number-preserving signal machine, a complete finite collision macro, and an outgoing collision section to which the macro returns with the same ordered labels and co-location pattern. With at most four live signals, the translation-reduced section has dimension at most two. We prove that validity of every finite prefix of the endlessly repeated macro is equivalent to an effectively constructed Boolean formula of integer polynomial signs of degree at most two in the initial gap numerators. A literal sign-and-logic compiler produces a sum-of-squares polynomial of degree at most four, with exactly one natural witness tuple on each accepted encoded input. The arity depends on the fixed macro, not on the number of repetitions.

The same construction classifies finite-time accumulation from the observed clock sequence, including exact cancellation of invisible unstable or neutral modes, and handles rational deadline queries. A four-signal spectator example has a strict one-cycle chamber, a weak limiting boundary, and a Zeno clock despite return spectral radius one. In any fixed finite population, rational initial data and a valid ultimately periodic complete macro imply rational finite accumulation time and rational limiting positions.

The proofs cover simultaneous collisions, all real spectral degeneracies, and the nonreal case. They concern finite pre-accumulation prefixes; no continuation through an accumulation is defined. The implemented emitter starts at a supplied quadratic sign formula. A general machine-and-macro frontend is specified mathematically but is not implemented. No literature-priority claim, general Positivity algorithm, or new general MRDP theorem is asserted.
\end{quote}
\noindent\textbf{Reading guide.} Sections~\ref{smc:pm:sec:claims}--\ref{smc:pm:sec:chamber} specify the model and exact chronological chamber. Sections~\ref{smc:pm:sec:sign}--\ref{smc:pm:sec:deadline} prove the sign, Diophantine, and clock claims. Sections~\ref{smc:pm:sec:example}--\ref{smc:pm:sec:allpopulation} give the spectator example and rational-limit obstruction. Sections~\ref{smc:pm:sec:evidence}--\ref{smc:pm:sec:prior} separate implementation, evidence, reproducibility, and prior work.

\section{The certificate class and its three conclusions}
\label{smc:pm:sec:claims}
We use $\NN=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. All witnesses below are natural numbers. Signal positions and time are real; every speed and local linear coefficient is rational. A rational initial gap vector is encoded as $x=p/q$ with $p\in\NN^d$ and $q\in\Z_{>0}$. Positivity conditions reject zero gap numerators where the section requires strict separation. An overall rational spatial translation may be supplied independently.

\begin{definition}[Fixed data and variable input]\label{smc:pm:n1.1}
A \emph{complete collision batch} contains every collision site at one timestamp, every incident signal at each site, and the selected local rule there. Consecutive batches have strictly positive time separation. Fix a rational signal machine whose local rules preserve the number of signals, an outgoing collision section, and a nonempty finite word $W$ of complete batches. The final section must have exactly the initial ordered label word and outgoing co-location pattern. The machine, rules, speeds, word, and sections are compiler data. Only the initial inter-site gaps and stated arithmetic query parameters are polynomial inputs.
\end{definition}

The standard collision convention requires pairwise distinct speeds within each incoming set and within each outgoing set~\cite{accumulations}. It excludes equal-speed co-located outputs. Equal-speed signals at different positions remain permitted. Completeness allows several disjoint collision sites at the same timestamp and collisions involving more than two signals. Zero-duration cascades are excluded, rather than silently merged into a permitted macro.

\begin{theorem}[Infinite periodic validity]\label{smc:pm:thm:validity}
For the fixed data above, with at most four live signals, one can effectively construct a Boolean combination of rational polynomial sign tests, each of degree at most two in the initial gaps, that is true exactly when every finite prefix of $W^\omega$ is the genuine complete collision history. After positive denominator clearing, the tests have integer coefficients. For integer gap numerators, an explicitly constructed ordinary integer sum-of-squares polynomial of degree at most four has exactly one natural witness tuple on each accepted encoded input and no witness on each rejected encoded input.
\end{theorem}

The number of witnesses is independent of the repetition count. It can grow with the finite supplied word. Thus the theorem does not provide one fixed arity over all macros. Matrix and macro coefficients must be fixed before introducing the gap variables: allowing them as additional polynomial inputs would require different degree accounting.

\begin{theorem}[Observable physical clock]\label{smc:pm:thm:clock}
On the valid inputs of Theorem~\ref{smc:pm:thm:validity}, finite total elapsed time is characterized by another degree-at-most-two sign formula. Validity together with Zeno behavior, and validity together with non-Zeno behavior, therefore admit the same unique-witness quartic construction. For rational initial gaps and a finite accumulation time, that time is rational and effectively computable. Equality to, and strict comparison with, a supplied rational deadline at section time zero also use degree-at-most-two integer sign tests.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rational limits for every fixed finite population]\label{smc:pm:thm:rational}
For any fixed finite number of signals, a valid ultimately periodic complete collision macro with rational speeds and rational initial positions can have only rational finite accumulation times and rational limiting positions of its periodically named collision sites.
\end{theorem}

The last theorem is conditional on validity and finite accumulation. It does not claim an effective validity test in arbitrary dimension. In particular, an execution with irrational accumulation time or irrational limiting location cannot admit a valid ultimately periodic complete macro of the specified kind. None of the three theorems specifies an execution at or after the accumulation instant.

\wtag\ [Theorem~\ref{smc:pm:thm:rational} is the general repeated-Zeno rational-accumulation statement of this report. Part~I's clock (Proposition~\ref{smc:cg:prop:clock}: accumulation at $S=u+v$) and Part~II's shuttle (Proposition~\ref{smc:sd:prop:sharpness}: accumulation at time~2) are instances for rational seeds, each, after a one-batch prefix, a two-batch macro of three signals that returns to its section after one bounce at each wall (the clock's return multiplies the remaining time $S-t$ by $1/3$, Part~I's proof; the shuttle's left times satisfy $a'=4/3+a/3$). The Zeno criteria and rational accumulation times of Part~XI's Reports~61--63 are special cases of it and of Theorem~\ref{smc:pm:thm:clock}; notes there point here. Together with Theorems~\ref{smc:pm:thm:validity} and~\ref{smc:pm:thm:clock} it answers in part Part~I's research direction on accumulation limits (Section~\ref{smc:cg:q:accumulation}): for supplied ultimately periodic complete macros the infinite repetition is certified by a finite formula and one witness tuple, not by an infinite sequence of finite checks, and the limit time is a rational formula; the direction stays open for executions without a supplied periodic macro and for any continuation beyond the accumulation.]

\section{The dimension of the outgoing collision section}\label{smc:x:sec:pmdim}
Immediately after a complete batch, list the $N$ outgoing signals by increasing position. Within each co-located group, order the signals by strictly increasing speed. Let $g_i$ be the gap from signal $i$ to signal $i+1$, for $1\leq i<N$, and let $Z$ be the indices of the zero gaps inside the co-located groups. All other gaps are strictly positive.

An outgoing collision section has at least one co-located pair, so $|Z|\geq1$. Remove the overall translation and set
\[
 d=N-1-|Z|.
\]
Let $L:\R^d\to\R^{N-1}$ insert zeros at the indices in $Z$, and let $R$ select the complementary coordinates. Then $RL=I$, and every section configuration has the form $g=Lx$ with $x>0$ componentwise. Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:dim}
 d\leq N-2\leq2\qquad(N\leq4).
\end{equation}
Two simultaneous disjoint binary collisions at population four have two zero gaps and $d=1$. A triple collision also has $d=1$, and a four-signal collision has $d=0$. At $d=0$, homogeneity forces every proposed flight time to be zero; hence a nonempty repeated macro with positive flight times is impossible.

This reduction is anchored \emph{immediately after a collision}. Retaining an arbitrary later observation phase would add a phase coordinate and invalidate~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:dim}. Sorting each co-located output group by speed is also essential: these groups then separate immediately into the stated order. An arbitrary within-site order would not represent the actual outgoing mode.

\section{A complete one-macro chronological chamber}
\label{smc:pm:sec:chamber}
In a fixed outgoing mode, let $v_i$ be signal $i$'s speed and put $c_i=v_i-v_{i+1}$. During a collision-free interval of duration $\tau$,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:gaps}
 g_i'=g_i-c_i\tau.
\end{equation}
Only an adjacent pair with $c_i>0$ can cause the next collision. Such a closing pair has $g_i>0$, since an outgoing co-located pair has the opposite strict speed order. Its candidate time is $g_i/c_i$. If no adjacent pair is closing, a proposed next batch is impossible.

Let $S$ be the specified incoming zero-gap indices at the next batch, and choose a pivot $j\in S$. Require $c_j>0$ and define $\tau=g_j/c_j$. Require $\tau>0$. For every other closing index $i$, impose
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:candidate}
 \frac{g_i}{c_i}-\tau
 \begin{cases}
 =0,&i\in S,\\
 >0,&i\notin S.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Reject structurally if an index of $S$ is not closing. Add all specified zero and strict-positive gap conditions in the initial and resulting outgoing sections. Every maximal consecutive block in $S$ is one collision site: check its entire incoming label set and rule, replace all sites simultaneously, and sort each output block by increasing speed. Number preservation keeps the number of gaps fixed. Within each output block the gaps are zero; outside those blocks the ordered inter-site gap indices retain their meaning.

\begin{lemma}[One-step exactness]\label{smc:pm:lem:step}
The structural conditions, section conditions, positive flight time, and candidate comparisons above are necessary and sufficient for the indicated complete next batch.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Necessity is first-collision semantics. Conversely, every adjacent gap remains nonnegative until the pivot time. A nonadjacent crossing would require a prior adjacent crossing. The strict comparisons exclude an earlier competitor and exclude any omitted collision site at the pivot time. The tied indices include every zero gap of every collision block, hence every incoming signal in a multiple collision. Strict gaps between the maximal blocks keep distinct purported sites distinct. The stated rules replace these blocks at once; distinct, speed-sorted outputs establish the next outgoing section. No collision is hidden by the representation.
\end{proof}

Each new gap, position increment, and flight time is a homogeneous rational linear form in the starting gaps. Symbolically compose these fixed finite linear operations over the $m$ batches of $W$. No physical trajectory has to be executed to perform this construction. It gives rational matrices $E,G,T$ and rows $\ell,r$ such that
\begin{align}
 \text{one macro is legal}&\iff Ex=0\ \text{and}\ Gx>0,\label{smc:pm:eq:chamber}\\
 \text{final full gaps}&=TLx,\nonumber\\
 \text{macro elapsed time}&=\ell x,\nonumber\\
 \text{leftmost position increment}&=rx.\nonumber
\end{align}
The equality matrix includes the final zero-gap conditions of the initial section. The strict matrix includes every positive flight time and every required strict gap. A mismatch of final labels or co-location pattern is structural rejection.

\wtag\ [Lemma~\ref{smc:pm:lem:step} and the chamber~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:chamber} are the one-macro case of Part~I's Theorem~\ref{smc:cg:thm:chamber}, whose typed endpoint conditions (Lemma~\ref{smc:cg:lem:endpoint}) play the role of the candidate comparisons~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:candidate}, specialized to number-preserving rules and to a word that ends on its own initial section. Part~II proves the same step for its normalized schemas (Lemma~\ref{smc:sd:lem:boundary}), and Part~III's Lemma~\ref{smc:cs:lem:event} is another one-batch case. Source~26 did not read those Parts (Section~\ref{smc:pm:sec:prior}); its proof is printed as its own account and claims no novelty for the chamber (Section~\ref{smc:pm:sec:prior}). New in source~26 are the return matrix of the closed word and the all-repetition criterion that follows.]

Set $M=RTL$. On the chamber, $TLx=LMx$. The condition need not hold at every point of the ambient vector space. Keeping redundant rows is harmless. A direct construction uses at most
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:rowbound}
 (2m+1)(N-1)+m\leq7m+3
\end{equation}
zero/strict rows: $(m+1)(N-1)$ section conditions, at most $m(N-1)$ candidate comparisons, and $m$ positive-time conditions. This is a loose row bound, not an optimized arithmetic-operation count.

\begin{proposition}[Exact infinite criterion]\label{smc:pm:prop:iterate}
Every finite prefix of $W^\omega$ is the unique actual complete history if and only if
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:infinite}
 EM^nx=0,\qquad GM^nx>0\qquad\text{for every }n\geq0.
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
An actual history satisfies the one-macro conditions at every repetition, giving necessity. For sufficiency, apply Lemma~\ref{smc:pm:lem:step} through the first macro. Its final section conditions give $TLx=LMx$ with the prescribed labels and co-locations. Apply the same argument to $Mx$, and continue by induction. The final section equalities at each stage justify each next invocation. This establishes every finite prefix without assuming that $M$ preserves the entire physical section off the legal orbit.
\end{proof}

\section{All cases of the order two sign problem}
\label{smc:pm:sec:sign}
Pad dimension one to two with a zero coordinate and a zero row and column of $M$. This leaves every physical scalar observation unchanged. For a row $a$, Cayley--Hamilton implies
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:allequal}
 aM^nx=0\text{ for all }n\geq0\quad\iff\quad ax=0\text{ and }aMx=0.
\end{equation}
One equality suffices in dimension one, but the padding causes no difficulty.

\subsection{The nonreal branch must be rejected before squaring}
Let $\delta_M=(\tr M)^2-4\det M$. If $\delta_M<0$, a real scalar observation has the form
\[
 aM^nx=\rho^n\bigl(A\cos(n\theta)+B\sin(n\theta)\bigr),\qquad 0<\theta<\pi.
\]
No nonzero such sequence remains nonnegative. If $\theta/(2\pi)$ is rational, the normalized values over a full period sum to zero, so nonnegativity would force them all to be zero. If it is irrational, the powers of $e^{i\theta}$ are dense in the unit circle; a nonzero real linear functional is negative on an open arc, reached by that orbit. The elementary density argument follows by applying the pigeonhole principle to fractional parts to obtain arbitrarily small nonzero rotation steps.

Thus weak nonnegativity holds only for the zero observation, and strict positivity never holds. A nonempty legal macro has a strictly positive flight-time guard. Therefore~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:infinite} is empty in this branch. This test precedes squaring: a pure-imaginary conjugate pair squares to a \emph{negative} scalar matrix and must not be mistaken for nonnegative real spectrum.

\subsection{Real spectrum and the parity reduction}
Assume $\delta_M\geq0$ and put $B=M^2$. Its eigenvalues satisfy $\alpha\geq\beta\geq0$. For each guard row $a$ and parity $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}$, set
\[
 A_0=aM^\varepsilon x,\qquad A_1=aM^{\varepsilon+2}x.
\]
The parity subsequence $v_n=aM^{2n+\varepsilon}x$ has these initial values and satisfies the characteristic recurrence of $B$. Write
\[
 t=\tr B,\qquad h=\det B,\qquad \Delta=t^2-4h.
\]
The following exhaustive list supplies exact infinite tests.

\begin{proposition}[Nonnegative-root recurrence tests]\label{smc:pm:prop:roots}
The sequence $v_n$ is strictly positive for every $n\geq0$ precisely under the conditions below:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\alpha>\beta>0$, then $A_0>0$ and $A_1-\beta A_0\geq0$.
\item If $\alpha>\beta=0$, then $A_0>0$ and $A_1>0$.
\item If $\alpha=\beta=\lambda>0$, then $A_0>0$ and $A_1-\lambda A_0\geq0$.
\item If $\alpha=\beta=0$, strict positivity is impossible.
\end{enumerate}
For weak nonnegativity, replace the first $A_0>0$ by $A_0\geq0$ in cases 1 and~3. In cases 2 and~4 the condition is $A_0\geq0$ and $A_1\geq0$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
In case 1, put $D=(A_1-\beta A_0)/(\alpha-\beta)$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:convex}
 \frac{v_n}{\alpha^n}=D+(A_0-D)(\beta/\alpha)^n.
\end{equation}
This is a convex interpolation between the initial value $A_0$ and the limiting value $D$. At each finite $n$, the coefficient of $A_0$ is positive. Hence $D=0$ is allowed even for strict positivity. Conversely the initial sign and limiting sign are necessary.

In case 2, the first term is $A_0$, and all later terms are $A_1\alpha^{n-1}$; the strict tail inequality cannot be weakened. In case 3, Cayley--Hamilton gives the Jordan formula
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:jordan}
 v_n=\lambda^n\left[A_0+n\left(\frac{A_1}{\lambda}-A_0\right)\right].
\end{equation}
The initial value must have the stated sign and the slope must be nonnegative. This includes the scalar case with zero slope and makes no diagonalizability assumption. In case 4, $B^2=0$, so the terms from index two onward vanish. (For $B=M^2$ here, $M^2=0$ already.) The weak conditions follow from the same formulas.
\end{proof}

Apply Proposition~\ref{smc:pm:prop:roots} to both parities. This covers positive and negative eigenvalues of $M$, distinct opposite eigenvalues of equal modulus, repeated negative eigenvalues with a Jordan block, and zero roots. For example, when the eigenvalues of $M$ are $\lambda,-\lambda$, $B$ is scalar but \emph{both} parity initial values must still be positive. A nonzero alternating observation fails.

\subsection{Removing the only square root without raising the degree}
Only case 1 may have a nonrational coefficient. Define
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:CH}
 C=2A_1-tA_0,\qquad H=\Delta A_0^2-C^2.
\end{equation}
Under $A_0\geq0$ and $\Delta>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:radical}
 A_1-\beta A_0\geq0
 \iff C\geq0\ \lor\ \bigl(C<0\ \land\ H\geq0\bigr).
\end{equation}
Indeed, twice the expression on the left is $C+A_0\sqrt\Delta$. If $C\geq0$ it is nonnegative. Otherwise compare two nonnegative quantities before squaring. This also proves the equivalence at $A_0=0$. In the repeated-root case $\lambda=t/2$ is rational. Every fixed rational denominator may be cleared by a positive integer.

Consequently all infinite strict or weak guards are Boolean formulas in integer linear or quadratic polynomials in $x$. One guard requires at most six distinct polynomials, namely $A_0,C,H$ for each parity; the other branches need fewer. An infinite equality requires at most two linear polynomials by~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:allequal}. This proves the sign-formula part of Theorem~\ref{smc:pm:thm:validity}. It is an explicit order-two calculation, not a proposed finite spectral test for arbitrary-order linear recurrences.

\section{A literal quartic with exactly one natural witness tuple}
\label{smc:pm:sec:compiler}
Let $\Phi(p)$ be a Boolean formula of sign tests of distinct integer polynomials $Q_1(p),\ldots,Q_A(p)$, each of degree at most two. Here $p$ denotes the chosen integer inputs; common positive denominator scaling preserves the homogeneous validity signs.

For each $Q$, introduce natural witnesses $e_-,e_0,e_+,z$ and the following six residuals:
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:gadget}
\begin{gathered}
 e_-(e_--1),\qquad e_0(e_0-1),\qquad e_+(e_+-1),\\
 e_-+e_0+e_+-1,\\
 Q-(e_+-e_-)(z+1),\qquad e_0z.
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Every residual has total degree at most two, including when $Q$ is quadratic.

\begin{lemma}[Canonical natural sign fiber]\label{smc:pm:lem:gadget}
For every encoded input $p$, the simultaneous zero set of~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:gadget} in natural witnesses consists of exactly one tuple. Its three flags indicate the sign of $Q(p)$; if $Q(p)\ne0$, then $z=|Q(p)|-1$, while if $Q(p)=0$, then $e_0=1$ and $z=0$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The first three residuals force Boolean flags. Their one-hot sum leaves one flag equal to one. The sign equation forces the selected sign and, when nonzero, the displayed magnitude. At zero, the final equation $e_0z=0$ eliminates the otherwise free slack. The displayed choices satisfy all six equations, proving existence and uniqueness.
\end{proof}

Read $Q>0$ as $e_+$, $Q=0$ as $e_0$, and $Q\geq0$ as the Boolean negation of $e_-$. Translate the formula to an acyclic AND/OR/NOT circuit, topologically ordered. For each of its $\Gamma$ gates introduce one natural output $b$ and one defining residual:
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:gates}
 \begin{array}{lll}
 \text{AND:}& b-uv,&\quad
 \text{OR:}\ b-u-v+uv,\\
 \text{NOT:}& b-1+u.&
 \end{array}
\end{equation}
The inputs of the first gates are uniquely Boolean by Lemma~\ref{smc:pm:lem:gadget}. Inductively every gate output is also uniquely Boolean, so separate gate-Boolean equations are unnecessary. Add the output residual $b_{\mathrm{out}}-1$ and take the sum of the squares of all residuals.

\begin{theorem}[Explicit arithmetic ledger]\label{smc:pm:thm:quartic}
This construction yields an ordinary integer polynomial $P_\Phi(p,w)$ of degree at most four. For every encoded input, $\Phi(p)$ is true if and only if $P_\Phi(p,w)=0$ for a natural witness tuple $w$, and that tuple is unique when it exists. Before optional constant-output simplifications, the ledger is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:ledger}
 \#w=4A+\Gamma,\qquad \#\text{residuals}=6A+\Gamma+1.
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
A sum of integer squares vanishes exactly when all its residuals vanish. Every residual has degree at most two, hence the sum has degree at most four. The sign witnesses and gate outputs are uniquely determined, and the final residual accepts exactly the true formula. Counting four witnesses and six residuals per atom, one of each per gate, and the final residual gives~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:ledger}. A constant-false formula can instead be represented by $1$, and constant true by $0$, with an empty witness tuple.
\end{proof}

\wtag\ [The source and the programme's review write the gate count $\Gamma$ as $J$: ``$4A+J$ witnesses and $6A+J+1$ residuals for A sign atoms/J logic gates''. It is not the contact count $J$ of source~29 or the witness $J_{\rm acc}$ of sources~28 and~29.]

For $S$ infinite strict/weak rows and $E_0$ infinite equality rows, the preceding sign construction gives $A\leq6S+2E_0$ before clock/deadline predicates are added. This is an explicit arity accounting, not an optimal count. Shifting each natural witness by one provides a strictly positive witness convention without changing degree or uniqueness.

No quadratic guard is multiplied by a selector: doing so could create a cubic residual. The sign equation in~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:gadget} is what preserves degree two. No MRDP theorem, Pell equation, exponentiation atom, square-root witness, or unbounded history code is used. ``Exactly one'' means per supplied input encoding. Two numerator/denominator encodings of the same rational geometry are distinct inputs; no canonical rational representation is asserted. This completes Theorem~\ref{smc:pm:thm:validity}.

\wtag\ [The one-hot sign gadget~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:gadget} with a unique slack is the same device as Part~I's unique-slack quadratic (Theorem~\ref{smc:cg:thm:quadratic}) and Part~IV's canonical quartics with a unique slack for each inequality (Section~\ref{smc:sl:sec:presburger-quartic}), applied here to quadratic sign atoms with a one-hot sign selector; it is printed as the source's own construction, and the source claims no novelty for its Boolean arithmetic (Section~\ref{smc:pm:sec:prior}).]

\section{Summability is a property of the observable clock}
\label{smc:pm:sec:zeno}
Under~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:infinite}, the macro durations
\[
 u_n=\ell M^nx
\]
are strictly positive, being sums of strictly positive flight times. Total elapsed time is $\sum_{n\geq0}u_n$. Test its even and odd subsequences using the same $(A_0,A_1,\alpha,\beta)$ notation as Section~\ref{smc:pm:sec:sign}, now with $a=\ell$.

\begin{proposition}[Exact clock classification]\label{smc:pm:prop:sum}
For a valid strictly positive parity subsequence, summability is determined as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\alpha>\beta>0$ and $\alpha<1$, it is summable.
\item If $\alpha\geq1>\beta>0$, it is summable exactly when $A_1-\beta A_0=0$.
\item If $\alpha>\beta\geq1$, it is not summable.
\item If $\alpha>\beta=0$, it is summable exactly when $\alpha<1$.
\item If $\alpha=\beta=\lambda>0$, it is summable exactly when $\lambda<1$.
\end{enumerate}
The nilpotent case has no valid strictly positive infinite clock. The full clock is summable exactly when both parity subsequences are summable.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
In the distinct positive-root case use~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:convex}. Both modes decay when $\alpha<1$. If $\alpha\geq1>\beta$, summability requires and is implied by vanishing of the dominant coefficient $D$. If both roots are at least one, a strictly positive sequence cannot be summable, including the case $D=0$. When $\beta=0$, strict validity forces $A_1>0$; its geometric tail converges exactly when $\alpha<1$. For a repeated positive root,~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:jordan} has a positive initial value and nonnegative slope. The geometric factor, with its possible linear factor $n$, is summable exactly when $\lambda<1$.
\end{proof}

In the cancellation branch, $\Delta>0$ and $A_0>0$, and
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:cancel}
 A_1-\beta A_0=0\quad\iff\quad C<0\ \land\ H=0.
\end{equation}
This is the exact equality version of the sign-separated squaring in~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:radical}. Comparisons of the fixed algebraic constants $\alpha,\beta$ with one are decidable exactly while compiling. They do not introduce algebraic coefficients into the emitted integer polynomial.

Conjoin validity with this Zeno formula, or with its negation for non-Zeno behavior, and apply Theorem~\ref{smc:pm:thm:quartic}. The observable $\ell M^nx$ may lose a neutral or unstable whole-matrix mode through exact cancellation along the input. Therefore $\rho(M)<1$ is not a necessary condition for a summable clock. Conversely a decaying visible component does not itself certify legal collisions: the full strict guard system remains essential.

\section{Rational clock values and exact deadline queries}
\label{smc:pm:sec:deadline}
For rational input $x=p/q$, define numerator observations
\[
 a_e=\ell p,\quad b_e=\ell M^2p,\quad
 a_o=\ell Mp,\quad b_o=\ell M^3p.
\]
Retain $t=\tr(M^2)$ and $h=\det(M^2)$. If the valid clock converges and $1-t+h\ne0$, its sum is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:time1}
 T=\frac{b_e+b_o+(1-t)(a_e+a_o)}{q(1-t+h)}.
\end{equation}
To obtain this formula for one parity recurrence, sum its characteristic recurrence, or evaluate its generating function
\[
 \frac{A_0+(A_1-tA_0)z}{1-tz+hz^2}
\]
at $z=1$ after any cancellations. Summing the two parity expressions gives~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:time1}. A denominator of either sign is allowed in this intermediate formula, including when an unstable mode has been canceled.

If $1-t+h=0$ and a valid convergent clock exists, $M^2$ has a simple root one and another root $\beta<1$. Both parity coefficients of the root-one mode vanish. The sum is then
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:time2}
 T=\frac{a_e+a_o}{q(2-t)}.
\end{equation}
A repeated root one cannot support a strictly positive summable clock. Formula~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:time2} is the remaining geometric sum, since $\beta=t-1$. These cases cover all valid convergent clocks and establish their rationality and effective evaluation in dimension at most two.

Clear the fixed rational coefficients and normalize the denominator sign to write $T=L(p)/(Dq)$ with $L$ an integer linear form and $D\in\Z_{>0}$ fixed. For a supplied deadline $H/K$, where $K>0$,
\begin{align}
 T=H/K&\iff DqH-KL(p)=0,\label{smc:pm:eq:deadlineeq}\\
 T<H/K&\iff DqH-KL(p)>0.\label{smc:pm:eq:deadlineineq}
\end{align}
These polynomials have total degree at most two in the integer inputs $p,q,H,K$. Conditions $q>0$ and $K>0$ may be encoded with the same sign compiler rather than promised as domains. Signed deadline numerators may be handled as signed integer inputs or by a separately specified natural encoding.

The stated degree accounting fixes the section time to zero. An initial rational time offset can be added by ordinary cross-multiplication, but if its numerator and denominator are new variables the degree ledger must be reconsidered. No uncounted variable-denominator offset is included here. Together with Section~\ref{smc:pm:sec:zeno}, this completes Theorem~\ref{smc:pm:thm:clock}.

\section{A spectator makes the limiting boundary visible}
\label{smc:pm:sec:example}
Consider five meta-signals with speeds
\[
 L:+1,\quad R:-1,\quad P:+3,\quad Q:-3,\quad S:-2.
\]
Use the two nontransparent collision rules
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:rules}
 \{P,R\}\longrightarrow\{Q,R\},\qquad
 \{L,Q\}\longrightarrow\{L,P\}.
\end{equation}
Every other allowed incoming set may use its transparent rule $C\to C$. Each rule preserves population and has distinct incoming/outgoing speeds. The example has four simultaneously live signals and five speed values across its meta-signals; these are different counts.

Immediately after a left bounce, put $L,P$ at zero, $R$ at $d$, and $S$ at $d+y$, with $d,y>0$. The outgoing order is $L,P,R,S$, and the full gap vector is $(0,d,y)$. The proposed macro is one $P$--$R$ bounce followed by one $Q$--$L$ bounce.

\wtag\ [Without the spectator $S$ this is the shrinking-wall shuttle of Part~I's clock (rules~\eqref{smc:cg:eq:clockrules}, speeds $0,2,-1,-2$) and of Part~II's bounded shuttle (speeds $3,2,4,0$), here with walls of speeds $\pm1$; Section~\ref{smc:sec:routes} compares the two. The source credits the mechanism to the literature~\cite{accumulations}; the spectator and the weak limiting boundary are what the example adds.]

\subsection{The exact complete two-bounce chamber}
The first bounce occurs after $d/4$, provided $y>d/4$: the competing $R$--$S$ candidate is at time $y$. The outgoing order after that bounce is $L,Q,R,S$ with gaps
\[
 (d/2,0,y-d/4).
\]
The second bounce takes a further $d/8$, provided $y-d/4>d/8$. Combining the conditions gives exactly
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:exchamber}
 d>0,\qquad y>3d/8.
\end{equation}
Throughout a legal prefix the spectator stays to the right of $R$, while the shuttle remains between $L$ and $R$ until each bounce. Thus no spectator--shuttle or spectator--left-wall collision precedes the $R$--$S$ candidate; these are complete chronology checks, not just a selection of desired bounces. At equality in~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:exchamber}, an additional remote spectator collision belongs to the endpoint batch, so the proposed batch is incomplete and must be rejected.

The return map, time, and leftmost displacement are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:exreturn}
 M\binom d y=\binom{d/4}{y-3d/8},\qquad
 \ell(d,y)=3d/8,\qquad r(d,y)=3d/8.
\end{equation}
After $k$ legal cycles, direct induction yields
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:exiterate}
 d_k=\frac{d}{4^k},\quad
 y_k=y-\frac d2(1-4^{-k}),\quad
 t_k=\frac d2(1-4^{-k}).
\end{equation}
For $K\geq1$, the first $K$ complete strict cycles are valid exactly when
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:Kcycles}
 y>\frac d2(1-4^{-K}).
\end{equation}
Equality gives an omitted spectator collision in that finite endpoint batch and is invalid. Intersecting~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:Kcycles} over every finite $K$ gives the different boundary condition
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:infiniteexample}
 d>0,\qquad y\geq d/2.
\end{equation}
At $y=d/2$ every finite prescribed batch is legal. The spectator reaches the common limiting position only at the accumulation time, which is outside the finite-prefix semantics.

\subsection{Two failures of tempting shortcuts}
The full return matrix and clock row are
\[
 M=\begin{pmatrix}1/4&0\\-3/8&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 \ell=\begin{pmatrix}3/8&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus $\rho(M)=1$, but every input in~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:infiniteexample} is Zeno, with
\[
 T=\sum_{n\geq0}\frac{3d}{8}\,4^{-n}=d/2.
\]
The neutral spectator-gap coordinate is invisible to the clock. This is a signal-realizable counterexample to ``Zeno if and only if the whole return matrix has spectral radius below one.''

There is also no finite repetition horizon depending only on this fixed machine and macro that certifies infinite validity for every rational or integer seed. For any $K\geq0$, take
\[
 d=4^{K+1},\qquad y=d/2-1.
\]
For $K\geq1$, the threshold for $K$ cycles is $d/2-2$, which is smaller than $y$. The next threshold is $d/2-1/2$, which is larger than $y$. Thus the first $K$ cycles succeed and the next fails by a genuine extra $R$--$S$ collision. For $K=0$, the empty prefix is valid and the first proposed bounce has a competing tie.

For positive integer $d,y$, the infinite predicate itself has the particularly small unique-witness quadratic
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:small}
 (2y-d-z)^2=0,\qquad z\in\NN.
\end{equation}
This example does not replace the general quartic theorem. The exported quartic deliberately passes the same predicate through the general sign compiler, making the ledger and canonical-zero branch inspectable. The shrinking-wall shuttle is classical~\cite{accumulations}; the added spectator isolates the weak boundary and observable-clock warning used here.

\section{Rational accumulation limits in every finite dimension}
\label{smc:pm:sec:allpopulation}
We now retain any fixed finite population, assuming that the repeated complete macro is valid. Its rational gap return matrix $M$ may have dimension greater than two. Let $x$ be rational and $f_n=\ell M^nx$ be its positive macro durations. The generating function is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:gen}
 F(z)=\sum_{n\geq0}f_nz^n=\ell(I-zM)^{-1}x\in\Q(z)
\end{equation}
as a formal rational generating function, and as an analytic identity near zero.

If $\sum f_n$ converges, Abel's theorem gives
\[
 \lim_{z\to1^-}F(z)=\sum_{n\geq0}f_n.
\]
The rational function agrees with the convergent series on the interval where the latter is defined, with removable cancellations understood. A rational function over $\Q$ having a finite limit at the rational point one has a rational limit: cancel common powers of $z-1$ and evaluate the remaining quotient. This value is effectively computable by polynomial arithmetic. The accumulation time is therefore rational, conditional on validity and convergence.

For positions, number preservation lets the $k$th \emph{spatially ordered} signal position $X_k(t)$ be followed continuously through every collision. All replaced signals at a site have the same position, and they are replaced by the same number of outgoing signals at that position. Let $V=\max|\text{speed}|$. Each ordered position is $V$-Lipschitz on every finite prefix. If the accumulation time $T$ is finite, it follows that every $X_k(t)$ has a limit as $t\to T^-$; the gaps have limits too.

The displacement of the leftmost position during macro $n$ is $rM^nx$, with
\[
 |rM^nx|\leq Vf_n.
\]
Its series converges absolutely. The same rational-generating-function argument makes its total displacement rational. For a convergent component sequence $h_n$ of $M^nx$, Abel summation gives
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pm:eq:abellimit}
 \lim_{n\to\infty}h_n
 =\lim_{z\to1^-}(1-z)\sum_{n\geq0}h_nz^n.
\end{equation}
The expression on the right is again a rational function over $\Q$ with a finite value at one. Hence all limiting gaps are rational, and adding the rational leftmost limit makes every limiting ordered position rational.

A fixed named collision site at a specified phase of the macro differs from an appropriate macro-boundary position by at most $V$ times that macro's duration. These durations tend to zero in a finite-time accumulation. Its limit is therefore one of the same rational ordered-position limits. A finite rational prefix before the repeated part contributes only rational event times and positions, so an ultimately periodic macro has the same conclusion. This proves Theorem~\ref{smc:pm:thm:rational}.

General signal-machine accumulations can have more complicated coordinates~\cite{accumulations}. The theorem is an obstruction to their description by the present exact finite periodic macros, not a contradiction of that broader literature. It supplies no arbitrary-dimensional recognition algorithm.

\section{Implemented objects and exact evidence}
\label{smc:pm:sec:evidence}
The mathematical construction above has two distinct implementation layers. The one-macro chamber frontend is explicit in Section~\ref{smc:pm:sec:chamber}, but no general parser from an arbitrary machine and macro was implemented in this work. The new implemented emitter starts with an integer sign formula of degree at most two. It builds sparse polynomial residuals, expands their sum of squares, and writes complete coefficient data for two concrete certificates.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}
\toprule
Export & Atoms & Gates & Witnesses & Residuals & Monomials\\
\midrule
Four-signal predicate & 2 & 2 & 10 & 15 & 65\\
Quadratic-sign diagnostic & 3 & 5 & 17 & 24 & 117\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Both expanded polynomials have exact degree four. The first recognizes $d>0$ and $2y\geq d$ on natural inputs. The second exercises AND, OR, and NOT using the nonsquare-spectrum recurrence matrix
\[
 A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
It recognizes strict positivity of the first coordinate of $A^n(x,y)$ for every $n\in\NN$, on natural $x,y$. This is a recurrence diagnostic. No physical complete collision macro realizing this particular matrix is asserted.

The source emitter receipt records $8\,774$ comparisons of the expanded polynomial with its residual sum, including $7\,936$ rejected one-coordinate mutations of canonical witnesses. These finite regressions support the implementation; they do not prove the infinite equivalences or uniqueness on untested inputs. Those are proved in Sections~\ref{smc:pm:sec:sign}--\ref{smc:pm:sec:compiler}.

The author-side exact arithmetic receipt includes $7\,938$ rational diagonal-mode comparisons, $882$ Jordan/nilpotent comparisons, $45\,000$ integer-matrix prefix probes, $15\,147$ sign-gadget assignments, $6\,912$ return-map identities, $64$ strict-endpoint/late-failure checks, $66$ clock-sum identities, and $12$ Boolean-gate cases. The matrix probes used a finite prefix; their observed agreement is not a finite-cutoff theorem.

An independent mathematical audit read the entire proof and found no substantive correction required. Its separately authored exact arithmetic checks cover strict and weak recurrence branches, radical signs, canonical witnesses, cancellation, clock sums, and spectator identities. One deliberately late failure has first nonpositive term at index $6\,932$, underscoring the distinction between a proof of infinite validity and a short experimental prefix. The proof audit is conventional mathematical review, not proof-assistant verification or journal peer review.

The frozen source proof is preserved byte-for-byte in the package. Its SHA-256 is
\sha{df7cefb472a76e6f34ce7fff0b1e8548782a82f4863fac2ecd2d682c69941a77}
A separate independent artifact audit reconstructed every sign gadget, gate residual, and atom polynomial, then independently expanded both sums of squares. The complete coefficient dictionaries agree exactly with both exported ordinary polynomials. This is an all-assignment polynomial identity, stronger than finite evaluation agreement. The canonical-fiber proof therefore transfers to these literal exports through exact residual and coefficient identities. \section{Reproducibility and execution boundary}
\label{smc:pm:sec:repro}
The release separates the editable article, frozen science, frozen independent audits, and newly authored release/replay tools. Exact path and hash inventories bind the artifacts to their evidence. The source and audit packets remain inert inputs except for explicitly inspected new arithmetic-only checker programs named by the replay contract.

The release utility verifies the exact file inventory, bytes, and POSIX modes against a manifest whose trusted SHA-256 is supplied separately. A PDF rebuild uses a fresh external directory, deterministic date settings, and \texttt{pdflatex} with shell escape disabled. Archive creation uses sorted members and fixed timestamps. Build and archive operations check preservation of the release inputs. The reproducibility instructions and machine-readable receipts state the tool versions, byte identities, and output requirements actually checked.

The arithmetic replay also uses a fresh external output location. It validates the frozen input pins before executing any permitted checker, copies the needed data into a separate working area, and compares regenerated evidence with the frozen receipts or exports. The assertion-based checks must run without Python optimization; removing assertions is not an independent successful check. The replay tools reject unsafe path overlap, reused outputs, and symlink-based output redirection, and their adversarial tests are included.

No upstream program, saved computation schedule, downloaded executable, physical simulator, or post-accumulation dynamics is executed. Evaluating a newly authored rational recurrence, expanding a polynomial, and checking the displayed return-map identities are arithmetic checks of the proof objects. They are not a simulation of the signal machine. The analytic diagram is drawn directly from its stated equations.

\textbf{What successful replay establishes.} It establishes agreement of the pinned finite exact arithmetic artifacts and the independently checked exports, preservation of the supplied sources, and reproducibility of the packaged build under the recorded environment. It does not convert finite regression tests into an infinite proof, remove the fixed-word hypothesis, or implement the missing general chamber frontend.

\section{A compact compiler checklist (source 26, Appendix A)}\label{smc:x:sec:pmchecklist}
For a fixed supplied machine, section, and word, the proof gives the following finite procedure.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Verify number preservation, distinct-speed collision sets, complete batches, and the exact return of ordered labels and outgoing co-locations. Reject structurally invalid data.
\item Remove translation and zero section gaps. If the remaining dimension is zero, reject any nonempty positive-flight macro. For population at most four, otherwise retain one or two gap coordinates.
\item Compose the finite symbolic gap updates, retaining every tie equality, strict competing-time comparison, section condition, and positive flight time. Produce $E,G,M,\ell,r$.
\item Replace each infinite equality by its first two observations. Check $\delta_M$ before squaring. Reject the nonreal branch using its impossible positive clock guard.
\item For real spectrum, square $M$, split each strict guard into even and odd subsequences, and use all four cases of Proposition~\ref{smc:pm:prop:roots}. Eliminate square roots using the sign-separated formula~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:radical}.
\item If requested, add both parity clock-summability tests, including exact dominant-mode cancellation. For valid Zeno inputs, select~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:time1} or~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:time2} and add the rational deadline predicates.
\item Clear fixed denominators positively; deduplicate sign polynomials. Introduce the six-residual canonical gadget for each atom and deterministic Boolean gates. Require the circuit output to be one and sum all residual squares.
\end{enumerate}
Only the sign-formula-to-polynomial part of this checklist is implemented generically in the supplied emitter. Earlier steps are proved mathematical constructions, not claimed software features.

\section{The exact theorem and its scope}\label{smc:x:sec:fvscope}
We write $\NN=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$. A signal machine has finitely many meta-signals, each with a fixed real velocity, and deterministic local collision rules. Every incoming and outgoing collision set has pairwise distinct velocities. Different meta-signals may share a velocity at distinct spatial positions. A number-preserving rule emits as many signals as it consumes. These are the standard conventions of~\cite{accumulations}.

Here all velocities are rational. Initial positions may be real for the geometric theorem; rational and integer initial-gap statements are proved separately. Some literature includes rational initial positions in the phrase ``rational signal machine,'' so we use ``rational-speed machine'' when that distinction matters. A live-signal count counts strands, including the two strands sharing a collision point, rather than occupied spatial points, speeds, or available labels.

\begin{definition}[The supplied macro problem]\label{smc:fv:n1.1}
Fix a machine, an outgoing collision section, and a nonempty finite word $W$ of complete collision batches. Completeness means that the batch contains every simultaneous collision site and every incident signal at each site. Successive batches have strictly positive time separation. The final section must restore the initial ordered labels and co-location pattern. The variable input is the initial vector of positive inter-site gaps. Its validity means that every finite prefix of $W^\omega$ is the genuine complete physical history.
\end{definition}

Our word has one binary site in each batch. Rules, speeds, and the entire word are fixed data. We do not search for a periodic itinerary, decide unrestricted machine behavior, or define a continuation through an accumulation.

\begin{theorem}[Explicit physical obstruction]\label{smc:fv:thm:main}
There is a rational-speed number-preserving machine with five live signals, 169 meta-signals, and exactly eight speeds, with a complete 138-binary-event word $W$, whose return on positive gaps is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:M}
M=\frac1{30}\begin{pmatrix}7&-2&10\\14&11&-10\\-6&6&15\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
The exact one-macro chamber is the intersection of the 36 strict rational linear guards in Section~\ref{smc:fv:app:guards}. Put
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:center}
D=g_1+g_2+g_3,\quad x=g_1,\quad y=g_1+g_2,\quad
\xi=x-D/3,\quad\eta=y-2D/3.
\end{equation}
For $D>0$, the infinitely valid inputs are exactly those for which $w=(\xi/D,\eta/D)$ belongs to
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:K}
\mathcal K=\{w:\|w\|<\rho\}\ \cup\
\left(\{w:\|w\|=\rho\}\setminus\{\rot^{-n}p:n\in\NN\}\right),
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:Rp}
\rot=\begin{pmatrix}3/5&-4/5\\4/5&3/5\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\rho^2=\frac4{1845},\qquad p=\left(\frac4{205},-\frac{26}{615}\right).
\end{equation}
The real validity cone is nonsemialgebraic. No finite polynomial-sign formula agrees with it on every positive rational gap triple, or even on every positive integer gap triple. These assertions allow arbitrary real coefficients in the alleged formula.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic and time]\label{smc:fv:thm:clock}
The rational-input validity predicate of Theorem~\ref{smc:fv:thm:main} is decidable by a finite elementary exact-arithmetic procedure. Every valid input is Zeno, with accumulation position $0$ and time, measured from the initial outgoing section,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:T}
T(D,\xi,\eta)=\frac{74528}{855}D+\frac{53102}{3705}\xi-\frac{144302}{3705}\eta.
\end{equation}
For rational initial data this time is rational. A separate 114-event variant has the same normalized chamber and set $\mathcal K$, but every valid infinite execution is non-Zeno.
\end{theorem}

The proofs occupy Sections~\ref{smc:fv:sec:primitives}--\ref{smc:fv:sec:time}. The real nonsemialgebraicity claim also excludes a finite description using quantifiers over real polynomial variables, by real quantifier elimination. Quantifiers over natural numbers are a different matter: neither that claim nor the integer sign obstruction rules out Diophantine representations. Section~\ref{smc:fv:sec:boundary} states exactly how Report56 enters.

\section{Five strands and a collision section}
\label{smc:fv:sec:section}
At the outgoing section, place four stationary marker identities at
\[
L=0<X=x<Y=y<D,
\]
and a messenger at $L$ with velocity $+1$. The stationary labels are $L0,X0,Y0,D0$, all with speed zero. The outgoing label order is
\[
(L0,Q_0,X0,Y0,D0),
\]
with the first two labels co-located. The free positive gaps are $g=(x,y-x,D-y)$. Overall translation and the fixed zero gap have been removed. Throughout the macro the messenger has speed $+1$ or $-1$. At most one marker moves at a time, with speed strictly between $-1$ and $1$, and it is restored to its stationary label before the current primitive ends.

The phrase ``marker identity'' tracks one strand as its phase label changes. The finite collection of temporary labels supplies a fixed controller for this particular finite word, not an unbounded program store. Every explicit collision consumes a messenger and one marker and emits a messenger and that same marker identity. Thus all executions of the supplied word have exactly five live signals.

For any binary collision at position $q$ and time $t$, two incoming velocities $v_1>v_2$ have positions $q-v_1\epsilon<q-v_2\epsilon$ just before it. Incoming local order is therefore decreasing velocity. Outgoing local order is increasing velocity. The construction respects both orders at every rule; the exhaustive local order receipt is provided with the packet. Since $|a|<1$ for a moving marker and $|v_Q|=1$, no output pair has equal speeds or remains co-located for a positive interval.

\section{Primitive geometry with complete chronology}
\label{smc:fv:sec:primitives}
All times in this section start at the current primitive's initial section. Reflection across the right anchor means using the coordinate $q\mapsto D-q$ and negating every nonzero physical velocity. It preserves all strict-order and timing arguments below.

\subsection{Scaling a marker about the anchor}
Let a stationary target be at $z>0$, the messenger at $0$ with speed $+1$, and all other markers stationary. For $u>0$, define
\[
a=\frac{u-1}{u+1}\in(-1,1).
\]
The primitive $L_z(u)$ launches the target at the first messenger hit, reflects the messenger to $-1$, reflects it again at the anchor, restores the target at the next hit while reflecting the messenger to $-1$, then reflects the messenger at the anchor back to $+1$. Every stationary spectator on each traversed segment is crossed transparently.

\begin{lemma}[Exact scaling primitive]\label{smc:fv:lem:L}
The target ends at $uz$. The prescribed complete binary word is valid exactly when $z$ and $uz$ lie strictly between the target's unchanged nearest stationary neighbors, with no upper-neighbor condition if there is no such neighbor. Its duration is $2(z+uz)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The principal events have time-position pairs
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:Ltimes}
(z,z),\quad(2z,0),\quad(2z+uz,uz),\quad(2z+2uz,0).
\end{equation}
Indeed the second target hit solves
\[
t-2z=z+a(t-z),
\]
and $(1+a)/(1-a)=u$. The target moves monotonically on the segment from $z$ to $uz$. Strict endpoint separation from its fixed nearest neighbors therefore excludes every target--stationary-marker encounter, including one remote from the messenger.

Every inner stationary spectator at $s<\min(z,uz)$ is crossed by the messenger at the four times
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:crossings}
s,\quad2z-s,\quad2z+s,\quad2z+2uz-s.
\end{equation}
The first and third traversals encounter spectators in increasing spatial order; the second and fourth encounter them in decreasing order. The strict inequalities $0<s<\min(z,uz)$ place every crossing strictly between the relevant principal events, and distinct spectator positions give distinct crossing times. No outer spectator is reached.

Immediately after target launch, the messenger's relative velocity is $-1-a<0$, so it separates toward the anchor. On its outward return the relative velocity is $1-a>0$ and the next meeting is the unique solution already computed. The last departure separates from the restored stationary marker. Thus the listed events are complete, binary, and strictly time-separated. No unlisted messenger or marker collision can occur. Conversely, reaching a neighbor gives a coincident forbidden contact; passing it forces an earlier target--neighbor contact. Either contradicts this complete word. The last time in~\eqref{smc:fv:eq:Ltimes} gives the duration.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Homothety toward a reflector}
\label{smc:fv:sec:H}
In every use of the next primitive, its target $x$ is the nearest marker to the active anchor. This restriction is part of the statement. Let a stationary reflector be at $z>x$, let the nearest unchanged neighbor beyond the target be $y\leq z$, and choose $v>0$. Put
\[
a=\frac{1-v}{1+v}\in(-1,1).
\]
The primitive $H_z(v)$ launches the target when the outward messenger hits it, without changing the messenger's speed $+1$. The messenger crosses any intervening stationary markers, reflects at $z$, crosses the same spectators inward, restores the target without changing its speed $-1$, and reflects at the anchor to $+1$.

\begin{lemma}[Exact reflector primitive]\label{smc:fv:lem:H}
The target ends at $x'=vx+(1-v)z$. The prescribed complete binary word is valid exactly when $0<x,x'<y$. Its duration is $2z$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The outward and inward messenger lines are $q=t$ and $q=2z-t$. Target restoration solves
\[
2z-t=x+a(t-x),
\]
giving $q=x'$ and $t=2z-x'$. The target is monotone between its endpoints, so the endpoint inequalities exclude every fixed-marker collision. A spectator $s$ strictly between the target's neighbor and reflector, or equal to that neighbor when it is not itself the reflector, is crossed at $s$ and $2z-s$. Since $x'<s$, its inward crossing precedes restoration; because $0<x'<z$, restoration is after the reflector hit and before the anchor hit. All spatial separations are strict, so all times are distinct. The messenger separates from the target after launch with relative speed $1-a>0$ and catches it inward with relative speed $-1-a<0$. There is no stationary marker below the target whose unlisted crossing could invalidate this chronology. Necessity follows from the same endpoint contact argument as Lemma~\ref{smc:fv:lem:L}. The messenger returns to the anchor at time $2z$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{A translation from two primitives}
For $c<1$, apply $L_x(1/(1-c))$ and then $H_z(1-c)$ to the nearest-anchor target. Denote the composite by $T_z(c)$. Both target phases have velocity $a=c/(2-c)$, although their labels are distinct. Algebra gives
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:translation}
x\longmapsto \frac{x}{1-c}\longmapsto x+cz.
\end{equation}
If $0<x,x+cz<y\leq z$, the middle point lies between the two endpoints. For $c>0$, the inequalities $x<x/(1-c)<x+cz$ follow from $x+cz<z$; for $c<0$, the reversed inequalities follow from $x<z$. The $c=0$ case is immediate. Thus Lemmas~\ref{smc:fv:lem:L} and~\ref{smc:fv:lem:H} prove necessity and sufficiency of just the two endpoint conditions, along with unchanged marker order. This is an exact guard reduction, not a sufficient safety margin. The target moves monotonically in the direction of $c$ throughout the composite.

\section{Three shears and all finite phases}
\label{smc:fv:sec:shears}
Two translations $T_y(c),T_D(-2c/3)$ send the left-based target to $x+c(y-2D/3)$. Repeating this pair twice with $c=-1/4$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:A}
A:\quad x\longmapsto x-y/2+D/3,\qquad y\longmapsto y.
\end{equation}
The two physical target velocities are $-1/9$ and $1/11$.

Transfer the messenger from $L$ to $D$ by transparently crossing $X,Y$ and reflecting at $D$. In the reflected coordinate, set $r=D-y$ and $s=D-x$. Repeat $T_s(2/5),T_D(-4/15)$ twice with $r$ the target. This gives $r\mapsto r+4s/5-8D/15$, hence
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:B}
B:\quad y\longmapsto y+4x/5-4D/15,\qquad x\longmapsto x.
\end{equation}
The reflected-coordinate target velocities are $1/4,-2/17$, so the physical velocities are $-1/4,2/17$. Transfer back by crossing $Y,X$ and reflecting at $L$. In every $H$ use, $X$ is nearest $L$, or $Y$ is nearest $D$, exactly as required in Section~\ref{smc:fv:sec:H}.

Apply $A$, then $B$, then $A$. In the centered coordinates~\eqref{smc:fv:eq:center},
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:rotation}
\binom{\xi'}{\eta'}=
\begin{pmatrix}1&-1/2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\4/5&1\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&-1/2\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\binom{\xi}{\eta}=\rot\binom{\xi}{\eta}.
\end{equation}
Equivalently $x'=3x/5-4y/5+2D/3$, $y'=4x/5+3y/5$, and $D'=D$. Each shear has two translations using the nearer reflector with eight events apiece, and two using the farther reflector with ten apiece: 36 events. Each anchor transfer has three events. The rotation word therefore has $3\cdot36+2\cdot3=114$ events.

Table~\ref{smc:fv:tab:phases} is the complete marker-identity chronology, including spectators. Indices are zero-based. Letters stand for the messenger's collision with that identity; the full labels and velocities appear in Section~\ref{smc:fv:app:rules}. Every L principal event reverses the messenger. H launch/restoration events preserve its direction; the reflector and anchor reverse it. Transparent crossings preserve direction.

\section{Exact chamber and all competitor exclusions}
\label{smc:fv:sec:chamber}
For an $A$ block with incoming coordinates $(x,y,D)$, define
\begin{align*}
a_0&=x,& a_1&=x-y/4,& a_2&=x-y/4+D/6,\\
a_3&=x-y/2+D/6,& a_4&=x-y/2+D/3.
\end{align*}
Require $0<y<D$ and $0<a_i<y$ for $0\leq i\leq4$, then replace $x$ by $a_4$. These twelve rows are precisely the initial/final endpoint conditions of its four translations and its fixed marker order.

For the $B$ block, form $r=D-y$, $s=D-x$ at its own incoming section and define
\begin{align*}
b_0&=r,&b_1&=r+2s/5,&b_2&=r+2s/5-4D/15,\\
b_3&=r+4s/5-4D/15,&b_4&=r+4s/5-8D/15.
\end{align*}
Require $0<s<D$ and $0<b_i<s$ for $0\leq i\leq4$, then replace $y$ by $D-b_4$. Again there are twelve rows. Both transfers are legal under the strict anchor/data order at their endpoints.

Pull back the first A's twelve rows, B's twelve rows through the first A, and the last A's twelve rows through the preceding blocks. The resulting 36 homogeneous rational linear rows are listed in Section~\ref{smc:fv:app:guards}. They are an exact system, not claimed to be irredundant. Let $C$ be their open cone and let $P$ be its $D=1$ slice in $(\xi,\eta)$ coordinates.

\begin{proposition}[Complete one-macro equivalence]\label{smc:fv:prop:chamber}
The complete 114-event rotation word is legal if and only if all 36 rows hold. There are no additional equality conditions, positive-flight conditions, earlier-competitor conditions, or omitted-tie conditions to impose.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Every legal word must have the stated ordered markers at each translation endpoint, so all rows are necessary. For sufficiency, the translation lemma places every internal scaling endpoint between checked endpoints. The active target is confined throughout each primitive to its open nearest-neighbor interval. Consequently no moving marker can collide with a stationary marker, and no two stationary markers meet. This excludes collisions remote from the messenger as well as adjacent ones.

The messenger has speed $\pm1$, faster in absolute value than the target. Lemmas~\ref{smc:fv:lem:L} and~\ref{smc:fv:lem:H} give its unique principal meetings and every intervening spectator crossing, with positive separation of successive times. At each such meeting all uninvolved markers are strictly elsewhere. Hence no additional earlier collision or simultaneous site exists, no third signal joins a binary event, and each intended output immediately separates in increasing-speed order. Inducting over primitives and transfers proves the complete word. A failed strict endpoint order either gives a forbidden coincident contact or forces a prior marker crossing; it cannot leave this word valid. This establishes exact equivalence, rather than only sufficient legality on a smaller region.
\end{proof}

\wtag\ [This is source~26's one-macro chamber~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:chamber} for this word, with no equality rows, proved here directly from the primitive lemmas rather than through source~26's candidate comparisons.]

At the center $x=D/3,y=2D/3$, every A target endpoint is $D/3$ or $D/6$, and every reflected B endpoint is $D/3$ or $3D/5$, between $0$ and its fixed neighbor $2D/3$. Thus $P$ contains the origin in its interior. The initial rows $0<x<y<1$ make $P$ bounded.

\section{Contraction and a finite deterministic rule table}
\label{smc:fv:sec:rules}
After the rotation, perform $L_x(1/2)$, then $L_y(1/2)$, then $L_D(1/2)$, each with target velocity $-1/3$. These phases contain respectively 4, 8, and 12 binary events, as shown in Table~\ref{smc:fv:tab:phases}.

There is no new guard. When a target is halved, all its inner stationary markers have already been halved and remain strictly below its endpoint; all outer markers are unscaled and strictly above its start. Its monotone motion therefore obeys Lemma~\ref{smc:fv:lem:L}. The complete word has 138 events, and its return is $M$ in~\eqref{smc:fv:eq:M}. The rational coordinate matrix is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:Q}
\begin{pmatrix}D\\\xi\\\eta\end{pmatrix}=Qg,
\qquad Q=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\2/3&-1/3&-1/3\\1/3&1/3&-2/3\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
Direct composition gives
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:conjugacy}
QMQ^{-1}=N=\diag(1/2,\rot/2).
\end{equation}
The eigenvalues are $1/2,(3+4i)/10,(3-4i)/10$. Therefore neither an all-real-spectrum claim nor a claim that all peripheral phases must be roots of unity holds for these physical periodic returns. The normalized coordinate $w$ rotates by $\rot$ while $D$ halves.

For $j=0,\ldots,137$ introduce a messenger label $Q_j$ whose velocity is the incoming messenger velocity at event $j$; set $Q_{138}=Q_0$, with $Q_0$ of speed $+1$. Give each of the 27 target primitives its own temporary moving-marker label. The four stationary labels are unchanged. At event $j$, with the prescribed incoming and outgoing marker labels $Z_{\rm in},Z_{\rm out}$, include the binary rule
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:rule}
\{Q_j,Z_{\rm in}\}\longrightarrow\{Q_{(j+1)\bmod138},Z_{\rm out}\}.
\end{equation}
Transparent crossings have $Z_{\rm in}=Z_{\rm out}$ and equal messenger velocities; anchor/reflector bounces have equal marker labels and opposite messenger velocities. Target launches and restorations exchange stationary and temporary labels exactly as the primitive proof prescribes.

Every explicit input contains its unique $Q_j$, so no two explicit input sets conflict. Each input and output has distinct speeds, because the messenger speed is $\pm1$ and the marker speed lies in $(-1,1)$. Complete the finite machine by the identity rule $S\mapsto S$ on every other allowed collision input set with pairwise distinct speeds. There are finitely many such sets. This completion is deterministic and globally number-preserving; it does not make an omitted triple contact part of the prescribed binary word.

There are $138+27+4=169$ meta-signals, and the exact speed set is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:speeds}
\left\{-1,-\frac13,-\frac14,-\frac19,0,\frac1{11},\frac2{17},1\right\}.
\end{equation}
Event 137 emits $\{Q_0,L0\}$ at $L$, with $Q_0$ moving right. The other markers are stationary and strictly ordered. The original labels, output order, and zero-gap pattern are therefore restored. Section~\ref{smc:fv:app:rules} prints all 138 rules in compact form; the JSON supplies every label definition and every explicit input/output set without compression.

\section{The exact tangent and a real forbidden collision}
\label{smc:fv:sec:geometry}
Write a guard as $aD+b\xi+c\eta>0$. Every $a$ is positive. On $D=1$, the squared distance of its supporting line from the origin is $a^2/(b^2+c^2)$. Exact rational comparison of the 36 rows gives block minima
\[
\frac1{45}\quad\text{for the first A},\qquad
\frac4{1845}\quad\text{for B},\qquad
\frac4{153}\quad\text{for the last A}.
\]
The unique global minimizer is row 18:
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:tangent}
\frac{D}{15}-\frac35\xi+\frac{13}{10}\eta>0.
\end{equation}
For $a=1/15$ and normal $n=(-3/5,13/10)$, the tangent point is $-an/\|n\|^2=p$, and $\|p\|^2=4/1845$. All other rows have strictly larger distance; each is strictly positive on the entire closed radius-$\rho$ disk. Row 18 is nonnegative there and vanishes only at $p$. Thus this disk touches the closed chamber at exactly one point, and its entire boundary except $p$ belongs to the open chamber.

This contact is physically identifiable. At $D=1$ and $w=p$ the initial positions are
\[
x=\frac{217}{615},\qquad y=\frac{128}{205}.
\]
After the first A, $x=46/123$. In the first reflected L phase, $r=1-y=77/205$ and $s=1-x=77/123$, so $(5/3)r=s$. The moving Y marker reaches X exactly at its prescribed restoration. The missing point is an actual omitted triple contact, not an arbitrary exclusion imposed by an overcautious guard.

Two exact integer examples are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:examples}
g_{\rm reject}=(217,167,231),\qquad
g_{\rm accept}=(233,171,211).

Both have sum $615$; they normalize respectively to $p$ and $\rot p=(28/615,-2/205)$. The second is valid by the oriented-orbit argument below. These examples distinguish the two directions of rotation at the boundary.

\section{Infinite validity and three sign obstructions}
\label{smc:fv:sec:obstruction}
\begin{lemma}[Infinite order and density]\label{smc:fv:lem:density}
The rotation $\rot$ has infinite order, and both one-sided orbits of every nonzero point are dense on its circle.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Its complex eigenvalue is $\zeta=(3+4i)/5$. If it were a root of unity, $\zeta+\zeta^{-1}=6/5$ would be a rational algebraic integer, hence an integer, a contradiction. Thus its angle divided by $2\pi$ is irrational. The standard elementary irrational-rotation argument now gives density: pigeonholing multiples of the angle modulo $2\pi$ produces arbitrarily small nonzero rotation steps, whose multiples approximate every circular position. Equivalently, the closure of its cyclic subgroup is a closed subgroup of the circle; a proper closed subgroup is finite, contrary to infinite order. Positive and negative one-sided powers have the same full-circle closure.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Exact infinitely legal set]\label{smc:fv:prop:K}
The set of normalized inputs satisfying every finite macro prefix is exactly $\mathcal K$ in~\eqref{smc:fv:eq:K}.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
By Proposition~\ref{smc:fv:prop:chamber} and cyclic label restoration, every finite prefix is valid exactly when $\rot^nw\in P$ for all $n\geq0$. Induction justifies applying the same guard system after each return; contraction cancels in normalization.

If $\|w\|<\rho$, each guard is strictly positive at every point of that smaller circle, so all iterates are legal. If $\|w\|=\rho$, the only failure point on the circle in one macro is $p$. Thus a future macro fails exactly when $\rot^nw=p$ for some $n\geq0$, or $w=\rot^{-n}p$. If $\|w\|>\rho$, the nearest guard is strictly negative on a nonempty open arc of that circle. Lemma~\ref{smc:fv:lem:density} forces the forward orbit into that arc. These three cases prove the formula, including its inverse orientation.
\end{proof}

\wtag\ [The first sentence of this proof is source~26's infinite criterion (Proposition~\ref{smc:pm:prop:iterate}) for this word, which has no equality rows; the reduction to it is the source's own.]

\begin{proposition}[Real nonsemialgebraicity]\label{smc:fv:prop:real}
The set $\mathcal K$ and its positive homogeneous gap cone are not semialgebraic.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The excluded set $E=\{\rot^{-n}p:n\geq0\}$ is countably infinite, since $\rot$ has infinite order and $p\ne0$. If $\mathcal K$ were semialgebraic, its complement on the algebraic circle $S=\{\|w\|^2=\rho^2\}$ would be semialgebraic. A semialgebraic subset of a circle is a finite union of isolated points and arcs. It cannot be countably infinite: an arc is uncountable, and a finite union of points is finite. Therefore $\mathcal K$ is not semialgebraic. A semialgebraic gap cone would give a semialgebraic $D=1$ section under the invertible rational coordinates~\eqref{smc:fv:eq:Q}, contradicting this result.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Rational-input sign obstruction]\label{smc:fv:prop:rational}
No finite Boolean formula of polynomial signs with real coefficients agrees with infinite validity on all positive rational gap triples.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
All points $\rot^kp$, for integer $k$, are rational. The rejected set $E$ and the accepted set $A=\{\rot^kp:k\geq1\}$ are disjoint: an equality would imply $\rot^{n+k}p=p$ with $n+k>0$. Both are dense in $S$. Their associated $D=1$ gap triples are strictly positive, because the entire critical disk lies inside the strict initial-order rows; only the different row 18 touches it.

Restrict an alleged formula to $D=1$ and then to $S$. Its truth set is semialgebraic. Away from finitely many partition points, it has constant membership on each remaining open arc. Every such arc contains both a point of $A$ and a point of $E$, which require opposite answers. This contradiction proves the claim. Real, rather than rational, coefficients do not evade the finite-arc property.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Integer-input sign obstruction]\label{smc:fv:prop:integer}
No finite Boolean formula of polynomial signs with real coefficients agrees with infinite validity on all $g\in\Z_{>0}^3$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Suppose $F$ did. The physical validity predicate is constant on each positive ray. For each polynomial $f=\sum_{j=0}^d f_j$, with homogeneous components $f_j$, the eventual sign of $f(tg)$ as $t\to+\infty$ is the sign of the highest-degree component $f_j(g)$ that is nonzero. If all components vanish, its sign is zero. For example, eventual positivity is the finite formula
\[
\bigvee_{j=0}^d\left(f_j(g)>0\ \land\ \bigwedge_{k=j+1}^d f_k(g)=0\right).
\]
There are analogous formulas for negative and zero sign. Replace every sign atom of $F$ by its eventual-sign formula to obtain a semialgebraic $F_\infty$. It is invariant under positive scaling, and for each fixed $g$ agrees with $F(tg)$ for all sufficiently large $t$.

For a positive integer vector $g$, all integer multiples $mg$ have the same correct physical answer. Hence their eventual answer $F_\infty(g)$ agrees with validity. Every positive rational vector has a positive integer multiple; scale invariance extends agreement to every positive rational vector, contradicting Proposition~\ref{smc:fv:prop:rational}. The original $F$ was never assumed homogeneous. This eventual-ray bridge is the necessary additional argument for the integer claim.
\end{proof}

Together these results prove the nonsemialgebraic part of Theorem~\ref{smc:fv:thm:main}. They obstruct finite polynomial-sign descriptions without natural-number witnesses. Even allowing real quantifiers still yields a semialgebraic set by quantifier elimination, but natural-number quantification does not share that property.

\section{Elementary exact membership on rational inputs}
\label{smc:fv:sec:membership}
First reject a gap triple that is not strictly positive. For positive rational gaps, compute $D,\xi,\eta$ and $w=(w_1,w_2)=(\xi/D,\eta/D)$ exactly. Compare $w_1^2+w_2^2$ with $4/1845$. A smaller value is accepted and a larger value rejected. Only equality needs an orbit test.

On the critical circle form the Gaussian rational
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:eta}
\gamma=\frac{w_1+iw_2}{p_x+ip_y}=\gamma_1+i\gamma_2\in\Q(i).
\end{equation}
By~\eqref{smc:fv:eq:K}, rejection is exactly
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:power}
\gamma=\left(\frac{3-4i}{5}\right)^n\quad\text{for some }n\in\NN.
\end{equation}
Let $q$ be the least common positive denominator of the reduced rational components $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$. This denominator determines the only possible exponent.

\begin{lemma}[Exact inverse-power denominators]\label{smc:fv:lem:denominator}
The least common denominator of the components of $((3-4i)/5)^n$ is exactly $5^n$ for every $n\geq0$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The $n=0$ case is $1$. For $n\geq1$, work modulo $5$ in the quotient ring with $i^2=-1$. One has $3-4i=3+i$ and $(3+i)^2=3+i$ there. Therefore the integer coefficient pair of $(3-4i)^n$ is congruent to $(3,1)$ modulo $5$. Neither coefficient is divisible by $5$, so the denominator $5^n$ cannot cancel in either component. The quotient ring need not be a field; only this multiplication identity is used.
\end{proof}

\wtag\ [This is the case $(a,b,c)=(3,4,5)$ of source~29's Lemma~\ref{smc:rf:lem:denom}; source~28 proves it again inside its recognition lemma (Lemma~\ref{smc:fd:n6.1}).]

The algorithm is now finite:
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $q$ is not a power of $5$, accept.
\item Otherwise divide by $5$ repeatedly to find the forced exponent $n$ with $q=5^n$.
\item Compute $(3-4i)^n$ by exact integer arithmetic and compare~\eqref{smc:fv:eq:power}. Reject exactly on equality.
\end{enumerate}
For $q=1$ the forced exponent is zero, so only $\gamma=1$ is excluded. The forward point $\gamma=(3+4i)/5$ is accepted even though its denominator is $5$: equality, not denominator alone, decides the answer. No unbounded orbit search or numerical density test appears in this algorithm.

Under a signed-integer/positive-denominator encoding, this establishes a recursive rational predicate. The MRDP theorem then implies the existence of an existential-natural Diophantine representation~\cite{matiyasevich71}. That observation does not provide a small polynomial, a fixed small witness count, a canonical or unique witness, or an efficient compiler. In particular, this report proves no quartic impossibility theorem. The failure of a finite sign classifier cannot be promoted to impossibility of a polynomial equation with integer-quantified auxiliary variables.

\wtag\ [Source~28 supplies such a representation explicitly, with 81 positive witnesses, 44 equations and exact degree~12 (Theorem~\ref{smc:fd:thm:native}); it does not give a unique witness or a quartic.]

\section{The exact Zeno clock and the separate non Zeno machine}
\label{smc:fv:sec:time}
Primitive times are computed from the proofs, without trajectory execution:
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:durations}
t_L(z,u)=2(1+u)z,\qquad t_H(z,v)=2z,\qquad
t_T(x,z,c)=\frac{2(2-c)}{1-c}x+2z.
\end{equation}
Each anchor transfer takes $D$. Substituting the successive target positions in the four translations of an A block yields
\[
t_A(x,y,D)=16x-y/5+16D/3.
\]
For the reflected B block in its own incoming coordinates $(r,s,D)$, it yields
\[
t_B(r,s,D)=\frac{1016}{57}r+\frac{2972}{285}s+\frac{1388}{855}D.
\]
Substitute the preceding shear outputs into the next block's time and add the two transfers. The 114-event rotation duration is
\begin{align}
\ell_R&=\frac{222}{5}D+\frac{30512}{1425}x-\frac{9942}{475}y\nonumber\\
&=\frac{32134}{855}D+\frac{30512}{1425}\xi-\frac{9942}{475}\eta.\label{smc:fv:eq:rotationclock}
\end{align}
The final three half-scalings take $3(x_{\rm rot}+y_{\rm rot}+D)$, equal to $6D+(21/5)\xi-(3/5)\eta$. Thus the contracted macro duration is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:ell}
\ell(D,\xi,\eta)=\frac{37264}{855}D+\frac{36497}{1425}\xi-\frac{10227}{475}\eta.
\end{equation}
It is positive on the legal chamber, because it is a sum of strictly positive physical flights; negative coefficients in this coordinate expression do not mean negative times.

Every moving point remains in the interval $[0,D]$ of its macro's initial anchors. The twelve translation L primitives each take less than $4D$, the twelve H primitives each take at most $2D$, transfers take $2D$, and the three final half-scalings take less than $9D$ together. Hence $\ell<83D$. Since $D_n=2^{-n}D_0$, every valid infinite run has total elapsed time less than $166D_0$. All five strand positions converge to the fixed left anchor $0$.

For the exact sum, let $\ell$ also denote its row vector and use $N$ from~\eqref{smc:fv:eq:conjugacy}. All its eigenvalues have modulus $1/2$, so
\[
\sum_{n\geq0}\ell N^n=\ell(I-N)^{-1}.
\]
Solving, or verifying the row identity $T-TN=\ell$, gives~\eqref{smc:fv:eq:T}. In uncentered coordinates the same time is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:fv:eq:Tx}
T(D,x,y)=\frac{1204366}{11115}D+\frac{53102}{3705}x-\frac{144302}{3705}y.
\end{equation}
The formula is conditional on infinite validity. Evaluating it at an invalid seed does not establish a physical accumulation time. Rational inputs give rational time, in agreement with Report56's arbitrary-fixed-population rational-limit theorem [Theorem~\ref{smc:pm:thm:rational}].

\subsection{The 114 event variant must be reclosed}
The supplied JSON is the 138-event contracted machine. Its zero-based event 113 emits $Q_{114}$, beginning contraction. Repeating its first 114 events is not a periodic run of that unchanged rule table.

For a separate machine, retain rules 0 through 113, change the messenger output of rule 113 from $Q_{114}$ to $Q_0$, and discard unused later messenger and temporary labels. This makes the last reflection restore the original $Q_0$ outgoing section. Its return is $2M$, conjugate to $\diag(1,\rot)$, and its exact 36-row normalized chamber is unchanged. Every macro includes two full transfers between anchors a fixed distance $D>0$ apart, so its duration is at least $2D$. Its valid infinite executions are consequently non-Zeno. This proves the variant assertion of Theorem~\ref{smc:fv:thm:clock} without treating a prefix as a cyclic machine.
