\section{The sharp population boundary and what it does not say}
\label{smc:fv:sec:boundary}
Report56 [source~26] proves, for any fixed rational number-preserving machine and supplied complete periodic macro with at most four live signals, an effective Boolean formula of rational polynomial signs of degree at most two in the initial gaps. After denominator clearing, its explicit compiler yields a degree-at-most-four sum-of-squares polynomial with exactly one natural witness tuple on each accepted encoded input. Its hypotheses include the same outgoing collision section, distinct-speed conventions, restored ordered labels and co-location pattern, complete simultaneous batches, and positive time between batches used here.

The dimension calculation explains the threshold. For $N$ signals and $z\geq1$ zero gaps inside outgoing co-location groups, translation reduction gives $N-1-z\leq N-2$ free coordinates. At population at most four this is at most two. Our binary outgoing section at population five has three positive gaps. Dividing by scale leaves two affine coordinates, but their constant baseline is the third homogeneous coordinate. Therefore a planar normalized rotation with an axial offset does not contradict Report56's two-dimensional homogeneous classification.

\begin{corollary}[Sharp universal sign-classification boundary]\label{smc:fv:n11.1}
Under the fixed-complete-macro hypotheses of Report56, all machines with at most four live signals have finite polynomial-sign validity classifiers, whereas some five-live-signal machine does not. The latter failure already holds if agreement is required only on rational gaps or only on positive integer gaps.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
The lower-population direction is the separately audited Report56 theorem [Theorem~\ref{smc:pm:thm:validity}], whose frozen proof and independent audit are included as an explicit dependency. The upper counterexample is Theorem~\ref{smc:fv:thm:main}. No reproof of the former is claimed by the new five-signal audit.
\end{proof}

This is a boundary for a particular universal representation property of supplied complete macros. It is not a boundary for decidability of arbitrary signal machines, nor a claim that every five-signal macro is nonsemialgebraic. The rational predicate of this very counterexample is decidable. It does not invalidate Report56's rational accumulation theorem in larger populations. It also does not prove that five signals prevent unique-witness or quartic Diophantine certificates by other methods; a finite-sign frontend and existential-natural polynomial representation are different resources.

\section{Prior work and useful next questions}
\label{smc:fv:sec:prior}
Dai and Xia already prove that nontermination sets of general three-variable linear loops need not be semialgebraic; their Section 4 uses a diagonal positive-spectrum update~\cite{daixia}. Ouaknine and Worrell discuss a closely related irrational-rotation cone with a non-strict guard in Example 3.1~\cite{owloops}. Thus neither abstract three-variable nonsemialgebraicity nor the general rotation-cone mechanism is claimed as new here. The strict guard is essential to the precise disk-minus-oriented-orbit set in this report.

Signal-machine definitions, distance encodings, geometric multiplication/division, shrinking, and acceleration are established in the literature~\cite{accumulations,agcintro,agc5}. The physical claim documented here is a particular fully specified five-live-signal realization with an exact complete-word chamber and the stated arithmetic behavior. Bounded literature and repository overlap checks found no matching construction; they do not establish priority. The eight-speed, 169-type, and 138-event counts are certified counts, not optimality claims.

\wtag\ [The repository searches (\texttt{signal rotation}, \texttt{non-semialgebraic}, \texttt{periodic collision}, \texttt{conservative stacks}) were pinned at \texttt{7ba8f64e6}, as the shipped \path{27-fivesignal-science-companion-BOUNDARY_AND_ARITHMETIC.md} records; at that pin the collection had no five-signal or nonsemialgebraic validity result, and this Part now has them.]

Several next questions stay within the demonstrated result:
\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{smc:fv:q:reduce} Can the number of phases, types, or distinct speeds be reduced while preserving a complete guarded physical realization? A smaller count needs its own full chronology audit.
\item\label{smc:fv:q:frontend} Can a general machine-and-macro frontend automatically derive an exact chamber and produce a checkable completeness certificate? The present release replays exact algebra and static rule verification, not physical event selection.
\item\label{smc:fv:q:other} Which other rotations, contractions, or guard geometries are realizable with five live signals? The example disproves universal spectral restrictions, but is not a realization theorem for arbitrary rational matrices. (\wtag\ Answered for every rational rotation of infinite order and every positive rational scale by source~29 (Theorem~\ref{smc:rf:thm:main}), and for every orientation-preserving rational planar map by Part~XI's Report~60; other guard geometries stay open.)
\item\label{smc:fv:q:diophantine} Can the elementary inverse-power test here be converted into a useful small Diophantine certificate, with explicit witness or degree bounds? MRDP alone supplies no economical answer. (\wtag\ Answered by source~28: 81 positive witnesses, 44 equations, 344 gates and exact degree~12 (Theorem~\ref{smc:fd:thm:native}), and for the family by source~29's $1+80J$ witnesses and $1+43J$ equations; whether smaller witness or degree bounds exist stays open.)
\item\label{smc:fv:q:strict} How do strict versus non-strict guards change representability for other supplied macros? Boundary orbit orientation and actual multiple-collision semantics must remain explicit.
\end{enumerate}
None of these questions is needed to certify the result above. No universal Positivity-to-signal-macro reduction is asserted.

\section{Evidence and portable reproducibility}
\label{smc:fv:sec:evidence}
The construction is a conventional proof, not proof-assistant checked. Its independent audit rederived the two primitives, every endpoint map and guard row, both returns, all supporting-line distances, the tangent and actual triple contact, the rational-membership criterion, and the clocks. It checked each of the 138 rules against separately written phase templates, including exact velocities, temporary-label lifetimes, local output order, transparent crossings, and cyclic labels. It returned PASS for that stated scope.

The release distinguishes three kinds of evidence. Mathematical arguments establish the all-input claims. Exact independent algebra and static checks verify the displayed finite data. Rendering, hash, replay, and archive checks establish artifact integrity. Finite checks are not substitutes for the proofs, and an artifact hash is not a mathematical correctness certificate.

The packet's top-level README gives executable commands. Frozen construction, companion, and audit inputs are preserved under \file{science/} and \file{independent_audit/}; the separate lower-population proof and audit are under \file{dependency_report56/}. The machine-readable rule table is \file{science/construction/RULES.json}; the guards are \file{science/construction/GUARDS.txt}. The exhaustive local-order receipt is \file{independent_audit/all_138_local_rule_checks.tsv}.

The portable adapter runs only the two newly authored independent checkers after verifying their exact approved hashes. It rebinds their input/output path constants in memory, leaving the frozen checker bytes unchanged, and sends every output to an exclusive fresh directory. It compares regenerated substantive receipts and captured stdout with pinned expected values. It does not execute the construction's emitter, its algebra or membership scripts, the saved JSON rule program, or a physical simulator. Its operations are exact rational algebra and inert structural validation. Release tools likewise refuse existing output targets and build deterministic PDFs and ZIPs in fresh locations; the manifest binds every included file. The README states the local tool prerequisites and the trusted external manifest pin required for integrity verification.

\section{The result and the objects being represented}
\label{smc:fd:sec:result}
Throughout, $\NN=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ and $\Np=\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$. A positive witness is an ordinary independent integer variable ranging over $\Np$. The input domain is also $\Np$; there is no promise that an input satisfies a separate code-validation test.

The machine is the fixed five-live-signal, rational, number-preserving machine of the pinned physical proof~\cite{fvproof}. Its outgoing section consists of four markers at $0<x<y<D$ and the right-moving messenger co-located with the left marker. The three positive section gaps are
\[
(g_1,g_2,g_3)=(x,y-x,D-y).
\]
Its complete contracted macro has 138 strictly time-separated binary collisions and return matrix
\[
M=\frac1{30}\begin{pmatrix}7&-2&10\\14&11&-10\\-6&6&15\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Normalized centered coordinates rotate by $(3+4i)/5$. We write $\Valid(g_1,g_2,g_3)$ when that specified complete macro can be iterated indefinitely. The inherited theorem includes legality of the complete physical collision word and its strict tie exclusions. It is not only an assertion about iterating a matrix. Report 57 [source~27] provides the physical proof and its independent audit; the exact proof and audit bytes used here are included in this package.

\begin{theorem}[Native positive-input certificate]
\label{smc:fd:thm:native}
The frozen arithmetic source \path{science/evidence/three-input-linear.dag.json} defines an explicit polynomial
\[
F_{\mathrm{nat}}\in\Z[g_1,g_2,g_3,w_1,\ldots,w_{81}]
\]
of exact total degree 12 such that, for every $(g_1,g_2,g_3)\in\Np^3$,
\[
\Valid(g_1,g_2,g_3)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists (w_1,\ldots,w_{81})\in\Np^{81}: F_{\mathrm{nat}}(g_1,g_2,g_3,w)=0.
\]
The source has 44 equation residuals and 344 binary arithmetic gates, consisting of 136 multiplications, 110 additions, and 98 subtractions.
\end{theorem}

The polynomial is given explicitly by the sum of the squares of the fourteen outer residuals in Section~\ref{smc:fd:sec:outer} and the two fifteen-equation power systems in Section~\ref{smc:fd:app:instances}, after the positive-domain substitutions of Section~\ref{smc:fd:sec:domains}. The frozen DAG fixes the literal expression sharing and hence the gate count. There are no exponentiation, division, comparison, or logical primitives in that source.

For naturals $a,b$, put
\[
\pair(a,b)=\frac{(a+b)(a+b+1)}2+b,
\qquad
\Ccode(g_1,g_2,g_3)=1+\pair\bigl(g_1-1,\pair(g_2-1,g_3-1)\bigr).
\]
The half in this mathematical definition is eliminated from the certificate by the two integer equations of Section~\ref{smc:fd:sec:cantor}.

\begin{theorem}[Paid one-input certificate]
\label{smc:fd:thm:one}
The frozen source \path{science/evidence/one-input-linear.dag.json} defines a polynomial
\[
F_{\mathrm{one}}\in\Z[z,w_1,\ldots,w_{85}]
\]
of exact total degree 12 with the following property. Every $z\in\Np$ has a unique decoded positive gap triple $g$, and
\[
\Valid(g)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists w\in\Np^{85}:F_{\mathrm{one}}(z,w)=0.
\]
Its 46 residuals and 367 binary gates include all decoding costs: 144 multiplications, 118 additions, and 105 subtractions.
\end{theorem}

\paragraph{What is and is not claimed.}
These are explicit existential positive-integer representations. The inherited impossibility of a finite polynomial-sign classifier does not preclude them. Neither theorem is a real-witness equivalence or a claim of finite-fold, singlefold, or unique witnesses. Signed-pair adapters in fact give infinitely many witnesses for each solvable input. No optimality, circuit lower bound, novelty priority, undecidability, or new physical population threshold is established. The construction does not use generic MRDP representability as its final representation, a variable-length conjunction, an unexpanded power oracle, or a hidden witness array.

\section{The inherited physical criterion in integer coordinates}
\label{smc:fd:sec:geometry}
Define the following arithmetic expressions:
\begin{align}
D&=g_1+g_2+g_3,&x&=g_1,&y&=g_1+g_2,\label{smc:fd:eq:gapcoords}\\
A&=3x-D,&B&=3y-2D,\label{smc:fd:eq:AB}\\
\Delta(g)&=4D^2-205(A^2+B^2),\label{smc:fd:eq:deficit}\\
U&=6A-13B,&V&=13A+6B.\label{smc:fd:eq:UV}
\end{align}
We reserve $\Delta(g)$ for the determined integer deficit and $\delta$ for its nonnegative witness below. The normalized centered point is
\[
\omega=\frac{A+iB}{3D}.
\]
The critical squared radius and tangency point from the physical theorem are
\[
\rho^2=\frac4{1845},\qquad
p=\frac4{205}-\frac{26}{615}i=\frac2{615}(6-13i).
\]
Direct rational calculation gives
\begin{align}
\rho^2-|\omega|^2&=\frac{\Delta(g)}{1845D^2},\label{smc:fd:eq:radiusidentity}\\
\gamma:=\frac{\omega}{p}&=\frac{U+iV}{2D},\label{smc:fd:eq:eta}\\
U^2+V^2&=205(A^2+B^2).\label{smc:fd:eq:norm}
\end{align}
Because $D>0$, the deficit has precisely the radius-deficit sign. On $\Delta(g)=0$, the number $\gamma$ has modulus one.

\begin{theorem}[Inherited complete-macro validity criterion]
\label{smc:fd:thm:physical}
For the fixed machine and every positive gap triple,
\begin{equation}
\Valid(g)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Delta(g)>0\quad\text{or}\quad
\left[\Delta(g)=0\ \text{and}\
\gamma\ne\left(\frac{3-4i}{5}\right)^m\text{ for every }m\in\NN\right].
\label{smc:fd:eq:physical}
\end{equation}
Inputs with $\Delta(g)<0$ are invalid. The $m=0$ contact is excluded.
\end{theorem}

Theorem~\ref{smc:fd:thm:physical} is the precise inherited dependency, independently checked in the pinned physical audit~\cite{fvaudit}. Its proof uses the complete strict chamber, the unique tangency point, and the infinite-order normalized rotation. It excludes an omitted triple contact at the tangency. The contraction cancels upon normalization, so the corresponding explicitly closed uncontracted machine has the same geometric criterion; our primary predicate remains the fixed contracted macro above. We do not reconstruct or execute its collision program here.

\wtag\ [Theorem~\ref{smc:fd:thm:physical} is source~27's Proposition~\ref{smc:fv:prop:K} in the integer coordinates $A=3\xi$, $B=3\eta$, with its exclusion test~\eqref{smc:fv:eq:power}; it is printed and proved there, and is not re-proved here.]

The inherited real, rational, and integer finite-polynomial-sign obstructions concern formulas with finitely many sign atoms in the input coordinates alone. The new certificate instead quantifies over 81 or 85 positive integer auxiliaries. The scopes are different and compatible. Section~\ref{smc:fd:sec:signcorollary} adds an elementary sign obstruction specific to the paid integer encoding.

\section{The complete outer certificate and its positive domains}
\label{smc:fd:sec:outer}
In addition to the input gaps, use the following conceptual integer quantities:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
\toprule
Domain & Quantities\\
\midrule
Natural & $\delta,n,k,L_C,H_C,L_S,H_S$\\
Positive & $h,q,r,s,t,J_{\rm acc}$\\
Signed & $u,v,a_1,a_2,a_3,C,S,\kappa$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Let the two explicit power systems supply positive outputs $P,T$, using the common natural exponent $n$, with bases 5 and $3+4\brad$, respectively, where
\begin{equation}
 \brad=4P+1.\label{smc:fd:eq:b}
\end{equation}
The statements $P=5^n$ and $T=(3+4\brad)^n$ are conclusions of those systems, not power gates or extra defining equations. All names such as $D,A,B,U,V,\brad$ denote expressions expanded into the DAG, not uncharged independent leaves.

The fourteen outer equations are
\begin{align}
4D^2&=205(A^2+B^2)+\delta,\tag{O1}\label{smc:fd:eq:O1}\\
U&=hu,\tag{O2}\\
V&=hv,\tag{O3}\\
2D&=hq,\tag{O4}\\
a_1u+a_2v+a_3q&=1,\tag{O5}\label{smc:fd:eq:bezout}\\
q&=Pr,\tag{O6}\\
r&=5k+s,\tag{O7}\\
s+t&=5,\tag{O8}\label{smc:fd:eq:remainder}\\
C+P&=L_C,\tag{O9}\\
P-C&=H_C,\tag{O10}\\
S+P&=L_S,\tag{O11}\\
P-S&=H_S,\tag{O12}\label{smc:fd:eq:bounds}\\
T-C-\brad S&=\kappa(\brad^2+1),\tag{O13}\label{smc:fd:eq:extraction}\\
\delta^2+(r-1)^2+(u-C)^2+(v+S)^2&=J_{\rm acc}.\tag{O14}\label{smc:fd:eq:accept}
\end{align}
The domains distinguish three essential cases. First, $\delta\in\NN$ allows the critical circle while excluding every exterior point. Second, the four bound slacks are natural, so the coefficient bounds are closed. Third, $J_{\rm acc}>0$ makes the final acceptance test strict. Also, both $s$ and $t$ must be positive.

\subsection{Every final quantifier is positive}
\label{smc:fd:sec:domains}
Every natural $z$ is replaced by one positive leaf $z^+$ through
\[
z=z^+-1.
\]
Every signed $z$ is replaced by two positive leaves $z^{\mathrm{pos}},z^{\mathrm{neg}}$ through
\[
z=z^{\mathrm{pos}}-z^{\mathrm{neg}}.
\]
For any integer $z$, one possible pair is $(\max(z,0)+1,\max(-z,0)+1)$. Thus this replacement is onto $\Z$. It uses one subtraction gate, rather than two shifts followed by a subtraction. The source names the leaves \path{.Plus}, \path{.Positive}, and \path{.Negative}.

Each directly positive quantity is one positive leaf. Thus the outer system contributes
\[
7+6+2\cdot8=29
\]
positive leaves. Each power system contributes 26, including its output. The native total is $29+26+26=81$; $P$ and $T$ are not counted twice.

For each named equation, form its left side minus its right side. Let $\res$ be the fixed list of 44 resulting residuals, including the thirty power residuals. The certificate is the integer polynomial
\begin{equation}
F_{\mathrm{nat}}=\sum_{R\in\res}R^2.\label{smc:fd:eq:sos}
\end{equation}
Over integers, $F_{\mathrm{nat}}=0$ is equivalent to every residual being zero, since each square is nonnegative. All loops used to describe this source range over fixed lists, never over an input or witness value. For the one-input source, the two decoder residuals are included in the same fixed sum.

\section{Primitive Gaussian fractions and the canonical exponent}
\label{smc:fd:sec:fraction}
\begin{lemma}[Exact common denominator]\label{smc:fd:n4.1}
Equations (O2)--(O5), with the stated domains, force
\[
h=\gcd(U,V,2D),\qquad
(u,v,q)=(U/h,V/h,2D/h),\qquad \gcd(u,v,q)=1.
\]
The positive integer $q$ is the least common positive denominator of both rational coordinates $u/q$ and $v/q$. Conversely these values admit signed B\'ezout coefficients satisfying (O5).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Any common divisor of $u,v,q$ divides the left side of (O5), so divides 1. Since $h>0$, equations (O2)--(O4) then give
\[
\gcd(U,V,2D)=h\gcd(u,v,q)=h.
\]
Conversely, $2D>0$ makes the gcd positive, and its primitive quotient admits an ordinary three-term integer B\'ezout identity.

If a positive integer $d$ clears both rational coordinates, then $q\mid du$ and $q\mid dv$. Multiply (O5) by $d$. Every term on the left is divisible by $q$, including $a_3dq$, so $q\mid d$. Since $q$ itself clears both coordinates, it is their exact common denominator. This proof does not assume that either coordinate is individually in lowest terms.
\end{proof}

Negative values of $U$ or $V$ cause no difficulty. If both vanish, $\gcd(0,0,2D)=2D$, so $u=v=0$ and $q=1$; choosing $a_3=1$ suffices. Thus the center has no exceptional or singular branch. The signed adapters preserve all B\'ezout coefficients.

\begin{lemma}[Canonical valuation]\label{smc:fd:n4.2}
Assuming $P=5^n$, equations (O6)--(O8) force
\[
n=v_5(q),\qquad q=5^n r,\qquad 5\nmid r,
\]
and conversely these values always supply the required witnesses.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Positivity of $s,t$ and $s+t=5$ give $s\in\{1,2,3,4\}$. Hence $r=5k+s$ is positive and not divisible by 5, with $k\in\NN$. Equation (O6) gives $q=5^n r$, which uniquely fixes $n$ as the 5-adic valuation. Conversely write $q=5^n r$ with $5\nmid r$ and use the division algorithm $r=5k+s$, $1\le s\le4$, then set $t=5-s>0$.
\end{proof}

In particular $q=1$ gives $n=0,r=1,k=0,s=1,t=4$. These clauses are imposed at every input, including interior points. There is no boundary selector and no uncharged test for whether the input lies on the critical circle.

\section{Bounded extraction of the Gaussian power}
\label{smc:fd:sec:extract}
For each $n\in\NN$, define ordinary integers $C_n,S_n$ by
\[
C_n+iS_n=(3+4i)^n.
\]
The modulus identity gives $C_n^2+S_n^2=25^n$, hence
\[
|C_n|,|S_n|\le5^n=P.
\]
These names are used in the proof; they are not additional witness variables or source operations.

\begin{lemma}[Exact bounded residue extraction]\label{smc:fd:n5.1}
If $P=5^n$, $\brad=4P+1$, and $T=(3+4\brad)^n$, then (O9)--(O13) are solvable and force $(C,S)=(C_n,S_n)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Reducing the binomial expansion in $\Z[X]/(X^2+1)$ gives
\[
(3+4X)^n\equiv C_n+S_nX\pmod{X^2+1}.
\]
Substitute the integer $X=\brad$. Then
\[
T\equiv C_n+\brad S_n\pmod{\brad^2+1}.
\]
Consequently the true pair satisfies (O13) with an integer $\kappa$, and its four closed bounds give natural slacks in (O9)--(O12).

Conversely those four equations impose $-P\le C,S\le P$. Put $d_C=C-C_n$ and $d_S=S-S_n$. The remainder congruence gives
\[
\brad^2+1\mid d_C+\brad d_S,
\]
while
\begin{align*}
|d_C+\brad d_S|&\le2P(1+\brad)=8P^2+4P\\
&<16P^2+8P+2=\brad^2+1.
\end{align*}
Thus $d_C+\brad d_S=0$. If $d_S\ne0$, integrality gives $|\brad d_S|\ge \brad$, whereas $|d_C|\le2P<\brad$. This contradicts $d_C=-\brad d_S$, so $d_S=0$ and then $d_C=0$.
\end{proof}

There is no restriction on the size or sign of $\kappa$. The bound argument controls the remainder pair, not the quotient. At $n=0$ the values are
\[
P=1,\quad \brad=5,\quad T=1,\quad C=1,\quad S=0.
\]
The value $C=P$ lies on a closed bound; making every bound slack positive would incorrectly exclude it. The strict inequality used in the uniqueness proof follows from $P\ge1$ and requires no extra witness or comparison gate.

\section{The strict final equation and the two directions}
\label{smc:fd:sec:iff}
\begin{lemma}[Recognition of the forbidden inverse orbit]\label{smc:fd:n6.1}
For the primitive fraction and canonical exponent above,
\[
\gamma=\left(\frac{3-4i}{5}\right)^m\text{ for some }m\in\NN
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
r=1,\quad u=C_n,\quad v=-S_n.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For $m\ge1$, reduce the Gaussian numerator modulo 5. Since
\[
3-4i\equiv3+i\pmod5,\qquad (3+i)^2\equiv3+i\pmod5,
\]
we have $(3-4i)^m\equiv3+i\pmod5$. Both numerator coordinates are nonzero modulo 5. Thus their joint denominator after division by $5^m$ is exactly $5^m$. This calculation occurs in the quadratic quotient ring over $\Z/5\Z$; it does not assume that this ring is a field. At $m=0$, the point is 1 and its denominator is 1.

If $\gamma$ equals such a point, its exact common denominator $q$ is $5^m$. The canonical factorization $q=5^n r$ therefore gives $m=n,r=1$. Equality of the primitive rational coordinates gives $(u,v)=(C_n,-S_n)$. Conversely these equalities and $q=5^n$ imply $\gamma=(C_n-iS_n)/5^n=((3-4i)/5)^n$.
\end{proof}

\wtag\ [The first paragraph of this proof is source~27's Lemma~\ref{smc:fv:lem:denominator}, proved again; source~29's Lemma~\ref{smc:rf:lem:denom} is the general version.]

The sign in (O14) is deliberately $v+S$. For example, the forward boundary point $(3+4i)/5$ has $u=3,v=4,q=5,n=1$, so $v+S=8$. Replacing the plus by a minus would confuse the accepted forward orbit with the excluded inverse orbit.

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{smc:fd:thm:native}, assuming the power lemma proved next]
\emph{Soundness.} Suppose a positive-integer assignment makes $F_{\mathrm{nat}}=0$. By the sum-of-squares identity every residual vanishes. Equation (O1) gives $\Delta(g)=\delta\ge0$. The two power systems give $P=5^n$ and $T=(3+4\brad)^n$. Sections~\ref{smc:fd:sec:fraction} and~\ref{smc:fd:sec:extract} supply the primitive fraction, canonical exponent, and exact coefficients $C_n,S_n$.

Because $J_{\rm acc}>0$, equation (O14) says that not all of $\delta$, $r-1$, $u-C_n$, and $v+S_n$ vanish. If $\delta>0$, the first alternative of the inherited criterion holds. If $\delta=0$, the preceding lemma says that the input is not a forbidden inverse-orbit point. Theorem~\ref{smc:fd:thm:physical} therefore gives infinite complete-macro validity.

\emph{Completeness.} Suppose $\Valid(g)$. Set $\delta=\Delta(g)\in\NN$. Choose the positive gcd and primitive quotients, and choose signed B\'ezout coefficients. Factor the positive denominator as $q=5^n r$, $5\nmid r$, and choose $k,s,t$ by the division algorithm. The constructive power lemma supplies all auxiliaries for the two systems at exponent $n$. Set $C=C_n,S=S_n$; choose their four natural bound slacks and the integer quotient $\kappa$ from Section~\ref{smc:fd:sec:extract}.

If $\delta>0$, the left side of (O14) is positive. If $\delta=0$, validity excludes the forbidden inverse orbit, so at least one of $r-1,u-C_n,v+S_n$ is nonzero. In either case set $J_{\rm acc}$ equal to the positive sum of squares. Replace every natural and signed quantity by positive leaves using Section~\ref{smc:fd:sec:domains}. All 44 equations then hold simultaneously and $F_{\mathrm{nat}}=0$.
\end{proof}

This is a finite mathematical argument in both directions. It performs no unbounded orbit search and needs no density argument after the physical theorem has been supplied.

\section{A fully explicit positive integer power system}
\label{smc:fd:sec:power}
We now specify and justify the only number-theoretic subsystem. Its exact dependency is the pinned source \path{Mathlib/NumberTheory/PellMatiyasevic.lean}, identified with mathlib4 commit
\sha{ac77769fabe23cb237559e7f56578dbead91499f}
The actual dependency checked here is the included local file, SHA-256
\sha{993760c797ad0ff66fa77064a616fce779550bc745cbf6c44e04f392fd0bed0a}
The theorem statements and constructive proof text were read as inert source. This work is not a new Lean kernel build or a new authentication of the remote commit. The independent specialization review~\cite{fdpoweraudit} records exact local line references and domain checks.

\subsection{Fifteen equations and twenty six leaves}
Fix an integer base $B_0\ge2$, a natural exponent $e$, and a positive output $o$. Introduce directly positive quantities
\[
o,w,\Theta,g,x,y,u,v,s,t,q_b,q_v,J_p,
\]
two positive leaves $a_{-1},\beta_{-1}$ and the expressions
\[
a=a_{-1}+1,\qquad\beta=\beta_{-1}+1,
\]
and eleven natural quantities
\[
d_{wb},d_{wk},d_{yk},\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,
\tau_1,\tau_2,\rho_1,\rho_2.
\]
The natural quantities each use one positive leaf minus one. Set $k_0=e+1$ and $m_0=B_0o$ as expressions. The complete system is
\begin{align}
x^2&=1+(a^2-1)y^2,\tag{P1}\label{smc:fd:eq:P1}\\
u^2&=1+(a^2-1)v^2,\tag{P2}\\
s^2&=1+(\beta^2-1)t^2,\tag{P3}\\
\beta&=1+4yq_b,\tag{P4}\\
\beta+u\alpha_1&=a+u\alpha_2,\tag{P5}\\
v&=y^2q_v,\tag{P6}\\
s+u\sigma_1&=x+u\sigma_2,\tag{P7}\\
t+4y\tau_1&=k_0+4y\tau_2,\tag{P8}\\
y&=k_0+d_{yk},\tag{P9}\\
w&=B_0+d_{wb},\tag{P10}\\
w&=k_0+d_{wk},\tag{P11}\\
\Theta&=m_0+J_p,\tag{P12}\\
a^2&=1+\bigl((w+1)^2-1\bigr)(wg)^2,\tag{P13}\label{smc:fd:eq:P13}\\
2aB_0&=\Theta+(B_0^2+1),\tag{P14}\\
x+\Theta\rho_1&=y(a-B_0)+m_0+\Theta\rho_2.\tag{P15}\label{smc:fd:eq:P15}
\end{align}
These are polynomial equations. The label $\POWER$ is only a name for this finite system. It is not an additional symbol in the resulting polynomial. Section~\ref{smc:fd:app:instances} prints both actual instances with their bases and output expressions substituted.

There are 13 directly positive leaves, 2 shifted-positive leaves, and 11 natural-adapter leaves, for a total of 26 including $o$. In the literal frozen source each instance has 70 body gates: 31 multiplications, 24 additions, and 15 subtractions. This includes all parameter shifts, natural adapters, the exponent shift, and multiplication $B_0o$; the global residual-square assembly is counted separately.

\begin{lemma}[Power-system equivalence]
\label{smc:fd:lem:power}
For every $B_0\ge2$, $e\in\NN$, and $o\in\Np$, the fifteen equations have the other 25 positive leaves if and only if $o=B_0^e$.
\end{lemma}

\subsection{The precise constructive dependencies}
The pinned source defines natural Pell sequences $(x_j(a),y_j(a))$ with initial pair $(1,0)$ and parameter $a>1$. Its theorem \texttt{Pell.matiyasevic}, lines 760--766, identifies the pair at index $k$ by three Pell equations, $k\le y$, and either the zero-index pair $(1,0)$ or natural witnesses with
\[
\begin{gathered}
\beta>1,\qquad \beta\equiv1\pmod{4y},\qquad
\beta\equiv a\pmod u,\qquad v>0,\qquad y^2\mid v,\\
s\equiv x\pmod u,\qquad t\equiv k\pmod{4y}.
\end{gathered}
\]
Its constructive direction is at lines 767--806 and reverse direction at 807--847. Equations (P1)--(P9) are precisely the nonzero branch with $k=k_0=e+1$.

The theorem \texttt{Pell.eq\_pow\_of\_pell}, lines 860--864, states in its nonzero-base, nonzero-index branch that $B_0^{k_0}=m_0$ is equivalent to natural witnesses $w,a,\Theta,g$, with $a>1$, satisfying
\[
\begin{gathered}
x_{k_0}(a)\equiv y_{k_0}(a)(a-B_0)+m_0\pmod \Theta,\\
2aB_0=\Theta+(B_0^2+1),\quad m_0<\Theta,\quad B_0\le w,\quad k_0\le w,\\
a^2-\bigl((w+1)^2-1\bigr)(wg)^2=1.
\end{gathered}
\]
The source writes these expressions in natural arithmetic. Its constructive proof is at lines 865--897 and reverse proof at 898--928. Equations (P10)--(P15) encode these conditions. The source theorem's modulus is here named $\Theta$; it must not be confused with the Pell coordinate $t$ in (P3) and (P8).

\subsection{Integer subtraction and congruence adapters}
For naturals $X,Y$, the truncated-natural equation $X-Y=1$ is equivalent to the integer equation $X=Y+1$, since the positive result forces $X>Y$. This converts all three ordinary Pell equations and (P13) in both directions. The inner quantities $a^2-1$, $\beta^2-1$, and $(w+1)^2-1$ are nonnegative under their domains.

The remaining difference $a-B_0$ must also be checked. Equations (P10) and (P13), together with $g>0$, give $w\ge B_0\ge2$ and
\[
a^2=1+(w^2+2w)w^2g^2>w^2.
\]
Thus $a>w\ge B_0$, so integer subtraction agrees with the theorem's natural subtraction before the power conclusion is invoked. Conversely, a natural witness $g=0$ from the constructive theorem would force $a^2=1$, contradicting $a>1$. Hence restricting $g$ to be positive loses no witness.

For any positive modulus $d$, the equation
\[
p+dr_1=q+dr_2,\qquad r_1,r_2\in\NN,
\]
is equivalent to $p\equiv q\pmod d$. If $p-q=dz$, choose $r_1=\max(-z,0)$ and $r_2=\max(z,0)$. This encodes either quotient sign, including zero. The four pairs in (P5), (P7), (P8), and (P15) are all retained. In particular $\beta-a=u(\alpha_2-\alpha_1)$, with the same orientation as the corresponding source congruence.

Equation (P12) has a positive $J_p$, not a natural slack. It therefore supplies the strict modulus bound $m_0<\Theta$. The source reverse proof uses this strictness to identify congruent natural numbers; replacing it by a weak inequality is not justified.

\subsection{Both directions and exponent zero}
\begin{proof}[Proof of Lemma~\ref{smc:fd:lem:power}]
\emph{Soundness.} From (P1)--(P9), the domains, and the exact subtraction conversion, the nonzero branch of \texttt{Pell.matiyasevic} applies at $k_0=e+1\ge1$. It yields
\[
x=x_{k_0}(a),\qquad y=y_{k_0}(a).
\]
Equations (P10)--(P15) then provide all conditions of the positive branch of \texttt{Pell.eq\_pow\_of\_pell}, including $m_0<\Theta$ and the justified natural subtraction $a-B_0$. Thus
\[
B_0^{e+1}=m_0=B_0o.
\]
Cancel positive $B_0$ to obtain $o=B_0^e$.

\emph{Completeness.} If $o=B_0^e$, set $k_0=e+1$ and $m_0=B_0o=B_0^{k_0}$. The constructive power theorem supplies natural $w,a,\Theta,g$ with its conditions. Here $w\ge B_0\ge2$, $\Theta>m_0>0$, and $g>0$ as shown above. Choose the positive leaf $a_{-1}=a-1$, positive $J_p=\Theta-m_0$, and natural $d_{wb}=w-B_0,d_{wk}=w-k_0$.

Take $x=x_{k_0}(a)$ and $y=y_{k_0}(a)$ and apply the constructive Pell-pair theorem. The zero branch is impossible because $k_0\le y$ and $k_0\ge1$. It supplies natural $u,v,s,t,\beta$ in the nonzero branch. Their stronger positive requirements follow: $y\ge k_0\ge1$; the Pell equations make $x,u,s>0$; $v>0$ is explicit in the theorem; and $\beta>1$ gives a positive $\beta_{-1}$. Divisibility $y^2\mid v$ gives a positive $q_v$, and $\beta\equiv1\pmod{4y}$ with $\beta>1$ gives a positive $q_b$. Finally $t\equiv k_0\pmod{4y}$ excludes $t=0$, because $1\le k_0\le y<4y$.

Set $d_{yk}=y-k_0\in\NN$ and choose the four natural quotient pairs as above. Replace all natural quantities by their positive-adapter leaves. This gives all required positive leaves simultaneously.
\end{proof}

At exponent $e=0$, the shifted index is $k_0=1$. Both proofs still use only the positive-index theorem branches; cancellation yields $o=1$. No selector or separate exponent-zero case is introduced in the source.

In the actual certificate, the first base is 5. The second base is
\[
3+4\brad=3+4(4P+1)=16P+7\ge23,
\]
because $P$ is a positive leaf even before the first module's semantics is used. Both modules use the same natural exponent $n$. Thus every hypothesis is justified without circular reasoning.

\section{Paid decoding to one positive input}
\label{smc:fd:sec:cantor}
For an external input $z>0$, introduce positive gap witnesses $g_1,g_2,g_3$ and one natural witness $j$. Put $a=g_1-1,b_0=g_2-1,c=g_3-1$; the temporary name $b_0$ here is unrelated to the extraction radix $\brad$. Add
\begin{align}
2j&=(b_0+c)(b_0+c+1)+2c,\tag{D1}\label{smc:fd:eq:decode1}\\
2(z-1)&=(a+j)(a+j+1)+2j.\tag{D2}\label{smc:fd:eq:decode2}
\end{align}
All four quantities are represented by positive leaves, with $j=j^+-1$. These are two ordinary integer polynomial equations, not a pairing-function primitive or a promise that the code is legal.

For any $N\in\NN$, there is a unique diagonal $d\in\NN$ such that
\[
\frac{d(d+1)}2\le N<\frac{(d+1)(d+2)}2.
\]
The offset $s=N-d(d+1)/2$ satisfies $0\le s\le d$, giving the unique pair $(d-s,s)$ with Cantor value $N$. Apply this first to $N=z-1$, obtaining $(a,j)$, and then to $j$, obtaining $(b_0,c)$. Consequently every positive input decodes to exactly one positive gap triple. Conversely every positive triple gives a positive code satisfying both equations.

Adding these residuals to the sum of squares and using Theorem~\ref{smc:fd:thm:native} proves Theorem~\ref{smc:fd:thm:one}. The uniqueness of decoded gaps is only a property of the transport. It does not imply uniqueness of the other existential witnesses.

The decoder contributes 17 body gates: 6 multiplications, 6 additions, and 5 subtractions. Two extra residual differences, their two squares, and two additions to the existing sum add 6 gates. Thus the exact increase is four witnesses, two equations, and 23 gates:
\[
8\ \text{multiplications}+8\ \text{additions}+7\ \text{subtractions}.
\]
The decoder residuals have degree two, so they do not alter the degree-twelve leading form.

\begin{proposition}[Exact leading homogeneous form]\label{smc:fd:n9.1}
For both primary sources, the total degree is exactly 12. In the actual independent positive leaves, its homogeneous degree-twelve part is
\begin{equation}
 w_5^8g_5^4+w_c^8g_c^4,\label{smc:fd:eq:topform}
\end{equation}
where the subscripts distinguish the two power systems.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Every outer residual has degree at most three, and every power residual has degree at most six. Each (P13) residual has leading term $-w^4g^2$, since
\[
a^2-1-\bigl((w+1)^2-1\bigr)(wg)^2
\]
has that unique degree-six term. The other residuals have smaller degree. Squaring and summing therefore gives exactly~\eqref{smc:fd:eq:topform}, with both coefficients equal to $+1$. The two monomials use distinct power-module leaves, so this homogeneous part is nonzero. The decoder residuals have degree two. Hence the joint degree in inputs and positive witness leaves is exactly twelve in both cases.
\end{proof}

The independent exact expansion confirmed the entire leading form, not only a syntactic upper bound. It also found every declared input and witness in the collected polynomial support. Graph liveness and algebraic liveness both hold; these are different checks.

\subsection{Malformed candidates identify essential guards}
At the rejected contact, take $n=0$ but falsely choose $(C,S)=(27,0)$. With $P=1,\brad=5,T=1$, equation (O13) still holds for $\kappa=-1$, and the final square sum is 676. The upper bound blocks it because $P-C=-26$. The independent audit constructed full positive leaves for all other equations and evaluated each raw DAG: the only failed residual was \path{complex.C_upper}, equal to $-26$, with total output 676.

If primitive B\'ezout were omitted, the contact could be represented by $(u,v,q)=(5,0,5)$, with $n=1,r=1$ and $(C,S)=(3,4)$. The false acceptance sum would be 20. Every B\'ezout combination of $(5,0,5)$ is divisible by 5, so the actual primitive equation forbids it.

At the forbidden point $(3-4i)/5$, undercounting $n$ as 0 would give $r=5$ and a false acceptance sum 36. It would require $s=5,t=0$, or $s=0$ after carrying, each violating positivity. Allowing a natural $J_{\rm acc}$ would admit the contact with $J_{\rm acc}=0$. Allowing a signed radius slack would admit exterior examples such as $(1,1,10)$, where $\Delta=-82449$, despite a positive squared acceptance sum. These examples show why the actual domains cannot be weakened.

\subsection{Complete positive Pell witnesses at exponent zero}
The independent audit did not merely substitute a claimed power output for these fixtures. It constructed all positive Pell auxiliaries for bases $B_0\in\{5,23\}$ and exponent zero. Put $w=B_0$ and choose
\[
a=x_w(w+1),\qquad g=y_w(w+1)/w.
\]
The elementary Pell recurrence gives $x_j\equiv1$ and $y_j\equiv j\pmod w$, proving this quotient integral. At shifted index $k_0=1$, take
\[
x=a,\quad y=1,\quad u=2a^2-1,\quad v=2a.
\]
Choose $\beta\equiv a\pmod u$, $\beta\equiv1\pmod4$, with $\beta>1$, then $s=\beta,t=1$. The remaining quotients and slacks follow from the displayed equations. Here $u$ is odd, so the two congruences for $\beta$ are compatible. The complete stored witness list has largest entry 78 decimal digits.

For each of the four DAG variants, full assignments were evaluated at the center $(1,1,1)$, the accepted boundary point $\gamma=-1$ with gaps $(193,243,179)$, and the accepted boundary point $\gamma=i$ with gaps $(231,191,193)$. These are twelve complete positive zero evaluations, stored in \path{independent_audit/full-positive-witnesses.json}. At the rejected contact, setting $J_{\rm acc}=1$ leaves only the final residual $-1$ and output 1. Changing a paid code while holding its decoded gaps fixed gives the expected decoder failure.

Every positive witness was separately incremented by one. All non-neutral mutations failed; the only neutral mutations were B\'ezout leaves multiplying a zero component. Neutrality in those cases is mathematically expected and was not misreported as a failed test.

The nonzero-exponent orbit and outer-arithmetic tests compute ordinary power outputs directly. They do not instantiate the potentially enormous full Pell auxiliary tuples for all such exponents. The all-exponent equivalence is proved by the pinned constructive theorems and the specialization in Section~\ref{smc:fd:sec:power}, not by extrapolating finite tests.

\section{An elementary obstruction for the paid integer encoding}
\label{smc:fd:sec:signcorollary}
The following encoding corollary is independent of the certificate's witness count or degree. It was checked in the independent audit and is included for clarity about the different representations.

\begin{corollary}\label{smc:fd:n11.1}
The transported predicate on positive codes cannot agree everywhere with a finite Boolean combination of univariate real-polynomial sign tests.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Each univariate real polynomial is either identically zero or has the sign of its leading coefficient at every sufficiently large positive argument. A finite Boolean combination of its sign atoms is therefore eventually constant.

For every positive integer $t$, the center gaps $(t,t,t)$ are accepted. The contact gaps $(217t,167t,231t)$ are rejected by homogeneity and Theorem~\ref{smc:fd:thm:physical}. Their respective Cantor codes are unbounded as $t$ grows. Thus arbitrarily large positive codes occur in both outcome classes, contradicting eventual constancy.
\end{proof}

This is an elementary statement about finite sign classifiers under this particular encoding. It establishes no arithmetic-circuit lower bound, undecidability theorem, physical threshold, or obstruction to existential positive-integer witnesses. Theorem~\ref{smc:fd:thm:one} explicitly supplies such witnesses.

\section{Reproducibility and provenance}
\label{smc:fd:sec:reproduce}
The release includes the complete frozen science packet and independent audit, byte-for-byte, alongside this editable LaTeX source and its rendered PDF. The physical proof and physical audit are the exact dependencies copied into \path{science/sources/}; the whole physical paper need not be duplicated in this manuscript. The pinned Pell source and its Apache 2.0 license are also included inertly.

\paragraph{Proof and source checks.}
The reusable checks concern exact source equality, explicit finite arithmetic challenges, positive witness evaluations, integrity of frozen inputs, and deterministic rendering. The audit scripts are independent of the author emitter and semantic checker. The included \path{portable_replay/replay_report58.py} authenticates the complete 33-file science tree and 11-file independent-audit tree before running the three pinned independent checkers. Their source bytes are compiled unchanged in isolated Python with assertions enabled. A narrow logical-path adapter redirects only approved reads and writes, preserving historical path strings in the receipts. All four regenerated receipt and witness files, and the arithmetic checker's stdout, are required to match the frozen references byte-for-byte. The release-copy replay passed those exact comparisons with the original and staged inputs preserved.

The portable adapter's historical external physical-audit lookup is served by the included authenticated physical-audit copy. It therefore rechecks those frozen bytes, rather than independently rereading an external original. The root audit had established the original byte identity. The included portability suite passed 33 cases, including relocated paths with spaces, read-only inputs, malformed and overlapping output paths, symlinks, altered inputs, unexpected inventory entries, and optimized-Python refusal. Python startup isolation and the logical-path adapter are not an operating-system or hostile-code sandbox. The package README and \path{portable_replay/REPLAY_README.md} give exact commands and further limits.

\paragraph{Output discipline.}
Release tools use explicit output directories, reject unsafe overwrites or overlap with frozen inputs, and keep temporary caches outside the packet. They must not execute any author emitter, upstream or saved program, physical simulator, trajectory replay, or Lean executable. Byte integrity and successful finite replay are evidence about the delivered files, not a fresh formal verification of the inherited mathematical dependencies.

\paragraph{Determinism.}
The PDF build uses fixed source-date metadata, disabled shell escape, and clean temporary build directories. The distributable archive uses a sorted file inventory, fixed timestamps, normalized modes, and a manifest of exact file sizes and SHA-256 digests. The archive's own digest is supplied separately to avoid a self-referential manifest. Render inventories and review receipts describe the actual reviewed PDF bytes. Final release status and package hashes are supplied by the accompanying manifest and README rather than being recursively embedded into the PDF.

\paragraph{Assurance boundaries.}
No generic MRDP theorem is being used as a black-box final representation. No real-witness, finite-fold, unique-witness, minimality, or universal lower-bound claim follows from this package. The complete geometric theorem is inherited; the Pell specialization is conventional mathematics checked against a pinned source, not a new proof-assistant build. Exact finite tests support the explicit all-input proofs.

\section{Both instantiated power systems (source 28, Appendix A)}
\label{smc:fd:app:instances}
This appendix removes the generic base and output names from the two fifteen-equation systems. Every symbol with subscript 5 or $c$ denotes a distinct local quantity. The shared exponent is $n\in\NN$. In each system $o,w,\Theta,g,x,y,u,v,s,t,q_b,q_v,J_p$ are positive, the parameters $a,\beta$ are their own positive leaves plus one, and each of the eleven $d,\alpha,\sigma,\tau,\rho$ quantities is a positive leaf minus one. The output is $P$ in the first system and $T$ in the second. These domain substitutions are part of the polynomial specification; no auxiliary domain oracle is used.

\subsection{Base five and output P}
\begin{align}
x_5^2&=1+(a_5^2-1)y_5^2,\tag{5.1}\\
u_5^2&=1+(a_5^2-1)v_5^2,\tag{5.2}\\
s_5^2&=1+(\beta_5^2-1)t_5^2,\tag{5.3}\\
\beta_5&=1+4y_5q_{b,5},\tag{5.4}\\
\beta_5+u_5\alpha_{1,5}&=a_5+u_5\alpha_{2,5},\tag{5.5}\\
v_5&=y_5^2q_{v,5},\tag{5.6}\\
s_5+u_5\sigma_{1,5}&=x_5+u_5\sigma_{2,5},\tag{5.7}\\
t_5+4y_5\tau_{1,5}&=(n+1)+4y_5\tau_{2,5},\tag{5.8}\\
y_5&=(n+1)+d_{yk,5},\tag{5.9}\\
w_5&=5+d_{wb,5},\tag{5.10}\\
w_5&=(n+1)+d_{wk,5},\tag{5.11}\\
\Theta_5&=5P+J_{p,5},\tag{5.12}\\
a_5^2&=1+\bigl((w_5+1)^2-1\bigr)(w_5g_5)^2,\tag{5.13}\\
2a_5\cdot5&=\Theta_5+(5^2+1),\tag{5.14}\\
x_5+\Theta_5\rho_{1,5}&=y_5(a_5-5)+5P+\Theta_5\rho_{2,5}.\tag{5.15}
\end{align}
The source's local prefix is \path{power5.}. In particular $J_{p,5}$ is its positive \path{strict} leaf, and $a_5={}$\path{aMinus1}${}+1$, $\beta_5={}$\path{betaMinus1}${}+1$ within that namespace.

\subsection{The second ordinary power and output T}
Here $\brad=4P+1$ is the outer expression, not an independent leaf. The second base is $3+4\brad$. The complete instance is
\begin{align}
x_c^2&=1+(a_c^2-1)y_c^2,\tag{c.1}\\
u_c^2&=1+(a_c^2-1)v_c^2,\tag{c.2}\\
s_c^2&=1+(\beta_c^2-1)t_c^2,\tag{c.3}\\
\beta_c&=1+4y_cq_{b,c},\tag{c.4}\\
\beta_c+u_c\alpha_{1,c}&=a_c+u_c\alpha_{2,c},\tag{c.5}\\
v_c&=y_c^2q_{v,c},\tag{c.6}\\
s_c+u_c\sigma_{1,c}&=x_c+u_c\sigma_{2,c},\tag{c.7}\\
t_c+4y_c\tau_{1,c}&=(n+1)+4y_c\tau_{2,c},\tag{c.8}\\
y_c&=(n+1)+d_{yk,c},\tag{c.9}\\
w_c&=(3+4\brad)+d_{wb,c},\tag{c.10}\\
w_c&=(n+1)+d_{wk,c},\tag{c.11}\\
\Theta_c&=(3+4\brad)T+J_{p,c},\tag{c.12}\\
a_c^2&=1+\bigl((w_c+1)^2-1\bigr)(w_cg_c)^2,\tag{c.13}\\
2a_c(3+4\brad)&=\Theta_c+\bigl((3+4\brad)^2+1\bigr),\tag{c.14}\\
x_c+\Theta_c\rho_{1,c}&=y_c\bigl(a_c-(3+4\brad)\bigr)+(3+4\brad)T+\Theta_c\rho_{2,c}.\tag{c.15}
\end{align}
The source's local prefix is \path{power_complex.}; it remains a system for an ordinary integer power. Complex-number notation appears only in the proof of bounded extraction. There are no complex-valued source leaves or complex arithmetic primitives.

\section{Theorems and quantifiers}\label{smc:x:sec:rfthm}
Let $a,b,c\in\Z$ satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:parameters}
c>1,\qquad a^2+b^2=c^2,\qquad \gcd(a,b,c)=1,
\qquad \rot=\frac1c\begin{pmatrix}a&-b\\b&a\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
These are exactly the rational planar rotations of infinite order. Fix any $\lambda\in\Q_{>0}$. The machine and its complete word are fixed \emph{after} these parameters are chosen; only the live population is uniformly five. Word length, alphabet and rule table need not be uniform in the rotation.

\begin{theorem}[Physical realization and exact domain]\label{smc:rf:thm:main}
There is an explicitly constructible finite rational-speed number-preserving one-dimensional signal machine with exactly five live signals and a fixed complete binary-collision macro whose return in rational homogeneous coordinates is
\[
(D,X,Y)\longmapsto N(D,X,Y),\qquad N=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda,\lambda\rot).
\]
Its exact one-macro domain on the normalized section $D=1$ is a bounded open rational polygon $P$ containing zero. If $\rho$ is the least distance from zero to its supplied nonconstant guard lines, and $E=\{p_1,\ldots,p_J\}$ is the set of distinct perpendicular contacts of all minimizing lines, then $J\geq1$, $\rho^2\in\Q_{>0}$, $E\subset\Q^2$, and the exact normalized infinite validity set is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:K}
\mathcal K=\bigcap_{n\geq0}\rot^{-n}P
=\{w:\enorm w<\rho\}\ \cup\!
\left(\{w:\enorm w=\rho\}\setminus
\bigcup_{j=1}^J\{\rot^{-n}p_j:n\geq0\}\right).
\end{equation}
No uniqueness, disjoint-orbit or noninitial-face assumption is imposed on the contacts.
\end{theorem}

The input section has four stationary markers at $0,x,y,D$ with $0<x<y<D$ and a right-moving messenger at the left anchor. Its three free positive gaps are
\[
g=(g_1,g_2,g_3)=(x,y-x,D-y),\quad
X=x-D/3,\quad Y=y-2D/3,\quad w=(X/D,Y/D).
\]
The messenger and left anchor are the two outgoing strands at their contact; they count as separate live signals.

\wtag\ [Source~29's $(X,Y)$ are source~27's centred coordinates $(\xi,\eta)$, and the section is source~27's. Theorem~\ref{smc:rf:thm:main} contains the shape of source~27's validity set (Theorem~\ref{smc:fv:thm:main}) as the case of one contact, for a different machine (Section~\ref{smc:rf:sec:evidence}). Part~XI's Report~60 [batch-91 manuscript~12] extends the realization to every orientation-preserving rational planar map and carries this source's frozen proof as a dependency.]

\begin{theorem}[Classification, decision and certificate]\label{smc:rf:thm:consequences}
The positive homogeneous gap cone of infinite validity is not semialgebraic. No finite Boolean formula in polynomial-sign atoms, even with arbitrary real coefficients, agrees with validity on every positive rational gap triple or every positive integer gap triple. Nevertheless, for each fixed compiled machine, rational membership is decidable in deterministic $O(L^3)$ bit operations under elementary arithmetic, where $L$ is the total input encoding length.

For ordinary positive integer gaps, validity has an explicit existential-positive-integer certificate with exactly $1+80J$ witnesses and $1+43J$ polynomial equations. Their sum of squares has exact total degree twelve. An optional paid one-input Cantor transport uses $5+80J$ witnesses and $3+43J$ equations, still of exact degree twelve.

On all positive real gaps, validity is $G_\delta$ but not $F_\sigma$, excludes finite existential mixed integer/real polynomial-sign certificates, and is properly co-semidecidable in the finite-time field-operation BSS model of Section~\ref{smc:rf:sec:realinputs}.

Every infinitely valid run is Zeno if and only if $0<\lambda<1$. Then all strands approach the fixed left anchor and the accumulation time is rational on rational input.
\end{theorem}

The finite-sign obstruction has no quantified integer witnesses. It therefore does not contradict the displayed Diophantine representation. The rational decision bound fixes the machine and its contacts; it is neither a uniform compilation bound nor a bound on finding Pell witnesses.

\section{Rotation parameters and shear synthesis}\label{smc:x:sec:rfshear}
Primitivity implies $a,b\ne0$, $c$ odd and $\gcd(a,c)=\gcd(b,c)=1$. Indeed, a common prime divisor of a leg and $c$ divides both legs. If $c$ were even, the parity equation would either make both legs even or give $2\equiv0\pmod4$.

Put $\zeta=(a+ib)/c$. If it were a root of unity, then $\zeta+\zeta^{-1}=2a/c$ would be a rational algebraic integer and therefore an integer. Thus $c\mid2$, contrary to odd $c>1$. Both the forward and backward powers of $\rot$ are dense in the planar rotation group. Conversely, the rational finite-order rotations have entries $0$ or $\pm1$ and primitive denominator one. This proves the parameter coverage in~\eqref{smc:rf:eq:parameters}.

Define
\begin{align}
t_x&=-\frac b{c+a},&t_y&=\frac bc,\label{smc:rf:eq:shearparams}\\
N_x&=\max(1,\lceil4|t_x|\rceil),&N_y&=\max(1,\lceil4|t_y|\rceil),\nonumber\\
\delta_x&=t_x/N_x,&\delta_y&=t_y/N_y,&\Kzero&=2N_x+N_y.\nonumber
\end{align}
Since $|a|<c$, $c+a>0$ even when $a<0$. The step sizes are nonzero and have absolute value at most $1/4$. For
\[
S_x(t)=\begin{pmatrix}1&t\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
S_y(s)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\s&1\end{pmatrix},
\]
one obtains
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:shearfactor}
S_x(t_x)S_y(t_y)S_x(t_x)
=\begin{pmatrix}1+t_xt_y&2t_x+t_x^2t_y\\t_y&1+t_xt_y\end{pmatrix}
=\rot.
\end{equation}
Chronologically performing $x$, then $y$, then $x$ shears gives this product; its equal outer factors remove any apparent convention reversal. Total shear size need not be small. The number of micro-shears grows while each step remains small.

\section{Five signals and complete primitive chronology}\label{smc:rf:sec:primitives}
During a primitive only one marker moves, with speed strictly between $-1$ and $1$. The messenger has speed $\pm1$; the remaining markers are stationary. Every spectator crossing belongs to the prescribed word. A complete word records all collisions, including any collision assigned the default identity rule.

\wtag\ [The two primitives and the translation below are source~27's (Lemmas~\ref{smc:fv:lem:L} and~\ref{smc:fv:lem:H} and~\eqref{smc:fv:eq:translation}), proved again in source~29's words; source~29 credits translation and scaling to the literature (Section~\ref{smc:rf:sec:prior}).]

\subsection{Single marker scaling}
For $u>0$, the primitive $L_z(u)$ begins with a target at anchor-distance $z>0$. At the first messenger hit give it speed
\[
h=\frac{u-1}{u+1}.
\]
Reflect the messenger left, reflect it at the anchor, restore the target to speed zero on the next hit, reflect left again, and return to the anchor. The four principal time--position pairs are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:Lchron}
(z,z),\quad(2z,0),\quad(2z+uz,uz),\quad(2z+2uz,0).
\end{equation}
The target line $q=z+h(t-z)$ meets the restoration point because $h(1+u)=u-1$. Thus the endpoint is $uz$ and the duration is $2(z+uz)$.

The exact guard requires both $z$ and $uz$ to lie strictly between the unchanged nearest stationary neighbors, with no upper-neighbor test for an outermost target. To prove sufficiency, the target moves monotonically between these endpoints, so cannot collide with a stationary marker. An inner marker $s<\min(z,uz)$ is met on the four legs at
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:Lspectators}
s,\quad2z-s,\quad2z+s,\quad2z+2uz-s.
\end{equation}
These are ordered by increasing, decreasing, increasing and decreasing spatial order, respectively. The target-end gaps are $z-s_{\max}$ and $uz-s_{\max}$; the anchor-end gaps are positive marker coordinates. No outer marker is reached by the messenger. Since $|h|<1$, messenger--target relative speeds have fixed strict signs on each leg, so there is no unlisted recollision. All other marker pairs are stationary and distinct. This also rules out a remote simultaneous collision.

For necessity, equality at a checked neighbor gives an extra or coincident contact by that checkpoint; passage beyond the neighbor forces one earlier by continuity. Equality with the anchor collapses required timing. Even an identity-default contact violates the selected complete word.

\subsection{Reflector homothety}
The target at $t$ is the nearest marker to the anchor, and a stationary reflector lies at $z>t$. For $v>0$, $H_z(v)$ launches the target at speed $h=(1-v)/(1+v)$ while keeping the messenger outward. The messenger crosses every intervening spectator, reflects at $z$, crosses the spectators in reverse order, restores the target while continuing inward, then reflects at the anchor. Solving the two world lines gives
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:Hchron}
t'=vt+(1-v)z,\qquad t_{\mathrm{restore}}=2z-t',\qquad
\operatorname{duration}=2z.
\end{equation}
The exact guard is $0<t,t'<s$, where $s\leq z$ is the unchanged nearest outer marker. A spectator $q$ is met at times $q$ and $2z-q$. The inequalities $t,t'<q$ place its crossings strictly after launch and before restoration; $0<t'<z$ places restoration strictly between reflector and final anchor bounces. With no spectator the same argument uses $q=z$ at the endpoints. Monotonicity excludes target--spectator contacts, and the fixed relative speeds exclude extra messenger hits. Failure yields an extra or tied contact or collapsed chronology as above.

The nearest-target hypothesis is essential. It holds in every use below: $X$ is targeted from $L$, or $Y$ from the reflected anchor $D$. No $H$ call omits a stationary marker between its anchor and target.

\subsection{Translation and reflection}
For $e<1$ compose
\[
T_z(e)=L_t\bigl(1/(1-e)\bigr)\ ;\ H_z(1-e).
\]
The target positions and common moving speed are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:T}
t\longmapsto \frac{t}{1-e}\longmapsto t+ez,\qquad
h=\frac e{2-e}.
\end{equation}
Suppose $0<t,t+ez<s\leq z$. If $e>0$, $t+ez<z$ implies $t<(1-e)z$, and
\[
\frac{t}{1-e}-t=\frac{et}{1-e}>0,\qquad
t+ez-\frac{t}{1-e}=\frac{e((1-e)z-t)}{1-e}>0.
\]
If $e<0$, $t<z$ makes both differences negative. At $e=0$ all positions agree. The intermediate endpoint is therefore between the checked start and finish, and the target is monotone across both moving phases and its intervening pause. The translation has precisely the start/end ordering guard, with no hidden extra inequality.

Reflection in $D$ changes a coordinate $q$ to $D-q$, takes $D$ as anchor and negates every physical velocity. The chronology and exact-guard results are unchanged.

\section{The macro and its exact finite chamber}\label{smc:rf:sec:chamber}
A left-based pair
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:micro}
T_y(\delta)\ ;\ T_D(-2\delta/3)
\end{equation}
updates $x$ to $x+\delta(y-2D/3)$, leaving $y,D$ fixed. The near translation uses eight events: four in $L$ and four in $H$ with reflector $Y$. The far translation uses ten: four in $L$ and six in $H$ with spectator $Y$ and reflector $D$. Thus each micro-shear has eighteen events.

Repeat~\eqref{smc:rf:eq:micro} $N_x$ times with $\delta_x$. Transfer the messenger to $D$ by crossing $X$, crossing $Y$, then reflecting at $D$. In reflected coordinates $r=D-y$, $s=D-x$, repeat $T_s(\delta_y);T_D(-2\delta_y/3)$ $N_y$ times. Since
\[
r'=r+t_y(s-2D/3),\qquad y'=y+t_y(x-D/3),
\]
this gives the centered $S_y(t_y)$ shear with the correct sign. Transfer back by crossing $Y$, crossing $X$, reflecting at $L$, then repeat the first $x$ block. The rotation word has
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:rotcount}
m_{\rm rot}=18\Kzero+6.
\end{equation}
All translation parameters satisfy $e<1$: $|\delta|\leq1/4$ and $|2\delta/3|\leq1/6$.

\subsection{Endpoint rows and necessity}
For an $x$ block with $n$ pairs and incoming $x,y,D$, put
\begin{align}
a_{2k}&=x+k\delta(y-2D/3) &&(0\leq k\leq n),\label{smc:rf:eq:endpoints}\\
a_{2k+1}&=x+k\delta(y-2D/3)+\delta y &&(0\leq k<n).\nonumber
\end{align}
Its exact guards are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:blockguards}
0<y<D,\qquad0<a_i<y\quad(0\leq i\leq2n).
\end{equation}
For the reflected block use the same expressions with $(x,y)$ replaced by $(r,s)$, obtaining $0<s<D$ and $0<b_i<s$. Each block supplies $4n+4$ strict homogeneous rational linear rows. Pull back the three sets through their preceding rational block maps. There are exactly
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:guardcount}
4\Kzero+12
\end{equation}
supplied rows in $(D,X,Y)$. They may include redundant or repeated rows. The ordered initial rows imply $D>0$, also understood as the ambient section assumption.

The primitive lemmas prove sufficiency by induction. For necessity on a positive initial section, take the first failed endpoint checkpoint. Previous primitives have their prescribed order. By the checkpoint the target must reach or cross a fixed neighbor, or two required event times collapse, forcing an extra or simultaneous contact. A failed initial-order row means the input is outside the required section. Thus these rows describe the whole complete-word domain, not merely a convenient sufficient neighborhood.

At the center $x=D/3$, $y=2D/3$, every pair returns its target to anchor-distance $D/3$. Its odd endpoint is
\[
D/3+2\delta D/3\in[D/6,D/2]\subset(0,2D/3).
\]
Every row is therefore strictly positive at the center, for arbitrarily many steps and either sign of $\delta$. The normalized polygon $P$ is open, convex and rational with zero in its interior. Initial-order rows place it inside $0<x<y<1$, so it is bounded.

\subsection{The loop invariant for every parameter}\label{smc:rf:sec:loop}
This proof links the arbitrary-parameter construction to the implemented static constructor. It is not a finite-fixture inference. At entry to pair $k$ of an anchor-based block, the invariant is:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The target row equals $t_0+k\delta(z-2D/3)$; the fixed reflector row $z$ and outer anchor-distance $D$ are unchanged
\item All four markers are stationary, and the messenger is at the same anchor in the same outgoing direction
\item The accumulated phase word includes every principal and spectator event, and its current target endpoints satisfy all preceding strict checkpoints
\item The duration row is the sum of the rational homogeneous primitive duration rows already appended
\end{enumerate}
The near translation appends $t_k+\delta z$; the far translation appends $t_{k+1}$. Their exact endpoint guards and primitive restoration prove the invariant for $k+1$. It holds at $k=0$ by the incoming section. This proves all block maps, rows, durations and counts for arbitrary finite $n$.

The transfers are valid by the terminal strict order, take duration $D$ each and reverse direction at the opposite anchor. Combining the invariant for the first $x$, reflected $y$ and second $x$ blocks proves~\eqref{smc:rf:eq:shearfactor} as an exact return. The center positivity argument proves the constructor's guard assertions mathematically; the assertions are not used as a substitute for that argument.

\section{Scaling, finite rules and the five live population}\label{smc:rf:sec:rules}
For $0<\lambda<1$, append $L_x(\lambda)$, $L_y(\lambda)$, $L_D(\lambda)$. Each inner neighbor has already been scaled and each outer neighbor is unscaled. If $s<z$, then $\lambda s<\lambda z$, so a target moving from $z$ to $\lambda z$ stays above its scaled inner neighbors and below unscaled outer neighbors. For $\lambda>1$ reverse the order to $D,Y,X$: every outer neighbor is already scaled and each inner neighbor remains unscaled, giving the analogous strict order proof. For $\lambda=1$ omit scaling.

The $X,Y,D$ scaling primitives use respectively $4,8,12$ events regardless of execution order. Their speed is $(\lambda-1)/(\lambda+1)\in(-1,1)$; they introduce no new guard and restore the complete outgoing section. If $x_{\rm rot},y_{\rm rot}$ denote postrotation coordinates, their duration is
\[
2(1+\lambda)(x_{\rm rot}+y_{\rm rot}+D).
\]
Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:allcounts}
m=18\Kzero+6+24\,\mathbf{1}_{\{\lambda\ne1\}},\qquad
N=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda,\lambda\rot).
\end{equation}
In ordinary gaps the return matrix is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:M}
M=\frac{\lambda}{3c}
\begin{pmatrix}
c+2a-b&c-a-b&c-a+2b\\
c-a+3b&c+2a&c-a-3b\\
c-a-2b&c-a+b&c+2a+b
\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
With
\[
Q=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\2/3&-1/3&-1/3\\1/3&1/3&-2/3\end{pmatrix}
\]
one has $QM=NQ$. Negative entries of $M$ outside the chamber do not assert a physically executable return there.

\subsection{Explicit finite grammar}
Give every pre-event messenger state a distinct label $Q_j$ for $0\leq j<m$, with its specified speed $\pm1$, and identify $Q_m=Q_0$. Each of the $4\Kzero$ elementary $L/H$ pieces in the translations gets a unique temporary target label; add three temporary labels when $\lambda\ne1$. Keep stationary labels $L_0,X_0,Y_0,D_0$. At event $j$ emit
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:rule}
\{Q_j,Z_{\rm in}\}\longrightarrow\{Q_{j+1\bmod m},Z_{\rm out}\}.
\end{equation}
Launch and restoration switch between stationary and temporary target labels; spectator and bounce events keep the stationary identity. In $L$, reverse messenger direction at all four principal events. In $H$, preserve direction at launch/restoration and reverse at reflector/anchor. Include all spectator crossings. Each transfer reverses direction only at its final anchor.

Every input and every output has pairwise distinct speeds because marker speeds have modulus less than one and messenger speeds are $\pm1$. Each $Q_j$ occurs in only one explicit input set, so prescribed rules cannot conflict. At a binary contact the incoming local order is decreasing speed and outgoing local order increasing speed; strands separate immediately. The strict endpoint proof keeps all other markers away and excludes remote collisions.

Assign identity to every other collision input set with pairwise distinct speeds. The alphabet is finite, hence this is a finite deterministic number-preserving completion. Default rules cannot hide extra contacts from the complete word. Each explicit rule consumes and emits one messenger and one marker of the same identity. Thus the live population is always five, although the meta-signal count is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:alphabet}
\#\text{meta-signals}=22\Kzero+10+27\,\mathbf{1}_{\{\lambda\ne1\}}.
\end{equation}
A meta-signal is a type; a live signal is an instance. Neither is the count of distinct speeds.

\subsection{Source-level invariant coverage}
The audited constructor is 158 lines. Its exact rational linear-row representation and finite loops have the following all-parameter interpretation:
\begin{itemize}
\item $L$ expands increasing inner-marker order, launch, decreasing order, anchor bounce, increasing order, restoration, decreasing order, anchor bounce. It adds $4+4k$ events for $k$ inner spectators and one temporary label
\item $H$ expands launch, forward spectators, reflector, reverse spectators, restoration, anchor. It adds $4+2k$ events and one temporary label; reflection negates all velocities
\item Every translation targets the anchor-nearest marker, so its $L$ inner list is empty. Near $H$ has no spectator; far $H$ has exactly the near reflector as spectator. Its duration row is $2(1+1/(1-e))t+2z$
\item The shear loop is governed by the invariant in Section~\ref{smc:rf:sec:loop}. The scaling branch uses $X,Y,D$ below one and $D,Y,X$ above one, with inner lists respectively empty, $[X]$, and $[X,Y]$
\item The rule loop advances distinct messenger labels cyclically, changes a target only at its paired launch/restoration, and preserves all four marker identities. It produces $m$ messenger labels, $4\Kzero+3\,\mathbf{1}_{\{\lambda\ne1\}}$ temporary labels and four stationary labels
\item The contact scan uses exact squared distances and exact equality, then deduplicates exact rational contacts. Serialization uses integer or rational strings, never floating-point approximations
\end{itemize}
The mathematical domain is the stated integer/rational parameter set. The constructor's assertions are development checks, not a security-hardened validator under Python optimization. There is no event selector or physical trajectory solver in the static constructor.

\section{Infinite validity and all tangency cases}\label{smc:rf:sec:geometry}
Write a normalized supplied row as $\alpha+v\cdot w>0$, with $\alpha>0$. Ignore constant-only rows. For each remaining row define
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:contact}
d_{\rm row}^2=\frac{\alpha^2}{v\cdot v},\qquad
p_{\rm row}=-\frac{\alpha v}{v\cdot v}.
\end{equation}
There is a nonconstant row because $P$ is bounded. Let $\rho^2$ be the positive rational minimum of the squared distances, and let $E$ deduplicate the contacts at this minimum. Every contact is nonzero, rational and has norm $\rho$.

For $\enorm w<\rho$, Cauchy--Schwarz makes every row strictly positive. On $\enorm w=\rho$, equality can occur only for a minimizing row at its perpendicular contact; every other row is strict. Thus the circle complement of $P$ is exactly $E$, including redundant, proportional and repeated guard rows. Above radius $\rho$, a nearest row is negative on a nonempty open arc. Every forward irrational rotation orbit meets that arc.

Normalization removes $\lambda$, so at each macro return $w$ updates by $\rot$. Exact finite-word equivalence now proves~\eqref{smc:rf:eq:K}. If a contact has positive initial gaps, its failed guard is a physical extra or tied contact. If it lies on an initial-order face, it is not an admissible initial section. Its shifted inverse-orbit points are still excluded by the same finite-chamber criterion.
