\subsection{Rational sign obstruction with co-orbital contacts}
Fix $p\in E$ and its full orbit $O=\{\rot^kp:k\in\Z\}$. Infinite order makes each orbit index unique. The set
\[
I=\{k\in\Z:\rot^kp\in E\}
\]
is finite, nonempty and contains zero. Put $k_* =\max I$. Restricted to $O$, the forbidden union of backward orbits consists exactly of indices $k\leq k_*$. Thus the accepted forward tail $\{\rot^kp:k>k_*\}$ and rejected backward tail $\{\rot^kp:k\leq k_*\}$ are both dense and rational. No algorithm for deciding whether contacts are co-orbital is needed in this proof.

The positive-gap restriction needs an additional check. The closed critical disk lies in the closed initial-order triangle. Each strict initial-order line can vanish on the circle at only one perpendicular contact. There are therefore only finitely many zero-gap circle points. Removing these from the rejected tail leaves it dense; the accepted tail is already in $P$ and has positive gaps.

A finite polynomial-sign formula restricts on the algebraic circle to a semialgebraic set, whose membership is constant on each of finitely many open arcs after removal of finitely many endpoints. It cannot accept one dense rational tail and reject the other. This works even for arbitrary real polynomial coefficients.

\subsection{Positive integer obstruction without homogeneous input formulas}
Suppose a finite Boolean polynomial-sign formula $F$ were correct on all positive integer gap triples. Decompose each polynomial as $f=\sum_d f_d$ into homogeneous components. For a fixed $g$, the eventual sign of $f(tg)$ as $t\to+\infty$ is the sign of the highest-degree component nonzero at $g$, or zero if all components vanish. This is a finite semialgebraic case distinction, invariant under positive rescaling.

Replace each sign atom by this eventual-sign distinction, giving a homogeneous semialgebraic formula $F_\infty$. The physical predicate is constant on positive rays. Correctness of $F$ at every positive integer multiple forces correctness of $F_\infty$ on each positive integer ray. Clearing denominators and rescaling extends this correctness to all positive rational gap triples, contradicting the preceding subsection. No homogeneity was assumed for the original $F$.

\section{All real inputs and finite certificate obstructions}\label{smc:rf:sec:realinputs}
The following strengthening concerns correctness on \emph{all positive real gaps}. It is a separate, independently audited application of classical topology, real algebraic geometry and the finite-path analysis of exact real computation. It leaves the encoded-rational and integer-input conclusions intact.

Let $G=(0,\infty)^3$, and let $V\subset G$ be the infinite-validity set for any one fixed compiled family member. Define the critical circle and its full excluded set by
\[
S=\{w:\enorm w=\rho\},\qquad
\mathcal B=\bigcup_{j=1}^J\{\rot^{-n}p_j:n\geq0\}.
\]
The set $\mathcal B$ is countably infinite and dense in $S$, irrespective of duplicated or co-orbital representatives. Equation~\eqref{smc:rf:eq:K} says that $\mathcal K$ is the closed disk with $\mathcal B$ deleted. Recall that $F_\sigma$ means a countable union of closed sets and $G_\delta$ a countable intersection of open sets in the stated topology.

\begin{theorem}[Proper topological class and real-input obstruction]\label{smc:rf:thm:realinput}
For every fixed family member, $V$ is $G_\delta$ but not $F_\sigma$, both relative to $G$ and in $\R^3$. Its relative complement is $F_\sigma$ but not $G_\delta$. There are no finite $k,m$ and finite Boolean polynomial-sign formula $\Phi$, with arbitrary fixed real coefficients, such that on every $g\in G$,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:mixed}
g\in V\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists n\in\NN^k\ \exists y\in\R^m\ \Phi(g,n,y).
\end{equation}
The same holds for signed integer witnesses. In the finite-time exact real field-operation BSS model specified below, $V$ is not semidecidable, even with finitely many arbitrary fixed real constants, whereas $G\setminus V$ is semidecidable using rational constants alone.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{The Baire argument and admissible closed arc}
An explicit open-set representation is
\[
\mathcal K=
\bigcap_{m\geq1}\{w:\enorm w^2<\rho^2+1/m\}
\ \cap\!\bigcap_{b\in\mathcal B}(\R^2\setminus\{b\}).
\]
Thus $\mathcal K$ is $G_\delta$. If $S\setminus\mathcal B$ were $F_\sigma$ relative to $S$, write it as a countable union of relatively closed sets. Each has empty interior because $\mathcal B$ is dense, so each is nowhere dense. The singleton members of $\mathcal B$ are also nowhere dense. This would cover the compact nonempty circle by countably many nowhere dense closed sets, contrary to the Baire category theorem. Consequently $\mathcal K$ is not $F_\sigma$.

The same proof works on any nondegenerate closed arc $A\subset S$. The intersection $\mathcal B\cap A$ is countable and dense in this perfect compact metric space. The elementary compact-arc Baire statement can also be proved directly: successively choose nested nonempty closed subarcs avoiding the successive closed nowhere dense sets, with diameters tending to zero. Compactness gives an intersection point outside the proposed cover.

To transfer to actual positive gaps, use the normalized initial-order triangle
\[
\mathcal D=\{(u,v):1/3+u>0,\ 1/3+v-u>0,\ 1/3-v>0\}.
\]
The map
\[
(d,(u,v))\longmapsto d(1/3+u,\ 1/3+v-u,\ 1/3-v)
\]
is a homeomorphism from $(0,\infty)\times\mathcal D$ onto $G$. The closed critical disk lies in the closed initial-order triangle. Each of the three affine gap forms is positive at zero and can vanish on its circle only at its single perpendicular contact. Hence at most finitely many points of $S$ fail the positive-gap condition, and some nondegenerate closed arc $A$ lies wholly inside $\mathcal D$.

Normalization is continuous on $G$, so $V$ is $G_\delta$ relative to $G$. As $G$ is ambient open, it is also $G_\delta$ in $\R^3$. Equivalently, the exact strict guard description expresses $V$ as $G\cap\bigcap_{n\geq0}(M^n)^{-1}C$, where $C$ is the open homogeneous chamber in gap coordinates, obtained by pulling the supplied guard rows back through $Q$. If $V$ were relatively $F_\sigma$, its preimage under the continuous fixed-scale embedding
\[
\iota:A\longrightarrow G,\qquad
\iota(u,v)=(1/3+u,\ 1/3+v-u,\ 1/3-v)
\]
would make $A\setminus\mathcal B$ $F_\sigma$ in $A$, a contradiction. Ambient $F_\sigma$ would imply relative $F_\sigma$, so is also impossible. Taking complements proves the asserted proper class for invalidity. No Borel-completeness claim is made.

\subsection{Why finitely many mixed witnesses cannot suffice}
Every semialgebraic subset of $\R^a$ is $F_\sigma$. For example,
\[
\{f>0\}=\bigcup_{j\geq1}\{f\geq1/j\}
\]
for a real polynomial $f$; analogous formulas handle $f<0$, while zero and weak-sign sets are closed. Resolve a finite Boolean sign formula into a finite union of finite intersections of these atoms. The class $F_\sigma$ is closed under finite intersections and countable unions. This argument does not assume an arbitrary semialgebraic set is itself locally closed.

For a fixed integer tuple $n$ in a hypothetical~\eqref{smc:rf:eq:mixed}, the set
\[
A_n=\{g\in\R^3:\exists y\in\R^m\ \Phi(g,n,y)\}
\]
is semialgebraic by Tarski--Seidenberg real projection, with no compactness restriction on the witnesses and allowing arbitrary fixed real coefficients~\cite{basuraag}. The union over countably many $n$ is $F_\sigma$. Agreement on all $G$ would therefore make $V$ relatively $F_\sigma$, impossible. This also rules out countable disjunctions of such certificates. In the special case $\exists n\ P(g,n)=0$, fixed-$n$ zero loci are already closed, so real projection is unnecessary.

This conclusion does not cover arbitrary alternating integer/real quantifiers or nonpolynomial oracle predicates. A formula required to agree only at integer inputs, or at discrete encodings of rational inputs, may behave differently at every other real input. Thus Section~\ref{smc:rf:sec:certificate}'s existential-positive-integer theorem is fully compatible with this obstruction.

\subsection{The exact real computation model and semidecision}
Use the ordinary finite-time Blum--Shub--Smale model with finite control, finitely many fixed real constants, real registers, field operations $+,-,\times,/$ where defined, copying/register shifts and exact equality and order tests. Ordinary loops and discrete control are allowed. There is no digit-extraction or floor primitive, one-step real-to-integer-word cast, oracle or completed-infinite-computation instruction. Semidecidability relative to $G$ means halting exactly on the members among inputs in $G$, with no condition outside that promise. The model and relative convention, and the $F_\sigma$ upper bound, are established in~\cite{gartnerziegler,calvertkm}.

For completeness, unroll a finite program into its countable family of finite accepting paths. A path fixes its branch outcomes and register accesses and uses finitely many instructions and registers. By induction, every encountered register is a rational function of the input, with coefficients in the field generated by the program's fixed real constants. Its path conditions consist of finitely many rational sign tests and every nonzero-divisor restriction. They are semialgebraic: for example, when $b\ne0$, $a/b>0$ is equivalent to $ab>0$, and $a/b=0$ to $a=0$. Retain intermediate division-domain restrictions even when a later expression cancels a denominator.

Each finite accepting-path domain is therefore semialgebraic; their countable union is $F_\sigma$. Intersecting with $G$ gives the same relative upper bound. Finitely many arbitrary real constants only change coefficients, not this argument. The proper class proved above rules out semidecision of $V$, and hence decision as well.

Invalidity has a direct rational semidecision. Maintain $q=g$. Evaluate every supplied $(D,X,Y)$ guard row at $Qq$; halt when one is nonpositive; otherwise replace $q$ by $Mq$ and repeat. Exact chamber equivalence guarantees that an invalid input has a finite failed iterate, including an equality at an excluded boundary orbit. Valid inputs never halt. This procedure uses only finitely many fixed rational rows and the rational return matrix; it neither simulates physical collisions nor inspects an infinite-time limit. Alternatively, normalize, halt above the disk and enumerate inverse iterates of all contacts, halting at an exact match. To classify nonpositive inputs as invalid too, add their initial sign test.

Thus validity is \emph{properly co-semidecidable} in this specified model. This is no Type-2 or oracle classification, BSS-degree completeness statement, physical hypercomputation claim, or Turing undecidability claim for encoded rationals. Encoded rational inputs supply numerator/denominator data that an arbitrary exact real register does not supply, and the $O(L^3)$ procedure below need not cover irrational inputs. Positive scaling cancels in normalization, so this real-input conclusion is independent of contraction and Zeno behavior.

\section{Exact rational membership and its bit bound}\label{smc:rf:sec:decision}
For rational positive gaps compute $w=(X/D,Y/D)$ and compare $\enorm w^2$ to $\rho^2$ exactly. Accept below, reject above. At equality, for every contact form the rational Gaussian quotient
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:eta}
\gamma_j=\frac{w_x+iw_y}{p_{jx}+ip_{jy}}.
\end{equation}
Invalidity is equivalent to one equality $\gamma_j=((a-ib)/c)^n$ for $n\geq0$.

\begin{lemma}[Exact power denominator]\label{smc:rf:lem:denom}
The joint reduced denominator of $((a-ib)/c)^n$ is exactly $c^n$ for every $n\geq0$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each prime $p\mid c$, $p$ is odd and divides neither $a$ nor $b$. In the algebra $(\Z/p\Z)[i]$, set $z=a-ib$. Since $a^2+b^2\equiv0$,
\[
z^2=2az,\qquad z^n=(2a)^{n-1}z\quad(n\geq1).
\]
Both coordinates on the right are nonzero modulo $p$. This computation does not presume the algebra is a field. Each integer numerator coordinate of $(a-ib)^n$ is consequently coprime to $c$, so the denominator is exactly $c^n$. The case $n=0$ has numerator pair $(1,0)$ and denominator one.
\end{proof}

\wtag\ [For $(a,b,c)=(3,4,5)$ this is source~27's Lemma~\ref{smc:fv:lem:denominator}, there proved by the identity $(3+i)^2=3+i$ modulo~5.]

For each $\gamma_j$, let $q_j$ be its least common positive denominator. Repeated division by the whole integer $c$ decides whether $q_j=c^n$. If not, no inverse-power match is possible. If yes, $n$ is forced; compare with that one Gaussian power exactly. Repeating this for the finite contact list decides membership. There is no unbounded orbit search and density is not used as an algorithm.

\subsection{Fixed machine polynomial time}
Fix all machine parameters, $J$, $\rho^2$ and contact coordinates. Encode input rational gaps by ordinary binary signed numerators and positive denominators, with total length $L$. Malformed or nonpositive inputs are rejected by exact checks. Initial lowest-term reduction is optional.

The radius test and each quotient formation use a constant number of rational operations. Products of a constant number of input numerators or denominators have $O(L)$ bits, so all intermediate fractions and reduced joint denominators do too. Schoolbook division and the Euclidean algorithm give a conservative $O(L^3)$ bound for this fixed number of reductions, comparisons and gcd operations.

The whole-integer power test uses at most $\log_c q_j=O(L)$ divisions of $O(L)$-bit integers by fixed $c$. If successful, compute $(a-ib)^n$ by $n=O(L)$ successive multiplications by the fixed Gaussian integer. At step $k\leq n$ each coefficient has magnitude at most $c^k\leq q_j$, hence $O(L)$ bits. These multiplications and the final comparison take polynomial time, indeed $O(L^2)$ with elementary fixed-coefficient arithmetic. Since $J$ is fixed, $O(L^3)$ bounds the whole procedure conservatively.

This is not an optimality claim, a uniform parameter-size or compilation bound, or a bound on finding the potentially enormous Diophantine witnesses. The decision algorithm never constructs the auxiliary ordinary powers used in the certificate.

\section{The exact Zeno classification and rational clock}\label{smc:rf:sec:clock}
There are $2\Kzero$ translation gadgets. Each $L$ portion takes less than $4D$ and each $H$ portion at most $2D$, so the rotation duration is less than $(12\Kzero+2)D$, including the two length-$D$ transfers. With scaling, the extra duration is less than $6(1+\lambda)D$. Thus a valid macro has a rational homogeneous linear duration row $\ell$ satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:duration}
0<\ell(D,X,Y)<C_\lambda D,\qquad
C_\lambda=12\Kzero+8+6\lambda
\end{equation}
when $\lambda\ne1$; the smaller rotation-only bound applies at one. Rational linearity follows from the primitive durations and endpoint maps.

At repetition $n$, $D_n=\lambda^nD_0$. For $\lambda<1$, the geometric upper bound gives finite total time, and every strand in macro $n$ lies in $[0,D_n]$, so all approach the fixed left anchor. Since all eigenvalues of $N$ have modulus $\lambda<1$,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:clock}
T(z)=\sum_{n\geq0}\ell N^nz=\ell(I-N)^{-1}z,\qquad z=(D,X,Y).
\end{equation}
This row has rational coefficients and gives rational accumulation time on rational gaps. For $\lambda\geq1$, the transfers alone contribute $2D_n$ per macro, whose sum diverges. This proves the exact iff. No continuation through an accumulation is asserted.

\wtag\ [Rational accumulation time on rational gaps is also the conclusion of source~26's Theorem~\ref{smc:pm:thm:rational}, which holds for every valid ultimately periodic complete macro; here the time is an explicit row. Source~27's clock~\eqref{smc:fv:eq:T} is the corresponding row for its machine at $\lambda=1/2$.]

The independent static check also obtains the duration using the closed sum
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}t_k=nt_0+\frac{\delta n(n-1)}2(z-2D/3),
\]
rather than the author's incremental loop, and matched every fixture duration row.

\section{A literal fixed arity degree twelve certificate}\label{smc:rf:sec:certificate}
This section concerns three ordinary positive integer input gaps and one fixed machine. Its contact set $E$ is computed first; all machine and contact quantities are fixed coefficients, not witnesses. Write $\rho^2=H/K$ in positive integer lowest terms and put
\begin{align}
D&=g_1+g_2+g_3,&x&=g_1,&y&=g_1+g_2,\nonumber\\
A&=3x-D,&B&=3y-2D,&\Delta&=9HD^2-K(A^2+B^2).\label{smc:rf:eq:delta}
\end{align}
Introduce one natural witness $d\in\NN$ and impose
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:radiuswitness}\Delta=d.\end{equation}
For each $p_j$ fix integers $r_j,s_j$ and $t_j>0$ with $p_j=(r_j/t_j,s_j/t_j)$. The contact is nonzero. Define fixed linear input expressions
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:UVQ}
U_j=t_j(r_jA+s_jB),\quad V_j=t_j(r_jB-s_jA),\quad
Q_j=3(r_j^2+s_j^2)D>0.
\end{equation}
Then $\gamma_j=(U_j+iV_j)/Q_j$, also at the center. These aliases are expressions, not additional leaves.

\wtag\ [This is source~28's construction (Sections~\ref{smc:fd:sec:outer}--\ref{smc:fd:sec:iff}) carried out for each contact of a general family member, with the radius equation shared; source~28 treats source~27's machine and gives a literal DAG and gate ledger, which source~29 does not. For $(a,b,c)=(3,4,5)$ the radix~\eqref{smc:rf:eq:powercalls} is $4P+11$, not source~28's $4P+1$. The opening of Part~\ref{smc:part:periodic} compares the ledgers.]

\subsection{The thirteen outer equations per contact}
For each $j$ independently introduce
\begin{align*}
&n,k,L_C,H_C,L_S,H_S\in\NN,\\
&h,q,r,s,t,J_{\rm acc}\in\Np,\\
&u,v,e_1,e_2,e_3,C,S,\kappa\in\Z.
\end{align*}
Let $\epsilon=\sgn b$ and use the explicit POWER module of the next subsection twice, with distinct internal witnesses, to define
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:powercalls}
P=\POWER(c,n),\qquad \brad=4P+2c+1,\qquad
T=\POWER(a+|b|\brad,n).
\end{equation}
The radix $\brad$ is a linear expression in $P$, not a module Pell parameter. Suppressing the contact index on witnesses, impose all thirteen equations:
\begin{align}
U_j&=hu,\tag{O1}\label{smc:rf:eq:O1}\\
V_j&=hv,\tag{O2}\\
Q_j&=hq,\tag{O3}\\
e_1u+e_2v+e_3q&=1,\tag{O4}\\
q&=Pr,\tag{O5}\\
r&=ck+s,\tag{O6}\\
s+t&=c,\tag{O7}\\
C+P&=L_C,\tag{O8}\\
P-C&=H_C,\tag{O9}\\
S+P&=L_S,\tag{O10}\\
P-S&=H_S,\tag{O11}\\
T-C-\brad S&=\kappa(\brad^2+1),\tag{O12}\label{smc:rf:eq:extract}\\
d^2+(r-1)^2+(u-C)^2+(v+\epsilon S)^2&=J_{\rm acc}.\tag{O13}\label{smc:rf:eq:accept}
\end{align}
All domains are essential. Replace a natural $z$ by $z_+-1$ with $z_+\in\Np$. Replace a signed $z$ by $z_+-z_-$ with both leaves in $\Np$. Positive quantities remain individual leaves. These are explicit affine substitutions throughout the displayed system.

\subsection{Exactness of the outer system}\label{smc:rf:sec:outerexact}
Equations (O1)--(O4) say that $(u,v,q)$ is the primitive joint quotient of $(U_j,V_j,Q_j)$. B\'ezout forces $\gcd(u,v,q)=1$; with $h>0$ this forces $h$ to be the positive gcd of the original triple. Since $Q_j>0$, $q$ is exactly the least common positive denominator of $u/q$ and $v/q$. Zero and negative numerator components are allowed. At the center, $U_j=V_j=0$ and $q=1$.

POWER gives $P=c^n$. Equations (O6)--(O7) imply $1\leq s\leq c-1$, $k\geq0$, and $c\nmid r$. Every positive $q$ has a unique factorization $q=c^nr$ with this condition, by repeated division by the \emph{whole} integer $c$. For composite $c$ this is not an additive prime-adic valuation and does not assert $\gcd(r,c)=1$.

Let $C_n+iS_n=(a+i|b|)^n$. Its modulus is $c^n=P$, so $-P\leq C_n,S_n\leq P$. Substitution of $i$ by $\brad$ modulo $\brad^2+1$ gives
\[
(a+|b|\brad)^n\equiv C_n+\brad S_n
\pmod{\brad^2+1}.
\]
Thus the true pair satisfies extraction and bounds. Conversely, any bounded solution $C,S$ has
\[
|(C-C_n)+\brad(S-S_n)|
\leq2P(1+\brad)<\brad^2+1.
\]
Indeed $\brad>4P$ gives
$\brad^2+1-2P(1+\brad)>8P^2-2P+1>0$ for $P\geq1$.
Divisibility forces this difference to zero; then $|C-C_n|\leq2P<\brad$ forces both coefficient differences to zero. Extraction is exact.

Negative $a$ creates no POWER-base problem. Already from positivity of the independent leaf $P$,
\[
a+|b|\brad\geq-(c-1)+(4P+2c+1)=4P+c+2>2.
\]
The first base is $c\geq5$, so both module hypotheses hold before invoking their semantic conclusion.

Lemma~\ref{smc:rf:lem:denom} now says that $\gamma_j$ is a forbidden inverse power precisely when
\[
r=1,\qquad u=C,\qquad v=-\epsilon S.
\]
The sign in (O13) is therefore $v+\epsilon S$. At $n=0$ one gets $P=1,C=1,S=0$, correctly excluding $\gamma_j=1$ on the boundary.

Equation~\eqref{smc:rf:eq:radiuswitness} forces $\Delta\geq0$. For $\Delta>0$, a positive acceptance witness exists for each contact because the sum in (O13) is already positive. At $\Delta=0$, each (O13) is solvable exactly when its contact is not a forbidden match. Conjoining all contacts yields precisely~\eqref{smc:rf:eq:K}. Conversely, choose gcds, B\'ezout coefficients, canonical $c$-power factors, true Gaussian coefficients, bounded slacks, congruence quotients and the POWER witnesses. Every valid input then supplies all witnesses, with $J_{\rm acc}$ equal to its nonzero displayed sum. This proves both directions without a boundary selector or a generic MRDP appeal.

\subsection{Specializing the constructive Pell theorems}\label{smc:rf:sec:pellproof}
\wtag\ [Second account (source~29) of the proof of Lemma~\ref{smc:fd:lem:power}, in source~29's names; it adds the explicit substitution dictionary from the mathlib statements.]

For the index characterization substitute source $a,k,x,y$ by $\alpha,k_0,x_p,y_p$, and source auxiliaries $u,v,s,t,b$ by $u_p,v_p,s_p,t_p,\beta$. Equations (P1)--(P3) are the three Pell identities. Equation (P4) gives $\beta\equiv1\pmod{4y_p}$; (P5) gives $\beta\equiv\alpha\pmod{u_p}$; (P6) gives $y_p^2\mid v_p$; (P7)--(P8) give the two remaining congruences; (P9) gives $k_0\leq y_p$. These are the positive-index branch, since $k_0=e+1\geq1$ and $y_p\geq k_0$ rule out the source's zero-index pair $(1,0)$. Thus $(x_p,y_p)$ is the Pell pair at index $k_0$ for $\alpha$.

The source uses natural truncated subtraction. For naturals, $X-Y=1$ in truncated subtraction is equivalent to the ordinary integer identity $X=Y+1$, precisely the form of the displayed Pell equations. No subtraction convention is changed without this equivalence.

For the power characterization substitute source $n,k,m$ by $B_0,k_0,m_0$, and its $w,a,t,z$ by $w,\alpha,\Theta,g$. Equations (P10)--(P11) give $w\geq B_0,k_0$; (P12) gives the required strict bound $\Theta>m_0$; (P13) is the auxiliary Pell identity; (P14) is the required relation $2\alpha B_0=\Theta+B_0^2+1$; (P15) is the congruence modulo $\Theta$ after identifying the Pell pair.

Since $g\geq1$ and $w\geq B_0\geq2$, (P13) forces $\alpha>w\geq B_0$. Its ordinary subtraction $\alpha-B_0$ therefore agrees with the source's natural subtraction. The theorem gives $B_0^{k_0}=m_0=B_0\mathrm{out}$. Cancelling the positive $B_0$ gives $\mathrm{out}=B_0^e$, including $e=0$ through the index shift.

Conversely, the constructive theorems supply witnesses for $B_0^{k_0}$. Their auxiliary $g$ is nonzero because $\alpha\geq2$. Pell $x$ coordinates are positive; $y_p\geq k_0\geq1$ and $v_p>0$ give $q_v>0$. The conditions $\beta>1$ and $\beta\equiv1\pmod{4y_p}$ give $q_b>0$. Since $t_p\equiv k_0\pmod{4y_p}$ and $1\leq k_0\leq y_p<4y_p$, $t_p\ne0$. The strict modulus bound gives $J_p>0$. Every signed congruence difference is represented by the difference of two natural multiples, exactly as the displayed paired variables. Thus the positive domains lose no solutions, proving both directions of the literal module.

\subsection{Witness ledger and exact degree}\label{smc:rf:sec:ledger}
The per-contact outer domains have six naturals, six positive quantities and eight signed quantities represented by sixteen positive leaves. Each POWER module contributes 26 leaves, with $P$ and $T$ counted only as their respective outputs. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{smc:rf:eq:ledger}
W=1+J(6+6+16+26+26)=1+80J,\qquad
E_q=1+J(13+15+15)=1+43J.
\end{equation}
The first $1$ is the shared radius witness or radius equation. Define $F$ literally as the sum of squares of all residual polynomials after substitution of every alias and affine domain adapter. This is a finite formula for each fixed chamber: $J$ is a machine-dependent fixed integer, not a witness-indexed array.

Outer residuals have total degree at most three in input and independent witness leaves. POWER residuals have degree at most six, even when the second base is affine in $P$. Residual (P13) has degree-six leading term $-w^4g^2$. Its square supplies a nonzero degree-twelve contribution. The degree-twelve homogeneous part of $F$ is a sum of squares of real homogeneous polynomials, which cannot cancel identically. As $J\geq1$, $\deg F=12$ exactly.

For a paid one-input transport, introduce positive gap witnesses $g_1,g_2,g_3$ and one natural witness $j$, and append
\begin{align}
2j&=(g_2+g_3-2)(g_2+g_3-1)+2(g_3-1),\label{smc:rf:eq:cantor1}\\
2(z-1)&=(g_1-1+j)(g_1+j)+2j.\label{smc:rf:eq:cantor2}
\end{align}
These encode the bijection $z=1+\operatorname{pair}(g_1-1,\operatorname{pair}(g_2-1,g_3-1))$. They add four positive leaves and two quadratic residuals, giving $5+80J$ witnesses and $3+43J$ equations, still of exact degree twelve. This has a different input ledger from the native three-gap theorem.

There is no exact gate count or emitted general arithmetic DAG claim. Positive-pair encodings of signed values alone admit infinitely many presentations, so neither uniqueness nor finite-foldness follows.

\section{Prior work and claim boundaries}\label{smc:rf:sec:prior}
Conservative rational signal arithmetic, translation, scaling and shrinking are established techniques. Durand-Lose's AGC6~\cite{dl2012} explicitly equates incoming and outgoing counts, implements rational stack operations through translation and scaling, and gives conservative shrinking. AGC8~\cite{accumulations} distinguishes meta-signals, live instances and speed counts and studies accumulations and rationality. The appearance of five reference markers or five meta-signals in AGC5~\cite{agc5} is not an exactly-five-total-live number-preserving result.

Dense rational-rotation semialgebraic obstructions also precede this work. Fijalkow--Ohlmann--Ouaknine--Pouly--Worrell, STACS 2017, Example 1~\cite{fopww17}, use the rational rotation $\frac15\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}4&-3\\3&4\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ and show that an unreachable circle target may lack a semialgebraic separating invariant. Their introduction recalls the polynomial-time Kannan--Lipton orbit decision theorem~\cite{kannanlipton}. Our fixed-machine denominator procedure is a direct special-case algorithm, not a new general orbit-decision phenomenon. The strict-boundary input classifier and complete physical word are distinct objects from an inductive nonreachability invariant.

Earlier three-variable linear-loop nonsemialgebraicity is established by Dai--Xia~\cite{daixia}; Ouaknine--Worrell~\cite{owloops} give an irrational-rotation loop with a non-strict guard whose nontermination set is a closed cone. Strictness is precisely what creates the boundary deletions here. The finite rational-tail argument and eventual-sign passage to integer rays still require their own proofs.

The contribution documented here is the explicit five-live-signal physical realization for each rational infinite-order rotation, with its exact complete-word chamber, exact strict-boundary classifier and literal fixed-arity arithmetic specialization. The bounded comparison found no matching complete realization in the inspected sources, but it is not an exhaustive novelty search or a priority certificate. No unchanged universal rotation table, arbitrary-matrix compilation, minimal population or word length, general undecidability, arithmetic gate optimality or continuation after accumulation is claimed.

Within this report the closest results are sources~26--28, which source~29 cites by Report number, and Part~XI's Report~60, which generalizes it. The machine depends on the rotation, as the source says; the programme's review makes the same point for the generalization in Report~60 (``without a generic emitted gate ledger or one unchanged universal table'', and ``Physical compilation cost/word length is not claimed polynomial in matrix bit length''), and it applies here too. \section{Release verification and reproducibility}\label{smc:rf:sec:release}

Exact build and render receipts accompany the archive rather than being treated as mathematical proof.

\section{Further questions and research (Part X)}\label{smc:x:sec:questions}
\wtag\ This section collects what the four sources state as possible, expected or not established without proving it, and the questions they leave, each with its origin, the argument that exists and what is missing. Source~27's own five questions are printed in its Section~\ref{smc:fv:sec:prior}, with notes on the two that sources~28 and~29 answer in part; they are not repeated. No claim of the sources was found to be false; the exact-arithmetic identities of sources~27 and~28 that were recomputed at this write (source~27's clock rows~\eqref{smc:fv:eq:rotationclock}, \eqref{smc:fv:eq:ell}, \eqref{smc:fv:eq:T} and~\eqref{smc:fv:eq:Tx}, its two boundary examples~\eqref{smc:fv:eq:examples}, source~28's identities~\eqref{smc:fd:eq:radiusidentity}--\eqref{smc:fd:eq:norm} on random gaps, and the equality of source~29's return matrix~\eqref{smc:rf:eq:M} at $(3,4,5)$, $\lambda=1/2$ with source~27's) all hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{X.\arabic*}]
\item\label{smc:x:q:frontend} \textbf{An audited machine-and-macro frontend} (source~26, Sections~\ref{smc:pm:sec:evidence} and~\ref{smc:pm:sec:prior}; source~27, Question~\ref{smc:fv:q:frontend}). The chamber, the infinite criterion and the sign formula are proved constructions (Sections~\ref{smc:pm:sec:chamber}--\ref{smc:pm:sec:compiler} and the checklist of Section~\ref{smc:x:sec:pmchecklist}), but only the last step, from a quadratic sign formula to the quartic, is implemented. Missing: a parser from a finite machine and a supplied word to the rows $E,G,M,\ell,r$, the sign formula and the quartic DAG, with an independent audit; source~27 adds a checkable completeness certificate for the derived chamber.
\item\label{smc:x:q:population} \textbf{Low-degree formulas beyond four live signals} (source~26, Section~\ref{smc:pm:sec:prior}: ``which larger-population macro classes admit comparable low-degree formulas, and how additional geometric restrictions might control arity''). Source~27 shows that a finite sign formula need not exist at five signals (Corollary~\ref{smc:fv:n11.1}); sources~28 and~29 give existential integer certificates of degree~12 for the rotation macros, and Part~XI's Report~60 extends them to elliptic planar returns. Missing: a statement for every supplied macro with five or more live signals (a bounded-degree existential certificate, or an obstruction to one), and any arity bound uniform over macros; source~26 states that its arity grows with the word.
\item\label{smc:x:q:offset} \textbf{Variable time offsets and signed deadlines} (source~26, Section~\ref{smc:pm:sec:deadline}). The source says that an initial rational time offset ``can be added by ordinary cross-multiplication, but if its numerator and denominator are new variables the degree ledger must be reconsidered'', and that signed deadline numerators may be handled ``by a separately specified natural encoding''. Neither encoding is given. Missing: the encodings and their degree and witness ledgers; the degree-at-most-two claim is proved only for section time zero and fixed coefficients.
\item\label{smc:x:q:validity} \textbf{An effective validity test in higher dimension} (source~26, Theorem~\ref{smc:pm:thm:rational} and the remark after it). The rational-limit theorem is conditional on validity and supplies ``no arbitrary-dimensional recognition algorithm''. For the return matrices of order at most two the test is Proposition~\ref{smc:pm:prop:roots}; in general the infinite criterion~\eqref{smc:pm:eq:infinite} is a conjunction of positivity problems for linear recurrences of higher order, whose general decidability is not known; source~26 asserts no general Positivity algorithm (it cites~\cite{owpositivity} for the low-order case) and no reduction from arbitrary Positivity instances. Missing: a decision procedure for the infinite criterion of a supplied macro with more than four live signals, or a reduction showing that one would decide Positivity.
\item\label{smc:x:q:unique} \textbf{Unique-witness, finite-fold or quartic certificates at five signals} (source~27, Section~\ref{smc:fv:sec:boundary}: its obstruction ``does not prove that five signals prevent unique-witness or quartic Diophantine certificates by other methods''; sources~28 and~29). The certificates of sources~28 and~29 have infinitely many witnesses for each accepted input (signed-pair adapters and the Pell witnesses), and degree~12. Missing: either a certificate for source~27's predicate with a unique (or finitely many) positive witnesses, or with degree four as at four signals, or a proof that none exists. A canonical choice of every signed pair and of the Pell witnesses would be one route, as Part~VIII's canonical height is for its outer history (Theorem~\ref{smc:ch:thm:combined}); it is not attempted by the sources.
\item\label{smc:x:q:counts} \textbf{Smaller certificates} (source~27, Question~\ref{smc:fv:q:diophantine}; sources~28 and~29). Sources~28 and~29 state that their counts are neither optimal nor lower bounds, and source~28's quartic variant trades one witness for six gates. Missing: lower bounds, or smaller representations of the same predicates; for source~29's family an emitted arithmetic DAG with a literal gate ledger (``No emitted generic arithmetic DAG or gate ledger'', the programme's review).
\item\label{smc:x:q:words} \textbf{Shorter words and fewer types} (source~27, Question~\ref{smc:fv:q:reduce}; source~29, Section~\ref{smc:rf:sec:prior}). Source~27's counts of eight speeds, 169 types and 138 events are not claimed minimal, and source~29's word length grows with $|b|/(c+a)$ (note at the end of Section~\ref{smc:rf:sec:prior}). Missing: a realization whose word length is polynomial in the bit length of $(a,b,c)$, or a lower bound; any reduction needs its own complete chronology proof.
\item\label{smc:x:q:real} \textbf{Finer classification of the real validity sets} (source~29, Section~\ref{smc:rf:sec:realinputs}). The real validity set is proved $G_\delta$ and not $F_\sigma$, and properly co-semidecidable in the finite-time BSS model; source~29 makes ``No Borel-completeness claim'' and no Type-2, oracle or BSS-degree statement. Missing: those classifications.
\item\label{smc:x:q:accumulation} \textbf{Accumulation without a supplied macro, and beyond it} (Part~I's direction, Section~\ref{smc:cg:q:accumulation}). Sources~26--29 certify infinite repetition of a supplied ultimately periodic macro and compute its accumulation time; none of them finds a periodic itinerary, treats executions that are not ultimately periodic, or defines any dynamics at or after the accumulation. Those parts of Part~I's direction stay open.
\end{enumerate}

\wtag\ \textbf{The common section.} All four sources work on one outgoing section of a finite deterministic rational-speed number-preserving signal machine: stationary markers $L=0<X=x<Y=y<R=D$ and a messenger leaving $L$ at speed $+1$. \wtag\ \textbf{What the four sources do.} They form one chain of realization theorems, each inheriting the previous one by a pinned byte copy.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Source~30 realizes every $A\in\GL_2(\Q)$ with $\det A>0$, at every positive rational scale $\lambda$, by a complete binary word returning $z\mapsto\lambda\diag(1,A)z$ on an exact bounded open rational polygon (Theorem~\ref{smc:pl:thm:physical}). It classifies the strict infinite-iteration kernel $\plKer(A,P)$ of every rational planar map on every bounded open convex rational polygon: it is nonsemialgebraic exactly in the infinite-order elliptic case (Theorem~\ref{smc:pl:thm:geometry}). It certifies that case with an explicit degree-twelve polynomial in $81J$ positive witnesses for $J$ contacts (Theorem~\ref{smc:pl:thm:certificate}), and every other case by a unique-slack quadratic (Corollary~\ref{smc:pl:cor:quadratic}).
\item Source~31 proves that a fixed complete binary word with positive flights induces an invertible rational linear map between full sections (Theorem~\ref{smc:iv:thm:inverse}), with determinant $(-1)^m\prod_j s_j^+/s_j^-$ (Theorem~\ref{smc:iv:thm:parity}). A seven-event reversal (Theorem~\ref{smc:iv:thm:reversal}) extends source~30 to all of $\GL_2(\Q)$, and a fixed-scale return $\lambda\diag(1,A)$ exists exactly when $\det A\ne0$ (Corollary~\ref{smc:iv:cor:gl}).

It exhibits one 44-event word with both clock behaviours (Theorem~\ref{smc:pj:thm:mixed}) and proves a spectral Zeno criterion on the active cyclic subspace (Theorem~\ref{smc:pj:thm:clock}).

\noindent{\large\bfseries Source 30 (batch-91 manuscript 12): Planar signal realization and strict validity kernels}\par
\noindent\emph{Exactly five live signals and explicit positive integer certificates}, ``Research Report~60'', 4 October 2026. \wtag\ From the archive \path{Planar_Signal_Realization_Source.zip} (main file \path{Report60/Report60.tex}, 28-page PDF); its labels carry the prefix \texttt{smc:pl:}. Its abstract follows.
\begin{quote}\small
Every rational orientation-preserving planar map admits an exactly five-live-signal realization with a finite complete collision word, rational speeds, full outgoing-phase closure and an exact bounded open rational guard polygon. The construction includes a centered determinant dilation, so it does not require a rational square root of the determinant. We then classify the strict infinite-iteration kernel of every rational planar map on every bounded open convex rational polygon containing the origin. Its sole nonsemialgebraic case is infinite-order elliptic dynamics: an open rational ellipse together with its boundary minus finitely many backward contact orbits. An elementary denominator test gives uniform polynomial-time rational membership in that branch. Finally, those orbit complements have an explicit positive-integer polynomial certificate with $81J$ witnesses, $44J$ residuals and exact degree twelve; the strict kernel adds one witness and one residual. All remaining rational-input branches have explicit quadratic certificates with uniquely forced positive slack tuples. Every equation, positivity adapter and inherited Pell dependency is displayed. Conventional proofs, frozen source packets, and fresh independent exact/static audits are kept distinct from physical simulation and formal proof certification.
\end{quote}


\section{The three results and their common interface}\label{smc:xi:sec:plstart}
An outgoing signal section has stationary markers at $0<x<y<D$ and a messenger at the left anchor moving at speed $+1$. Put
\[
 \xi=x-D/3,\qquad \eta=y-2D/3,\qquad w=(\xi/D,\eta/D)^T.
\]
The messenger and left anchor are distinct outgoing strands at their shared contact. Live-signal count is a strand count, not a count of occupied spatial sites. A complete word records \emph{all} collisions, including spectator crossings and any unprescribed contact receiving an identity rule.

\begin{theorem}[Physical realization]\label{smc:pl:thm:physical}
For every $A\in\GL_2(\Q)$ with $\det A>0$ and every $\lambda\in\Q_{>0}$, an effective finite deterministic number-preserving rational-speed signal machine has exactly five live signals and a fixed complete binary-collision word returning
\[
 (D,\xi,\eta)^T\longmapsto \lambda\diag(1,A)(D,\xi,\eta)^T.
\]
The word restores every marker label and the messenger's outgoing left-anchor phase. Its exact normalized domain is a bounded open rational polygon $P$ with $0\in\operatorname{int}P$. Infinite repetition is valid precisely when
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:kernel}
 w\in\plKer(A,P):=\bigcap_{n\ge0}A^{-n}P.
\end{equation}
Every valid infinite run is Zeno exactly when $0<\lambda<1$; then all strands approach the left anchor, and the accumulation time is rational for rational initial data.
\end{theorem}
Here $A^{-n}P$ means preimage, even in the later abstract classification where singular $A$ is allowed. ``Fixed'' means fixed after $A,\lambda$ have been selected. This is not one unchanged finite machine accepting arbitrary matrix inputs.

\wtag\ [As existence statements, the physical realizations of Part~X are cases of Theorem~\ref{smc:pl:thm:physical}: source~29's (Theorem~\ref{smc:rf:thm:main}) is the case of an infinite-order rotation $A\in\mathrm{SO}_2(\Q)$ at a positive rational scale, and source~27's contracted rotation (Theorem~\ref{smc:fv:thm:main}) is one such case; their words are different constructions. The last sentence of the theorem, the rational accumulation time, is a special case of source~26's Theorem~\ref{smc:pm:thm:rational} (Remark~\ref{smc:xi:rem:zeno}).]

\begin{theorem}[Exact planar geometry and decision]\label{smc:pl:thm:geometry}
Let $A\in\Q^{2\times2}$ and $P=\{w:h_iw<b_i,1\le i\le m\}$ be bounded, open, convex, rational and contain $0$. Then $\plKer(A,P)$ is nonsemialgebraic exactly when
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:ellipticcriterion}
 \det A=1,\qquad -2<\tr A<2,\qquad \tr A\notin\{-1,0,1\}.
\end{equation}
In that case there are effective rational $Q=Q^T>0$, $r^2>0$, and a nonempty finite set $E\subset\Q^2\setminus\{0\}$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:ellipseformula}
 \plKer=\{w:w^TQw<r^2\}\ \cup\
 \left(\{w:w^TQw=r^2\}\setminus\bigcup_{z\in E,n\ge0}\{A^{-n}z\}\right).
\end{equation}
No finite real-coefficient polynomial-sign formula agrees with this predicate on every rational point. In all other cases the real kernel is a finite conjunction of real-algebraic linear equalities and rational strict or weak affine guards restricted to the bounded-orbit subspace; rational-input membership has a finite rational linear-sign formula.

For each fixed $A$, rational membership is polynomial-time in the encoding of $P,w$. The elliptic branch is polynomial-time uniformly in $A,P,w$. Uniform explicit affine-sign output can require exponentially many atoms. A credited low-order recurrence result also gives a uniform counting-hierarchy upper bound; no uniform polynomial-time result is inferred from it.
\end{theorem}
\wtag\ [The kernels of source~27 (Theorem~\ref{smc:fv:thm:main}) and source~29 (Theorem~\ref{smc:rf:thm:consequences}) are instances of the elliptic case. Source~29 also proves an obstruction on all positive real inputs (Theorem~\ref{smc:rf:thm:realinput}), which source~30 does not restate; source~30's sign obstructions are for rational and positive integer inputs. The rotational-density mechanism is prior work of Fijalkow et al.~\cite{fopww17}, as source~30 says in Section~\ref{smc:pl:sec:literature}.]

\begin{theorem}[Explicit positive-integer certificate]\label{smc:pl:thm:certificate}
Fix an infinite-order elliptic rational $A$ and $J\ge1$ nonzero rational contacts. For a rational point encoded by integer linear expressions $(X/N,Y/N)$ with $N>0$, avoidance of their backward orbits has an explicit integer-coefficient sum-of-squares polynomial of exact degree $12$, existentially quantified over $81J$ ordinary positive integer witnesses. There are $44J$ residual equations before squaring.

For the strict kernel \eqref{smc:pl:eq:ellipseformula}, the ledger is $1+81J$ witnesses and $1+44J$ residuals. Three positive physical gaps can be used directly as inputs. An optional paid one-positive-input Cantor transport adds four witnesses and two quadratic residuals, giving $5+81J$ and $3+44J$ respectively, still of degree $12$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{remark}[\wtag\ Three ledgers]\label{smc:xi:rem:ledgers}
Part~X prints two earlier ledgers for related objects. Source~28 certifies one fixed rotation machine with 81 positive witnesses and 44 equations (85 and~46 with paid one-input transport). Source~29 certifies the rotation family with $1+80J$ witnesses and $1+43J$ equations, where $J$ counts the distinct nearest contacts. Source~30's $81J$ and $44J$ (and $1+81J$, $1+44J$ for the strict kernel) count a different construction, for an arbitrary infinite-order elliptic map and any $J$ fixed contacts. Per contact it has fourteen outer equations (O1)--(O14) and seven strictly positive variables, where source~29 has thirteen equations and six. Source~30 excludes the time-zero match and the positive-time matches by two separate positive witnesses $J_0$ and~$J_1$, and it notes that for a general elliptic map the times zero and one both have denominator one and must be distinguished (Section~\ref{smc:pl:sec:extraction}). Source~29's single gate (O13) also excludes the time-zero match of a rotation, whose Gaussian data at exponent $0$ are $P=1$, $C=1$, $S=0$. Whether source~30's two gates can be merged is open (Question~\ref{smc:xi:q:gates}). The three counts are explicit upper bounds for three constructions, not competing measurements of one object, and none is claimed minimal; Table~\ref{smc:x:tab:ledgers} in Part~X tabulates them.
\end{remark}

Outside the infinite-order elliptic case, the finite rational linear description instead gives a quadratic sum-of-squares certificate with a unique positive slack tuple for each valid fixed integer-gap input (Corollary~\ref{smc:pl:cor:quadratic}).

The elliptic certificate is a fully displayed finite polynomial schema. It is not a generic emitted arithmetic DAG, an optimized gate count, a small-witness algorithm, or a finite-fold representation. The sign obstruction has no quantified integer witnesses and so does not contradict this certificate. No universal Turing-completeness theorem, priority claim, minimal live-signal lower bound, or continuation through a Zeno point is asserted.

\section{Complete collision primitives}\label{smc:pl:sec:primitives}
Distances below are measured from the current stationary anchor. The messenger points into the interval at primitive entrance and has speed $\pm1$. Only one target marker can move, always with speed of modulus less than one. Reflecting about the right anchor reverses physical velocities and preserves every distance inequality and duration.

\subsection{Anchor scaling}
For $u>0$, launch a target initially at distance $z$ with speed
\[
 h=\frac{u-1}{u+1}\in(-1,1)
\]
when the outward messenger reaches it. Reverse the messenger, bounce it at the anchor, restore the target on the next outward meeting, and reverse and bounce the messenger once more. The four principal time--position pairs are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:scaleevents}
 (z,z),\quad (2z,0),\quad (2z+uz,uz),\quad (2z+2uz,0).
\end{equation}
Indeed $z+h((2z+uz)-z)=uz$. Denote this operation by $L_z(u)$; its duration is $2(z+uz)$.

The exact guards require $z$ and $uz$ to lie strictly between the same unchanged nearest stationary neighbors. The lower endpoint is the anchor for the nearest target; the outermost target has no upper neighbor. Monotonicity of the target between these endpoints prevents all target--neighbor contacts. For each stationary inner spectator at distance $s$, all four messenger crossings are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:scalespectator}
 s,\quad 2z-s,\quad 2z+s,\quad 2z+2uz-s.
\end{equation}
The inequalities $s<z$ and $s<uz$ put these groups in the prescribed outward, reversed, outward and reversed orders between the principal events. Outer markers are never reached. The strict speed bound separates the launch and restoration strands and gives a unique intersection. Thus there are exactly $4+4k$ events with $k$ inner spectators.

Necessity is equally important. If a prospective endpoint reaches or crosses a neighbor, continuity forces a target--neighbor contact by that checkpoint. Equality may instead give a simultaneous contact or collapse a prescribed interval. None preserves the selected globally time-separated complete binary word. The argument stops at the first obstruction and does not assume an affine continuation remains physical after it.

\subsection{Reflector homothety}
Let the target at $t$ be nearest to the anchor, and let a stationary reflector be at $z>t$. For $v>0$, its first outward hit launches the target at $h=(1-v)/(1+v)$ while the messenger continues outward, crosses every spectator, reflects at $z$, crosses those spectators in reverse, restores the target on its inward leg, and bounces at the anchor. Solving the two lines gives
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:homothety}
 t'=vt+(1-v)z,\qquad T_{\rm restore}=2z-t',\qquad T_{\rm finish}=2z.
\end{equation}
Call the operation $H_z(v)$. Its exact guards are $0<t,t'<s$, where $s\le z$ is the nearest unchanged outer marker. The target remains in this interval by monotonicity. A spectator $q$ is crossed at $q$ and $2z-q$; $t'<q$ places its returning crossing before restoration. Also $0<t'<z$ places restoration between the reflector and final anchor bounces. There are $4+2k$ events for $k$ intermediate spectators. Failed endpoints force the same first-contact or collapsed-interval obstruction as for scaling.

\subsection{Translation and its complete guard reduction}
For $e<1$, concatenate
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:translation}
 T_z(e):=L_t\!\left(\frac1{1-e}\right)\ ;\ H_z(1-e),
 \qquad t\longmapsto \frac{t}{1-e}\longmapsto t+ez.
\end{equation}
Both target-moving phases have speed $e/(2-e)\in(-1,1)$. The exact guard is simply $0<t,t+ez<s\le z$. To justify the omitted internal row, put $k=t/(1-e)$ and $f=t+ez$. Then
\[
 k-f=\frac{e(f-z)}{1-e}.
\]
For $0<e<1$, $t<k<f$ because $f<z$; for $e<0$, $f<k<t$ because $t<z$; for $e=0$ all three coincide. Thus the internal endpoint lies between the retained endpoints. Conversely an invalid internal endpoint already breaks the scale; if it is valid and the final endpoint fails, the homothety breaks the word. This proves necessity and sufficiency for the grouped translation.

Zero parameters are retained. When $e=0$ or $u=v=1$, the temporary target label has speed zero, but its messenger partner has speed $\pm1$. These are nonempty positive-duration collision sequences, not empty-word conventions.

\subsection{Full anchor transfers}
With every marker stationary and $0<x<y<D$, a left-to-right transfer crosses $x$, crosses $y$ and reflects at $D$, at relative times $x,y,D$. The final messenger points left. The reverse transfer crosses $y$, crosses $x$ and reflects at $0$, at times $D-y,D-x,D$, and ends pointing right. Each costs time $D$ and three events. Its guard is exactly the existing strict ordering; it is never a zero-time phase switch.

\section{Signed shears and determinant dilation}\label{smc:pl:sec:synthesis}
Write
\[
 U(t)=\plMat{1}{t}{0}{1},\qquad V(t)=\plMat{1}{0}{t}{1}.
\]
For rational $t$, let $N=\max(1,\lceil4|t|\rceil)$ and $\delta=t/N$, so $|\delta|\le1/4$, including $\delta=0$.

\subsection{Exact centered shear blocks}
A left-anchor micro-shear is $T_y(\delta)$ followed by $T_D(-2\delta/3)$. It sends $x$ to $x+\delta(y-2D/3)$ and fixes $y,D$, hence acts by $U(\delta)$ on $(\xi,\eta)$. Its first translation has $4+4$ events. The second has $4+6$, including both crossings of the $y$ spectator. The total is $18$ events and four temporary target labels.

For all $N$ steps, define the incoming-coordinate endpoints
\begin{align}
 a_{2k}&=x+k\delta(y-2D/3) &&(0\le k\le N),\label{smc:pl:eq:shearendpoints}\\
 a_{2k+1}&=a_{2k}+\delta y &&(0\le k<N).
\end{align}
The exact supplied rows are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:shearguards}
 y>0,\quad D-y>0,\quad a_i>0,\quad y-a_i>0\quad(0\le i\le2N).
\end{equation}
There are $4N+4$ rows. The translation lemma supplies all hidden internal checkpoints, so these rows characterize all $18N$ events, including spectator crossings. The return is $U(t)$.

For a right-anchor block put $r=D-y$, $s=D-x$, and use the same construction with $(x,y)=(r,s)$. It sends $r$ to $r+t(s-2D/3)$, so
\[
 y'=y+t(x-D/3),
\]
which is $V(t)$ with the \emph{same} sign. Its $4N+4$ rows are $s>0,D-s>0,b_i>0,s-b_i>0$, using the reflected endpoint formulas. It also has $18N$ events and four temporary labels per micro-step.

At the center $x=D/3,y=2D/3$, every completed micro-shear fixes its target. The intermediate translation endpoint is
\[
 D/3+2\delta D/3\in[D/6,D/2],
\]
strictly inside the interval ending at $2D/3$. Thus every retained row is center-strict, for arbitrarily large total shear: large parameters are realized by finitely many small legal steps.

\subsection{Every determinant-one factorization and zero pivot}
Let $B=\plMat abcd$ with $ad-bc=1$. Products act on column vectors; the rightmost factor is performed first. Direct multiplication gives the following exhaustive branches:
\begin{align}
 c\ne0:\quad &B=U((a-1)/c)V(c)U((d-1)/c),\label{smc:pl:eq:factorc}\\
 c=0, b\ne0:\quad &B=V((d-1)/b)U(b)V((a-1)/b),\label{smc:pl:eq:factorb}\\
 b=c=0:\quad &B=U(a-1)V(1)U(a^{-1}-1)V(-a).\label{smc:pl:eq:factordiag}
\end{align}
For \eqref{smc:pl:eq:factorc}, the upper-right entry is $(ad-1)/c=b$. For \eqref{smc:pl:eq:factorb}, the lower-left entry is $(ad-1)/b=c$. The diagonal branch first establishes $a\ne0$ and $d=a^{-1}$, and works for negative $a$. No other branch divides by $a$ or $d$, so zero diagonal pivots are covered.

The chronological axis lists are respectively $x,y,x$; $y,x,y$; and $y,x,y,x$, with reversed parameter order from the displayed products. Start at the left anchor, insert a full transfer whenever the next axis changes anchor, and end with a return to the left if required. For $B_0$ blocks and indicators $\sigma_j=0$ for $x$, $1$ for $y$, the transfer count is
\[
 T=\sigma_1+\sum_{j=1}^{B_0-1}|\sigma_{j+1}-\sigma_j|+\sigma_{B_0}.
\]
The branches give $T=2,4,4$ respectively, with $B_0=3,3,4$. The initial and final transfers in the second branch cannot be omitted. If $K$ is the sum of the subdivision counts, the shear word has $18K+3T$ events, $4K+4B_0$ supplied guards and $4K$ temporary labels. All markers and the messenger phase close.

For $B=I$ the retained list is $y(-1),x(0),y(1),x(0)$. It has $K=10,T=4$ and $192$ events; it is a genuine positive-duration closed word. No identity simplification is used in these counts.

\subsection{A centered one-axis dilation}
For $q\in[3/4,5/4]$, perform
\[
 L_x(q)\ ;\ T_D((1-q)/3).
\]
The target endpoints are $x,qx,x'=qx+(1-q)D/3$, hence $\xi'=q\xi$, $\eta'=\eta$, $D'=D$. Its translation parameter is in $[-1/12,1/12]$. The exact eight rows are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:dilationguards}
 \begin{gathered}
 y>0,\quad D-y>0,\qquad x>0,\quad y-x>0,\\
 qx>0,\quad y-qx>0,\qquad x'>0,\quad y-x'>0.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
The endpoint $qx$ must remain. For example $q=5/4,x=1/2,y=3/5,D=1$ gives $x'=13/24\in(0,y)$ but $qx=5/8>y$. The translation's own internal endpoint needs no extra row by \eqref{smc:pl:eq:translation}. At the center the guarded positions are $D/3,qD/3,D/3$, with $qD/3\in[D/4,5D/12]$. The block has $14$ events, three temporary labels and a center-strict exact chamber.

For arbitrary $q>0$, $q\ne1$, set
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:qtelescope}
 H=\max\left(1,\left\lceil\frac{4|q-1|}{\min(1,q)}\right\rceil\right),
 \quad u_j=1+\frac{j(q-1)}H,\quad q_j=\frac{u_j}{u_{j-1}}.
\end{equation}
All $u_j\ge\min(1,q)>0$, and $|q_j-1|\le1/4$. Their product telescopes to $q$. Compose these $H$ small blocks to realize $C_q=\diag(q,1)$, using $14H$ events, $3H$ temporary labels and $8H$ guards. For $q=1$, put $H=0$ and omit only this suffix.

Given $A$ with $q=\det A>0$, define $B=C_q^{-1}A\in\SL_2(\Q)$. Perform the shear word for $B$, complete its left-anchor return, and then perform $C_q$. The return is $C_qB=A$. In particular nonsquare determinants such as $2$ and $3/2$ require no irrational square root and no extra live signal.

\subsection{Arbitrary positive global scale and full ledger}
If $\lambda<1$, scale targets $x,y,D$ in that order by $\lambda$, always about the left anchor. Inner neighbors have already been scaled and outer neighbors have not. Both target endpoints therefore stay in the unchanged neighbor interval. For $\lambda>1$ use $D,y,x$ in reverse order, so outer neighbors have already been scaled. The same monotonicity argument applies. The event counts $4,8,12$ sum to $24$; there are three temporary labels and no additional guard. For $\lambda=1$ omit this suffix.

Writing $\varepsilon=\mathbf1_{\lambda\ne1}$, the complete counts are
\begin{align}
 m_{\rm events}&=18K+3T+14H+24\varepsilon,\label{smc:pl:eq:physicalledger}\\
 m_{\rm guards}&=4K+4B_0+8H,\nonumber\\
 m_{\rm temporary}&=4K+3H+3\varepsilon,\nonumber\\
 m_{\rm metasignals}&=22K+3T+17H+27\varepsilon+4,\nonumber\\
 m_{\rm live}&=5.\nonumber
\end{align}
The alphabet consists of one messenger phase for each event, the temporary target labels, and the four permanent stationary labels. These counts are not minimized and need not be polynomial in the bit length of $A$.

\section{Exact chamber and finite deterministic completion}\label{smc:pl:sec:chamber}
Pull every supplied row back through earlier homogeneous rational returns in coordinates $z=(D,\xi,\eta)^T$. Each has form $\alpha D+\beta\xi+\gamma\eta>0$ with rational coefficients. Transfers and global scaling introduce no extra rows. On $D=1$ their conjunction defines $P$.

Sufficiency follows by induction over the exact primitive chronology. Every nonmoving marker is stationary, the sole moving marker stays in its strict neighbor interval, and every messenger leg lists all stationary points it crosses. The strict speed inequalities exclude hidden target intersections and ensure all binary contacts are separated in time.

For necessity, take the first primitive or grouped translation with a failed prospective endpoint, all previous checkpoints being ordered. Its preceding word prefix is valid. A scale or homothety then forces an additional, simultaneous, collapsed or reordered contact by the failed checkpoint. For a translation, the internal scale either already fails, or its endpoint is valid and the final homothety fails. Initial row failure means the section itself was not allowed. This uses affine equations only until the first physical obstruction. Default rules cannot erase extra contacts from a \emph{complete} collision word.

Every completed shear and determinant dilation fixes the center, and all internal center checkpoints were verified. Therefore every pulled-back row is strict at $0$. The first block's rows imply $0<x<y<D$; for a right-based first block, $0<r<s<D$ is the equivalent condition. Hence $P$ is a full-dimensional bounded open convex rational polygon. Supplied rows may be repeated or redundant: exactness is a statement about their conjunction, not facet irredundancy.

Give the messenger a fresh label $Q_j$ before event $j$, for $0\le j<m_{\rm events}$, and identify the final outgoing $Q_m$ with $Q_0$. Temporary target labels carry their rational speeds in $(-1,1)$. At the prescribed event emit
\[
 \{Q_j,Z_{\rm in}\}\longrightarrow
 \{Q_{(j+1)\bmod m},Z_{\rm out}\}.
\]
Only launch and restoration change the marker label. Spectators and anchor/reflector bounces preserve the stationary marker. Input keys are distinct because $Q_j$ is distinct. Incoming and outgoing pairs have distinct speeds, since the messenger speed is $\pm1$. Incoming order is decreasing speed and outgoing order increasing speed, so outgoing strands separate. At the final event every permanent marker label is restored and $Q_0$ points right at the left anchor.

Complete the finite rule table with the identity output on every other legal input set of pairwise distinct speeds, including larger sets. This is deterministic and preserves cardinality. The prescribed rules consume and emit one messenger and one marker, and the default completion also preserves cardinality. There are exactly five live strands throughout every finite part of a valid run. The standard outgoing-collision convention is consistent with the definition and initial-configuration discussion in Becker et al.~\cite{accumulations}.

\section{Iteration and the rational Zeno clock}\label{smc:pl:sec:clock}
At a completed word $D'=\lambda D$ and $w'=Aw$. Full label and phase restoration allows literal word repetition; the exact chamber then proves \eqref{smc:pl:eq:kernel}. Its center is always valid, so the infinite domain is nonempty. The compiler's $P$ is its actual exact chamber; no claim permits arbitrary replacement of $P$ while retaining the physical counts.

Every primitive duration is a rational homogeneous linear form in its incoming positions. Thus the full duration is a fixed rational row $\ell z$. Before the global suffix all positions lie in $[0,D]$. A translation takes less than $6D$, a micro-shear less than $12D$, a centered dilation less than $10D$, and a transfer exactly $D$. The global suffix takes
\[
 2(1+\lambda)(x+y+D)<6(1+\lambda)D.
\]
Every retained micro-shear contains a far-reflector $H_D$ phase of duration $2D$, and at least one such step remains even for the identity. Consequently, throughout the exact chamber,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:durationbound}
 2D\le\ell z<\bigl(12K+T+10H+6(1+\lambda)\varepsilon\bigr)D.
\end{equation}
At iteration $n$, $D_n=\lambda^nD_0$. The two-sided comparison with a geometric series proves Zeno behavior exactly for $0<\lambda<1$. In that case every point of the $n$th word lies in $[0,\max(1,\lambda)D_n]$, hence all strands tend to the fixed left anchor. For $\lambda\ge1$ the lower bound forces divergent total time.

For rational data and $\lambda<1$, write $N_0=\lambda\diag(1,A)$ and take the rational cyclic subspace
\[
 V=\Span_{\Q}\{z,N_0z,N_0^2z\}.
\]
It is invariant by Cayley--Hamilton. A valid normalized orbit stays in bounded $P$, so $N_0^nz\to0$. Since $z$ is cyclic on $V$, the restriction has no eigenvalue of modulus at least one. Thus $I-N_0$ is invertible on $V$ over $\Q$, and
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:zenoclock}
 T_\infty=\ell\bigl((I-N_0)|_V\bigr)^{-1}z\in\Q.
\end{equation}
A rational basis of $V$ reduces this to rational linear algebra. The full-space inverse need not exist: an unused expanding eigenmode of $A$ can have eigenvalue $1/\lambda$. Formula \eqref{smc:pl:eq:zenoclock} avoids that singularity. No state or continuation after accumulation is defined.
\begin{remark}[\wtag\ A second route to a Part~X theorem]\label{smc:xi:rem:zeno}
The rationality of $T_\infty$ is a special case of source~26's Theorem~\ref{smc:pm:thm:rational} (Part~X): a valid ultimately periodic complete macro of any fixed finite population, with rational speeds and rational initial positions, has only rational finite accumulation times. The cyclic-subspace computation \eqref{smc:pl:eq:zenoclock}, which avoids an unused expanding mode, is source~30's own route and is printed here once. Sources~31, 32 and~33 repeat it for their compositions (Remark~\ref{smc:xi:rem:zenoiv}, equation~\eqref{smc:pj:eq:active-time} and Remark~\ref{smc:hl:cor:clock}); source~32's Theorem~\ref{smc:pj:thm:clock} adds a spectral criterion.
\end{remark}
\section{The bounded-orbit subspace and every spectral case}\label{smc:pl:sec:spectral}
This part applies to \emph{every} rational $2\times2$ matrix, including singular and negative-determinant matrices, independently of the physical realization theorem. Let
\[
 P=\{w\in\R^2:h_iw<b_i, 1\le i\le m\}
\]
be bounded, open, convex and rational with $0\in P$. All $b_i>0$. Discard constant rows; redundant nonconstant rows are allowed. Define
\[
 \plBnd(A)=\{w:\sup_{n\ge0}\|A^nw\|<\infty\}.
\]
Because $P$ is bounded, $\plKer(A,P)\subseteq\plBnd(A)$.

In real Jordan coordinates, $\plBnd(A)$ is the sum of the entire generalized eigenspaces for $|\mu|<1$ and the ordinary eigenspaces for $|\mu|=1$. Expanding modes contribute only zero. A stable Jordan block has a polynomial times geometric decay; a nontrivial Jordan block at $\pm1$ grows linearly unless the generalized coordinate vanishes. An expanding block grows for every nonzero component. An invertible eigenbasis prevents unbounded components from canceling in norm. These observations give an effective real-algebraic basis, using quadratic roots and linear equations.

Repeated eigenvalues are rational, equal to $\tr(A)/2$. A repeated stable eigenvalue, including a nontrivial block or $A^2=0$, gives $\plBnd=\R^2$. At $\pm1$, the scalar case gives $\R^2$ and a nontrivial block gives the ordinary eigenline. A repeated expanding eigenvalue gives $\{0\}$. Distinct real eigenvalues contribute their stable and unit eigenspaces. Nonreal conjugates have common modulus $\sqrt{\det A}$ and yield $\R^2$ when that modulus is at most one, or $\{0\}$ when it is greater than one. This exhausts the planar possibilities.

\begin{lemma}[Closure, without replacing strict validity]\label{smc:pl:lem:closure}
For
\[
 C=\bigcap_{n\ge0}\{w:h_iA^nw\le b_i\text{ for every }i\},
\qquad \cl(\plKer)=C.
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The forward inclusion follows from continuity. For $w\in C$ and $0\le s<1$, $h_iA^n(sw)\le sb_i<b_i$, so $sw\in\plKer$ and $sw\to w$. The assertion concerns the closure only, not the membership of every point on its boundary.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Zero and one bounded dimension}
If $\plBnd=\{0\}$, then $\plKer=\{0\}$. If $\plBnd$ is a line, $A$ acts on it by a real $\mu$ with $|\mu|\le1$, and
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:linekernel}
 \plKer=\begin{cases}
 \plBnd\cap P,&0\le\mu\le1,\\
 \plBnd\cap P\cap A^{-1}P,&-1\le\mu<0.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
For nonnegative $\mu$ the orbit lies in $[0,w]$; for negative $\mu$ its even and odd subsequences lie in $[0,w]$ and $[0,Aw]$. Convexity and $0\in P$ prove both formulas, including $0,\pm1$. The guard rows are rational in ambient coordinates, but the line itself need not be rational.

For example,
\[
 A=\plMat01{-1}3,\qquad P=(-1,1)^2,\qquad \mu=(3-\sqrt5)/2
\]
gives the nontrivial kernel segment on $y=\mu x$. No finite Boolean combination of rational affine signs describes this \emph{real} segment. Otherwise, at every point at least one nonconstant atomic form would vanish, since nonzero signs persist in an ambient disk. Finitely many rational lines cannot cover an irrational-slope segment: each meets it in at most one point.

The same line contains no nonzero rational point. Thus its rational-input predicate is simply $w=0$. More generally, a rational nonzero eigenvector makes its eigenvalue rational by dividing a nonzero coordinate of $Aw$ by the corresponding coordinate of $w$, and a rational eigenvalue has a rational eigenspace. This proves the coefficient-field distinction required in Theorem~\ref{smc:pl:thm:geometry}.

\subsection{Two stable dimensions and a finite strict horizon}\label{smc:pl:sec:stable}
Suppose every eigenvalue has modulus less than one. Enumerate exact rational powers until
\[
 \|A^k\|_\infty\le1/2,\qquad k\ge1,\qquad
 C_A=\max_{0\le j<k}\|A^j\|_\infty.
\]
Termination follows from $A^n\to0$. Compute rational $R,\epsilon>0$ with
\[
 P\subset[-R,R]^2,\qquad[-\epsilon,\epsilon]^2\subset P.
\]
An outer $R$ follows by enumerating the closed polygon's vertices. One may take $\epsilon=\min_i b_i/(2\|h_i\|_1)$. Choose $q_0\ge0$ with $2^{-q_0}C_AR<\epsilon$ and put $N=q_0k$. For $n=lk+j\ge N$, $l\ge q_0$, $0\le j<k$, every $w\in P$ satisfies
\[
 \|A^nw\|_\infty\le2^{-l}C_AR<\epsilon.
\]
All later guards are automatically strict, so
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:finitehorizon}
 \plKer=\bigcap_{0\le n\le N}A^{-n}P.
\end{equation}
The redundant time $N$ makes the convention valid also when $N=0$. This is a finite open rational polygon. Neither diagonalizability, positivity, invertibility nor a rational eigenbasis was used.

For fixed $A$, $k,C_A$ are constants. In dimension two, candidate vertices come from pairs of supplied lines; exact feasibility and Cramer's rule have polynomial bit cost. Their coordinates, $R$, and $\epsilon$ have polynomial bit length in the input length $L$. Thus $\log(R/\epsilon)=O(L)$ and $N=O_A(L)$. The powers through $N$ and all pulled-back rows have polynomial bit length, proving fixed-$A$ polynomial membership. If $A$ is input, the enumeration is only an effective procedure; it does not prove a uniform polynomial horizon or output size.

\subsection{Real unit spectra and mixed unit--stable spectra}
If $\plBnd=\R^2$ and both real eigenvalues have modulus one, semisimplicity gives $A^2=I$, so $\plKer=P\cap A^{-1}P$. Otherwise consider distinct eigenvalues $\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}$ and $\mu$ with $|\mu|<1$. Since the trace is rational, $\mu$ is rational. Let
\[
 E=\frac{A-\mu I}{\varepsilon-\mu},\qquad F=I-E,\qquad A=\varepsilon E+\mu F.
\]
If $0<|\mu|<1$, write $r=\mu^2\in(0,1)$. For $j=0,1$,
\[
 A^{2k+j}w=\varepsilon^jEw+r^k\mu^jFw.
\]
Each scalar guard is a convex interpolation of its initial parity value $h_iA^jw$ and limiting value $h_i\varepsilon^jEw$. Since $r^k>0$, all finite values are strict exactly when the first is strict and the second weak. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:mixedkernel}
 \plKer=P\cap A^{-1}P\cap
 \{w:Ew\in\cl(P),\ \varepsilon Ew\in\cl(P)\}.
\end{equation}
Necessity follows from $k=0$ and the limit; sufficiency follows from positive weight on the strict endpoint. Both signs of both eigenvalues are covered.

If $\mu=0$, the limit is actually reached at times one and two. The correct formula instead is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:mixedzero}
 \plKer=P\cap A^{-1}P\cap A^{-2}P,
\end{equation}
with every guard strict. For $\varepsilon=1$ the last factor is redundant. Weak limiting inequalities cannot be used at an attained limit.

A concrete half-open example is
\[
 A=\diag(1,1/2),\qquad
 P=\{(x,y):-1<x<2, -1<y<1, x+y<1\}.
\]
The rectangle guards persist. The remaining guards $x+2^{-n}y<1$ for all $n$ are equivalent to $x+y<1$ and $x\le1$, so $\plKer=P\cap\{x\le1\}$. It contains $(1,-1/2)$ even though the limiting point $(1,0)$ is outside $P$. No finite strict time prefix gives this set, because such an intersection is open. Finite linear description and finite strict-prefix determination are different properties.

\section{The rational critical ellipse and its missing orbits}\label{smc:pl:sec:ellipse}
For a nonreal unit spectrum, $\det A=1$ and $t=\tr A\in(-2,2)$. Choose nonzero $v\in\Q^2$. The columns of $S=[v,Av]$ are independent, since $A$ has no real eigenvector. Cayley--Hamilton yields
\[
 AS=SC,\qquad C=\plMat0{-1}1t.
\]
For $H=\plMat1{t/2}{t/2}1$, direct multiplication gives $C^THC=H$. Since $1-t^2/4>0$, $H$ is positive definite. Therefore
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:metric}
 Q=S^{-T}HS^{-1}\in\Q^{2\times2},\qquad Q>0,\qquad A^TQA=Q.
\end{equation}
A real change of basis makes the map a Euclidean rotation. A rational Euclidean conjugacy is neither needed nor automatic.

If an eigenvalue is a root of unity, its sum with its inverse is the rational algebraic integer $t$, hence an integer. The only possibilities are $-1,0,1$, giving orders $3,4,6$. Conversely each such trace gives that order. These cases have the finite open polygon
\[
 \plKer=\bigcap_{0\le n<\operatorname{ord}(A)}A^{-n}P.
\]
Every other rational trace in $(-2,2)$ is an irrational-angle rotation, and every nonzero orbit is dense in its $Q$-ellipse.

For each nonzero supplied row put
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pl:eq:contacts}
 d_i=h_iQ^{-1}h_i^T>0,\qquad r_i^2=\frac{b_i^2}{d_i},\qquad
 z_i=\frac{b_i}{d_i}Q^{-1}h_i^T.
\end{equation}
All these data are rational and $z_i^TQz_i=r_i^2$. Set $r^2=\min_i r_i^2$ and deduplicate the contacts $z_i$ attaining that minimum to obtain nonempty $E$. The $Q$-inner-product Cauchy--Schwarz inequality gives
\[
 h_iw\le\sqrt{d_i}\sqrt{w^TQw}.
\]
Every point below radius $r^2$ therefore satisfies every guard strictly. On the critical ellipse a guard can fail only by equality, exactly at its minimizing contact. On a larger ellipse a minimizing guard is strictly violated on a nonempty open arc, reached by orbit density. This proves \eqref{smc:pl:eq:ellipseformula}, including all strict-boundary exceptions.

For example $A=\plMat0{-1}1{1/2}$ preserves $Q=\plMat1{1/4}{1/4}1$. Its Euclidean rotation has cosine $1/4$ and sine $\sqrt{15}/4$. Rational conjugation of a rational matrix stays rational, so no rational basis can turn this map into that Euclidean rotation matrix. The metric formulation is the correct general one.
