\section{Results and the physical section}\label{smc:pj:sec:results}
The outgoing section has stationary markers $L=0$, $X=x$, $Y=y$, $R=D$ with $0<x<y<D$, and one messenger at $L$ outgoing at speed $+1$. The anchor and messenger are two outgoing strands at one contact. Counting them separately gives exactly five live signals. Put
\[
 \xi=x-D/3,\qquad \eta=y-2D/3,\qquad
 u=(\xi,\eta)^{\mathsf T},\qquad z=(D,u)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
The standard centered ray is $u=0$, $D>0$. A complete word lists every contact in order, including transparent crossings and remote contacts. Its chamber consists of exactly those initial section points that realize that word with strictly positive flights and no simultaneous or omitted event.

\begin{theorem}[Fixed center projective realization]\label{smc:pj:thm:main}
For every rational $s_0>0$, row $b\in\Q^{1\times2}$ and $A\in\GL_2(\Q)$, there is an effectively constructible finite deterministic rational-speed number-preserving signal machine and a fixed complete binary word whose literal section return is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:main}
 z\longmapsto Nz,\qquad N=\begin{pmatrix}s_0&b\\0&A\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
Its exact chamber is a finite intersection $Q=\{z:Gz>0\}$ of strict rational homogeneous rows, supplied by an explicit finite pullback construction. The normalized chamber $P$ on $D=1$ is a bounded open rational polygon containing the centered origin strictly. All section labels and the outgoing messenger phase are restored. On $P$ the normalized return is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:projective}
 f(w)=\frac{Aw}{s_0+bw},\qquad w=u/D,\qquad s_0+bw>0.
\end{equation}
There are exactly five live signals throughout each finite portion of the execution.
\end{theorem}
These are precisely the rational projective planar transformations fixing this center that admit the indicated invertible lift positive on its ray. A common scalar multiple of $N$ gives the same projective transformation, but a different homogeneous return and potentially a different clock. The theorem realizes the specified lift itself.

\begin{theorem}[One machine with two clock behaviors]\label{smc:pj:thm:mixed}
For every rational $v>1$ an explicit 44-event word on the same five-signal section has infinite complete-word validity exactly on
\[
 0<x<y<D,\qquad D\geq\frac32y.
\]
Equality gives Zeno runs, and strict inequality gives non-Zeno runs. On positive integer native gaps $g=(x,y-x,D-y)$ the validity, Zeno-validity and non-Zeno-validity predicates have quadratic single-polynomial certificates with respectively one, zero and one positive-integer witnesses, uniquely determined on each accepted input.
\end{theorem}
The exact 44-rule declaration is in Section~\ref{smc:pj:app:rules}; the proof and clocks are in Section~\ref{smc:pj:sec:mixed}. A center-strict one-word chamber can have its center on the boundary of the infinite-validity set.

\wtag\ [Source~27 in Part~X needs two machines for its two clock behaviours: a 138-event Zeno word and a separately reclosed 114-event non-Zeno variant with the same chamber and the same set $K$ (Theorem~\ref{smc:fv:thm:clock}). Here a single word has both behaviours. Question~\ref{smc:xi:q:bridge} asks how far this extends.]

\paragraph{Scope.}
The construction is fixed after its rational parameters are chosen. It does not give one unchanged machine for all matrices, arbitrary prescribed guard polygons, polynomial compilation size, optimal event/speed counts, global rule reversibility, or evolution after an accumulation. Singular $A$ is excluded by the inherited full-section invertibility theorem under its binary, positive-flight, open-chamber hypotheses. A nonpositive $s_0$ cannot give this literal return on a chamber containing the standard center, whose final $D$ would be nonpositive. No general $\GL_3(\Q)$ or fixed-word Turing-completeness claim is made.
\section{Exact elementary chronology}\label{smc:pj:sec:primitives}
\subsection{The inherited compiler interface}
Write $F(C,\lambda)$ for the preserved planar compiler of Reports 60 and 61. For every $C\in\GL_2(\Q)$ and rational $\lambda>0$, it supplies a nonempty positive-duration complete word with return
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:interface}
 F(C,\lambda):\quad z\longmapsto\lambda\diag(1,C)z.
\end{equation}
It supplies its finite exact homogeneous guard rows, a center-strict chamber, and literal section closure. For $\det C>0$, every event involves the messenger. For $\det C<0$, a positive compiler is followed by a seven-event orientation-reversing block $\Jrev{}$ containing one marker-only event. Its messenger label does not change at that remote event. Fresh phase copies are required at interfaces.

Section~\ref{smc:pj:app:compiler} gives the complete arithmetic factorization, primitive endpoint lists, orientation-reversing interface and count convention used here. The two unchanged dependency proofs are included in the evidence package. The present new proof invokes this interface rather than silently treating an arbitrary planar change of coordinates as a physical operation.

\wtag\ [$F(C,\lambda)$ is source~30's Theorem~\ref{smc:pl:thm:physical} for $\det C>0$ and source~31's Corollary~\ref{smc:iv:cor:gl} for $\det C<0$. Source~32's restatement of their constructions (its Appendix~A) is the pointer Remark~\ref{smc:xi:rem:pjcompiler} in Section~\ref{smc:pj:app:compiler}. The two dependency proofs are shipped once, as \path{30-planar-science-physical-PROOF.md} and \path{31-invertible-science-frozen-proof-PROOF.md}.]

\subsection{Anchor scaling and global homotheties}
\begin{remark}[\wtag\ Source~30's primitive, restated]\label{smc:xi:rem:pjscale}
Source~32 restates source~30's anchor scaling $L_z(u)$ and its ordered global scaling (Section~\ref{smc:pl:sec:primitives}, equations \eqref{smc:pl:eq:scaleevents}--\eqref{smc:pl:eq:scalespectator}, and Section~\ref{smc:pl:sec:synthesis}), with the same chronology and first-obstruction proof. In source~32's notation, a target at distance $q>0$ from a stationary anchor is scaled by a rational $a>0$ with launch speed $h_a=(a-1)/(a+1)$, $|h_a|<1$. Relative to the entrance, the principal time-position pairs are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:scale-table}
 (q,q),\quad(2q,0),\quad(2q+aq,aq),\quad(2q+2aq,0),
\end{equation}
the duration is $2(1+a)q$, and a stationary inner spectator at $p$ is crossed at
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:spectator}
 p,\quad2q-p,\quad2q+p,\quad2q+2aq-p.
\end{equation}
The exact condition is that $q$ and $aq$ stay strictly between the same unchanged nearest neighbours. The word has $4+4k$ events with $k$ inner spectators, and $a=1$ gives a legitimate timed identity. A global homothety by $\lambda<1$ scales $X,Y,R$ in that order, and one by $\lambda>1$ scales $R,Y,X$. It has $4+8+12=24$ events, needs no new condition, has homogeneous return $\lambda I_3$ and takes
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:global-time}
 T_{\mathrm{global}}=2(1+\lambda)(x+y+D),
\end{equation}
because each marker's position when its own scale starts is its original incoming position.
\end{remark}

\section{An eight event outer marker operation}\label{smc:pj:sec:outer}
Fix $v\in\Q_{>0}$ and set
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:outer-parameters}
 h=\frac{v-1}{v+1},\qquad
 d=vD+(1-v)y=y+v(D-y),\qquad
 t_*=(v+2)D-(v+1)y.
\end{equation}
The messenger crosses $X,Y$ transparently, launches $R$ at speed $h$ and reflects left, bounces at $Y$, restores $R$ and reflects left, crosses $Y,X$, then bounces at $L$. Distinct phases distinguish a transparent $Y$ crossing from its middle bounce.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}clll@{}}\toprule
Event&Time&Messenger position&Contact and action\\\midrule
1&$x$&$x$&Cross $X$\\
2&$y$&$y$&Cross $Y$\\
3&$D$&$D$&Launch $R$ at $h$; reflect\\
4&$2D-y$&$y$&Bounce at $Y$\\
5&$t_*$&$d$&Restore $R$; reflect\\
6&$t_*+d-y$&$y$&Cross $Y$\\
7&$t_*+d-x$&$x$&Cross $X$\\
8&$t_*+d$&$0$&Bounce at $L$\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The eight flight durations, including the initial outgoing flight, are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:outer-flights}
 x,\quad y-x,\quad D-y,\quad D-y,\quad
 v(D-y),\quad v(D-y),\quad y-x,\quad x.
\end{equation}
They are all positive exactly on the prescribed ordered section. The restoration identity and the moving $R/Y$ gap at the middle bounce are
\[
 d-D=h(t_*-D),\qquad R(2D-y)-y=\frac{2v(D-y)}{v+1}>0.
\]
Both target endpoints $D,d$ lie strictly beyond $y$, so monotonicity excludes every target-spectator contact. Between $Y$ and $R$ there is no unlisted spectator. All inner-marker crossings before and after that interval occur in the table. Relative messenger/target speeds are nonzero; after a contact the stipulated directions separate immediately. Thus there is neither an omitted contact nor a simultaneous remote event. Conversely, there is no additional guard in \eqref{smc:pj:eq:outer-flights} once the initial order holds. The exact return and duration are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:outer-return}
 (D,x,y)\longmapsto(d,x,y),\qquad
 T_{\mathrm{outer}}=2[(1+v)D-vy]=2[D+v(D-y)].
\end{equation}
This includes $v=1$, for which the temporary $R$ label has speed zero and all eight events are retained.

\section{Twenty event recentering}\label{smc:pj:sec:raw}
Put $s=(v+2)/3$. After the outer operation, scale both $x$ and $y$ about $L$ by $s$, keeping $d$ fixed. For $s<1$ use $X$ then $Y$; for $s>1$ use $Y$ then $X$; at $s=1$ retain both identity words in the first order. The two scales always use $4+8=12$ events and two fresh temporary marker labels.

For contraction, $sx<x<y<d$, and the later $Y$ endpoints satisfy $sx<sy\leq y<d$. For expansion, $Y$ moves first. Its only new obstruction is $sy\geq d$; if $sy<d$, its endpoints stay between $x$ and $d$. The later $X$ endpoints stay between $0$ and $sy$. Consequently the exact raw chamber is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:raw-guards}
 x>0,\qquad y-x>0,\qquad D-y>0,\qquad
 d-sy=vD+\frac{1-4v}{3}y>0.
\end{equation}
The fourth row is redundant for $v\leq1$. For $v>1$ it is essential: if it fails, the outward-moving $Y$ reaches or crosses stationary $R$ during its first scale. Equality gives simultaneous contact at the proposed restored endpoint; strict failure gives a prior extra contact. Thus \eqref{smc:pj:eq:raw-guards} is exact, not just a safe sufficient subchamber.

Each scale starts and ends at $L$ with outgoing messenger. The $Y$ word is ``cross $X$, launch $Y$, cross $X$, bounce $L$, cross $X$, restore $Y$, cross $X$, bounce $L$,'' at the then-current stationary $X$. Equations~\eqref{smc:pj:eq:scale-table}--\eqref{smc:pj:eq:spectator} prove strict ordering of every crossing. There is no zero-time phase transfer.

The resulting raw return and duration are
\begin{align}
 (D,x,y)&\longmapsto(d,sx,sy),\label{smc:pj:eq:raw-return}\\
 T_{\mathrm{raw}}&=2[(1+v)D-vy]+2(1+s)(x+y).\label{smc:pj:eq:raw-time}
\end{align}
In centered coordinates its matrix is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:Nv}
 N_v=\begin{pmatrix}s&0&1-v\\0&s&(v-1)/3\\0&0&v\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
At $x=D/3,y=2D/3$, $d=sD$ and $d-sy=sD/3>0$. The endpoint proof also checks all internal scale positions. Thus this 20-event, three-temporary-label, four-supplied-row word is center-strict for every rational $v>0$. Its determinant $vs^2>0$ agrees with even collision parity.
\section{Scale shears and arbitrary fixed center returns}\label{smc:pj:sec:realization}
\subsection{Compensation of the planar action}
The lower-right block of \eqref{smc:pj:eq:Nv} and its compensation are
\[
 A_v=\begin{pmatrix}s&(v-1)/3\\0&v\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 C_v=sA_v^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&(1-v)/(3v)\\0&s/v\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Since $\det C_v=s/v>0$, the positive inherited compiler applies. Follow the raw word by $F(C_v,1/s)$, equivalently by $F(C_v,1)$ and a global scale $1/s$. Direct multiplication gives
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:kick}
 \diag(1/s,A_v^{-1})N_v
 =E_{(0,k)}:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&k\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad k=\frac{3(1-v)}{v+2}.
\end{equation}
This changes only the outer scale coordinate: $D\mapsto D+k\eta$. Its exact chamber includes the raw rows and \emph{all} compiler rows pulled back by $N_v$. Keeping only the raw endpoint row after compensation would lose necessary chronology conditions. Because $N_v$ sends the central ray to a positive multiple of itself, all these rows remain center-strict.

The parameter correspondence is a rational bijection
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:krange}
 v>0\quad\longleftrightarrow\quad -3<k<3/2,
 \qquad v=\frac{3-2k}{3+k}.
\end{equation}
For arbitrary $k\in\Q$, let $n=\max(1,\lceil|k|\rceil)$ and $\delta=k/n$. Since $|\delta|\leq1$, it lies strictly in this range. Concatenate $n$ copies of $E_{(0,\delta)}$. Their coefficients add, yielding $E_{(0,k)}$. Every completed factor fixes the center exactly, so the finite pullback intersection remains center-strict. No large-coefficient empty-domain obstruction appears. A zero requested shear can be omitted when another nonempty block supplies the timed return.

\subsection{One coefficient suffices for every scale row}
For nonzero $r=(a,b)$, set
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:B}
 B=\begin{pmatrix}b&-a\\a&b\end{pmatrix},\qquad\det B=a^2+b^2>0.
\end{equation}
Chronologically perform $F(B,1)$, then $E_{(0,1)}$, then $F(B^{-1},1)$. Their product is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:rowconj}
 \diag(1,B^{-1})E_{(0,1)}\diag(1,B)
 =E_r:=\begin{pmatrix}1&r\\0&I_2\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
Indeed the added row is $(0,1)B=(a,b)$, while the planar product is $B^{-1}B=I_2$. Both physical conjugating compilers have positive determinant and exact center-strict chambers. This uses one fixed coefficient-one shear, at the cost of two parameter-dependent planar compilers. For $r=0$ omit this prefix.

For \eqref{smc:pj:eq:main}, first compile $E_{b/s_0}$, then $F(A/s_0,s_0)$. The product is exactly
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:assemble}
 [s_0\diag(1,A/s_0)]E_{b/s_0}
 =\begin{pmatrix}s_0&b\\0&A\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
If $\det A<0$, the last factor uses the inherited seven-event $\Jrev{}$ extension. No additional live signal is introduced.

\subsection{Exact chambers and first failure}\label{smc:pj:sec:guards}
Suppose a chronological list of blocks has full return matrices $M_1,\ldots,M_q$ and exact guard matrices $G_1,\ldots,G_q$. Its exact rows, in the initial coordinates, are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:pullback}
 G_1z>0,\quad G_2M_1z>0,\quad\ldots,\quad
 G_qM_{q-1}\cdots M_1z>0.
\end{equation}
The inherited endpoint lists are finite rational expressions, the new raw block uses \eqref{smc:pj:eq:raw-guards}, and global homotheties need no extra row. Thus this is an effective finite rational-arithmetic procedure, not a trajectory search.

Sufficiency follows by induction through the complete chronology of each block. For necessity, consider the earliest block whose guard fails, after a valid prefix. Its first-failure proof forces an extra collision, simultaneous contact, nonpositive flight or wrong order, so the selected complete word fails. Prospective affine formulas are invoked only until that first obstruction, never as a supposed physical continuation after it.

Every completed block sends the center to a positive multiple of itself, and every internal chamber is center-strict. Hence \eqref{smc:pj:eq:pullback} contains an open neighborhood of the center on $D=1$. The first block's section rows imply $0<x<y<1$, making this open rational polygon bounded. Redundant supplied rows are retained. The chamber is not replaced by its closure or by a smaller convenient neighborhood.

The ordered cone, in centered coordinates, is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:cone}
 C=\{D>0,\ D/3+\xi>0,\ D/3+\eta-\xi>0,\ D/3-\eta>0\}.
\end{equation}
Endpoint compatibility requires $Q\subset C\cap N^{-1}C$. On normalized input put $h=s_0+bw$ and $q=Aw$. The output rows are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:outputguard}
 h>0,\quad q_1+h/3>0,\quad q_2-q_1+h/3>0,\quad h/3-q_2>0.
\end{equation}
These are strict affine rows and are strict at $w=0$. They imply the positive denominator in \eqref{smc:pj:eq:projective}, but cannot replace intermediate collision guards. Together with the next phase argument, this completes the proof of Theorem~\ref{smc:pj:thm:main}.

\subsection{Finite deterministic rules and literal closure}
Give each incoming messenger flight a fresh label at its prescribed rational speed; emit the successor phase at its contact, identifying the final outgoing phase with the whole word's initial label. Give each launch and restoration its own temporary marker labels, including speed-zero identity scales. Section marker labels are shared by physical role.

All new raw and positive-compiler events involve the messenger. Their input sets are distinct because their phase labels are distinct. Their incoming and outgoing speeds are distinct: the messenger speed is $\pm1$ and every moving target speed has modulus less than one. The possible $\Jrev{}$ suffix has its separately checked speeds and one marker-only collision. That collision must leave the messenger phase unchanged. Its fresh temporary fast-$X$ label makes its input set unique, and interface phase copies prevent an accidental rule shared with the standalone $\Jrev{}$ entry phase.

Assign identity output to every other finite input set whose speeds are pairwise distinct. There are finitely many labels and hence finitely many such sets. This is deterministic and cardinality-preserving. Every explicit event consumes and emits two signals; the completion preserves cardinality too. An extra collision remains an extra collision, even when its rule is identity, so completion does not enlarge the selected word chamber. Exactly five live signals persist throughout each finite portion. This establishes literal phase closure without asserting global injectivity of collision rules.

\section{Explicit compilation counts}\label{smc:pj:sec:counts}
For the selected inherited $F(C,\lambda)$ write $m,t,g$ for event, temporary-marker-label and supplied-guard counts. In the positive case its factorization has shear subdivision sum $K$, full-transfer count $T$, shear-block count $B_{\mathrm{num}}\in\{3,4\}$, determinant subdivision count $H$, and $\varepsilon=\mathbf1_{\lambda\ne1}$. Section~\ref{smc:pj:app:compiler} specifies every parameter. Then
\begin{align}
 m(C,\lambda)&=18K+3T+14H+24\varepsilon,\label{smc:pj:eq:countm}\\
 t(C,\lambda)&=4K+3H+3\varepsilon,\\
 g(C,\lambda)&=4K+4B_{\mathrm{num}}+8H.
\end{align}
The raw word always has $(m,t,g)=(20,3,4)$, retaining both identity inner scales at $v=1$. The corrected shear therefore has counts
\[
 20+m(C_v,1/s),\quad3+t(C_v,1/s),\quad4+g(C_v,1/s).
\]
All its events involve the messenger, so the phase-isolated number of meta-signals is $m+t+4$. This counts label types, not simultaneous occurrences. No minimization is asserted.

\subsection{A 780 event coefficient one ledger}
For $k=1$, equations~\eqref{smc:pj:eq:krange} and \eqref{smc:pj:eq:kick} give
\[
 v=\frac14,\qquad s=\frac34,\qquad
 C_v=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The positive compiler first factors
\[
 \diag(1/3,1)C_v=\begin{pmatrix}1/3&1/3\\0&3\end{pmatrix}\in\SL_2(\Q).
\]
Its chronological shear list is $y(-2),x(1/3),y(6)$, with subdivision counts $8,2,24$. Hence $K=34$, $T=4$, $B_{\mathrm{num}}=3$. The determinant factor $3$ has $H=8$. The exact ledger is
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrr@{}}\toprule
Operation&Events&Temporary labels&Supplied rows\\\midrule
Raw outer and recentering word&20&3&4\\
Signed shear steps&612&136&148\\
Four full transfers&12&0&0\\
Eight centered dilation steps&112&24&64\\
Global compensation $4/3$&24&3&0\\\midrule
Total&780&166&216\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The fixed-scale compensation uses $612+12+112=736$ events, and $780+166+4=950$ meta-signals suffice. For the main theorem with $b\ne0$, put $r=b/s_0$ and use \eqref{smc:pj:eq:B}. An explicit total event count is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:maintotal}
 m(B,1)+780+m(B^{-1},1)+m(A/s_0,s_0).
\end{equation}
The analogous temporary-label and guard counts add with $166$ and $216$ for the middle kick. For $b=0$ only the final nonempty compiler is used.

When the final planar determinant is negative, its selected positive component acquires seven events, three temporary $X$ labels, one marker-only event and the four pulled-back supplied $\Jrev{}$ guard rows. If $r_{\Jrev}$ counts these marker-only events, phase-isolated messenger labels can number $m-r_{\Jrev}$; the total meta-signal count is $m-r_{\Jrev}+t+4$. Here $r_{\Jrev}\leq1$. The full determinant is $s_0\det A$. Positive components have even length and a negative final component adds one odd $\Jrev{}$ block, agreeing with $\sgn\det N=(-1)^m$.

\paragraph{Speeds.}
All parameters in the anchor, reflector, signed-shear and dilation formulas are rational, so every speed is rational. For the main construction all messenger speeds outside $\Jrev{}$ are $\pm1$ and all target speeds there lie in $(-1,1)$. The $\Jrev{}$ extension adds messenger speeds $-3/2,-1/4$ and target speeds $-1/2,2$. Repeated values on different labels are allowed. There is no uniform or optimal distinct-speed count claimed for arbitrary $N$. For the concrete 44-event family, Section~\ref{smc:pj:sec:mixed} gives exactly six distinct speed values.
\section{Repeated validity and exact clocks}\label{smc:pj:sec:clocks}
Let $Q=\{z:Gz>0\}$ be the exact cone of Theorem~\ref{smc:pj:thm:main}. Literal closure gives
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:infinite}
 \text{infinite complete-word validity}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 GN^nz>0\text{ for every }n\geq0.
\end{equation}
Equivalently, the normalized survivor set is
\[
 K=\{w:f^n(w)\text{ is defined and belongs to }P\text{ for every }n\geq0\}.
\]
Every valid denominator is positive. On $D=1$, \eqref{smc:pj:eq:infinite} is an intersection of countably many strict rational affine half-planes in the initial $w$. Thus $K$ is convex and contains the center. A countable intersection of open sets need not be open. No semialgebraicity classification is established here, and the fixed-scale planar classification cannot simply be applied to the nonlinear normalized map $f$.

Every prescribed flight time is a rational homogeneous linear form on the exact chamber; so is the full duration $T(z)=\ell z$ for a rational row $\ell$. For this compiler there are constants $c_1,c_2>0$ with
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:clockbound}
 c_1D\leq\ell z\leq c_2D\qquad(z\in Q).
\end{equation}
One can take $c_1=2$: if $b\ne0$, the first $F(B,1)$ already takes at least $2D$; if $b=0$, the retained final planar compiler has that bound. For the upper bound, all finitely many intermediate times and positions are fixed linear forms in the initial coordinates. The closure of the normalized ordered input triangle is compact, so their absolute values have finite maxima. No shape denominator enters before normalization. This also bounds all positions during a valid macro by a constant times its entrance scale.

\begin{theorem}[Active cyclic spectrum]\label{smc:pj:thm:clock}
For an infinitely valid input $z$, put $z_n=N^nz$ and $D_n=(z_n)_0>0$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:zeno-spectrum}
 \text{Zeno}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \sum_{n\geq0}D_n<\infty
 \ \Longleftrightarrow\ N^nz\longrightarrow0
 \ \Longleftrightarrow\ |\mu|<1\text{ for every }\mu\in\spec(N|_{V_z}),
\end{equation}
where $V_z=\Span\{z,Nz,N^2z\}$, with dependent vectors removed to choose a basis. This space is invariant by Cayley--Hamilton.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The first equivalence is \eqref{smc:pj:eq:clockbound}. Valid normalized marker positions are bounded, so each coordinate of $z_n$ is $O(D_n)$; summability forces $z_n\to0$. Conversely, decompose the cyclic subspace into its real or complex generalized eigenspaces. A component with eigenvalue $\mu$ contributes a polynomial in $n$ times $\mu^n$. Since $z$ is cyclic in $V_z$, every eigenvalue of $N|_{V_z}$ is active. Terms from any $|\mu|\geq1$ prevent convergence to zero; distinct spectral projections make cancellation between different generalized eigenspaces irrelevant. When all moduli are below one, polynomial-geometric decay is absolutely summable. This proves both remaining equivalences and the converse summability.
\end{proof}
At the center the criterion reduces to $s_0<1$. It generally does not reduce to that scalar condition for every input.

If $N,z$ are rational and the run is Zeno, $V_z$ has a rational basis and $I-N$ restricted to it is invertible. Therefore the total accumulation time is rational and computable by a rational linear system:
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:active-time}
 T_{\mathrm{total}}=\ell\bigl[(I-N)|_{V_z}\bigr]^{-1}z.
\end{equation}
The inverse means an operator on $V_z$, embedded back into the full space. The full $I-N$ can be singular because of an inactive unit mode; its unrestricted inverse must not be used without checking. Since positions during macro $n$ are $O(D_n)$, all five signals approach the fixed left anchor during a Zeno run. No continuation through that accumulation is specified.

\wtag\ [The rationality of \eqref{smc:pj:eq:active-time} is a special case of source~26's Theorem~\ref{smc:pm:thm:rational}, by source~30's cyclic-subspace argument (Remark~\ref{smc:xi:rem:zeno}). The spectral equivalences of Theorem~\ref{smc:pj:thm:clock} are printed here once; source~33 restates them as Remark~\ref{smc:hl:cor:clock}.]

\section{A 44 event word with both clock behaviors}\label{smc:pj:sec:mixed}
Fix rational $v>1$. Append to the raw 20-event word the 24-event global contraction by $1/v$. Set
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:mixed-parameters}
 s=\frac{v+2}{3},\qquad r=\frac{s}{v}=\frac{v+2}{3v},\qquad
 a=\frac{v-1}{v},\qquad\frac13<r<1.
\end{equation}
Its physical-coordinate return and exact one-word chamber are
\begin{align}
 D'&=D-ay,\qquad x'=rx,\qquad y'=ry,\label{smc:pj:eq:mixed-return}\\
 x&>0,\quad y-x>0,\quad D-y>0,\quad
 3vD+(1-4v)y>0.\label{smc:pj:eq:mixed-chamber}
\end{align}
The suffix introduces no additional guard. The last row is equivalent to $D'>y'$. This word has 44 messenger-involving events, six temporary marker labels, four supplied rows, 44 messenger phases and 54 meta-signals. The explicit labels and rules in Section~\ref{smc:pj:app:rules} restore all section labels and phase $Q_0$ at event 44.

The six distinct speed values are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:six-speeds}
 -1,\quad-h,\quad0,\quad p,\quad h,\quad1,
 \qquad\text{where }
 h=\frac{v-1}{v+1},\quad p=\frac{v-1}{v+5}.
\end{equation}
Here $0<p<h<1$, so the listed six values are pairwise distinct. (The label count is larger because phases at equal speed must remain distinct.)

The exact duration is
\begin{align}\label{smc:pj:eq:mixed-time}
 T(z)={}&2[(1+v)D-vy]+2(1+s)(x+y)\notag\\
 &+2(1+1/v)\,[s(x+y)+vD+(1-v)y].
\end{align}
These summands are respectively the outer operation, the two inner scales, and the three global scales. In particular $T(z)>2D$. A convenient bound on \eqref{smc:pj:eq:mixed-chamber} is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:mixed-upper}
 T(z)<[2(1+v)+4(1+s)+2(1+1/v)(2s+v)]D.
\end{equation}
Indeed $x,y<D$, and for $v>1$ the last bracketed position sum is less than $(2s+v)D$.

\subsection{Exact infinite validity including equality}
Define $c=D-3y/2$. Since $1-r=2a/3$, \eqref{smc:pj:eq:mixed-return} leaves $c$ invariant. Algebraic powers, before any physical first failure, are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:mixed-powers}
 x_n=r^nx,\qquad y_n=r^ny,\qquad
 D_n=c+\frac32yr^n.
\end{equation}
The extra one-word guard at macro $n$ is equivalent to
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:nthguard}
 D_{n+1}-y_{n+1}=c+\frac12yr^{n+1}>0.
\end{equation}
If $c\geq0$, this is strictly positive at every finite $n$. So are the section rows $x_n>0$, $y_n-x_n>0$ and $D_n-y_n=c+yr^n/2>0$. Induction through the exact one-word chamber proves that every macro is physically valid. If $c<0$, \eqref{smc:pj:eq:nthguard} eventually becomes negative; hence a finite first guard failure occurs. This uses a prospective algebraic formula only to locate a failing checkpoint, and does not suppose that physical dynamics follows it after a wrong collision. Infinite validity is exactly $c\geq0$, proving the first part of Theorem~\ref{smc:pj:thm:mixed}.

For $c=0$, all section coordinates contract by $r$. Homogeneity of duration gives $T_n=r^nT_0$, hence
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:mixed-zeno-time}
 T_{\mathrm{total}}=\frac{T_0}{1-r}<\infty.
\end{equation}
This is rational on rational input. For $c>0$, the outer phase alone is longer than $2D_n\geq2c$ at every macro, so total time diverges. Both behaviors belong to the same finite machine and the same repeated word.

On $D=1$ the infinite-validity set is $0<x<y\leq2/3$. Its accepted equality boundary $y=2/3$ is entirely Zeno. The center $(1/3,2/3)$ lies on that boundary, while strictly inside the one-word chamber. The return matrix in \eqref{smc:pj:eq:mixed-return} has eigenvalues $1,r,r$. The invariant $c$ detects its unit mode: equality uses only contracting modes, while strict validity uses the unit mode. Its determinant $r^2>0$ matches 44-event parity.

\paragraph{Two exact inputs in the same machine.}
For $v=2$, $r=2/3$ and direct simplification of \eqref{smc:pj:eq:mixed-time} gives
\[
 T(D,x,y)=12D+\frac{26}{3}x+\frac53y.
\]
At $(D,x,y)=(1,1/3,2/3)$, $c=0$, $T_0=16$ and the accumulation time is $48$. At $(1,1/4,1/2)$, $c=1/4$ and the macro durations are $T_n=3+12(2/3)^n$. The first $n$ macros take $3n+36(1-(2/3)^n)$, which diverges. These values are direct evaluations of the displayed formulas.

\subsection{Native positive integer gap certificates}\label{smc:pj:sec:certificates}
Restrict $g_1=x$, $g_2=y-x$, $g_3=D-y$ to $\Z_{>0}$. Positivity of these original inputs already supplies the full initial order. Since
\[
 c=g_3-\frac{g_1+g_2}{2},
\]
the following single-polynomial equations give the promised exact predicates:
\begin{align}
 \text{infinite validity:}\quad &(2g_3-g_1-g_2-w+1)^2=0,
 &&w\in\Z_{>0},\label{smc:pj:eq:cert-valid}\\
 \text{Zeno validity:}\quad &(2g_3-g_1-g_2)^2=0,
 &&\text{no witnesses},\label{smc:pj:eq:cert-zeno}\\
 \text{non-Zeno validity:}\quad &(2g_3-g_1-g_2-w)^2=0,
 &&w\in\Z_{>0}.\label{smc:pj:eq:cert-nonzeno}
\end{align}
All have total degree two and use the native input gaps directly, without auxiliary aliases. A square of an integer vanishes precisely when its base does. Writing $L=2g_3-g_1-g_2$ only as a displayed abbreviation, \eqref{smc:pj:eq:cert-valid} uniquely forces $w=L+1$, positive exactly for integer $L\geq0$. Equation~\eqref{smc:pj:eq:cert-nonzeno} uniquely forces $w=L$, positive exactly for $L>0$. Equation~\eqref{smc:pj:eq:cert-zeno} accepts exactly $L=0$ and has one empty witness tuple on an accepted input, none on a rejected input. This proves the remaining part of Theorem~\ref{smc:pj:thm:mixed}.

The integer-domain qualification is essential: replacing positive integer witnesses by positive real or rational witnesses would make the first formula test $L>-1$, not $L\geq0$, for arbitrary real or rational gaps. These elementary certificates establish no broader arithmetic classification for general projective survivor sets.

\wtag\ [They are the unique-slack certificates of Part~I's Theorem~\ref{smc:cg:thm:quadratic} for one weak row, one equality and one strict row in $L$.]
\section{The fixed ray boundary of the result}\label{smc:pj:sec:scope}
For an arbitrary rational homogeneous matrix $M$, a necessary map-level condition for an open positive ordered-section domain is
\[
 C\cap M^{-1}C\ne\varnothing.
\]
The intersection is open; nonemptiness gives an open set of compatible input/output pairs, but no signal-machine construction. Theorem~\ref{smc:pj:thm:main} provides a construction near its specified rational central eigenray, not a proof that this necessary condition suffices in general.

\subsection{Rational fixed rays and changed encodings}
Write $M=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&c\\d&B\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and suppose a rational finite point $p\in\Q^2$ obeys
\[
 M(1,p)^{\mathsf T}=\lambda(1,p)^{\mathsf T},\qquad\lambda>0.
\]
For $T=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\p&I_2\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, direct multiplication gives
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:reencoding}
 T^{-1}MT=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda&c\\0&B-pc\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
If $M$ is invertible, then $\det(B-pc)=\det M/\lambda\ne0$. The fixed-center compiler therefore applies in this explicitly changed rational encoding. This algebra does not implement $T$ or $T^{-1}$ physically on the original marker coordinates. It must not be described as a literal original-section realization of $M$ without an additional conversion construction.

An affine chart change preserving $D$ cannot move a ray at infinity to a finite center. A general rational basis change can re-encode any rational eigenray, but then the normalization functional, sign and domain must be specified anew. If the ray is to retain the same positive physical marker meaning, it must lie inside $C$ and have positive multiplier. A nonzero rational eigenvector has a rational eigenvalue, by dividing any nonzero coordinate of its image by that coordinate.

\subsection{A positive compatible matrix without a rational eigenray}
In positive gap coordinates consider
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:uncovered}
 P_g=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\1&2&1\\1&1&3\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 \det P_g=2,\qquad\chi_{P_g}(t)=t^3-6t^2+8t-2.
\end{equation}
All entries are positive, so every positive gap vector maps to a positive one. A rational root of this monic cubic could only be $\pm1,\pm2$, and the respective values are $1,-17,-2,-50$, all nonzero. Thus the cubic has no rational root and the matrix has no rational eigenray.

The change to centered coordinates is
\[
 D=g_1+g_2+g_3,\quad
 \xi=(2g_1-g_2-g_3)/3,\quad
 \eta=(g_1+g_2-2g_3)/3.
\]
In these coordinates the same matrix is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:pj:eq:uncovered-centered}
 M=\begin{pmatrix}
 4&-1&-1\\-1/3&1/3&1/3\\-1/3&-1/3&5/3
 \end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
It preserves $C$ globally, yet no rational conjugacy can put it into a form fixing a rational ray. This is an explicit uncovered case of the present construction and rational-conjugacy argument, not an impossibility theorem for some other signal construction.

\wtag\ [Answered by source~33 (Section~\ref{smc:hl:sec:example}). There the same matrix, written $K$ in gap coordinates and $N$ in centred coordinates, is realized on the original section, on some full-dimensional open set. The realization runs source~32's fixed-centre compiler for $N_0=T_{-q}NT_p$ and then one 26-event physical translation; it needs no rational eigenray and no change of encoding. Source~32's sentence stays true: $P_g$ is not covered by source~32's own construction and rational-conjugacy argument.]

\section{Primary literature and attribution}\label{smc:pj:sec:literature}
Fixed-itinerary fractional-linear algebra predates this construction. Mestl, Lemay and Glass~\cite{mestl1996} derive wall maps $x\mapsto Cx/(1+c^{\mathsf T}x)$ and their cycle compositions in Glass networks, with exit-dependent domains. Their equations (2.3)--(2.4), printed page 35, and (4.2), printed page 40, give the closest algebraic precedent. Their flow and clock assumptions are different; they do not establish this five-live-signal realization.

Alishah, Duarte and Peixe~\cite{alishah2020}, Section 5, give oblique constant-flow projections, their trajectory domains and inverses, and pulled-back itinerary domains. Their equations (5.2)--(5.5), Proposition 5.4 and Definition 5.7 situate the underlying section-map geometry. This is a polytope-flow analysis, not the finite signal compiler proved here.

Durand-Lose~\cite{DL07}, Sections 3.1--3.2, uses scale-relative distances to represent registers and implements addition and constant multiplication by signals. Those arithmetic constructions have their own register and population resources. They cannot be cited as if they already implied the exact five-live-signal number-preserving full-section theorem.

Becker and coauthors~\cite{agc10}, Section 2, Definitions 1--2, specify label-dependent constant speeds, deterministic rules and distinct-speed incoming and outgoing collision sets. Multiple labels may share a speed, and five live signals is not five meta-signals. The affine transformations treated in~\cite{accumulations}, Section 2.3, act on all speeds and on the common spatial coordinate; they do not implement arbitrary two-dimensional marker-shape conjugacies.

Belgacem, Edwards and Farcot~\cite{belgacem2024}, Section III, equations (6)--(12), explicitly track positive denominators and strict itinerary cones for fractional-linear Glass-network maps. This is a useful domain-audit precedent. No accompanying code was executed for this report.

The construction-specific content is the exact five-live-signal realization of the positive fixed-center lift, its complete chronology, exact chambers, literal phase closure and the mixed-clock example. No novelty, priority, exhaustive-search, general universality or minimality conclusion follows from the bounded source review.

\section{Further questions}\label{smc:pj:sec:questions}
\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{smc:xi:q:pj1} \textbf{Realization beyond a rational center.} Can a finite five-live-signal construction realize \eqref{smc:pj:eq:uncovered-centered} in the original coordinates on a nonempty open chamber? A positive answer needs a new physical mechanism, not just rational fixed-ray conjugacy.
\item\label{smc:xi:q:pj2} \textbf{Exact projective survivor geometry.} Classify the set $\{z:GN^nz>0\ (n\geq0)\}$ on $D=1$ for the present rational triangular lifts. Which such sets are semialgebraic, and which limiting strict boundaries are accepted? The mixed example shows why closure loses clock information.
\item\label{smc:xi:q:pj3} \textbf{Efficient compilation.} Reduce the 780-event coefficient-one implementation or the size dependence of its planar conjugators, while preserving the same exact guard and literal phase accounting. No current count is a lower bound.
\item\label{smc:xi:q:pj4} \textbf{Uniformity and speed resources.} Determine what can be shared among parameter-dependent machines, and what distinct-speed or label resources suffice under a precisely fixed encoding. A finite universal rule table is a separate claim requiring its own proof.
\item\label{smc:xi:q:pj5} \textbf{Arithmetic descriptions on native gaps.} Extend the elementary unique-witness certificates beyond the half-space example, without hidden aliases, unrestricted auxiliary dimensions or a transfer from a different dynamical model.
\end{enumerate}
Each question is open within this report's scope. None is answered by the standard full-coordinate dimension count, by collision number preservation, or by familiar projective algebra alone.

The matrix \eqref{smc:pj:eq:uncovered-centered} is realized in the original coordinates on a nonempty open chamber. Questions~\ref{smc:xi:q:pj2}--\ref{smc:xi:q:pj5} are open. Source~33's escaping-gap matrix bears on Question~\ref{smc:xi:q:pj2}: it is a compatible map with an empty survivor set, but it does not classify survivor sets.]

\begin{quote}\small
A rational $3\times3$ homogeneous matrix is realized by a positive-duration literal return of exactly five live signals on some full-dimensional open part of the standard four-marker section if and only if it is nonsingular and sends at least one ordered input to an ordered output. The sufficient construction physically translates any rational interior shape to any other, using 26-event steps with exact intermediate-corner guards. Left and right translations reduce an arbitrary compatible matrix to the preserved fixed-center compiler without requiring a rational eigenray. The full return realizes the specified homogeneous representative, including scale. We prove the ten-event translation chronology and its exact guard, give a rational polynomial-time compatibility decision, and work out a positive-gap matrix with no rational eigenray. Local realizability has an explicit degree-six Diophantine representation with eight positive-integer witnesses and literal native gap-input arithmetic DAGs of 48 and 57 binary operations. A conditional cyclic-subspace clock criterion is separated from local existence; a compatible escaping-gap map has no infinitely valid input. \section{The exact local criterion}\label{smc:hl:sec:criterion}
Consider four stationary markers
\[
 L=0,\qquad X=x,\qquad Y=y,\qquad R=D,\qquad 0<x<y<D,
\]
and a messenger at $L$ outgoing to the right with speed $+1$. There are exactly five live signals, counting the two outgoing strands at the initial $L$/messenger contact. Translation of the entire configuration has been quotiented out, but scale remains a coordinate. Write
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:centered}
 z=(D,\xi,\eta)^{\mathsf T},\qquad \xi=x-D/3,\qquad \eta=y-2D/3.
\end{equation}
The ordered cone and its normalized shape triangle are
\begin{align}
 \plCone&=\{z:D/3+\xi>0,\ D/3+\eta-\xi>0,\ D/3-\eta>0\},\label{smc:hl:eq:cone}\\
 \Omega&=\{w\in\R^2:(1,w)^{\mathsf T}\in\plCone\}.
\end{align}
Adding the three inequalities proves $D>0$. In particular $0\in\Omega$.

\begin{theorem}[Full homogeneous local realization]\label{smc:hl:thm:main}
For $N\in\Q^{3\times3}$ the following conditions are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item A finite deterministic rational-speed, number-preserving signal machine has a nonempty positive-duration complete binary word that returns literally to the stated section and acts by $z\mapsto Nz$ on a nonempty full-dimensional open set.
\item $\det N\ne0$ and $\plCone\cap N^{-1}\plCone\ne\varnothing$.
\end{enumerate}
Incoming and outgoing speeds at each prescribed binary collision are distinct. Under condition~2, a machine, word, and finite list of strict rational homogeneous guard rows $Gz>0$ can be constructed effectively. Its exact chamber
\[
 \plChamber=\{z:Gz>0\}
\]
contains a rational ray $(1,p)^{\mathsf T}$ with $p\in\Omega$. On $D=1$ it is a bounded nonempty open rational polygon. The return restores all stationary labels and the original outgoing messenger phase, and realizes $N$ itself, not only its projective class.
\end{theorem}

The theorem is a local one-pass statement. It does not require the chosen word to work on every compatible input, and it does not prescribe its chamber or make that chamber invariant. In particular it need not supply any infinitely valid input. The matrix-dependent finite rule table and word need not have polynomial description size. Global reversibility, continuation after accumulation, Turing completeness, novelty, and optimal counts are not claimed.

\subsection{The model and inherited interfaces}
A meta-signal is a label carrying a fixed rational velocity. The finite rule table assigns an outgoing set to each admissible incoming set, with pairwise distinct incoming speeds and pairwise distinct outgoing speeds. Equal velocities on labels used in different phases are allowed. A complete binary word lists every contact, including messenger crossings of a stationary marker; it may not silently discard a contact. All valid words here preserve the population at five.

Two preserved results are used with explicit scope.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The fixed-center compiler from Report~62 realizes every rational matrix
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:inherited}
 M=\begin{pmatrix}s&b\\0&A\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 s>0,\quad b\in\Q^{1\times2},\quad A\in\GL_2(\Q),
\end{equation}
on an exact chamber whose complete homogeneous guard list is strict at $\plEzer=(1,0,0)^{\mathsf T}$. Its positive-duration complete word is nonempty, literal on the present section, and supports fresh phase copies at interfaces. The orientation-reversing case $\det A<0$ is included. We retain its full guard list, not merely endpoint inequalities.
\item The fixed-word full-section theorem from Report~61 makes every fixed complete binary return invertible in the three translation-quotiented positional coordinates. In the present literal section chart, an $m$-event return obeys
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:parity}
 \sgn(\det N)=(-1)^m.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
The relevant proof and accepted fixed-center review are copied unchanged into the source archive. The translation chronology below is re-established directly, using the nearest-target geometry of the preserved positive-planar proof. No earlier executable constructor or saved trajectory is needed.

\section{A physical nearest-target translation}\label{smc:hl:sec:primitive}
Use distance coordinates from a stationary anchor: a nearest target at $t$, a stationary spectator at $s$, and the far stationary reflector at $D$. Thus these are precisely the four markers, with one spectator between target and reflector. Fix a rational parameter $e<1$, and define
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:primitive-data}
 u=\frac{t}{1-e},\qquad t'=t+eD,\qquad h=\frac{e}{2-e}.
\end{equation}
Then $-1<h<1$. The proposed word consists of a homothety about the anchor by $1/(1-e)$ followed by a homothety about the far reflector by $1-e$. Both use fresh temporary target labels, even when $e=0$.

\begin{lemma}[Exact ten-event primitive]\label{smc:hl:lem:primitive}
The word described below takes the target from $t$ to $t+eD$, fixes the other markers, and returns the messenger to the anchor pointing outward. Its exact guard is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:primitive-guard}
 0<t<s<D,\qquad 0<t'<s.
\end{equation}
Every collision is binary with distinct incoming and outgoing speeds. The duration is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:primitive-duration}
 2\left(t+\frac{t}{1-e}\right)+2D,
\end{equation}
strictly between $2D$ and $6D$ on this chamber.
\end{lemma}

\subsection{All ten contacts and their chronology}
The first four event time/position pairs, starting with the messenger at the anchor pointing outward, are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:four-events}
 (t,t),\quad(2t,0),\quad(2t+u,u),\quad(2t+2u,0).
\end{equation}
At event~1 the target is launched with distance velocity $h$ and the messenger reverses. Event~2 bounces the messenger at the anchor. Event~3 restores the target and reverses the messenger; event~4 bounces at the anchor. The target restoration equation is
\[
 t+h(t+u)=u.
\]
No spectator lies between the target and its anchor.

Set $\alpha=2t+2u$. The remaining six event pairs are
\begin{align}\label{smc:hl:eq:six-events}
 &(\alpha+u,u),\quad(\alpha+s,s),\quad(\alpha+D,D),\notag\\
 &(\alpha+2D-s,s),\quad(\alpha+2D-t',t'),\quad(\alpha+2D,0).
\end{align}
At event~5, launch the target with velocity $h$ while the messenger continues outward. Cross the spectator at event~6, bounce at the reflector at event~7, cross the spectator inward at event~8, restore the target while continuing inward at event~9, and bounce at the anchor at event~10. Here
\[
 u+h\bigl((2D-t')-u\bigr)=t'
\]
is the restoration identity. Figure~\ref{smc:hl:fig:chronology} shows both moving target phases and every messenger contact.

\subsection{Why endpoint guards are exact for this primitive}
The internal restored target position $u$ lies between $t$ and $t'$ because
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:between}
 u-t=\frac{et}{1-e},\qquad t'-u=\frac{e(D-t')}{1-e}.
\end{equation}
Both differences have the sign of $e$ under~\eqref{smc:hl:eq:primitive-guard}; at $e=0$ both vanish. Thus $0<u<s$. The first four flight lengths are $t,t,u,u$. The last six are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:flights}
 u,\quad s-u,\quad D-s,\quad D-s,\quad s-t',\quad t'.
\end{equation}
Every flight is strictly positive. During each moving phase the target moves monotonically between two points of $(0,s)$, so it cannot collide with anchor, spectator, or reflector. The messenger has speed $\pm1$, while the target has speed $h\in(-1,1)$; prescribed departures and returns are transverse. The two spectator contacts listed above exhaust all such contacts. There is no other moving marker. This proves complete chronology, not only correct endpoints.

Conversely, start with a valid ordered section and consider the first failed required endpoint. If an endpoint leaves $(0,s)$, either the continuously moving target reaches an adjacent stationary marker or a prescribed event interval collapses or reorders, no later than the proposed restoration. If the first scale is obstructed, the argument stops there; otherwise it applies to the second homothety. It never continues a prospective trajectory through an earlier wrong collision. This first-failure argument proves necessity as well as sufficiency of~\eqref{smc:hl:eq:primitive-guard}.

Summing the flights gives~\eqref{smc:hl:eq:primitive-duration}. Since $0<t,u<D$, the duration is strictly between $2D$ and $6D$. At $e=0$ the word is still a genuine ten-event timed identity. Temporary labels of speed zero are legitimate: their collision partners have speed $\pm1$. Reflection about $R$ negates physical velocities and preserves all distance-coordinate times, inequalities, and counts. We denote the primitive by $T_D(e)$ with its chosen target understood.

\section{Translation between arbitrary rational interior shapes}\label{smc:hl:sec:translation}
For $a\in\Q^2$ define the homogeneous shape translation
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:T}
 T_a=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\a_1&1&0\\a_2&0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
It fixes $D$ and acts by $w\mapsto w+a$. We now implement it with the same five signals and original marker roles.

Define the normalized gap forms
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:gamma}
 \gamma_1(w)=\tfrac13+w_1,\quad
 \gamma_2(w)=\tfrac13+w_2-w_1,\quad
 \gamma_3(w)=\tfrac13-w_2.
\end{equation}
For $p,q\in\Omega\cap\Q^2$ let
\begin{align}\label{smc:hl:eq:n}
 m&=\min\{\gamma_i(p),\gamma_i(q):1\le i\le3\}>0,\notag\\
 \Delta&=q-p,\quad M=\max(|\Delta_1|,|\Delta_2|),\quad
 n=\max\{1,\lceil2M/m\rceil\},\quad \delta=\Delta/n.
\end{align}
Every point on the segment from $p$ to $q$ has gaps at least $m$, because the $\gamma_i$ are affine. Also $m\le1/3$ and $|\delta_j|\le m/2\le1/6$, so both primitive parameters $\delta_1$ and $-\delta_2$ are less than one.

\begin{lemma}[Literal physical shape translation]\label{smc:hl:lem:translation}
For every rational $p,q\in\Omega$, a complete word realizes $T_{q-p}$ on an exact rational chamber containing $(1,p)^{\mathsf T}$. The selected construction has $26n$ events and $4n$ temporary target labels, with $n$ as in~\eqref{smc:hl:eq:n}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For $k=0,\ldots,n-1$ execute these four blocks.
\begin{enumerate}
\item At $L$, apply $T_D(\delta_1)$ to nearest target $X$. This uses ten events and changes $x$ to $x+\delta_1D$.
\item Transfer $L\to R$: cross $X$, cross $Y$, and reflect at $R$. These are three events of total duration $D$.
\item At $R$, apply reflected $T_D(-\delta_2)$ to nearest target $Y$. Its distance $D-y$ decreases by $\delta_2D$, so $y$ increases by $\delta_2D$. This uses ten events.
\item Transfer $R\to L$: cross $Y$, cross $X$, and reflect at $L$. These are three events of total duration $D$.
\end{enumerate}
At nominal input $p$, the completed-step shapes are $p+k\delta$. The X-first intermediate shape is
\[
 c_k=p+k\delta+(\delta_1,0).
\]
Its gaps differ from those at $p+k\delta$ by $\delta_1,-\delta_1,0$; hence all are at least $m/2>0$. Thus both translations have strictly ordered initial and final endpoints. Lemma~\ref{smc:hl:lem:primitive} supplies their entire chronology, including their hidden scale endpoints. Transfers need only the retained section ordering. Every nominal contact is legitimate. Each step restores all stationary labels and the outgoing messenger at $L$, and acts by $T_\delta$. The product is $T_\delta^n=T_\Delta$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The exact chamber includes the intermediate corners}
Set
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:H}
 H=\begin{pmatrix}1/3&1&0\\1/3&-1&1\\1/3&0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 Hz=(x,y-x,D-y)^{\mathsf T}.
\end{equation}
An exact guard list for this translation is
\begin{align}
 HT_{k\delta}z&>0 &&(k=0,\ldots,n),\label{smc:hl:eq:translation-guards}\\
 HT_{((k+1)\delta_1,k\delta_2)}z&>0 &&(k=0,\ldots,n-1).\notag
\end{align}
There are $6n+3$ supplied scalar rows, allowing redundancy: three rows at each of $2n+1$ checkpoints. Necessity and sufficiency follow from the exact primitive guards, applied to the first invalid checkpoint after a valid prefix. Merely testing the original and final endpoints would not justify discarding intermediate X-first corners. All supplied rows are strict at $(1,p)^{\mathsf T}$, so the finite intersection contains a full-dimensional open neighborhood of that ray.

Each step uses $10+3+10+3=26$ events and four temporary marker labels. With a fresh messenger phase at each event and the final phase closed to the initial one, a standalone translation uses $26n$ messenger labels, $4n$ temporary target labels, and four stationary labels: $30n+4$ meta-signals. These are construction counts, not minima. For $p=q$ retain $n=1$, $\delta=0$ to obtain a nonempty 26-event identity. Such an identity may be omitted only if another nonempty macro supplies the timed return.

The duration of a step starting at $(D,x,y)$ is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:step-duration}
 6D+2\left(1+\frac1{1-\delta_1}\right)x
    +2\left(1+\frac1{1+\delta_2}\right)(D-y).
\end{equation}
The X-first operation does not change the second target's incoming distance $D-y$. Both scale parts are positive and less than $4D$, giving
\[
 6D<T_{\rm step}<14D,\qquad
 6nD<T_{\rm translation}<14nD.
\]
The latter uses that $D$ is unchanged during the translation.
\section{Left and right normalization proves sufficiency}\label{smc:hl:sec:reduction}
Assume $\det N\ne0$ and $\plCone\cap N^{-1}\plCone\ne\varnothing$. This intersection is open and contains a rational point. Normalize its positive first coordinate to obtain
\[
 \plEp=(1,p)^{\mathsf T},\qquad p\in\Omega\cap\Q^2.
\]
Write
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:pq}
 N\plEp=s(1,q)^{\mathsf T},\qquad s>0,\qquad q\in\Omega\cap\Q^2.
\end{equation}
Set
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:Nzero}
 N_0=T_{-q}NT_p.
\end{equation}
Then $N_0\plEzer=s\plEzer$, so
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:fixed-form}
 N_0=\begin{pmatrix}s&b\\0&A_0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 \det A_0=\det N/s\ne0.
\end{equation}
More explicitly, for $N=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\c&B\end{smallmatrix}\right)$,
\[
 s=a+bp,\qquad q=(c+Bp)/s,\qquad A_0=B-qb.
\]
All quantities are rational. There is no eigenray requirement: $p$ and $q$ are generally different.

Execute in chronological order the physical translation $p\to0$, the inherited fixed-center compiler for $N_0$, and the physical translation $0\to q$. Their actual matrix product is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:product}
 T_qN_0T_{-p}=N.
\end{equation}
Each factor is a literal five-signal complete word on the original section. Thus the algebra is implemented physically, rather than by relabeling an encoding.

\subsection{Pulling back every exact guard}
Let $G_-$, $G_0$, and $G_+$ be the exact guard matrices of the three words. Their composite chamber is exactly
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:full-guards}
 G_-z>0,\qquad G_0T_{-p}z>0,\qquad G_+N_0T_{-p}z>0.
\end{equation}
The first list is strict at $\plEp$ by Lemma~\ref{smc:hl:lem:translation}. The middle word starts there at $\plEzer$, and every one of its guards is strict. The last word starts at $s\plEzer$; its guards are homogeneous and strict at $\plEzer$, hence at $s\plEzer$. Every row in~\eqref{smc:hl:eq:full-guards} is consequently strict at $\plEp$.

Sufficiency follows by completing the three exact words. For necessity, take the first word whose exact guard fails after a successful prefix; no prospective formula is used past that failure. The first input ordering bounds the normalized chamber by $\Omega$, so the $D=1$ section is a bounded nonempty open rational polygon containing $p$. Final order implies
\[
 \plChamber\subseteq\plCone\cap N^{-1}\plCone.
\]
Equality is not asserted and is not required.

\subsection{Deterministic phase closure and the population count}
Give each messenger-involving event a fresh incoming messenger phase with its prescribed rational speed, and output the next phase. Identify only the last outgoing phase of the full composite with the first. Temporary target labels are fresh at every launch/restoration, including speed-zero identities. Stationary marker labels retain their roles. Thus interfaces never merge unrelated standalone messenger rules and do not require instantaneous phase-switch events.

Every new translation contact has a messenger of speed $\pm1$ and a target of speed in $(-1,1)$ or a stationary partner. Both incoming and outgoing pairs have distinct speeds. The optional seven-event orientation-reversing middle component has one marker-only event. Its messenger phase is unchanged there, and a fresh copy of its temporary marker label isolates that input set, as in the inherited compiler.

Each prescribed rule consumes two signals and emits two. Complete the table by identity rules on all other admissible finite label sets with pairwise distinct speeds. There are finitely many such sets. This gives a finite deterministic number-preserving machine, but an unlisted contact still does not belong to the selected complete word. The live population remains exactly five throughout valid finite execution; global injectivity of the rule map is not claimed.

If the physical translations use $n_-,n_+$ steps and the middle compiler uses $m_0$ events, $t_0$ temporary marker labels, and $g_0$ guard rows, then
\begin{align}
 m&=26(n_-+n_+)+m_0,\notag\\
 t&=4(n_-+n_+)+t_0,\label{smc:hl:eq:counts}\\
 g&=(6n_-+3)+g_0+(6n_++3).\notag
\end{align}
With $r$ marker-only events, fresh labels total $m-r+t+4$. The chosen inherited compiler has $r\le1$. Both translations have determinant one and even length, so the determinant parity~\eqref{smc:hl:eq:parity} is inherited from the middle component.

\subsection{Necessity completes the criterion}
Suppose a realization agrees with $N$ on a nonempty full-dimensional open chamber. The full-section fixed-word theorem makes its ambient homogeneous positional map invertible. Agreement on an open set identifies that ambient linear map with $N$, hence $\det N\ne0$. Both an input in the chamber and its output are ordered, so $\plCone\cap N^{-1}\plCone\ne\varnothing$. This proves the converse and completes Theorem~\ref{smc:hl:thm:main}.
\section{An exact rational compatibility decision}\label{smc:hl:sec:decision}
The inverse of~\eqref{smc:hl:eq:H} is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:Hinv}
 H^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\2/3&-1/3&-1/3\\1/3&1/3&-2/3\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
Set $K=HNH^{-1}$. Cone compatibility is equivalent to the existence of $g$ with $g>0$ and $Kg>0$. By positive scaling, impose $\boldsymbol1^{\mathsf T}g=1$. Solve the rational linear program
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:lp}
\begin{aligned}
 \text{maximize}\quad &\varepsilon\\
 \text{subject to}\quad &\boldsymbol1^{\mathsf T}g=1,\\
 &g_i\ge\varepsilon,\quad(Kg)_i\ge\varepsilon\quad(i=1,2,3),\\
 &0\le\varepsilon\le1.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
A strictly positive $g$ gives a positive feasible $\varepsilon$ after normalization, and any feasible $\varepsilon>0$ supplies a strict witness. Thus compatibility holds exactly when the program is feasible with positive optimum. Infeasibility or optimum zero means incompatibility. Its feasible set, when nonempty, is compact: $g$ belongs to the closed standard simplex and $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$.

No numerical tolerance is required. There are four variables, one equality, and eight inequalities. Enumerate the at most
\[
 \binom83=56
\]
triples of inequality boundaries. Solve each together with the equality whenever the four rows have full rank, reject candidates violating any weak inequality, and select the greatest $\varepsilon$. Every nonempty compact polytope has a vertex, including lower-dimensional feasible sets, so this finds the exact optimum or proves infeasibility. Exact Gaussian elimination or Cramer's rule uses only a fixed number of rational operations in fixed dimension and has polynomial bit complexity in the rational input length. Computing $\det N$ is polynomial as well.

A positive rational optimum provides all data for the compiler:
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:lp-shapes}
 \plEp=H^{-1}g,\quad s=\boldsymbol1^{\mathsf T}Kg>0,\quad
 q=\frac{\bigl((H^{-1}Kg)_2,(H^{-1}Kg)_3\bigr)}s.
\end{equation}
The first coordinate of $H^{-1}g$ is one, so the remaining coordinates give $p$.

This proves a polynomial-time endpoint-feasibility and local-realizability \emph{decision}. It does not bound the size of the output collision word polynomially. The translation count can grow like the reciprocal interior margin, and the inherited compiler can have large subdivision counts. Small binary matrix descriptions can produce very large explicit words in this construction. Decidability is not a Turing-universality assertion.

\section{A compatible matrix with no rational eigenray}\label{smc:hl:sec:example}
Consider the strictly positive integer gap matrix
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:example}
 K=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\1&2&1\\1&1&3\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 N=H^{-1}KH=
 \begin{pmatrix}4&-1&-1\\-1/3&1/3&1/3\\-1/3&-1/3&5/3\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
It has $\det K=\det N=2$ and maps every strictly positive gap vector to a strictly positive vector. Its characteristic polynomial is
\[
 t^3-6t^2+8t-2.
\]
None of the possible rational roots $\pm1,\pm2$ is a root. A rational matrix acting on a nonzero rational eigenvector would have a rational eigenvalue, so neither $K$ nor $N$ has a rational eigenray.

Nevertheless choose $p=0$. Then
\[
 N\plEzer=(4,-1/3,-1/3)^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 s=4,\qquad q=(-1/12,-1/12),
\]
and
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:example-Nzero}
 N_0=\begin{pmatrix}4&-1&-1\\0&1/4&1/4\\0&-5/12&19/12\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
Its lower block has determinant $1/2$, so the inherited fixed-center compiler applies. For the suffix $0\to q$, the endpoint gap margin is $m=1/4$ and $M=1/12$, giving $n=1$. Thus one 26-event physical suffix after the $N_0$ compiler realizes $N$ exactly. The identity prefix may be omitted because the middle compiler is nonempty, or retained for uniform bookkeeping.

At the nominal input $D=1$, the middle word finishes with $D=4$, $x=4/3$, $y=8/3$. The suffix first moves $X$ to $1$, then $Y$ to $7/3$, retaining $R=4$. Every intermediate order is strict. Final normalized gaps are
\[
 (1/4,\ 1/3,\ 5/12).
\]
This example closes the rational-eigenray gap without changing the section or the specified homogeneous representative.

\section{A degree six positive integer certificate}\label{smc:hl:sec:certificate}
This section represents local physical realizability, not infinite repetition. Let $K=(k_{ij})$ be an \emph{integer} matrix in gap coordinates, and let $q>0$ be a fixed or externally supplied integer denominator. The gap return is $K/q$, and the corresponding centered return is $H^{-1}(K/q)H$. Positive common scaling affects neither nonsingularity nor positive-cone compatibility.

Use eight positive-integer witnesses
\[
 g_1,g_2,g_3,\ h_1,h_2,h_3,\ b,d
\]
and the single integer polynomial
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:F}
\begin{split}
 F(K;g,h,b,d)={}&\sum_{i=1}^3\bigl((Kg)_i-h_i\bigr)^2\\
 &+\bigl[\det K-(2b-3)d\bigr]^2+\bigl[(b-1)(b-2)\bigr]^2.
\end{split}
\end{equation}

\begin{corollary}\label{smc:hl:cor:dio}
Equation $F=0$ has a positive-integer witness tuple if and only if the represented rational return is locally physically realizable on the standard five-signal section.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
A sum of nonnegative integer squares vanishes exactly when every residual vanishes. Therefore $Kg=h>0$, $b\in\{1,2\}$, and $\det K=(2b-3)d\ne0$. These are the two conditions of Theorem~\ref{smc:hl:thm:main} in gap coordinates.

Conversely, strict real feasibility of rational linear inequalities gives a positive rational vector $g$ by openness. Clear a common positive denominator to obtain positive integer $g$ and $h=Kg$. Choose $b=1$ if $\det K<0$, $b=2$ if $\det K>0$, and $d=|\det K|$. All five residuals vanish.
\end{proof}

The interface has nine signed integer matrix-entry inputs and eight positive-integer witnesses. There are five squared residuals: three vector coordinates, one determinant/sign residual, and one two-value gate. The exact total degree of the polynomial in all its input and witness variables is six, since the cubic determinant is squared; all other displayed terms have degree at most four. An optional positive denominator is an extra input that does not occur in the polynomial.

Representing $k_{ij}=a_{ij}-c_{ij}$ externally with positive input leaves changes nine signed matrix-entry inputs to eighteen positive external inputs, adds no witnesses, and preserves exact degree six. There is no finite-fold statement. Whenever a witness tuple exists, replacing $(g,h)$ by $(rg,rh)$ for every positive integer $r$ gives infinitely many distinct witness tuples with $b,d$ unchanged.

\subsection{Centered inputs require an explicit conversion}
For a native signed integer centered numerator $M$ with $N=M/q$, put
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:SB}
 S=3H=\begin{pmatrix}1&3&0\\1&-3&3\\1&0&-3\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 B=3H^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}3&3&3\\2&-1&-1\\1&1&-2\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
Then $SB=BS=9I$, and the integer matrix $\widetilde K=SMB$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:centered-conversion}
 H(M/q)H^{-1}=\frac{\widetilde K}{9q},\qquad
 \det\widetilde K=729\det M.
\end{equation}
Thus the centered-input polynomial is explicitly
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:Fcenter}
\begin{split}
 F_{\rm center}(M;g,h,b,d)={}&\sum_{i=1}^3\bigl(((SMB)g)_i-h_i\bigr)^2\\
 &+\bigl[729\det M-(2b-3)d\bigr]^2
 +\bigl[(b-1)(b-2)\bigr]^2.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
This has nine signed matrix-entry inputs, eight positive witnesses, five squared residuals, and exact total degree six. The fixed linear substitution creates no hidden witness or alias variable. Eighteen positive external leaves can encode the entries of $M$ by differences. The positive denominator factor $9$ adds no condition. No centered-input arithmetic operation count is asserted here.

The signed-input graph has leaves for the nine entries, eight witnesses, and constants $1,2,3$. Gate outputs are unrestricted integers. A square is one multiplication, and multiplication by the constant $2$ is counted. These are arithmetic expression graphs, not collision schedules or additional Diophantine witnesses.

\section{Repeated validity and clocks are conditional}\label{smc:hl:sec:clocks}
Let $\plChamber=\{z:Gz>0\}$ denote the actual full chamber~\eqref{smc:hl:eq:full-guards}. Literal phase closure gives the exact equivalence
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:infinite}
 \text{the complete word is infinitely valid at }z
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad GN^nz>0\quad\text{for every integer }n\ge0.
\end{equation}
The chamber need not be forward invariant. The set in~\eqref{smc:hl:eq:infinite} may be empty even when the local criterion holds.

\subsection{A local realization with no infinitely ordered input}
In gap coordinates take
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:escape}
 K_{\rm esc}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\-1&0&1\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
It has determinant one and is compatible for $g_3>g_1>0$, $g_2>0$. Yet
\[
 K_{\rm esc}^ng=(g_1,g_2,g_3-ng_1)^{\mathsf T},
\]
so every strictly positive input eventually leaves the ordered cone. Theorem~\ref{smc:hl:thm:main} locally realizes $H^{-1}K_{\rm esc}H$, while no repeatedly valid realization with this same full return has an infinitely valid input. Figure~\ref{smc:hl:fig:local-repeated} makes the distinction explicit.

\subsection{A duration bound for the retained-translation construction}
Retain both physical translations, including an identity when needed. The first translation alone takes more than $6D$. On the actual chamber every event time and endpoint coordinate is a fixed rational homogeneous linear form in $z$. The closure of the normalized triangle $\Omega$ is compact. Consequently the finitely many such forms yield an effective finite upper bound on total duration and intermediate positions proportional to incoming $D$. Thus the full duration is $\ell z$ for a rational row $\ell$, and there are constants $c_1,c_2>0$ with
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:clock-bound}
 c_1D\le\ell z\le c_2D\quad(z\in\plChamber),\qquad c_1=6\text{ available}.
\end{equation}
The lower bound here is for this retained-translation construction; omitting a timed identity is harmless to local realization but does not invoke this particular argument unchanged.

\begin{remark}[\wtag\ Conditional spectral clock criterion, printed once as Theorem~\ref{smc:pj:thm:clock}]\label{smc:hl:cor:clock}
Source~33's Corollary~8.1 states the following. For an infinitely valid input $z$, write $z_n=N^nz$ and $D_n=(z_n)_1>0$. For the construction retaining both translations,
\begin{align}\label{smc:hl:eq:clock}
 \text{Zeno}
 &\Longleftrightarrow\sum_{n\ge0}D_n<\infty
 \Longleftrightarrow N^nz\longrightarrow0\notag\\
 &\Longleftrightarrow
 \text{every eigenvalue of }N|_{V_z}\text{ has modulus }<1,
 \qquad V_z=\Span\{z,Nz,N^2z\}.
\end{align}
If $z$ is rational and Zeno, its total time
\begin{equation}\label{smc:hl:eq:clock-sum}
 T_\infty=\ell\,(I-N|_{V_z})^{-1}z\in\Q
\end{equation}
is rational, the inverse being taken within $V_z$. No ambient inverse is required: unused unit eigenmodes may make $I-N$ singular. This is source~32's Theorem~\ref{smc:pj:thm:clock} with its formula \eqref{smc:pj:eq:active-time}, for source~33's construction: the bound \eqref{smc:hl:eq:clock-bound}, with $c_1=6$, replaces source~32's \eqref{smc:pj:eq:clockbound}. Source~33's proof is source~32's: sum the bound, bound $\xi_n$ and $\eta_n$ by the ordering, apply the Jordan estimates on the cyclic subspace and Cayley--Hamilton. The rationality is a special case of source~26's Theorem~\ref{smc:pm:thm:rational} (Remark~\ref{smc:xi:rem:zeno}).
\end{remark}
All clock claims assume~\eqref{smc:hl:eq:infinite}. They do not decide the general infinite-validity set, provide such an input, or continue a trajectory beyond an accumulation. The local theorem does not depend on this optional corollary.
\section{Relation to the literature and scope}\label{smc:hl:sec:scope}
The signal-machine model used here is consistent with Becker et al.\ \cite{agc10}: finitely many labels carry constant velocities; collision input and output sets have distinct velocities; and the operational next event occurs at the smallest positive meeting time. Their intrinsic universality construction concerns macro-signals and simulations of entire machines. It does not establish the present five-live-signal local criterion.

The oblique constant-flow section maps, itinerary domains, and path compositions in Alishah, Duarte, and Peixe\ \cite{alishah2020} give related geometric precedents. Their setting is flows on polytopes. Durand-Lose\ \cite{DL07} gives scale-relative signal-distance arithmetic in the linear Blum--Shub--Smale setting. That arithmetic does not alone imply the fixed-population, full-section realization proved here.

The construction-specific contribution presented in this report is the exact local criterion, obtained from the physical translation chronology and left/right reduction relative to the preserved fixed-center compiler. The explicit degree-six certificate describes that decidable criterion. The literature is positioning rather than a priority or exhaustive novelty search.

\section{Further research directions}\label{smc:hl:sec:further}
The construction suggests several precise next questions. They are questions left open by this report, not claims that the wider literature has no answer.
\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{smc:xi:q:hl1} \textbf{Guard coverage.} Can alternative physical factorizations enlarge the realized chamber toward the full endpoint-compatible region? Characterizing which prescribed polygons can be exact word chambers would strengthen the current existential result.
\item\label{smc:xi:q:hl2} \textbf{Compilation size.} The selected rational subdivision can be large when the interior margin is small. Bounds on event counts, temporary labels, and arithmetic description length should be studied separately from the fixed-dimensional polynomial-time decision.
\item\label{smc:xi:q:hl3} \textbf{Repeated validity.} For which matrix and guard classes can the set $\{z:GN^nz>0\text{ for all }n\ge0\}$ be decided or described effectively? The escaping-gap example shows that endpoint compatibility alone cannot answer this.
\item\label{smc:xi:q:hl4} \textbf{Physical branching.} A finite family of compatible linear returns is not yet a physical piecewise program. A further construction would need explicit branch detection, mutually consistent collision rules, complete chronology, and phase interfaces before a universality claim could follow.
\end{enumerate}
\wtag\ [Status at this write: Question~\ref{smc:xi:q:hl4} is answered by source~34 in Part~XII. A finite table tests two branches on the full section without destroying it (Theorem~\ref{smc:br:thm:test}), and every fixed two-counter program is compiled with five live signals (Theorem~\ref{smc:br:thm:compiler}). Five-live-signal counter computation itself is Durand-Lose's prior work, credited there. Questions~\ref{smc:xi:q:hl1}--\ref{smc:xi:q:hl3} are open.]

\subsection{Manuscript and release tooling}
The editable source is supplied both as modular \LaTeX{} and as a deterministic standalone flattening. Owned release tools authenticate the frozen files, flatten the manuscript, typeset it in an isolated fresh TeX format with shell escape disabled, record all format and document-pass inputs, render every PDF page, and create a deterministic evidence archive. They do not run scientific checkers as part of a typesetting or packaging command.

The build lock records the invoked interpreter/executable bytes and the union of system TeX and font-map inputs, with a preflight comparison and a post-build comparison. It does not inventory operating-system libraries or Python's standard library and is not a sandbox for hostile source. Separate reviewer evidence covers the current owned tooling and the final manuscript. Direct model all-page visual inspection remains distinct from PDF-text, page-count, PNG, and dependency authentication checks.

A release manifest authenticates exact file inventories, bytes, modes, and nanosecond modification times. The supplied extraction path restores those metadata so that relocated verification can use the same trusted external manifest pin. Ordinary ZIP extraction is not claimed to retain all authenticated metadata. Integrity hashes are commitments, not digital signatures; a digest acquired from the same untrusted object does not constitute independent authentication.


\section{What Part~XI does not claim, its questions, and its provenance}\label{smc:xi:sec:status}

\subsection{Non-claims of the four sources}\label{smc:xi:sec:nonclaims}
\wtag\ The four sources state the following limits; none of them is lifted by printing them together.
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{All four.} The proofs are conventional proofs supported by finite exact and static checks. None is a proof-assistant formalization, and no Lean or Rocq development certifies any statement of this Part. No physical simulation, next-event search or saved collision schedule was run, and finite fixtures do not replace the all-parameter proofs. No priority, novelty, exhaustive literature search, minimality or optimality (events, labels, speeds, population, degree, witnesses, gates) is claimed. Each machine is fixed after its rational parameters: there is no unchanged universal table and no polynomial-size compiler. Number preservation is not global reversibility. No run is continued through a Zeno accumulation point. Hashes are integrity commitments, not signatures, and overlapping check counts must not be summed.
\item \emph{Source~30.} The physical compiler covers $\GL_2^+(\Q)$ at a fixed positive rational scale only. The abstract classification also covers singular and negative-determinant matrices, but without a physical realization and without a physical impossibility. There is no uniform polynomial physical compiler, no generic emitted arithmetic graph, no gate count and no Turing completeness. A real kernel on an irrational stable line may need algebraic coefficients. A finite sign obstruction is not an obstruction to existential integer certificates. Fixed-$A$ polynomial membership, uniform elliptic polynomial membership, the credited counting-hierarchy bound and the exponential explicit output are four different claims. Erratum~E1 changes only the wording of a bound: at most $\lfloor\log_2 b\rfloor$ divisions and $1+\lfloor\log_2 b\rfloor$ recurrence steps; no theorem changes. Figure~\ref{smc:pl:fig:ellipse} is analytic geometry, not a trajectory.
\item \emph{Source~31.} The singular obstruction holds only under the full-section, open-chamber, binary, positive-flight and fixed-scale hypotheses. It says nothing about projected, lower-dimensional, nonbinary, population-changing or limit models. The two-witness corollary and the finite clock are manuscript additions, not contents of the frozen packet. Seven events are not claimed minimal, and the inverse map need not be implemented by the machine.
\item \emph{Source~32.} The realization is for a fixed rational centre only. There is no realization of an arbitrary $\GL_3$ matrix in the original coordinates, and rational conjugacy is not a physical change of chart. The native-gap certificates are for the stated half-space example only; the integer-domain qualification is essential.
\item \emph{Source~33.} The theorem gives some local chamber: not every compatible input, not a prescribed or invariant chamber, and no infinitely valid input. A polynomial-time decision is not a polynomial-size compiler. There is no finite-fold statement. The 48/57 graph counts exclude the conversion from centred inputs, and the clock criterion is conditional on repeated validity.
\end{itemize}
