\subsection{A common rational speed set}
The inherited core uses the sufficient 19-speed set
\[
\{0\}\ \cup\ \pm\left\{1,\frac13,\frac1{79},\frac1{41},\frac32,\frac14,4,\frac12,2\right\}.
\]
Padding adds
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ck:eq:addspeeds}
\pm\left\{\frac{39}{196},\frac{18}{25},\frac9{25},\frac{63}{655},
\frac{10}{71},\frac6{53},\frac{12}{13},\frac{10}{61},\frac6{47},12\right\}.
\end{equation}
These ten positive magnitudes are pairwise distinct and disjoint from the nine core magnitudes, so the total set has $1+2(9+10)=39$ elements. A label never changes its assigned speed. New phase labels emitted at actual contacts implement all speed changes. Neither the set of speed values nor its size depends on counter values, scale or the particular finite program.

\subsection{Finite control and physical composition}
For every instruction and realized branch, make a fresh copy of its padding word. Retarget only the core's existing last $L$ rule: it now emits the fresh padding-entry label at the same old speed $+1$. Thus no core trajectory, duration, contact or counter output changes. The branch-specific core label chooses the branch's fixed padding copy. Its finite phase labels carry the chosen successor $j$ until the final loop emits $Q_j$.

Every padding rule keeps the stationary markers at the exact positions $(0,x',y',D)$ with literal labels $L,X_0,Y,R$. No data is hidden in a relabeled marker or altered scale. Two signals are consumed and two produced at every new contact. Fresh instruction, branch and stage labels give a finite deterministic rule table for a fixed finite program. Identity completion preserves cardinality on unused distinct-speed inputs. Encoded executions use only the proved words, so exactly five live signals persist.

Induction now proves Theorem~\ref{smc:ck:thm:clock}. The core is guarded at every encoded input, returns the correct output, and the padding restores that output with the correct successor label. Starting at time zero, the $n$th completed instruction section is at $30nD$. Each instruction contains at most 54 strictly separated contacts. An infinite run therefore cannot have finite-time accumulation, either between sections or inside a finite word. Before halt all positions remain in $[0,D]$.

Halt is designated full-section reachability, not the extinction of motion. Under the optional escape convention $Q_H$ makes identity crossings with $X,Y,R$ and then leaves to the right. Those exactly three post-halt contacts are not an additional source instruction. At $k=0$ the initial label is already $Q_H$, and the first-halt time is zero.

\section{Native positive gaps and paid decoding}\label{smc:ck:sec:decoding}
From now on the three external variables are $g_1,g_2,g_3\in\Np$, with $D,x,y$ defined by \eqref{smc:ck:eq:gaps}. This ensures the ordered section even before the encoding test. Introduce positive shifted counters $A,B$ and outputs $P,Q$. The two POWER modules displayed in Section~\ref{smc:ck:sec:power} enforce
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ck:eq:powers}
P=2^{A-1},\qquad Q=2^{B-1}.
\end{equation}
Add the two residuals
\begin{align}
G_1&=(20g_1-D)P-2D,\label{smc:ck:eq:G1}\\
G_3&=(20g_3-D)Q-2D.\label{smc:ck:eq:G3}
\end{align}
When both vanish, positivity of $D,P,Q$ forces $20g_1-D>0$ and $20g_3-D>0$. Division only by positive nonzero integers gives
\[
\frac{g_1}{D}=\frac1{20}+\frac{1}{10P},\qquad
\frac{g_3}{D}=\frac1{20}+\frac{1}{10Q},
\]
which is exactly \eqref{smc:ck:eq:nativeencoding} with $a=A-1,b=B-1$. Conversely an encoded triple supplies $A,B,P,Q$ and satisfies these two equations. The POWER modules supply all remaining decoding witnesses. Thus signs, denominators and powers are enforced internally, without a free exponential input.

Whenever decoding exists, it is unique:
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ck:eq:decoder}
P=\frac{2D}{20g_1-D},\qquad Q=\frac{2D}{20g_3-D}.
\end{equation}
A positive integral power of two has a unique nonnegative exponent, hence unique $A,B$. An elementary exact decoder can reject a nonpositive denominator, a nonintegral quotient, or a quotient that is not a power of two. This algorithmic observation does not replace the polynomial equations. Every accepted endpoint gap is in $(D/20,3D/20]$, so the middle gap lies in $[7D/10,9D/10)$.

\section{Two fully displayed POWER modules}\label{smc:ck:sec:power}
The two module copies use disjoint leaves. For $i=A,B$, let $(C_i,o_i)=(A,P)$ or $(B,Q)$ respectively. The thirteen directly positive leaves per copy are
\[
o_i,w_i,M_i,\eta_i,x_i,y_i,u_i,v_i,s_i,t_i,q_{b,i},q_{v,i},J_i.
\]
Here $M_i$ is a modulus witness, $\eta_i$ is an auxiliary Pell witness, and $x_i,y_i$ are Pell coordinates; they are unrelated to the physical $x,y$ or native $g_j$. Two further positive leaves $\alpha_{+,i},\beta_{+,i}$ define
\[
\alpha_i=\alpha_{+,i}+1,\qquad \beta_i=\beta_{+,i}+1.
\]
The eleven natural aliases in each copy are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ck:eq:nataliases}
d_{w2,i},d_{wC,i},d_{yC,i},\alpha_{1,i},\alpha_{2,i},
\sigma_{1,i},\sigma_{2,i},\tau_{1,i},\tau_{2,i},r_{1,i},r_{2,i}.
\end{equation}
Each alias is, by definition, its own positive leaf minus one. These are substitutions, not extra variables or equations. Thus each copy has exactly $13+2+11=26$ positive leaves \emph{including its output}, or 25 auxiliary leaves beyond that output. The index $C_i$ is the already counted shifted initial counter, not a new module leaf.

\subsection{The A module}
The fifteen residuals $R_{A,1},\ldots,R_{A,15}$ are the left sides below, with the stated positive substitutions fully understood:
\begin{align}
 x_A^2-1-(\alpha_A^2-1)y_A^2&=0,\label{smc:ck:eq:powerA}\\
 u_A^2-1-(\alpha_A^2-1)v_A^2&=0,\nonumber\\
 s_A^2-1-(\beta_A^2-1)t_A^2&=0,\nonumber\\
 \beta_A-1-4y_Aq_{b,A}&=0,\nonumber\\
 \beta_A+u_A\alpha_{1,A}-\alpha_A-u_A\alpha_{2,A}&=0,\nonumber\\
 v_A-y_A^2q_{v,A}&=0,\nonumber\\
 s_A+u_A\sigma_{1,A}-x_A-u_A\sigma_{2,A}&=0,\nonumber\\
 t_A+4y_A\tau_{1,A}-A-4y_A\tau_{2,A}&=0,\nonumber\\
 y_A-A-d_{yC,A}&=0,\nonumber\\
 w_A-2-d_{w2,A}&=0,\nonumber\\
 w_A-A-d_{wC,A}&=0,\nonumber\\
 M_A-2P-J_A&=0,\nonumber\\
 \alpha_A^2-1-\bigl((w_A+1)^2-1\bigr)(w_A\eta_A)^2&=0,\nonumber\\
 4\alpha_A-M_A-5&=0,\nonumber\\
 x_A+M_Ar_{1,A}-y_A(\alpha_A-2)-2P-M_Ar_{2,A}&=0.\nonumber
\end{align}
\subsection{The B module}
The independent fifteen residuals $R_{B,1},\ldots,R_{B,15}$ are
\begin{align}
 x_B^2-1-(\alpha_B^2-1)y_B^2&=0,\label{smc:ck:eq:powerB}\\
 u_B^2-1-(\alpha_B^2-1)v_B^2&=0,\nonumber\\
 s_B^2-1-(\beta_B^2-1)t_B^2&=0,\nonumber\\
 \beta_B-1-4y_Bq_{b,B}&=0,\nonumber\\
 \beta_B+u_B\alpha_{1,B}-\alpha_B-u_B\alpha_{2,B}&=0,\nonumber\\
 v_B-y_B^2q_{v,B}&=0,\nonumber\\
 s_B+u_B\sigma_{1,B}-x_B-u_B\sigma_{2,B}&=0,\nonumber\\
 t_B+4y_B\tau_{1,B}-B-4y_B\tau_{2,B}&=0,\nonumber\\
 y_B-B-d_{yC,B}&=0,\nonumber\\
 w_B-2-d_{w2,B}&=0,\nonumber\\
 w_B-B-d_{wC,B}&=0,\nonumber\\
 M_B-2Q-J_B&=0,\nonumber\\
 \alpha_B^2-1-\bigl((w_B+1)^2-1\bigr)(w_B\eta_B)^2&=0,\nonumber\\
 4\alpha_B-M_B-5&=0,\nonumber\\
 x_B+M_Br_{1,B}-y_B(\alpha_B-2)-2Q-M_Br_{2,B}&=0.\nonumber
\end{align}
These displays define ordinary integer polynomials after replacing every natural alias and $\alpha_i,\beta_i$ by its specified positive-leaf expression. No POWER predicate remains uninterpreted.

\subsection{The exact Pell dependency}
The substantive arithmetic input is the pinned mathlib4 theorem pair \texttt{Pell.matiyasevic} and \texttt{Pell.eq\_pow\_of\_pell} in \texttt{Mathlib/NumberTheory/PellMatiyasevic.lean}, commit
\begin{center}\small\texttt{ac77769fabe23cb237559e7f56578dbead91499f}.
\end{center}
The source, its license and attribution are retained inertly. \wtag\ [In this report the Lean source file and its Apache-2.0 licence are not shipped; they are cited by commit and SHA-256, and the arrival archive keeps them. The delivered \path{NOTICE.md} is shipped as \path{28-diophantine-science-sources-NOTICE.md}, and the dependency record \path{pell-dependency.json} as \path{data/09-chrono-matrix-independent_audit-pell-dependency.json} of the report \path{group-theoretic-substrates}; both are byte-identical to source~35's copies.] The two theorem statements are at lines 760--766 and 860--864 of the pinned source. This report uses their stated constructive equivalences; it does not claim a fresh Lean verification. The source SHA-256 is
\begin{center}\scriptsize\texttt{993760c797ad0ff66fa77064a616fce779550bc745cbf6c44e04f392fd0bed0a}.
\end{center}
The earlier general module used base $B_0\geq2$, semantic exponent $e\geq0$, Pell index $e+1$, and target $B_0\,o$. \wtag\ [This is the module of source~28 (Lemma~\ref{smc:fd:lem:power}) and source~30 (Section~\ref{smc:pl:sec:power}), whose proofs source~35 carried as \path{POWER58_PROOF.md} and \path{POWER60_PROOF.md}; they are shipped once, as \path{28-diophantine-science-PROOF.md} and \path{30-planar-science-arithmetic-PROOF.md}. Here $B_0$ is that module's base; in Section~\ref{smc:ck:sec:trace} $B_0$ is the input counter~$B$.] Here substitute
\[
B_0=2,\qquad e=C_i-1,\qquad k_0=C_i,\qquad m_0=2o_i.
\]
In particular the modulus identity becomes $4\alpha_i=M_i+5$. The semantic exponent can be zero even though the Pell index $C_i$ is strictly positive.

\begin{lemma}[Positive base two POWER equivalence]\label{smc:ck:lem:power}
For $C_i,o_i\in\Np$, the 15 residuals in one module have a solution in their 25 remaining positive leaves if and only if $o_i=2^{C_i-1}$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For soundness, equations 1--9 instantiate the nonzero-index branch of \texttt{Pell.matiyasevic}. They enforce $\alpha_i>1$, $y_i\geq C_i\geq1$, three Pell identities, $\beta_i>1$, and the four congruences
\[
\beta_i\equiv1\pmod{4y_i},\quad
\beta_i\equiv\alpha_i\pmod{u_i},\quad
s_i\equiv x_i\pmod{u_i},\quad
t_i\equiv C_i\pmod{4y_i},
\]
together with $v_i>0$ and $y_i^2\mid v_i$. Paired natural aliases express signed congruence quotients without a sign restriction. The theorem identifies $(x_i,y_i)$ with the Pell pair of index $C_i$.

Equations 10--15 impose $w_i\geq2$, $w_i\geq C_i$, $M_i>2o_i$, the auxiliary Pell identity, $4\alpha_i=M_i+5$, and the final congruence
\[
x_i\equiv y_i(\alpha_i-2)+2o_i\pmod{M_i}.
\]
Since $w_i\geq2$ and $\eta_i\geq1$, equation 13 implies
\[
\alpha_i^2=1+\bigl((w_i+1)^2-1\bigr)(w_i\eta_i)^2>w_i^2,
\]
so $\alpha_i>w_i\geq2$. In particular $\alpha_i-2$ agrees with the source's natural subtraction. The theorem \texttt{Pell.eq\_pow\_of\_pell} gives $2^{C_i}=2o_i$, and cancellation proves the required power.

For completeness start from $2^{C_i}=2o_i$ and use the constructive power theorem. Its auxiliary $\eta_i$ cannot be zero, because that would force $\alpha_i=1$. Apply the constructive nonzero-index Matiyasevic equivalence to the resulting Pell pair. The Pell coordinates $x_i,u_i,s_i$ are positive. Since $y_i\geq C_i\geq1$ and $v_i>0$, the divisibility quotient $q_{v,i}$ is positive. Since $\beta_i>1$ and $\beta_i\equiv1\pmod{4y_i}$, $q_{b,i}$ is positive. The congruence $t_i\equiv C_i\pmod{4y_i}$ and $1\leq C_i\leq y_i<4y_i$ exclude $t_i=0$. The strict inequality $M_i>2o_i$ supplies positive $J_i$. Every signed quotient can be written as the difference of two naturals, and all inequality slacks are nonnegative. Their shifted leaves are positive. This includes $C_i=1$.

For natural $u,v$, the source equality $u-v=1$ is equivalent to $u=v+1$. The interior differences $\alpha_i^2-1$, $\beta_i^2-1$ and $(w_i+1)^2-1$ are nonnegative. Thus replacing the source's truncated subtraction by the displayed integer equations neither loses nor adds solutions.
\end{proof}
\wtag\ [Lemma~\ref{smc:ck:lem:power} is source~28's Lemma~\ref{smc:fd:lem:power} at $B_0=2$ and $e=C_i-1$, with renamed leaves; the proof above is a second route for this instance, written for positive adapters and the Pell index $C_i\ge1$.]

For either module, $C_i=o_i=1$ has the following assignment, with natural aliases given before their positive shifts:

\begin{gathered}
w_i=2,\quad M_i=63,\quad\eta_i=3,\quad\alpha_i=\beta_i=17,\\
x_i=17,\ y_i=1,\ u_i=577,\ v_i=34,\ s_i=17,\ t_i=1,\\
q_{b,i}=4,\quad q_{v,i}=34,\quad J_i=61,\quad d_{wC,i}=1.

This finite fixture checks the exponent-zero boundary; Lemma~\ref{smc:ck:lem:power}, not the fixture, proves all exponents.

\section{Complete bounded trace equations}\label{smc:ck:sec:trace}
Assign distinct fixed integer codes to states. Each edge $e$ has fixed source $u_e$, target $v_e$, and changes $d_e,f_e\in\{-1,0,1\}$. Increment has one edge. A conditional has a zero edge with both changes zero and a positive edge decrementing its tested counter. Add exactly one virtual edge $h$ from $H$ to $H$ with changes zero. There are no duplicate edges or other outgoing halt edges.

For $T\geq1$ introduce positive leaves
\[
w_{t,e}\quad(0\leq t<T,\ 1\leq e\leq E),\qquad
A_t,B_t\quad(1\leq t\leq T).
\]
Define $s_{t,e}=w_{t,e}-1$, $A_0=A$, $B_0=B$. The full residual list $\mathcal R_{\rm trace}$ is \wtag\ [source~34's residuals \eqref{smc:br:eq:selector}--\eqref{smc:br:eq:controlresidual}, collected in one display]
\begin{align}
S_{t,e}&=(w_{t,e}-1)(w_{t,e}-2),
&&0\leq t<T,\ 1\leq e\leq E,\label{smc:ck:eq:trace}\\
O_t&=\sum_e s_{t,e}-1,&&0\leq t<T,\nonumber\\
U_t&=A_{t+1}-A_t-\sum_e d_es_{t,e},&&0\leq t<T,\nonumber\\
V_t&=B_{t+1}-B_t-\sum_e f_es_{t,e},&&0\leq t<T,\nonumber\\
Z_{t,e}&=s_{t,e}(A_t-1),&&\text{each A-zero edge and }0\leq t<T,\nonumber\\
Z_{t,e}&=s_{t,e}(B_t-1),&&\text{each B-zero edge and }0\leq t<T,\nonumber\\
C_{\rm initial}&=\sum_e u_es_{0,e}-q_0,\nonumber\\
C_t&=\sum_e v_es_{t,e}-\sum_e u_es_{t+1,e},&&0\leq t<T-1,\nonumber\\
C_{\rm final}&=\sum_e v_es_{T-1,e}-H.\nonumber
\end{align}
At $T=0$, replace the whole list by the single constant residual
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ck:eq:Tzero}
\mathcal R_{\rm trace}=(q_0-H),
\end{equation}
and introduce no trace witnesses. \wtag\ [As in source~34, Equation~\eqref{smc:br:eq:horizonzero}.] Count residual \emph{slots}, retaining any that specialize to the zero polynomial for a particular program. The exact trace ledger in both cases is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ck:eq:tracecounts}
\#W_{\rm trace}=T(E+2),\qquad
\#\mathcal R_{\rm trace}=T(E+Z+4)+1.
\end{equation}
Indeed there are $TE$ selector equations, $3T$ one-hot/update equations, $TZ$ zero guards and $T+1$ control equations for $T\geq1$.

\begin{remark}[\wtag\ restatement of source~34's Theorem~\ref{smc:br:thm:quartic}: trace correctness and uniqueness]\label{smc:ck:lem:trace}
\wtag\ Source~35's Lemma~7.1 states: \emph{For fixed positive $A,B$, the trace equations have a positive solution exactly when the computation from $(q_0,A-1,B-1)$ reaches $H$ by $T$. When a solution exists its trace witness tuple is unique.} This is the residual-level content of source~34's Theorem~\ref{smc:br:thm:quartic}, proved in Section~\ref{smc:br:sec:certificate}; source~35's own proof, a condensed form of that argument, follows.
\end{remark}
\begin{proof}
The selector equations give $w_{t,e}\in\{1,2\}$, so $s_{t,e}\in\{0,1\}$. The one-hot equation selects exactly one edge per time. The control equations force its source to be $q_0$ initially, link each target to the next source, and give final target $H$. Distinct state codes make equality of codes equality of states.

The update equations give the exact shifted-counter transitions. A selected zero edge forces its tested counter to equal 1. A decrement selected at value 1 would force its next positive leaf to be zero, which is impossible. Therefore decrement edges automatically require a positive unshifted counter; no guard witness is missing. At a nonhalting state exactly the appropriate deterministic edge can be selected. At $H$ only $h$ remains. Induction gives the real computation followed, if necessary, by virtual halt steps. It determines every selector and counter leaf uniquely. Conversely the computation padded through time $T$ supplies these leaves and zeros every residual. For $T=0$, \eqref{smc:ck:eq:Tzero} is exactly initial halt; the trace is the empty tuple.
\end{proof}

For $T\geq1$ define the additional residual
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ck:eq:early}
H_{\rm early}=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}s_{t,h}.
\end{equation}
Its summands are nonnegative, so its vanishing excludes every virtual halt-loop use. With the final control equation it enforces first arrival at $H$ exactly at $T$. For $T=0$ the by-horizon and exact-horizon predicates coincide and use \eqref{smc:ck:eq:Tzero}. The halt loop pads an arithmetic trace only; it is not a physical continuation after the designated halt section.

\section{One polynomial and its exact resource ledger}\label{smc:ck:sec:polynomial}
After all aliases have been replaced by their defining expressions, set
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ck:eq:polynomial}
F_{M,T}=G_1^2+G_3^2+
\sum_{j=1}^{15}R_{A,j}^2+
\sum_{j=1}^{15}R_{B,j}^2+
\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{\rm trace}}r^2.
\end{equation}
This finite sum defines every coefficient of an ordinary integer polynomial; monomial expansion is not needed to specify it. Program data are fixed coefficients and $T$ fixes the finite index sets. There is no division or exponentiation left in \eqref{smc:ck:eq:polynomial}. There are no undeclared variables, auxiliary predicates or variable-length conjunctions for a fixed $M,T$.

Over integers a sum of squares vanishes exactly when each residual vanishes. Lemma~\ref{smc:ck:lem:power} gives \eqref{smc:ck:eq:powers}, and \eqref{smc:ck:eq:G1}--\eqref{smc:ck:eq:G3} then give the unique encoded input. Remark~\ref{smc:ck:lem:trace} gives the bounded halting trace. This proves soundness of Theorem~\ref{smc:ck:thm:native}. For completeness take an encoded computation halting by $T$, use its shifted counters and power outputs, choose the two constructive POWER witnesses and the unique padded trace, and substitute. Every residual vanishes.

\begin{table}[htbp]\centering\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.25}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrr@{}}\toprule
Component & Positive witnesses & Residual slots\\\midrule
Initial shifted counters $A,B$ & 2 & 0\\
A module including $P$ & 26 & 15\\
B module including $Q$ & 26 & 15\\
Native gap constraints & 0 & 2\\
Bounded trace & $T(E+2)$ & $T(E+Z+4)+1$\\\midrule
Total & $T(E+2)+54$ & $T(E+Z+4)+33$\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{The exact construction ledger. $P,Q$ are already counted inside their respective modules.}\label{smc:ck:tab:arithledger}
\end{table}
Equivalently one may count $A,B,P,Q$ as four and the two modules' remaining 25 leaves as fifty. Counting four plus twice 26 would count the two outputs twice. Including the three native inputs, there are $T(E+2)+57$ total variables. In instruction counts, witnesses and residual slots are respectively
\[
T(I+2J+3)+54,\qquad T(I+3J+5)+33.
\]
The exact-halt version adds $H_{\rm early}^2$ at $T\geq1$, increasing only the residual count by one.

\subsection{Degree exactly twelve}
The two gap residuals have degree two and trace residuals have degree at most two. In either POWER module residuals 1--3 have degree at most four; residual 6 has degree three; residuals 4--5, 7--8 and 15 have degree at most two; residuals 9--12 and 14 have degree at most one. Residual 13 has degree six, with highest homogeneous part
\[
-w_i^4\eta_i^2.
\]
No other residual has degree six. Consequently the complete degree-12 homogeneous part of $F_{M,T}$ is exactly
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ck:eq:leading}
w_A^8\eta_A^4+w_B^8\eta_B^4.
\end{equation}
The two distinct monomials have coefficient one and cannot cancel. Degree is joint in all independent positive leaves and native inputs, before imposing any equations on those leaves. It remains exactly 12 at $T=0$ and in the exact-halt version.

\subsection{Unique decoding does not mean unique full witnesses}
For fixed gaps, \eqref{smc:ck:eq:decoder} and the uniqueness of powers of two fix $A,B,P,Q$. Remark~\ref{smc:ck:lem:trace} then fixes the trace leaves. Nevertheless a nonempty full fiber is infinite. Given any full witness and any $n\in\NN$, increase both $\alpha_{1,A}$ and $\alpha_{2,A}$ by $n$. These aliases appear only in residual 5 of the A module, where their equal increments cancel. All positive adapters remain positive and no other residual changes. Distinct $n$ give distinct witnesses. This specific polynomial is neither single-fold nor finite-fold. That loss of uniqueness is an exact property of the paid decoding construction.

\subsection{Transport to the exactly clocked machine}
For encoded native inputs the physical and arithmetic initial states agree. If the first halt is after $k\leq T$ source instructions, Theorem~\ref{smc:ck:thm:clock} gives first physical halt at
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ck:eq:haltclock}
30kD=30k(g_1+g_2+g_3),
\end{equation}
with at most $54k$ contacts before that section. For exact $T$, the time is precisely $30T(g_1+g_2+g_3)$. The by-horizon formula asserts some such $k\leq T$, not necessarily arrival at time $30TD$. Virtual arithmetic padding does not force physical instructions at $H$. At $T=0$, $q_0=H$ is necessary and sufficient after successful decoding, and the physical first-halt time is zero.

\section{Primitive integer initialization and its exact cost}\label{smc:ck:sec:primitive}
Every nonnegative counter pair admits native positive integer gaps. The scale needed by this particular encoding can be found exactly, including its exceptional small cases and the factor of five.

\begin{theorem}[Exact primitive initialization]\label{smc:ck:thm:primitive}
Let $a,b\geq0$, $m=\max(a,b)$, and define
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ck:eq:UVW}
U=2^m+2^{m-a+1},\quad
W=2^m+2^{m-b+1},\quad
V=20\cdot2^m-U-W.
\end{equation}
These are positive integers. Their greatest common divisor $c=\gcd(U,V,W)$ is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ck:eq:gcd}
c=\begin{cases}
1,&(a,b)=(0,0),\\
4,&(a,b)=(1,1),\\
2,&\{a,b\}=\{0,1\},\\
10,&m\geq2\text{ and }a\equiv b\equiv3\pmod4,\\
2,&m\geq2\text{ otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
The primitive triple and exact minimum positive integer total scale are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ck:eq:primitive}
g^*=\left(\frac Uc,\frac Vc,\frac Wc\right),\qquad
D_{\min}=\frac{20\cdot2^m}{c}.
\end{equation}
Every positive integer gap triple encoding the same $(a,b)$ is a unique positive integer multiple of $g^*$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Division by $20\cdot2^m$ gives exactly \eqref{smc:ck:eq:nativeencoding}. Since $U,W\leq3\cdot2^m$, $V\geq14\cdot2^m>0$.

At $m=0$, $(U,V,W)=(3,14,3)$, so $c=1$. At $m=1$, the equal case gives $(4,32,4)$ and the mixed cases give $(6,30,4)$ or its reflection; their gcds are 4 and 2.

For $m\geq2$, at least one of $a,b$ equals $m$. Its endpoint gap is $2^m+2$, with exact 2-adic valuation one. Both endpoint gaps and $V$ are even, so $c$ has exact 2-adic valuation one. Also $c$ divides $U+V+W=20\cdot2^m$. Thus the only possible odd prime factor is 5, with exponent at most one. Since
\[
U=2^{m-a}(2^a+2),
\]
we have $5\mid U$ exactly when $2^a\equiv-2\pmod5$, namely $a\equiv3\pmod4$ by the order four of 2 modulo 5. The same criterion holds for $W$. When both endpoint gaps are divisible by 5, so is $V$ because their sum is divisible by 5. This proves \eqref{smc:ck:eq:gcd}.

Normalization makes $g^*$ primitive. Every other integer realization has the same normalized coordinates and therefore equals $\lambda g^*$ for a positive rational $\lambda$. Since $\gcd(g^*)=1$, integer B\'ezout coefficients combine the entries of $g^*$ to 1. Applying the same combination to the integer entries of $\lambda g^*$ gives $\lambda\in\Z$. It is positive and unique. Thus \eqref{smc:ck:eq:primitive} has the smallest possible positive integer total scale for this chosen encoding.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Bit height and binary counter input}
For a positive integer $n$ write $\bit(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$. Equations~\eqref{smc:ck:eq:gcd}--\eqref{smc:ck:eq:primitive} give the exact formula
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ck:eq:bitscale}
\bit(D_{\min})=\begin{cases}
5,&(a,b)=(0,0),\\
4,&(a,b)=(1,1),\\
5,&\{a,b\}=\{0,1\},\\
m+2,&m\geq2\text{ and }a\equiv b\equiv3\pmod4,\\
m+4,&m\geq2\text{ otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
For $m\geq2$, $D_{\min}$ equals either $2^{m+1}$ or $10\cdot2^m$, proving the last two cases and the bounds
\[
2^{m+1}\leq D_{\min}\leq10\cdot2^m.
\]
The middle gap is always largest: $g_2^*\geq7D_{\min}/10$, whereas $g_1^*,g_3^*\leq3D_{\min}/20$. Since $D_{\min}/2<g_2^*<D_{\min}$,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:ck:eq:bitgap}
\bit(D_{\min})-1\leq \max_j\bit(g_j^*)\leq\bit(D_{\min}).
\end{equation}
Therefore the primitive description has bit height $m+O(1)$ and numeric height $\Theta(2^m)$. If $m\geq1$ itself has binary length $\ell=\lfloor\log_2m\rfloor+1$, then $2^{\ell-1}\leq m<2^\ell$. Its gap bit height is $\Theta(2^\ell)$ as a function of the largest counter's binary input length. In particular it is $\Theta(m)$, not $\Theta(\log m)$.

The exact primitive initialization is a theorem about this powers-of-two coordinate representation. It is not a universal lower bound for all simulations, encodings, counter algorithms or Diophantine witnesses. No height bound for the potentially much larger Pell auxiliaries is proved here.

Conversely the positive integer denominators in \eqref{smc:ck:eq:decoder} imply $P,Q\leq2D$, and hence
\[
a,b\leq\lfloor\log_2(2D)\rfloor.
\]
One can decode an accepted input by polynomial-time integer arithmetic in the binary length of its three gaps: form $D$, test the denominator signs, divide exactly, and check the binary power-of-two condition. This does not make producing the exponentially longer gap description polynomial-time in the binary counter input length, and it does not decide unbounded halting.

\section{Prior work and limits of interpretation}\label{smc:ck:sec:prior}
Durand-Lose's MCU 2004/2005 construction already uses two fixed scale signals, two counter-position signals and one instruction signal with cardinality-preserving rules \cite{dl2004mcu}. It is substantive prior art for five-live-signal counter computation. Report~64 [source~34] supplied the particular fixed ordered full-section interface used here, with explicit guard coverage and nondestructive branching. Report 65 does not newly establish five-signal universality.

Bouncing signals are also an established delay mechanism. Durand-Lose and Emmanuel explicitly choose speeds for a border-and-back motion to obtain a delay proportional to width \cite{dle2021agc11}. The present clock contribution is the six-template exact output-linear compensation at this five-live-signal interface, including its inherited $+1$ entry, complete contact accounting and literal restoration. It is not a claim to invent waiting by bouncing. Reversing speeds and collision rules is standard in the reversible signal-machine literature \cite{DL06}; no global reversibility theorem for the completed compiler is asserted.

Finite counter traces and sum-of-squares conjunctions are elementary encodings. Dudenhefner provides a precise modern treatment of the relevant counter instruction model and emphasizes that computational claims depend on the instruction set \cite{dudenhefner2022}. Our source language and edge semantics have therefore been stated explicitly. The substantive number-theoretic dependency is the pinned constructive Pell pair \cite{mathlibpell}. Its license and attribution travel with the copied source. \wtag\ [Not in this report: the Lean source and its licence are not shipped~\cite{mathlibpell}.]

The literature check was targeted to these mechanisms and dependencies, not exhaustive. No firstness, priority or absence-of-equivalent-prior-construction claim is made. Nor are $30$, $54$, $39$, degree 12, witness count or residual count asserted to be optimal. The exact counts describe this construction. Robustness, finite precision, minimality and efficient Pell witnesses are not established.

\section{Questions opened by the construction}\label{smc:ck:sec:future}
The following are research questions, not established conclusions.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Smaller exact clocks.} What is the smallest sufficient $C$ for the six core branches if one varies the physically valid padding words? The present output-linear lemma deliberately pays a $2D$ entry loop and two transfers; removing a cost requires a new contact-level interface proof, not only a rearranged linear identity.
\item \textbf{Fewer speeds or contacts.} Can different rational loop combinations reduce the common speed set or the worst-case contacts without changing the five-live-signal population or fixed section? Tradeoffs between clock size, speed magnitudes and word length remain open here.
\item \textbf{More general elapsed-time functions.} Which functions of the output section admit finite identity padding with fixed rational speeds and no extra live signal? The present lemma covers homogeneous linear functions. It does not handle arbitrary nonlinear costs or input-dependent speed assignment.
\item \textbf{Alternative native arithmetic interfaces.} Can the exact 54-witness decoding overhead or degree 12 be reduced with a different explicit POWER representation? A fair comparison must count positive adapters, index shifts, outputs and sign conventions consistently, and must pay for initialization internally. \wtag\ (Added 4 October 2026: answered in part by source~37 in Part~XIII. Its Theorem~\ref{smc:pp:thm:modules} gives base-two POWER presentations with 22, 16, 14, 13 and 12 leaves including the output, the 22- and 16-leaf ones at degree~12, and its Theorem~\ref{smc:pp:thm:maincomposition} composes two of them with paid gap decoding and source~36's three-witness compiler in place of the trace, into $2\ell+5$ positive witnesses at every horizon, at a degree that grows with~$T$ (source~35's degree is 12 at every horizon). None of those presentations has degree below~12, so the degree half stays open.)
\item \textbf{Control of witness multiplicity.} Can the positive congruence-quotient redundancy be removed constructively while maintaining soundness and completeness? The current common-shift freedom proves infinite fibers. It gives no finite-fold claim for another formula. \wtag\ (Added 4 October 2026: the redundancy itself is removed by source~37 in Part~XIII: its 22-leaf normalization drops the paired congruence quotients with soundness and completeness kept (Section~\ref{smc:pp:sec:positive22}), and its Section~\ref{smc:pp:sec:infinite} proves that every accepted fibre nevertheless stays infinite, by genuine parameter variation. No finite-fold representation results, and the compositions of Part~XIII also have infinite full fibres.)
\item \textbf{Height bounds.} What explicit bounds can be given for the Pell witnesses as a function of the native input gaps and fixed horizon? Primitive gap height is settled here for this encoding; auxiliary certificate height is a separate issue.
\item \textbf{An independent formalization.} A future machine-checked proof could formalize the clock's local rules, the all-section chronology, the exact native formula and their composition. Reading a pinned formal theorem and evaluating finite static certificates are not substitutes for such a new formalization. \wtag\ (Open. The repository has no Lean or Rocq development of these constructions.)
\end{enumerate}

\section{Conclusion}
A fixed ordered-section counter compiler can be clocked exactly with its existing five live signals. The explicit six words give $30D$ per instruction, at most 54 contacts and a common sufficient set of 39 rational speeds. The native arithmetic continuation removes free exponential initialization by enforcing unique powers-of-two decoding inside two explicit POWER modules, then attaches a complete bounded trace. This yields exactly $T(E+2)+54$ positive witnesses, $T(E+Z+4)+33$ residual slots and joint degree 12. The combination identifies first physical halt after $k$ instructions with exact time $30kD$. Its scope remains encoded inputs and a growing-arity bounded-horizon family, with unique decoded traces but infinite full witness fibers. Exact primitive initialization quantifies the representation cost rather than hiding it.

\begin{remark}[\wtag\ The positive $A$-test bound is attained]\label{smc:xii:rem:atest}
Section~\ref{smc:br:sec:compiler} of source~34 states that on the positive branch ``$D/20<x\le D/10$ gives $25D/18<T<25D/9$''. The upper inequality is not strict. Take $a=1$ and any~$b$. \[
T_{\mathrm{test},\mathsf N}=\frac{250x}{9}=\frac{25D}{9}.

Since $x=D/20+(D/10)2^{-a}$ decreases strictly in~$a$, the correct statement is $25D/18<T_{\mathrm{test},\mathsf N}\le25D/9$ on the positive branch, with equality exactly at $a=1$. By reflection the same holds for the $B$ test, with equality at $b=1$. Nothing downstream changes. Since $25D/9<4D$, the bounds $D<T_{A\text{-test}}<4D$ and $3D<T_{B\text{-test with transfers}}<6D$ and Equation~\eqref{smc:br:eq:instructiontime} hold as printed. \end{remark}

\phantomsection\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Source 36: Bounded halting certificates and exact encoded gap counts}
\noindent{\large\bfseries Source 36 (batch-91 manuscript 18): Bounded halting certificates and exact encoded gap counts}\par
\noindent\emph{Two arithmetic continuations of native integer initialization}, ``Research Report 66'', 4 October 2026. \wtag\ From the archive \path{Bounded_certificates_and_encoded_gap_counts_source.zip}, main file \path{Report66/Report66.tex} (770 lines; a 21-page PDF); its labels carry the prefix \texttt{smc:bc:}, its sections are Sections~\ref{smc:bc:sec:overview}--\ref{smc:bc:sec:future} here, and its equations are numbered by section. Its six bibliography entries are this report's \cite{bccompression}, \cite{bccounting}, \cite{bcnative}, \cite{mathlibpell}, \cite{bccountaudit} and~\cite{bcboundaudit}. Its table of contents and page breaks are omitted. Its abstract follows.
\begin{quote}\small
A finite counter horizon admits a finite classification even when the initial counters are unbounded. We prove that clipping each native counter at $T$ preserves every control decision through $T$ transitions. Integer interpolation of the resulting $(T+1)^2$ classes yields an explicit sum of six squares with exactly three positive witnesses, uniquely determined whenever a witness exists. For $T\geq1$ its joint degree is at most $4(T+1)^2-4$ and its expanded support has at most $16(T+1)^2-5$ monomials. The finite acceptance table, coefficients and storage costs are paid explicitly. Two fully displayed POWER modules compose this certificate with three native integer gaps, giving 57 positive witnesses and 38 residual slots; the full composed fibers are infinite.

Independently of any program or halting predicate, we count all encoded positive integer gap triples by their total. Exact floor and digit formulas give slope $743/1125$, while distinct represented totals have density $3/20$. We prove a shell formula, an exact residue-class error law on a power-of-two subsequence, sharp normalized logarithm-squared error envelopes, and the inverse law with multiplicity, of slope $1125/743$. These are separately compiled bounded-horizon polynomial families and arithmetic counts of all encoded initializations. No fixed-polynomial unbounded-halting result, halting-input density, optimality or priority claim follows.
\end{quote}

\section{The two questions and the main conclusions}\label{smc:bc:sec:overview}
The first question is how many existential variables a \emph{fixed-horizon} counter certificate needs when its coefficients may depend effectively on the horizon. The answer below is three for a displayed construction. This is a trade between witness count and the finite table, degree and coefficients. The second question is how many positive integer triples realize the native gap encoding up to a given total. That count concerns geometry and divisibility alone; no counter program is run or selected by it.

The two parts share the encoding
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:encoding}
\frac{g_1}{D}=\frac1{20}+\frac1{10}2^{-a},\qquad
\frac{g_3}{D}=\frac1{20}+\frac1{10}2^{-b},\qquad
D=g_1+g_2+g_3,
\end{equation}
where $g_1,g_2,g_3>0$ are integers and $a,b\in\NN=\{0,1,\ldots\}$. Its ordered counter pair is unique because $a\mapsto2^{-a}$ is injective. We distinguish the interpolation size $Q=(T+1)^2$, an individual gap total $D$, and the counting height $X$ throughout.

\begin{theorem}[Three positive witnesses]\label{smc:bc:thm:main}
Fix a finite deterministic two-counter program $M$, its initial state $q_0$ and its halt state $H$. For every fixed integer $T\geq0$, the construction in Sections~\ref{smc:bc:sec:clip}--\ref{smc:bc:sec:cost} gives an integer polynomial
\[
P_{M,T}(A,B;j,r,s)
\]
with positive inputs $A,B$ and exactly three positive witnesses $j,r,s$, such that a witness exists if and only if $M$ reaches $H$ within $T$ transitions from counters $(A-1,B-1)$. The witness is unique. The polynomial is a sum of six specified residual squares, has degree at most $4Q-4$ and support at most $16Q-5$ for $T\geq1$, and has degree two at $T=0$. First halt exactly at $T$ has the same counts and bounds.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Paid native gap composition]\label{smc:bc:thm:gapmain}
The construction in Section~\ref{smc:bc:sec:gaps} gives one integer polynomial in three external positive gaps and 57 positive witnesses. It is a sum of 38 residual squares. Its zeros assert that the gaps are encoded and that their decoded counters satisfy the chosen bounded-halting predicate. Its joint degree is $\max(12,\deg P_{M,T})$. The decoded counters and the three compressed witnesses are unique, but every nonempty complete witness fiber is infinite. The all-exponent POWER equivalence uses the explicitly pinned constructive Pell theorem pair.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[All encoded initializations]\label{smc:bc:thm:countmain}
Let $\mathcal A(X)$ be the number of encoded positive integer triples with total at most $X$, and set $\rho=743/1125$. Then
\[
\mathcal A(X)=\rho X-E(X),\qquad E(X)\geq0,
\]
with exact floor and digit formulas below. For integer $X\to\infty$,
\[
\liminf\frac{E(X)}{(\log_2X)^2}=0,\qquad
\limsup\frac{E(X)}{(\log_2X)^2}=1.
\]
The represented totals are exactly the multiples of 10 or 16. If $D_n$ is the total of the $n$th triple, \emph{counting multiplicity}, then
\[
D_n=\frac{1125}{743}n+O(\log^2 n),
\]
and the normalized nonnegative inverse deviations have liminf zero and limsup $1125/743$.
\end{theorem}

The three-witness theorem is independent of the physical compiler and of Pell theory. The counting theorem needs only the elementary primitive-scale classification proved in Section~\ref{smc:bc:sec:primitive}. Physical transport is conditional on the retained encoded-input compiler theorem. None of these statements classifies arbitrary unencoded physical executions.

The primitive-scale classification is source~35's Theorem~\ref{smc:ck:thm:primitive}, with the same proof; it is quoted as a note in Section~\ref{smc:bc:sec:primitive}. Theorem~\ref{smc:bc:thm:main}'s degree bound is sharpened to exact values by source~37 (Theorem~\ref{smc:pp:thm:maincomposition}), its three witnesses are reduced to two and one by source~38 (Propositions~\ref{smc:la:prop:tensor} and~\ref{smc:la:prop:one}), and Theorem~\ref{smc:bc:thm:gapmain}'s 57 witnesses become 29 (source~37) and 28 or~27 (source~38). Source~36's own statements are unchanged by these later improvements.]

\section{Exact finite horizon clipping}\label{smc:bc:sec:clip}
A native instruction either increments one counter and moves to a specified successor, or tests one counter for zero, moving to one successor at zero and otherwise decrementing that counter and moving to another successor. The other counter is unchanged. The control graph is finite and may contain loops. We count transitions, so the initial state occurs at time zero. For bookkeeping only, extend the computation after $H$ by leaving both counters and the state unchanged.

\begin{lemma}[Exact clipping]\label{smc:bc:lem:clip}
For a fixed $T\geq0$, replace an initial pair $(a,b)$ by
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:nativeclip}
(a^*,b^*)=(\min(a,T),\min(b,T)).
\end{equation}
The original and clipped runs have identical states $q_0,\ldots,q_T$ and choose identical branches at entry times $0,\ldots,T-1$. In particular their first arrival at $H$, when it is at most $T$, agrees.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The initial states agree. Suppose the branches through the first $t$ transitions agree, where $t<T$. Each corresponding counter has then received the same changes. If its original initial value was below $T$, the two values are identical. Otherwise its representative started at $T$ and can have decreased by at most $t$, so its current value is at least $T-t>0$. The original equals it plus the nonnegative initial difference and is also positive. Every tested counter therefore has the same zero/nonzero outcome in both runs. The next branch and changes agree. Increment instructions and virtual halt steps also agree. Induction proves the claim through transition $T$; the control states determine first arrival at $H$.
\end{proof}

The strict inequality is needed at instruction \emph{entry}, not after the last transition. A representative counter can reach zero at time $T$ while the original is still positive. Their final counters, final zero status and behavior beyond the horizon need not agree. At $T=0$ there are no branches to compare, and the only halting question is whether $q_0=H$.

The threshold is sharp for this uniform clipping argument when $T\geq1$. Consider the one-instruction loop that moves to $H$ if $a=0$ and otherwise decrements $a$ and repeats. Initial $a=T-1$ first halts on transition $T$, whereas initial $a=T$ first halts on transition $T+1$. Clipping at $T-1$ would merge different answers. This establishes no lower bound on polynomial degree or witness arity.

\wtag\ [Sources~37 and~38 restate this lemma with the same proof, source~37 also with the same sharpness example; their statements are quoted in Remarks~\ref{smc:pp:lem:clipping} and~\ref{smc:la:lem:clip}. The Hilbert's-tenth programme's review checked this proof: ``through transition $T$, a counter initially at least $T$ and its clipped representative make the same zero tests, since tests occur before the final decrement''~\cite{reviewarith91}.]

With shifted positive inputs, put
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:shiftclip}
A=a+1,\quad B=b+1,\quad K=T+1,\quad Q=K^2,\qquad
u=\min(A,K),\quad v=\min(B,K).
\end{equation}
Thus the exact shifted threshold is $T+1$, rather than the more conservative $T+2$.

\section{A finite table and integer interpolation}\label{smc:bc:sec:interp}
Index the $Q$ representative pairs by
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:nodes}
i=(u-1)K+v,\qquad
u_i=1+\left\lfloor\frac{i-1}{K}\right\rfloor,\qquad
v_i=1+((i-1)\bmod K),\qquad 1\leq i\leq Q.
\end{equation}
In this formula the symbol $u_i$ denotes the first coordinate; we use $u$ for its selected value below. Let $S_{M,T}$ contain the indices whose representative inputs $(u_i-1,v_i-1)$ first reach $H$ at some time at most $T$. For the exact-halt variant use $S^{=}_{M,T}$, containing precisely those with first arrival at time $T$.

Both sets are effectively computable finite tables. In principle, each of the $Q$ representatives is evaluated for at most $T$ transitions, checking $q_0$ first. At most $QT$ native transitions suffice, and representative counters remain at most $2T$. These evaluations are a cost of constructing coefficients, not a free oracle. No native interpreter is executed in this report. If $q_0=H$, the by-horizon table is full for every $T$, and the exact-horizon table is empty for $T>0$.

Fix either table and call it $S$. Let $d=(Q-1)!$, with $0!=1$. Define integer polynomials
\begin{align}
\ell_i(z)&=(-1)^{Q-i}\binom{Q-1}{i-1}
 \prod_{\substack{1\leq h\leq Q\\h\ne i}}(z-h),\label{smc:bc:eq:basis}\\
U_0(z)&=\sum_{i=1}^{Q}u_i\ell_i(z),&
V_0(z)&=\sum_{i=1}^{Q}v_i\ell_i(z),\label{smc:bc:eq:uv}\\
R(z)&=\prod_{i=1}^{Q}(z-i),&
H_S(z)&=\prod_{i\in S}(z-i).\label{smc:bc:eq:rootpolys}
\end{align}
An empty product is one. At the $i$th node,
\[
\prod_{h\ne i}(i-h)=(-1)^{Q-i}(i-1)!(Q-i)!,
\]
so $\ell_i(i)=d$ and $\ell_i(h)=0$ at all other nodes. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:interpolation}
U_0(i)=d u_i,\qquad V_0(i)=d v_i,\qquad 1\leq i\leq Q.
\end{equation}
This directly proves the interpolation identities. Every coefficient is an integer; the only denominator clearing is by the fixed integer $d$, which depends on the horizon and not on any input or witness. The degrees of $U_0,V_0$ are at most $Q-1$. The roots of $H_S$ are exactly the accepted codes, with no roots when $S$ is empty.

\section{Six residuals and a unique witness triple}\label{smc:bc:sec:certificate}
Use exactly three positive integer witnesses $j,r,s$. Define
\begin{align}
R_0&=R(j),\nonumber\\
R_A&=(dA-U_0(j))(U_0(j)-dK),&
L_A&=dA-U_0(j)-d(r-1),\nonumber\\
R_B&=(dB-V_0(j))(V_0(j)-dK),&
L_B&=dB-V_0(j)-d(s-1),\nonumber\\
R_H&=H_S(j),\label{smc:bc:eq:sixresiduals}
\end{align}
and set
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:P}
P_{M,T}=R_0^2+R_A^2+L_A^2+R_B^2+L_B^2+R_H^2.
\end{equation}
These finite formulas completely specify the polynomial. Program and horizon data determine coefficients; they are not additional polynomial variables. Six is a literal presentation count. Some slots can coincide or be identically zero.

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{smc:bc:thm:main} apart from its size bounds]
An integer sum of squares vanishes exactly when each square vanishes. If $P_{M,T}=0$, then $R(j)=0$ forces $j\in\{1,\ldots,Q\}$. Write $u=u_j$ and $v=v_j$. Using \eqref{smc:bc:eq:interpolation} and dividing only by the fixed positive $d$, the two $A$ residuals imply
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:clipequations}
(A-u)(u-K)=0,\qquad A-u=r-1\geq0.
\end{equation}
If $u<K$, the first equation forces $A=u$. If $u=K$, the second forces $A\geq K$. These are exactly the cases $u=\min(A,K)$. The same argument proves $v=\min(B,K)$. Therefore $j$ is the unique clipped class. The equation $H_S(j)=0$ puts that class in the chosen acceptance table, and Lemma~\ref{smc:bc:lem:clip} gives the asserted halting predicate.

Conversely, if that predicate holds, take
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:uniquewitness}
u=\min(A,K),\quad v=\min(B,K),\quad
j=(u-1)K+v,\quad r=A-u+1,\quad s=B-v+1.
\end{equation}
All three witnesses are positive. The range and acceptance residuals vanish. Each classification product vanishes because its coordinate either equals its input or equals $K$. The two slack residuals vanish by definition. Thus $P_{M,T}=0$.

Finally the soundness argument forces $u,v$ and then $j$. Each linear residual forces its slack. This proves uniqueness, including the bounds
\[
1\leq j\leq Q,\qquad 1\leq r\leq A,\qquad 1\leq s\leq B.
\]
No trace values, sign choices, inactive selectors or interpolation denominators remain as free witnesses.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Horizon zero}
When $T=0$, we have $K=Q=d=1$ and $U_0=V_0=1$. Both classification products vanish identically, while $L_A=A-r$ and $L_B=B-s$. If $q_0=H$ then
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:zeroaccept}
P_{M,0}=2(j-1)^2+(A-r)^2+(B-s)^2.
\end{equation}
Otherwise
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:zeroreject}
P_{M,0}=(j-1)^2+(A-r)^2+(B-s)^2+1.
\end{equation}
The accepted case has the unique tuple $(1,A,B)$ and the rejected case has none. Both displayed polynomials have degree two and nine nonzero monomials. The fixed count of three witnesses at this trivial horizon is a presentation convention, not a necessity claim. The by-horizon and exact-horizon questions coincide here.

\section{Degree coefficient support and preprocessing costs}\label{smc:bc:sec:cost}
All degree statements are joint in the five variables $A,B,j,r,s$. For $T\geq1$, $Q\geq4$. The degrees of $R_0,R_H$ are at most $Q$, those of $L_A,L_B$ at most $Q-1$, and those of $R_A,R_B$ at most $2Q-2$. Squaring gives
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:degree}
\deg P_{M,T}\leq\max(2Q,4Q-4,2Q-2)=4Q-4.
\end{equation}
Cancellations can lower this bound; equality is not asserted or enforced artificially.

\subsection{Coefficient height}
For an integer polynomial $f$, let $\lonenorm f$ be the sum of the absolute values of its coefficients. Set
\[
\Lambda=K\,2^{Q-1}(Q+1)!.
\]
The norm of a product of factors $z-h$ is at most the product of $1+h$. From \eqref{smc:bc:eq:basis}, the binomial sum $2^{Q-1}$, and $u_i,v_i\leq K$, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:norms}
\lonenorm{U_0},\lonenorm{V_0}\leq\Lambda,\quad
\lonenorm R,\lonenorm{H_S}\leq(Q+1)!\leq\Lambda,\quad dK,d\leq\Lambda.
\end{equation}
Coefficient norms are subadditive and submultiplicative. Each classification residual has norm at most $4\Lambda^2$; each linear slack residual has norm at most $4\Lambda$. Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:normP}
\lonenorm{P_{M,T}}\leq2\Lambda^2+2(4\Lambda^2)^2+2(4\Lambda)^2
=32\Lambda^4+34\Lambda^2\leq66\Lambda^4.
\end{equation}
This also holds at $T=0$. A nonzero coefficient therefore needs at most
$7+4\lceil\log_2\Lambda\rceil$ unsigned magnitude bits, plus a sign bit if required. The resulting bound is
\[
O(Q\log(Q+1))=O(T^2\log(T+2))
\]
for positive horizons. It is uniform in the program because the program changes only a subset of the same finite node set.

\subsection{Sparse expanded support}
A dense five-variable monomial bound would conceal the special structure. Put $m=Q-1$. The first classification residual has the form
\[
R_A=A f_A(j)+g_A(j),\qquad
f_A=d(U_0-dK),\quad g_A=-U_0(U_0-dK),
\]
with degrees at most $m$ and $2m$. Its square has a pure-$j$ part of degree at most $4m$, an $A$ part of $j$-degree at most $3m$, and an $A^2$ part of $j$-degree at most $2m$. The $B$ classification has the same structure. Moreover
\[
L_A=dA-dr+(d-U_0(j)),
\]
so its square adds only pure-$j$, $A$, and $r$ terms and the monomials $A^2,r^2,Ar$; the coefficient of $r$ has $j$-degree at most $m$. The $B,s$ counterpart is identical. The remaining two squares are pure-$j$ and have degree at most $2Q\leq4m$.

Grouping disjoint monomial types gives the explicit ceiling in Table~\ref{smc:bc:tab:support}.
\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{@{}lr@{}}\toprule
Monomial type & Maximum number\\\midrule
Pure powers of $j$ & $4m+1$\\
$A^2$ or $B^2$ times powers of $j$ & $2(2m+1)$\\
$A$ or $B$ times powers of $j$ & $2(3m+1)$\\
$r$ or $s$ times powers of $j$ & $2(m+1)$\\
$r^2,s^2,Ar,Bs$ & $4$\\\midrule
Total & $16m+11=16Q-5$\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{An expanded-support bound for $T\geq1$. Shared terms are grouped before counting, and cancellations can only decrease the support.}\label{smc:bc:tab:support}
\end{table}
No monomial contains both $A$ and $B$, both $r$ and $s$, or any undeclared combination of these four variables. Storing each nonzero coefficient in signed binary and its five exponents in binary costs at most
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:storage}
O(Q^2\log(Q+1))=O((T+1)^4\log(T+2))
\end{equation}
bits. This is an upper bound for that expanded storage convention, not an optimality result.

\subsection{What the effective generator pays}
For the selected predicate the acceptance table consists of exactly $Q$ Boolean values. In principle constructing it takes at most $QT$ native transitions. The table is independent of the eventual large inputs $A,B$, but determining it is substantive finite work.

A direct coefficient generator can build each of the $Q$ basis products by repeated multiplication by a linear factor, requiring $O(Q^2)$ integer arithmetic operations per product and $O(Q^3)$ overall. Adding, scaling and ordinary convolution to expand the six squares fit within $O(Q^3)$ further integer arithmetic operations. Product and triangle bounds as above keep intermediate magnitudes within $O(Q\log(Q+1))$ bits. This is an arithmetic-operation bound, not a unit-cost bit-complexity claim.

There is one uniform effective procedure which takes the finite program and horizon and produces the appropriate polynomial. Nevertheless, each $T$ selects a separately compiled polynomial with its own degree and coefficients. When $T$ is written in binary, these costs need not be polynomial in its input length. The theorem supplies no faster method for deciding one bounded instance than its ordinary simulation, and no free access to its acceptance table.

\subsection{Why an unbounded horizon does not give one polynomial}
For a fixed program, halting is of course equivalent to acceptance at some finite horizon. But the expression $P_{M,T}$ changes its table, factorial, products, degrees and coefficients with $T$. Placing an existential phrase ``there is a $T$'' outside this family does not express those changes inside a single fixed polynomial. This construction contains no fixed arithmetic module encoding the map from $T$ to its coefficient table. Its unique bounded witness triples therefore imply no single-fold or finite-fold fixed-polynomial representation of unbounded halting. Using first-halt tables changes that conclusion in no way.
\section{Composition with paid native gap decoding}\label{smc:bc:sec:gaps}
The external inputs are arbitrary positive integers $g_1,g_2,g_3$, and $D=g_1+g_2+g_3$ remains an expression, not a new variable. The predicate now includes both encoding \eqref{smc:bc:eq:encoding} and bounded halting of the decoded counters. Introduce positive shifted-counter witnesses $A,B$ and positive power outputs $p,q$. Two independent copies of the following module enforce
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:powers}
p=2^{A-1},\qquad q=2^{B-1}.
\end{equation}
The construction replaces the growing trace in the retained native-gap certificate by the compressed polynomial \eqref{smc:bc:eq:P}; it leaves the original source packet unchanged.

\subsection{All leaves and all residuals of one POWER module}
For a positive input index $C$ and output $o$, one copy has thirteen directly positive leaves
\[
o,w,M_0,g,x_p,y_p,u_p,v_p,s_p,t_p,q_b,q_v,J_p.
\]
Two more positive leaves $\alpha_+,\beta_+$ define expressions
$\alpha=\alpha_++1$ and $\beta=\beta_++1$. Eleven natural aliases
\[
d_{wb},d_{wk},d_{yk},\alpha_1,\alpha_2,
\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\tau_1,\tau_2,\rho_1,\rho_2
\]
are each represented by their own distinct positive leaf minus one. These are substitutions, not new equations or extra uncounted variables. Thus a copy contains $13+2+11=26$ positive leaves including $o$, or 25 auxiliaries beyond its output. The already counted $C$ is not a module leaf. $M_0$ is unrelated to the source program $M$, and the module leaf $g$ is unrelated to the three external gaps.

After all these substitutions, the fifteen residual polynomials are
\begin{align}
E_1&=x_p^2-1-(\alpha^2-1)y_p^2,\nonumber\\
E_2&=u_p^2-1-(\alpha^2-1)v_p^2,\nonumber\\
E_3&=s_p^2-1-(\beta^2-1)t_p^2,\nonumber\\
E_4&=\beta-1-4y_pq_b,\nonumber\\
E_5&=\beta+u_p\alpha_1-\alpha-u_p\alpha_2,\nonumber\\
E_6&=v_p-y_p^2q_v,\nonumber\\
E_7&=s_p+u_p\sigma_1-x_p-u_p\sigma_2,\nonumber\\
E_8&=t_p+4y_p\tau_1-C-4y_p\tau_2,\nonumber\\
E_9&=y_p-C-d_{yk},\nonumber\\
E_{10}&=w-2-d_{wb},\nonumber\\
E_{11}&=w-C-d_{wk},\nonumber\\
E_{12}&=M_0-2o-J_p,\nonumber\\
E_{13}&=\alpha^2-1-\bigl((w+1)^2-1\bigr)(wg)^2,\nonumber\\
E_{14}&=4\alpha-M_0-5,\nonumber\\
E_{15}&=x_p+M_0\rho_1-y_p(\alpha-2)-2o-M_0\rho_2.\label{smc:bc:eq:powerresiduals}
\end{align}
Every leaf in one copy is distinct from every leaf in the other copy, the external gaps, $A,B$, and $j,r,s$.

\subsection{The precise imported theorem and positive adapters}
\begin{remark}[\wtag\ restatement of source~35's Lemma~\ref{smc:ck:lem:power}]\label{smc:xiii:rem:bcpower}
Source~36 states: ``The sole substantive number-theoretic dependency is the constructive theorem pair
\texttt{Pell.matiyasevic} and \texttt{Pell.eq\_pow\_of\_pell} in the pinned mathlib source~\cite{mathlibpell}. Their statements were read as inert text; no Lean execution is part of this report. The specialization yields
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:poweriff}
\bigl(\exists\text{ the 25 positive auxiliary leaves}:E_1=\cdots=E_{15}=0\bigr)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad o=2^{C-1},\quad C,o>0\text{.''}
\end{equation}
This module and this equivalence are source~35's (Section~\ref{smc:ck:sec:power} and Lemma~\ref{smc:ck:lem:power} of Part~XII), with the letters renamed from source~35 to source~36 as $\eta_i\mapsto g$, $M_i\mapsto M_0$, $(x_i,y_i,u_i,v_i,s_i,t_i)\mapsto(x_p,y_p,u_p,v_p,s_p,t_p)$, $J_i\mapsto J_p$, $(d_{w2,i},d_{wC,i},d_{yC,i})\mapsto(d_{wb},d_{wk},d_{yk})$, $(r_{1,i},r_{2,i})\mapsto(\rho_1,\rho_2)$ and $(C_i,o_i)\mapsto(C,o)$; the fifteen residuals~\eqref{smc:bc:eq:powerresiduals} are source~35's, in the same order. Source~36's proof of~\eqref{smc:bc:eq:poweriff} (soundness through the nonzero-index branch of \texttt{Pell.matiyasevic} and $\alpha>w\geq2$; completeness through the constructive power theorem with every positive adapter, including $C=1$; and the remark that natural subtraction adds no loophole) and its exponent-zero fixture ($C=o=1$, $w=2$, $M_0=63$, $g=3$, $\alpha=\beta=17$, $x_p=s_p=17$, $y_p=t_p=1$, $u_p=577$, $v_p=q_v=34$, $q_b=4$, $J_p=61$, $d_{wk}=1$ and every other natural alias zero) are source~35's proof and fixture, step for step, and are not printed twice. Source~36 adds one warning: ``The exponent is $C-1$, but the \emph{Pell index is $C$}; using index $C-1$ would mishandle the boundary.'' The same module is the 26-leaf predecessor of source~37 (Section~\ref{smc:pp:sec:positive22}) and the base-two case of the general-base POWER system of Report~58 [source~28, Part~X], itself a re-derivation of the fifteen-equation Pell macro \texttt{ptr:ai:lem:exp} of the collection's report \emph{periodic-turmite-first-revisits}. The module letters $\rho_1,\rho_2$ have nothing to do with the slope $\rho=743/1125$ of Section~\ref{smc:bc:sec:error}.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The full composed polynomial and its ledger}
Add the two gap residuals
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:gapresiduals}
G_1=(20g_1-D)p-2D,\qquad G_3=(20g_3-D)q-2D.
\end{equation}
Let $E_i^A$ and $E_i^B$ be the independent copies of \eqref{smc:bc:eq:powerresiduals} with $(C,o)=(A,p)$ and $(B,q)$. Define
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:fullF}
F_{M,T}=G_1^2+G_3^2+\sum_{i=1}^{15}(E_i^A)^2
 +\sum_{i=1}^{15}(E_i^B)^2+P_{M,T}(A,B;j,r,s).
\end{equation}
Equations \eqref{smc:bc:eq:sixresiduals}, \eqref{smc:bc:eq:powerresiduals} and \eqref{smc:bc:eq:gapresiduals} specify every residual in the final polynomial. No power relation remains uninterpreted.

\begin{proof}[Correctness]
A zero of $F_{M,T}$ makes every residual vanish. Equation~\eqref{smc:bc:eq:poweriff} forces \eqref{smc:bc:eq:powers}. Since $D,p,q>0$, the gap equations force positive denominators $20g_1-D$ and $20g_3-D$. Dividing by positive quantities gives exactly \eqref{smc:bc:eq:encoding}, with $a=A-1,b=B-1$. Theorem~\ref{smc:bc:thm:main} then gives the required bounded-halting predicate. Conversely, an encoded input satisfying that predicate supplies its unique $A,B,p,q$, constructive POWER auxiliaries and the triple \eqref{smc:bc:eq:uniquewitness}. Every residual vanishes.
\end{proof}

\centering
\begin{tabular}{@{}lr@{}}\toprule
Resource in the displayed native gap formula & Count\\\midrule
External positive inputs & $3$\\
Shifted-counter witnesses $A,B$ & $2$\\
Two POWER copies including outputs $p,q$ & $2\cdot26$\\
Compressed witnesses $j,r,s$ & $3$\\\midrule
All positive witnesses & $57$\\
All variables including the inputs & $60$\\
Residual slots & $2+30+6=38$\\
Final polynomial equations & $1$\\\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Literal counts for every $T\geq0$, for either by-horizon or exact-horizon acceptance. Identically zero or duplicate slots at $T=0$ are retained.}\label{smc:bc:tab:gapledger}
\end{table}

The gap residuals have degree two. In each POWER copy, $E_{13}$ has degree six with leading monomial $-w^4g^2$, and every other residual has degree at most four. Its square therefore contributes $w^8g^4$ with coefficient one. The two such monomials use separate module leaves and cannot cancel with each other or with $P$, which uses no module leaf. Hence
\begin{align}
\deg F_{M,T}&=\max(12,\deg P_{M,T}),\label{smc:bc:eq:degreeF}\\
\deg F_{M,T}&\leq\max(12,4(T+1)^2-4)\quad(T\geq1),\nonumber\\
\deg F_{M,0}&=12.\nonumber
\end{align}
If $\deg P>12$, its top terms cannot be affected by the fixed degree-twelve base. This proves the equality in the first line without claiming equality in the second. The POWER and gap base has coefficients independent of $M,T$, so its addition preserves the stated coefficient-bit asymptotic, up to a fixed contribution.

\subsection{Unique projection and infinite full fibers}
For a given accepted input, the gap equations force
\[
p=\frac{2D}{20g_1-D},\qquad q=\frac{2D}{20g_3-D}.
\]
Their powers-of-two exponents determine $A,B$ uniquely, and the compressed theorem fixes $j,r,s$. But the complete 57-tuple is never unique when it exists. In the first module, increase $\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_2$ by the same nonnegative integer. They appear only together in $E_5$; every residual is preserved, and both positive adapters remain positive. Arbitrarily many such shifts yield infinitely many distinct full witnesses. Unique decoding and unique compressed projection must therefore not be described as a finite-fold full gap representation.

\subsection{Conditional physical interpretation}
The retained unclocked five-signal theorem identifies each native transition with one ordered instruction section on encoded inputs. Conditional on that theorem, \eqref{smc:bc:eq:fullF} certifies bounded instruction-section reachability from those inputs. If first halt is at $k>0$, the retained physical prefix takes strictly between $kD$ and $10kD$ time and at most $32k$ binary contacts. At $k=0$ the initial section is already halted. These are the retained theorem's bounds; the present arithmetic result does not re-audit the physical construction or depend on the clock refinement of Report 65 \textup{[source~35, Theorem~\ref{smc:ck:thm:clock}]}. A physical collision horizon is not identified with a native instruction horizon, and virtual absorbing halt steps are only arithmetic bookkeeping.

\wtag\ [The ``retained unclocked five-signal theorem'' is source~34's Theorem~\ref{smc:br:thm:compiler} (Part~XII), at most 32 binary collisions per instruction with duration strictly between $D$ and $10D$. With source~35's clock every instruction takes exactly $30D$; source~36 does not use that refinement.]
\section{Primitive integer realization and the counting object}\label{smc:bc:sec:primitive}
The remainder of the report counts \emph{all} encoded initializations. Neither $M$ nor $T$ occurs in the counting definitions. An initialization is a positive integer triple, counted once; its Diophantine witness tuples are not counted.

\begin{remark}[\wtag\ restatement of source~35's Theorem~\ref{smc:ck:thm:primitive}: exact primitive scale]\label{smc:bc:prop:primitive}
Source~36 states, as its Proposition~7.1: ``For each ordered pair $(a,b)\in\NN^2$, put $m=\max(a,b)$ and
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:uvw}
U=2^m+2^{m-a+1},\qquad W=2^m+2^{m-b+1},\qquad
V=20\cdot2^m-U-W.
\end{equation}
If $c=\gcd(U,V,W)$, then the primitive triple is $(U,V,W)/c$, and every encoded integer triple for this pair is a unique positive integer multiple of it. Its total is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:dscale}
d(a,b)=\begin{cases}
20,&(a,b)=(0,0),\\
10,&(a,b)=(1,1),\\
20,&\{a,b\}=\{0,1\},\\
2^{m+1},&m\geq2\text{ and }a\equiv b\equiv3\pmod4,\\
10\cdot2^m,&m\geq2\text{ otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
In every case $d(a,b)\geq2^{m+1}$.''

This is source~35's Theorem~\ref{smc:ck:thm:primitive} (Part~XII), whose gcd list $c\in\{1,4,2,10,2\}$ gives $d(a,b)=20\cdot2^m/c$, the minimum total $D_{\min}$ there. Source~36's proof is source~35's: the small cases $(3,14,3)$, $(4,32,4)$ and $(6,30,4)$ directly; for $m\geq2$ exact 2-adic valuation one and the only possible odd factor~5, which divides $U$ exactly when $a\equiv3\pmod4$ because 2 has order four modulo~5; and a B\'ezout argument for the integer multiple. It is not printed twice. The added lower bound holds because $c\leq10$, so $d(a,b)\geq2\cdot2^m$. Source~36 cites this classification as inherited, from the retained native-gap proof (its bibliography entry~\cite{bcnative}, Sections~3 and~6), and its independent counting review re-derived it through least common multiples of reduced denominators (Section~\ref{smc:bc:sec:evidence}).
\end{remark}

Here $a\equiv b\equiv3\pmod4$ means \emph{both} counters have residue 3, and does not require $a=b$. Each counter pair supplies a ray of integer multiples; distinct ordered pairs have distinct ratios and therefore disjoint rays.

\subsection{Counter index and numeric height are different}
For $m\geq2$, the primitive total lies between $2^{m+1}$ and $10\cdot2^m$, so its bit length is $m+O(1)$ and its numeric size is $\Theta(2^m)$. At a counting height $X$, a ray can contribute only if $m\leq\log_2 X-1$. Thus only logarithmically many counter layers occur, but the early rays contribute linearly many multiples. The counter-layer index $m$ is not the counting height, the primitive total, or the rank of a triple.

If the largest native counter is itself given in binary with length $\ell$, then $m$ can be of order $2^\ell$. The chosen gap description's bit height is correspondingly exponential in $\ell$. This is a cost of this particular encoding, not a general encoding lower bound and not a bound on the larger Pell witnesses.

\begin{definition}[Triple count and shell count]\label{smc:bc:def:count}
For integer $X\geq0$, let $\mathcal A(X)$ count encoded positive integer triples with $D\leq X$, and set $\mathcal A(0)=0$. For $X\geq1$, put
\[
\mathcal J(X)=\mathcal A(X)-\mathcal A(X-1).
\]
Thus $\mathcal J(X)$ counts triples at the one total $X$.
\end{definition}
By Remark~\ref{smc:bc:prop:primitive} and disjointness of the rays,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:countfloor}
\mathcal A(X)=\sum_{a,b\geq0}\left\lfloor\frac{X}{d(a,b)}\right\rfloor.
\end{equation}
Only finitely many summands are nonzero. This counts neither distinct counter pairs, distinct totals, witness tuples nor halting inputs.

\section{Exact floor formulas and a digital identity}\label{smc:bc:sec:floor}
For integers $b\geq2$ and $n\geq0$, define
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:Fb}
F_b(n)=\sum_{k\geq0}(2k+1)\left\lfloor\frac{n}{b^k}\right\rfloor.
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Exact cumulative formula]\label{smc:bc:thm:floor}
For every integer $X\geq0$,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:exactcount}
\mathcal A(X)=F_2\!\left(\left\lfloor\frac X{10}\right\rfloor\right)
+F_{16}\!\left(\left\lfloor\frac X{16}\right\rfloor\right)
-F_{16}\!\left(\left\lfloor\frac X{80}\right\rfloor\right).
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
There are $2m+1$ ordered pairs with maximum $m$. Assign all of them the baseline scale $10\cdot2^m$. The pair $(0,0)$ actually changes a contribution $\lfloor X/10\rfloor$ to $\lfloor X/20\rfloor$, whereas $(1,1)$ makes the inverse change. These two low-counter corrections cancel exactly.

The remaining exceptional pairs have maximum $m=4k+3$. Among the $k+1$ possible counter values $3,7,\ldots,4k+3$, exactly $(k+1)^2-k^2=2k+1$ ordered pairs have that maximum. For each, replace the old scale $80\cdot16^k$ by $16^{k+1}$. Summing the baseline and corrections gives \eqref{smc:bc:eq:exactcount}, using
$\lfloor\lfloor X/c\rfloor/b^k\rfloor=\lfloor X/(cb^k)\rfloor$.
\end{proof}

Write the base-$b$ digits of $n$ as $n=\sum_{j\geq0}\delta_jb^j$, and define
\[
s_b(n)=\sum_j\delta_j,\qquad w_b(n)=\sum_j j\delta_j.
\]
Both sums are zero at $n=0$.

\begin{proposition}[Digit form]\label{smc:bc:prop:digits}
For every integer base $b\geq2$ and integer $n\geq0$,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:digit}
F_b(n)=\frac{b(b+1)n-(3b-1)s_b(n)}{(b-1)^2}
-\frac{2w_b(n)}{b-1}.
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Expanding each floor and reversing the finite sums gives
\[
F_b(n)=\sum_j\delta_j\sum_{k=0}^{j}(2k+1)b^{j-k}.
\]
The inner sum is
\[
\frac{b(b+1)b^j-(3b-1)}{(b-1)^2}-\frac{2j}{b-1}.
\]
To verify this without importing a summation identity, observe that its value at $j=0$ is 1, and that both this expression and the inner sum satisfy the recurrence $S_j=bS_{j-1}+(2j+1)$. Substitution establishes the displayed value and then \eqref{smc:bc:eq:digit}.
\end{proof}

Equations \eqref{smc:bc:eq:exactcount} and \eqref{smc:bc:eq:digit} express the complete cumulative count by floors, digit sums and weighted digit sums. No external sequence identification is needed.

\section{Shell multiplicities and represented total scales}\label{smc:bc:sec:shell}
Let $v_2(X)$ be the exponent of 2 dividing $X\geq1$, including value zero for odd $X$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact shell]\label{smc:bc:thm:shell}
Writing $v=v_2(X)$,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:shell}
\mathcal J(X)=\begin{cases}
v^2,&5\mid X,\\
\lfloor v/4\rfloor^2,&5\nmid X.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
Consequently the represented positive totals are exactly the multiples of 10 or 16. Their distinct-scale count is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:bc:eq:distinct}
\mathcal B(X)=\left\lfloor\frac X{10}\right\rfloor
+\left\lfloor\frac X{16}\right\rfloor
-\left\lfloor\frac X{80}\right\rfloor
=\frac3{20}X+O(1).
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
A primitive scale $d$ contributes exactly one triple at total $X$ if and only if $d\mid X$. The low-counter exchange in the proof of Theorem~\ref{smc:bc:thm:floor} also cancels for these divisor indicators.

If $5\mid X$, a baseline scale $10\cdot2^m$ divides $X$ precisely for $0\leq m\leq v-1$. Their multiplicities sum to $1+3+\cdots+(2v-1)=v^2$, with an empty sum at $v=0$. Each exceptional old scale $80\cdot16^k$ divides $X$ exactly when its replacement $16^{k+1}$ does, namely when $v\geq4k+4$. All special corrections therefore cancel.

If $5\nmid X$, no baseline scale divides $X$. Only the replacement scales contribute, with $0\leq k<\lfloor v/4\rfloor$. Their multiplicities sum to $\lfloor v/4\rfloor^2$. This proves \eqref{smc:bc:eq:shell}. Positivity of that formula is equivalent to $10\mid X$ or $16\mid X$. Inclusion-exclusion, with common multiples 80, gives \eqref{smc:bc:eq:distinct}.
\end{proof}

The two counts answer different questions: $\mathcal B$ counts a represented total once, whereas $\mathcal A$ counts it $\mathcal J(X)$ times. For example, total 20 supports four triples, and total 80 supports sixteen. The density $3/20$ is a density among positive integer totals, not a triple-count slope.
