\section{Finite tables, domains, and the main tradeoff}\label{smc:la:sec:setup}
Write $\NN=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ and $\Np=\{1,2,\ldots\}$. Fix $T\in\NN$, put $K=T+1$, and define
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:clipping}
\clip(x)=\min(x,K),\qquad
U_S=\{(A,B)\in\Np^2:(\clip(A),\clip(B))\in S\},
\end{equation}
where $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,K\}^2$ is fixed coefficient data. The table is never a free input or an existentially selected table. Degrees below are joint total degrees in every actual input and witness, before imposing any equations. We set $\deg0=-\infty$; a nonzero constant has degree zero. A residual-square count refers to the literal displayed slots, even if some are zero or repeated.

\begin{theorem}[Native compilers, stated together]\label{smc:la:thm:summary}
For every fixed table $S$ there are explicit integer polynomials with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item A sum $P_S(A,B;r,s)$ of five residual squares represents $U_S$ with exactly two declared positive witnesses, unique whenever they exist. For $T\ge1$,
\[
\deg P_S=\max\{2K,4,2\deg F_S\}\le4T,
\]
where $F_S$ is the rejection interpolant in \eqref{smc:la:eq:tensor}. A separate $T=0$ definition has exact degree two.
\item A globally nonnegative polynomial $Q_S(A,B,w)$ represents $U_S$ with one declared positive witness, again unique whenever it exists. For $T\ge1$,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:degree-one-summary}
\deg Q_S=D_S:=2n_I+4Tn_E+8Tn_C\le10T^2+8T,
\end{equation}
where $n_I,n_E,n_C$ count accepted cells with zero, one and two tail coordinates. The empty product is $1$, with $D_S=0$.
\item With no degree restriction, the minimum number of positive existential auxiliary variables in a single integer-polynomial equality defining $U_S$ is zero or one. It is zero exactly when the coordinate-flat closure condition of Theorem~\ref{smc:la:thm:classification} holds.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

Each construction is given and proved below. In particular, the arity classification concerns a \emph{fixed finite table} and unrestricted degree. It does not assert that the two-witness linear-degree formula is arity-minimal, or that any degree is minimal. The one-witness full-table product reaches its displayed worst-case degree even though the full predicate itself has the zero polynomial as a zero-witness representation.

\subsection{Why bounded counter programs give such tables}
Fix a finite deterministic two-counter program $M$, initial state $q_0$ and halt state $H$. A nonhalt instruction either increments one counter and takes its specified successor, or tests a counter for zero, taking its zero successor when zero and otherwise decrementing it and taking its positive successor. The other counter is unchanged. Both counters are natural integers; arbitrary loops are allowed. Make $H$ virtually absorbing with no counter change solely to describe a finite prefix.

\begin{remark}[\wtag\ restatement of source~36's Lemma~\ref{smc:bc:lem:clip}: clipping through the last tested entry]\label{smc:la:lem:clip}
Source~38 states, as its Lemma~1.2: ``The runs from $(a,b)$ and $(\min(a,T),\min(b,T))$ have the same control states $q_0,\ldots,q_T$ and the same branches in their first $T$ transitions. Thus first arrival at $H$ at or before $T$ is preserved.'' This is source~36's Lemma~\ref{smc:bc:lem:clip} (source~38 states only the by-$T$ conclusion here and treats first halt exactly at $T$ in the next paragraph). Its proof, by induction on the common branches with the remark that a representative may become zero only \emph{after} transition~$T$, is source~36's and is not printed twice.
\end{remark}

Positive inputs $A,B$ represent native counters $A-1,B-1$. The shift converts the native threshold $T$ to $K=T+1$. Define $S$ by testing representatives $(i-1,j-1)$ either for reaching $H$ by $T$ or for first reaching $H$ exactly at $T$. Remark~\ref{smc:la:lem:clip} proves \eqref{smc:la:eq:clipping} for all positive input sizes in both cases. If $q_0=H$, the by-$T$ table is always full, and the exact-$T$ table is empty for $T>0$. At $T=0$ both predicates are full exactly when $q_0=H$.

There are $K^2$ table bits. A direct finite construction examines the initial state and at most $T$ transitions from each representative: at most $K^2T$ native transitions, with each representative counter at most $2T$. This is an effective finite preprocessing bound, not an executed interpreter in this report. It is not free advice and does not imply a faster bounded-halting algorithm. The horizon indexes different polynomials, with different products, factorials and table coefficients.

\section{A two-witness tensor compiler}\label{smc:la:sec:tensor}
Assume $T\ge1$, so $K\ge2$, and put $c=(K-1)!$. For $1\le i\le K$ define
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:basis}
\ell_i(z)=(-1)^{K-i}\binom{K-1}{i-1}
  \prod_{\substack{1\le h\le K\\h\ne i}}(z-h).
\end{equation}
The difference product at $i$ is $(-1)^{K-i}(i-1)!(K-i)!$. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:nodes}
\ell_i(h)=c\,\mathbf1_{i=h}\quad(1\le h\le K),
\qquad \sum_{i=1}^K\ell_i(z)=c.
\end{equation}
The second identity follows because the two sides have degree at most $K-1$ and agree at $K$ distinct nodes. Every coefficient is integral. Define
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:tensor}
F_S(x,y)=\sum_{(i,j)\notin S}\ell_i(x)\ell_j(y),
\qquad (i,j)\in\{1,\ldots,K\}^2.
\end{equation}
It has degree at most $K-1$ in each coordinate, at most $2K-2$ jointly, and at a grid node equals zero on $S$ and $c^2$ off $S$. In particular the full table gives $F_S=0$ and the empty table gives $F_S=c^2$. The notation $x,y$ defines this polynomial; it introduces no witnesses in the compiler.

Set the expressions
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:uv}
u=A-r+1,\qquad v=B-s+1,\qquad R_K(z)=\prod_{i=1}^K(z-i).
\end{equation}
Use precisely the five residuals
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:five}
\begin{aligned}
D_1&=R_K(u),&D_2&=R_K(v),\\
D_3&=(r-1)(u-K),&D_4&=(s-1)(v-K),\\
D_5&=F_S(u,v),&P_S&=\sum_{i=1}^5D_i^2.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Here $A,B,r,s$ are ordinary positive integer variables. Before the equations hold, $u,v$ are not assumed positive. There are no implicit range constraints and no input-dependent denominators.

\begin{proposition}[Both directions and the whole native fiber]\label{smc:la:prop:tensor}
For positive $A,B$, there exist positive $r,s$ with $P_S=0$ exactly when $(A,B)\in U_S$. Every such zero has
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:unique-two}
r=A-\clip(A)+1,\qquad s=B-\clip(B)+1.
\end{equation}
In particular the native witness fiber is a singleton or empty, and $1\le r\le A$, $1\le s\le B$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
A sum of real squares vanishes only when every residual vanishes. The first two force $u,v\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$. From \eqref{smc:la:eq:uv}, $A-u=r-1\ge0$. If $u<K$, then $D_3=0$ forces $r=1$ and $A=u$. If $u=K$, positivity of $r$ forces $A\ge K$. These alternatives give exactly $u=\clip(A)$ and the first equality in \eqref{smc:la:eq:unique-two}; similarly $v=\clip(B)$. The fifth residual now asserts table membership, proving soundness and uniqueness.

Conversely, if $(A,B)\in U_S$, the positive pair in \eqref{smc:la:eq:unique-two} gives those clipped representatives. The range residuals vanish. Each classification product vanishes because either its slack is one or its representative is $K$. The fifth residual vanishes at the accepted node. Thus $P_S=0$.
\end{proof}

Strict positivity is essential. If $r=0$ were allowed, an input $A=K-1$ could produce $u=A-r+1=K$; the classification product would vanish via $u-K$, selecting an incorrect tail class. Positivity is part of the theorem's domain, not an inequality that the displayed polynomial supplies on its own.

\subsection{Horizon zero is a separate definition}
When $T=0$, put $\epsilon=0$ for the full one-cell table and $\epsilon=1$ for the empty table. Use the five residual slots
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:T0}
A-r,\ B-s,\ 0,\ 0,\ \epsilon,
\qquad P_S=(A-r)^2+(B-s)^2+\epsilon.
\end{equation}
This has exact degree two, six nonzero monomials if accepted and seven if rejected. Accepted inputs have the unique positive pair $(r,s)=(A,B)$. Inserting $K=1$ in the unchanged generic formula \eqref{smc:la:eq:five} would retain unnecessary quadratic classification residuals and degree-four squares. Equation~\eqref{smc:la:eq:T0} explicitly replaces that formula; it does not silently simplify its degree claim.

\subsection{Exact degree and a fixed sharpness example}
\begin{lemma}[No cancellation at the highest square degree]\label{smc:la:lem:sos}
For real polynomials $h_1,\ldots,h_m$, not all zero,
$\deg\sum h_i^2=2\max_i\deg h_i$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The top homogeneous component is the sum of squares of the top components of maximal degree. If it vanished identically, evaluation at every real point and nonnegativity would force each such component to vanish identically, a contradiction.
\end{proof}
The substitution $x=A-r+1$, $y=B-s+1$ preserves the degree of every nonzero polynomial $f(x,y)$. Its top part becomes $f_{\rm top}(A-r,B-s)$, nonzero because setting $r=s=0$ recovers $f_{\rm top}(A,B)$. The range residuals have exact degree $K$ and the classification residuals exact degree two. Therefore
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:degree-two}
\deg P_S=\max\{2K,4,2\deg F_S\}\le4K-4=4T.
\end{equation}
Empty and full tables have degree $2K$. At $T=1$, every table has degree four.

For a fixed program attaining the upper bound, use states $Q_A,Q_B,L,H$, initial state $Q_A$, and the instructions
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lll}
\toprule
State & Zero branch & Positive branch\\
\midrule
$Q_A$: test $a$ & go to $Q_B$ & decrement $a$, go to $L$\\
$Q_B$: test $b$ & go to $H$ & decrement $b$, go to $L$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
At $L$, increment $a$ and return to $L$. The only accepted input is $(a,b)=(0,0)$, first reaching $H$ on transition two. For every by-horizon $T\ge2$, the table is $S=\{(1,1)\}$. Then
\[
F_S(x,y)=c^2-\ell_1(x)\ell_1(y),
\]
whose $x^{K-1}y^{K-1}$ coefficient is $-1$. It has degree $2K-2$, and \eqref{smc:la:eq:degree-two} is exactly $4T$ for this one fixed program at every such horizon.

This is sharpness of the \emph{displayed construction}, not a lower bound against other polynomials. For the same fixed program, first-exactly-$T$ acceptance is empty when $T>2$. At each individual exact horizon $T\ge2$, a chain of $T-2$ increments on the successful path after the second test yields the same singleton table; that delayed program depends on $T$.
\section{One witness from disjoint clipped cells}\label{smc:la:sec:one}
For $K\ge2$, define
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:pK}
p_K(x)=\prod_{h=1}^{T}(x-h)^2.
\end{equation}
This is nonnegative on $\R$. On positive integers it is zero exactly for $x<K$, and strictly positive exactly for $x\ge K$. The second assertion uses the discrete domain: every positive integer smaller than $K=T+1$ is one of its roots.

\centering

For each table cell define a globally nonnegative factor:
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:cell-factors}
\begin{aligned}
f_{ij}&=(A-i)^2+(B-j)^2+(w-1)^2 &&(i,j<K),\\
f_{iK}&=(A-i)^2+(w-p_K(B))^2 &&(i<K),\\
f_{Kj}&=(B-j)^2+(w-p_K(A))^2 &&(j<K),\\
f_{KK}&=(w-p_K(A)p_K(B))^2.&
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Set
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:one-product}
Q_S(A,B,w)=\prod_{(i,j)\in S}f_{ij}(A,B,w),
\end{equation}
with empty product $1$. All coefficients are integers, and $Q_S\ge0$ on all of $\R^3$.

\begin{proposition}[One witness, with no inactive freedom]\label{smc:la:prop:one}
For positive $A,B,w$, a cell factor in \eqref{smc:la:eq:cell-factors} vanishes exactly on its own clipped cell and at the following witness value:
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:one-witness}
w=
\begin{cases}
1,&A,B<K,\\
p_K(B),&A<K\le B,\\
p_K(A),&B<K\le A,\\
p_K(A)p_K(B),&A,B\ge K.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
Consequently $\exists w\in\Np:Q_S(A,B,w)=0$ is equivalent to $(A,B)\in U_S$, and its positive witness is unique.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
An interior factor is zero exactly when $A=i$, $B=j$ and $w=1$. An edge factor $f_{iK}$ is zero exactly when $A=i$ and $w=p_K(B)>0$, which forces $B\ge K$ by \eqref{smc:la:eq:pK}; the other edge is symmetric. At the corner, $w=p_K(A)p_K(B)>0$ forces both factors positive, since they are nonnegative, hence $A,B\ge K$. The displayed choices prove every converse.

A real product is zero exactly when some factor is zero. On positive integer inputs the clipped cells partition the domain, so at most one factor can vanish for a positive witness. Its cell is accepted if and only if it occurs in \eqref{smc:la:eq:one-product}. Equation~\eqref{smc:la:eq:one-witness} then proves existence and uniqueness. Every listed value is a positive integer on its stated cell.
\end{proof}

Allowing $w=0$ would break this proof: in an edge factor, $p_K(B)=0$ at a below-threshold positive integer could mimic the tail. No additional inequality is hidden in the equation; strict positivity is an explicit domain obligation.

At $K=1$, the separate one-witness definitions are $(w-1)^2$ for the full table and $1$ for the empty table. Their degrees are two and zero. The accepted witness is $w=1$; the rejected polynomial has no solution and its formally declared witness is unused.

\subsection{Exact degree and the distinction between a block and a square}
Each factor is nonzero. Their exact degrees, in the order of \eqref{smc:la:eq:cell-factors}, are $2,4T,4T,8T$: $p_K$ has leading term $x^{2T}$, and its squared corner product has leading term $A^{4T}B^{4T}$. Total degree is additive under products of nonzero polynomials. Thus \eqref{smc:la:eq:degree-one-summary} is exact. The ceiling uses $n_I\le T^2$, $n_E\le2T$ and $n_C\le1$, and is attained by the full-table \emph{displayed product}. For nonempty $S$, the coefficient of $w^{2|S|}$ is one, so $w$ genuinely occurs.

Each interior factor has three residual-square slots, each edge has two, and the corner has one. Fully distributing their product gives precisely
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:distributed}
L_S=3^{n_I}2^{n_E}
\end{equation}
literal square slots: pick one squared residual from each factor and square the product of those residuals. The empty-product convention gives the one square $1^2$. Coincident or zero terms need not be combined; this is a presentation count, never a minimum SOS length.

The compact $Q_S$ is a product of sums of squares and is not generally one residual square. Replacing it by $Q_S^2$ preserves its zero set and witnesses, costs one additional multiplication, and changes its degree from $D_S$ to $2D_S$. Exponential distributed SOS length does not imply exponential collected monomial support; degree and the fixed number of variables give the polynomial bounds in Section~\ref{smc:la:sec:costs}.
\section{Exactly when zero native witnesses suffice}\label{smc:la:sec:classification}
For a clipped cell $a=(a_1,a_2)$ define its tail positions
$J(a)=\{\ell:a_\ell=K\}$. Its \emph{coordinate-flat closure in the table} consists of all cells obtained by replacing any or all coordinates in $J(a)$ by arbitrary indices in $\{1,\ldots,K\}$, while keeping the other coordinates fixed.

\begin{samepage}
\begin{theorem}[Exact zero-versus-one native classification]\label{smc:la:thm:classification}
Fix $K\ge1$ and $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,K\}^2$. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item An integer polynomial $R(A,B)$, with no witnesses, vanishes on positive integer inputs exactly on $U_S$.
\item Every accepted cell's coordinate-flat closure is contained in $S$.
\item If $(i,K)$ is accepted then every $(i,j)$ is accepted; if $(K,j)$ is accepted then every $(i,j)$ is accepted; an accepted $(K,K)$ forces the full table.
\end{enumerate}
Within one polynomial equality, with fixed table-dependent coefficients and no degree bound, the minimum number of positive existential auxiliary variables is zero when these conditions hold and one otherwise.
\end{theorem}
\end{samepage}

The quantified indices in the last condition range from $1$ to $K$. Joint replacement at the corner is essential. This is not the usual coordinatewise order-ideal condition: fixed coordinates smaller than $K$ need not be replaced.

\begin{proof}[Necessity]
Suppose $R$ vanishes on all positive integer points of an accepted cell. Fix its non-tail coordinates at that cell's exact values. The resulting polynomial in the tail coordinates vanishes on the entire Cartesian product $\{K,K+1,\ldots\}^{|J(a)|}$.

A polynomial zero on a product of infinite real sets is identically zero. For one variable this is the finite-root theorem. Inductively, view it as a polynomial in its last variable; fixing all earlier coordinates in their infinite sets forces every coefficient to vanish there, and the induction hypothesis makes those coefficient polynomials zero. Therefore the restriction of $R$ to the entire coordinate flat is identically zero. In particular, each former tail coordinate may take any positive value below $K$ as well. Exact representation requires the corresponding jointly replaced clipped cells to be accepted. This argument even allows real coefficients and makes no SOS assumption on $R$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Sufficiency and the minimum]
Let $X_1=A$, $X_2=B$ and define
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:zero-witness}
Z_a(X)=\sum_{\ell\notin J(a)}(X_\ell-a_\ell)^2,
\qquad R_S(X)=\prod_{a\in S}Z_a(X).
\end{equation}
An empty sum is zero and an empty product is one. A factor vanishes exactly on its coordinate flat. If the closure condition holds, every positive point on that flat is accepted; conversely an accepted point makes its own cell's factor zero. This proves exact representation. For the empty table, $R_S=1$. An accepted all-tail cell forces a full table and contributes the zero factor, yielding $R_S=0$, as required.

If $S$ is nonempty and has no all-tail cell, each factor is a nonzero degree-two polynomial, so the displayed $R_S$ has degree exactly $2|S|$. That degree need not be minimal. Necessity rules out zero variables if closure fails, while Proposition~\ref{smc:la:prop:one} supplies one. These two observations establish the exact minimum in the stated class.
\end{proof}

At $K=1$, both possible tables have minimum zero, represented by $0$ and $1$. Finite interior-only tables also satisfy closure. For example, a single interior point admits $(A-i)^2+(B-j)^2=0$ with no witness. A single edge cell at $K\ge2$ fails closure: its tail ray cannot be cut off below $K$ by a witness-free polynomial equality. These examples explain why a uniform one-witness construction is not minimal for every table.

\wtag\ [Batch-91 manuscript~21 restates this theorem with proof and counts the tables it classifies: among the tables of a fixed size, those that need no auxiliary variable number $C_n=1+a_n$, with $a_n$ the OEIS sequence A196460. That manuscript is printed in the collection's report \path{SetTheory/Cardinals/docs/reports/generating-functions-and-asymptotics/oeis-sequence-asymptotics/a196460-clipping-tables}, written together with this Part; its normalization of the table size is stated there. The Hilbert's-tenth programme's review notes that the classification is ``for fixed finite clipping tables with unrestricted degree, not arbitrary c.e.\ languages''~\cite{reviewarith91}.]

\subsection{The fixed-dimensional extension}
Fix an integer $d\ge1$, $K\ge2$ and $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,K\}^d$. Inputs $X_1,\ldots,X_d$ and witness $w$ are all positive integers. For a cell $a$, put $J(a)=\{\ell:a_\ell=K\}$, $t(a)=|J(a)|$, and define
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:d-extension}
\begin{aligned}
f_a(X,w)&=\sum_{\ell\notin J(a)}(X_\ell-a_\ell)^2
 +\left(w-\prod_{\ell\in J(a)}p_K(X_\ell)\right)^2,\\
Q_S(X,w)&=\prod_{a\in S}f_a(X,w).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The inner empty product is one. Positivity of $w$ forces every tail factor $p_K(X_\ell)$ to be positive; the fixed-coordinate squares force every other input coordinate. Thus each factor defines exactly its clipped cell, and disjointness proves the same equivalence and uniqueness. Its unique witness is the product over the actual tail coordinates, or one if there are none.

A no-tail factor has degree two; a factor with $t(a)\ge1$ tails has degree $4Tt(a)$. Degree additivity gives the exact sum of these cell degrees (zero for empty $S$). In the full table, there are $T^d$ no-tail cells and total tail-coordinate incidence $dK^{d-1}$, whence
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:d-degree}
\deg Q_S\le 2T^d+4dT(T+1)^{d-1}.
\end{equation}
For fixed $d$ this is $O(T^d)$ and the support has at most
$\binom{\deg Q_S+d+1}{d+1}$ monomials. The constants and exponents here may depend on $d$; no dimension-uniform polynomial bound is asserted. The fully distributed SOS presentation may still be exponential in $|S|$. At $K=1$, again use $(w-1)^2$ or $1$.

The infinite-grid necessity proof and the zero-witness construction \eqref{smc:la:eq:zero-witness} hold verbatim in $d$ coordinates. Consequently Theorem~\ref{smc:la:thm:classification}'s exact zero-versus-one classification holds for every fixed finite-dimensional clipping table, with the same single-equation, positive-integer and unrestricted-degree qualifications.

For $K=n+1$ the tables whose exact auxiliary minimum is zero number $C_n=1+a_n$, where $a_n=\sum_j\binom nj(1+2^j)^n$ is OEIS A196460, so the zero-witness fraction is asymptotic to $\tfrac12\,4^{-n}$; that report restates this theorem and the one-witness construction with proof, as a restatement, and derives fixed-order and uniform asymptotics of $a_n$. \section{Coefficient, support, storage and circuit costs}\label{smc:la:sec:costs}
All bounds in this section concern the displayed formulas, uniformly in the table at a fixed $K\ge2$. They are upper bounds, not instancewise comparisons or optimality statements. For an integer polynomial $f$, let $\lonenorm f$ denote the sum of absolute values of its collected coefficients. This norm is subadditive and submultiplicative. Integer arithmetic operations are counted separately from bit complexity, and the finite-table preprocessing from Section~\ref{smc:la:sec:setup} must be added.

\subsection{Tensor coefficients after every affine substitution}
Put
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:two-norm}
B_K=(K+1)!,\qquad L_K=2^{K-1}B_K,\qquad
H_K=L_K^4+2B_K^2+8(K+1)^2.
\end{equation}
The affine factor $u-i=A-r-(i-1)$ has norm $i+1$. Product and triangle bounds, with the binomial sum $2^{K-1}$, therefore give
\begin{align*}
\lonenorm{R_K(u)},\lonenorm{R_K(v)}&\le B_K,\\
\sum_i\lonenorm{\ell_i(u)},\ \sum_i\lonenorm{\ell_i(v)}&\le L_K,\\
\lonenorm{F_S(u,v)}&\le L_K^2.
\end{align*}
Each classification residual has norm at most $2(K+1)$, so
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:Pheight}
\lonenorm{P_S}\le H_K.
\end{equation}
Every coefficient magnitude thus needs at most $\ceil{\log_2(H_K+1)}=O(K\log(K+1))$ bits, with an additional sign bit if desired. No substitution-dependent coefficient cost is omitted.

The tensor square has degree at most $2K-2$ in the pair $(A,r)$ and separately at most $2K-2$ in $(B,s)$. Its support is at most $\binom{2K}{2}^2$. The other squares each use only one of those pairs, and have degree at most $2K$. Only the two additional degree layers can lie outside that tensor support envelope; they contribute at most
$2[\binom{2K+2}{2}-\binom{2K}{2}]=8K+2$. Hence a complete support ceiling is
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:two-support}
N_K=K^2(2K-1)^2+8K+2=O(K^4).
\end{equation}
For example, fixed-field records for coefficients and four exponents need at most
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:two-storage}
N_K\left[\ceil{\log_2(H_K+1)}+1+
4\ceil{\log_2(2K+1)}\right]
\end{equation}
bits, apart from a format header. Thus the expanded storage ceiling is $O(K^5\log(K+1))$. Cancellations may substantially reduce support.

\subsection{Tensor factored gates and coefficient generation}
Let $m=K^2-|S|$ be the rejected-cell count. Reuse the $2K$ factors $u-i,v-i$. Computing every one-dimensional basis by multiplying its $K-1$ factors and its signed binomial coefficient uses at most $2K(K-1)$ multiplications. The two ranges cost $2(K-1)$ more, the two classification products two more, the rejected tensor products $m$, and the five final squares five. Thus
\begin{align}\label{smc:la:eq:two-gates}
\text{multiplications}&\le2K^2+m+5,\\
\text{additions/subtractions}&\le2K+10+\max(m-1,0),\notag
\end{align}
including $u,v$, factors, shifted slacks and the final sum. A uniform combined ceiling is $4K^2+2K+14$. There is no division. Signed binomial constants have $O(K)$ bits each, nodes have $O(\log K)$ bits, the table has $K^2$ bits, and a straightforward gate-index encoding uses $O(K^2\log(K+1))$ bits in all. These counts do not treat large integer operands as fixed-bit objects.

For one explicit expanded-construction procedure, build the $K$ univariate bases by successive linear multiplication in $O(K^3)$ integer coefficient operations. Sum their outer products across the table in $O(K^4)$, and square the bivariate polynomial by naive convolution in $O(K^4)$. Precompute the powers of $A-r+1$ and $B-s+1$ through $2K-2$. Substitute one coordinate by a separable coefficient transform in $O(K^4)$ operations, leaving $O(K^3)$ entries, and then the other in $O(K^5)$. The remaining four squares are smaller. This gives $O(K^5)$ integer coefficient operations after the table is known. Triangle/product bounds, even with the coarse affine-expansion factor $3^{4K}$, keep coefficient intermediates at $O(K\log(K+1))$ bits. Index handling is separate; no unit-cost bit-complexity or polynomial-in-$\log T$ assertion follows.

\subsection{One-witness heights and expanded storage}
Set
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:one-norm}
\begin{aligned}
P_K&=(K!)^2,& M_I&=2K^2+4,\\
M_E&=K^2+(1+P_K)^2,&M_C&=(1+P_K^2)^2,\\
C_S&=M_I^{n_I}M_E^{n_E}M_C^{n_C}.&&
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
All roots of $p_K$ are positive with even multiplicity, so its coefficients alternate in sign and
$\lonenorm{p_K}=\prod_{h=1}^T(1+h)^2=P_K$. Equation~\eqref{smc:la:eq:cell-factors} gives norms at most $M_I,M_E,M_C$ for the three cell types: for instance $\lonenorm{(A-i)^2}=(i+1)^2\le K^2$ and $\lonenorm{(w-p_K(B))^2}\le(1+P_K)^2$. Therefore
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:Qheight}
\lonenorm{Q_S}\le C_S,\qquad
\ceil{\log_2(C_S+1)}=O(K^2\log(K+1)).
\end{equation}
The last bound uses the actual cell counts:
$\log C_S\le T^2\log M_I+2T\log M_E+\log M_C$.
Applying the corner estimate to all cells would lose this sharper bound. Nonnegative polynomial \emph{values} do not imply nonnegative coefficients.

There are only three actual variables, and total degree $D_S$. Thus the support is at most $\binom{D_S+3}{3}=O(K^6)$, and a fully expanded sparse record list uses at most
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:one-storage}
\binom{D_S+3}{3}
\left[\ceil{\log_2(C_S+1)}+1+3\ceil{\log_2(D_S+1)}\right]
\end{equation}
bits apart from its header, with a constant-size convention for $D_S=0$. This is $O(K^8\log(K+1))$. For $Q_S^2$, replace $D_S,C_S$ by $2D_S,C_S^2$; the same asymptotic support and storage bounds hold. Horizon zero is constant size.

\subsection{One-witness gates and expansion work}
Form $A-h,B-h$ and their squares for $1\le h\le T$, then multiply the $T$ squares in each coordinate. This costs $2T$ subtractions and $4T-2$ multiplications. Preparing the four witness squares in \eqref{smc:la:eq:cell-factors} costs four subtractions and five multiplications. Interior factors add twice, edge factors once, and the corner is already prepared. For $N=|S|\ge1$,
\begin{align}\label{smc:la:eq:one-gates}
\text{multiplications}&\le4T+3+\max(N-1,0),\\
\text{additions/subtractions}&\le2T+4+2n_I+n_E.\notag
\end{align}
The combined ceiling is $3T^2+10T+7$. If $S$ is empty, return the constant one with no arithmetic. Squaring $Q_S$ adds one multiplication. The table, constants and gate indices admit an $O(K^2\log(K+1))$-bit factored description. Input-dependent values such as $p_K(A)$ require full precision, so these gates are not a bit-time claim.

For an explicit conservative expansion bound, interior factors have at most seven monomials; edge factors at most $6T+5$; the corner at most
$1+(2T+1)^2+(4T+1)^2$. This follows by expanding $w^2-2wp+p^2$ and the corner analogue. Their support bounds sum over $S$ to $O(K^2)$. Build $p_K$ in $O(K^2)$ coefficient operations. Each intermediate partial product has at most $\binom{D_S+3}{3}=O(K^6)$ monomials, so successive naive monomial convolutions and collection use $O(K^8)$ coefficient operations, with $O(K^2\log(K+1))$-bit coefficient intermediates. A further naive self-convolution for $Q_S^2$ uses $O(K^{12})$ operations. These are deliberately conservative bounds, with indexing/bookkeeping separate.

\subsection{Comparison with the accepted three-witness construction}
The earlier class-code compiler uses three positive witnesses and six square slots. Its retained upper bounds are degree $4K^2-4$, coefficient magnitude bits $O(K^2\log(K+1))$, support at most $16K^2-5$, and expanded storage $O(K^4\log(K+1))$, for $T\ge1$. They remain correct upper bounds; Report 66 \textup{[source~36]} did not claim equality in every instance. The separately accepted parity refinement in Report 67 \textup{[source~37, Theorem~\ref{smc:pp:thm:interpolants}]} gives exact degree $4K^2-4$ for even $K$ and $4K^2-8$ for odd $K\ge3$, independently of the acceptance table. Its special horizon-zero degree is two. The full exact-degree proof and accepted audit are retained as comparison sources.

The tensor construction reduces arity and the degree ceiling, and improves the coefficient-bit ceiling, but loses the predecessor's narrow univariate class-code support. Its expanded support/storage upper bounds are worse. The one-witness product saves another variable while increasing the degree and expanded-storage ceilings further. None of these upper-bound comparisons proves that every instance of one construction is larger than every instance of another. Reports 66--68 \textup{[sources~36 and~37, and the undelivered Report~68]} and their original counts are unchanged.
\section{Paid composition with the accepted POWER module}\label{smc:la:sec:power}
Only this section imports the accepted constructive number-theoretic dependency. The native finite-table results above do not use it. We repeat all base-two residuals and the domain recovery to specify the composed polynomial without an unexpanded POWER predicate.

\subsection{Twelve positive leaves, including the output}
For positive index $C$ and output $o$, the module has six directly positive leaves
\[
o,\ g,\ q_b,\ q_v,\ J,\ q_\alpha,
\]
and six distinct positive adapter leaves for the natural aliases
\[
d_{wb},\ d_{wC},\ d_{yC},\ q_\sigma,\ q_\tau,\ q_r.
\]
Each alias $z$ means $z^+-1$, where $z^+\in\Np$ is its own actual leaf. Thus the count is twelve including $o$, or eleven auxiliary leaves beyond a supplied output. The index $C$ is counted separately. In particular $q_\alpha$ is a directly positive integer, not a natural alias. Define only expressions
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:power-expressions}
\begin{aligned}
\omega&=2+d_{wb},&y&=C+d_{yC},&\beta&=1+4yq_b,\\
v_p&=y^2q_v,&t&=C+4yq_\tau,&M_p&=2o+J,\\
Z&=2o+J+5,&X&=y(Z-8)+8o+4M_pq_r,\\
U&=4\beta-Z,&V&=q_\alpha X+Uq_\sigma.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The complete residuals are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:power-five}
\begin{aligned}
H_1&=X^2-16-(Z^2-16)y^2,\\
H_2&=U^2-16q_\alpha^2-(Z^2-16)q_\alpha^2v_p^2,\\
H_3&=V^2-16q_\alpha^2-16q_\alpha^2(\beta^2-1)t^2,\\
H_4&=\omega-C-d_{wC},\\
H_5&=Z^2-16-16((\omega+1)^2-1)(\omega g)^2.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Every adapter and expression is substituted before treating the sum as a polynomial. No division appears in this formula.

\begin{remark}[\wtag\ restatement of source~37's Theorem~\ref{smc:pp:thm:modules} for twelve leaves at base two: imported POWER12 theorem]\label{smc:la:prop:power}
Source~38 states, as its Proposition~6.1: ``For positive integers $C,o$, the five equations \eqref{smc:la:eq:power-five} have eleven positive auxiliary leaves beyond $o$ if and only if $o=2^{C-1}$. The sum of their squares has exact joint degree twenty. Every accepted $(C,o)$ has infinitely many full module tuples, including when $C=1$.'' This is source~37's Theorem~\ref{smc:pp:thm:modules} for $\ell=12$ at $b=2$, with its exact degree~\eqref{smc:pp:eq:degree12fixed} and its infinite fibres (Section~\ref{smc:pp:sec:twelve}); the displays~\eqref{smc:la:eq:power-expressions} and~\eqref{smc:la:eq:power-five} are source~37's base-two display after~\eqref{smc:pp:eq:H12}, with source~37's $w,v,M,A_*,S,u$ written $\omega,v_p,M_p,Z,V,u_p$ and $d=4$.
\end{remark}

The accepted proof and its independent audit are retained in the source packet. Their all-exponent dependency is the constructive theorem pair \texttt{Pell.matiyasevic} and \texttt{Pell.eq\_pow\_of\_pell} in mathlib4, at the exact source revision identified in Section~\ref{smc:la:sec:provenance}. We import that theorem pair, not a claim of a new Lean execution. The following argument records the local recovery and explains precisely how this theorem is used.

\subsection{Recovered integrality, signs and the constructive boundary}
\wtag\ [Source~38's argument here is source~37's proof (Sections~\ref{smc:pp:sec:pell}, \ref{smc:pp:sec:infinite} and~\ref{smc:pp:sec:twelve}) at $b=2$ in the letters just listed, and is not printed twice. Its steps: $\alpha=Z/4$ and $u_p=U/(4q_\alpha)$ have integer squares by $H_5=0$ and $H_2=0$, so they are integers (source~37's Lemma~\ref{smc:pp:lem:rationalsquare}); $\alpha>\omega\geq2$; the sign $u_p>0$ follows from $\beta=\alpha+q_\alpha u_p\geq5$ and the \emph{integer} bound $q_\alpha\geq1$, a step that ``would not be valid for arbitrary positive rational leaves''; with $x=y(\alpha-2)+2o+M_pq_r$ and $s_p=x+u_pq_\sigma$ one has $X=4x$ and $V=4q_\alpha s_p$, and all fifteen equations of the older module are recovered,
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:recovered-old}
\begin{aligned}
x^2&=1+(\alpha^2-1)y^2,&u_p^2&=1+(\alpha^2-1)v_p^2,\\
s_p^2&=1+(\beta^2-1)t^2,&\beta&=1+4yq_b,\\
\beta&=\alpha+u_pq_\alpha,&v_p&=y^2q_v,\\
s_p&=x+u_pq_\sigma,&t&=C+4yq_\tau,\\

\alpha^2&=1+((\omega+1)^2-1)(\omega g)^2,\\

\end{equation}
so that the positive-index branch of \texttt{Pell.matiyasevic} and \texttt{Pell.eq\_pow\_of\_pell} give $2^C=2o$. For completeness the constructive theorems supply such a tuple, the residue lemma (source~37's Lemma~\ref{smc:pp:lem:residue}; for the last congruence $x^2-[y(\alpha-2)]^2=(4\alpha-5)y^2+1>0$) makes its quotients nonnegative, and the Pell recurrence
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:pell-recurrence}
\begin{aligned}
X_0(z)&=1,&Y_0(z)&=0,\\
X_{n+1}(z)&=zX_n(z)+(z^2-1)Y_n(z),&
Y_{n+1}(z)&=X_n(z)+zY_n(z)
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
(source~37's~\eqref{smc:pp:eq:pellrec}) gives, with the old $\alpha,\omega,M_p,g,x,y,u_p,v_p$ held fixed and every integer $k\geq1$, the progression
\begin{align}\label{smc:la:eq:progression}
\beta_k&=\beta_0+4yu_pk,&
q_{b,k}&=q_{b,0}+u_pk,&
q_{\alpha,k}&=q_{\alpha,0}+4yk,\\
s_k&=X_C(\beta_k),&t_k&=Y_C(\beta_k)&&\notag
\end{align}
(source~37's~\eqref{smc:pp:eq:betafamily}), which preserves every equation, makes $q_\alpha$ strictly positive and, through the strictly increasing $q_{b,k}$, gives infinitely many full module tuples; this is existential equivalence, not a bijection with the old tuples having $q_\alpha=0$. Finally the residual degrees are $4,10,10,1,6$, and the term $-J^2q_\alpha^2(d_{yC}^+)^4q_v^2$ of $H_2$ squares to the coefficient-one monomial
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:power-top}
J^4q_\alpha^4(d_{yC}^+)^8q_v^4
\end{equation}
of degree twenty (source~37's~\eqref{smc:pp:eq:degree12fixed}), so the module has exact degree twenty.]

\subsection{Three external gaps and both compiler substitutions}
Let $g_1,g_2,g_3$ be arbitrary positive integer inputs and let $D=g_1+g_2+g_3$ be an expression. Introduce positive witnesses $A,B$ and two independent twelve-leaf modules with $(C,o)=(A,p)$ and $(B,q)$. All their leaves are mutually distinct and distinct from the compiler witnesses. Set
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:gaps}
G_1=(20g_1-D)p-2D,\qquad G_3=(20g_3-D)q-2D,
\end{equation}
and define the common twelve-square decoding block
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:decode}
E=G_1^2+G_3^2+\sum_{i=1}^5(H_i^A)^2+\sum_{i=1}^5(H_i^B)^2.
\end{equation}
Its paid witness count is $2+2\cdot12=26$, including $p,q$ once each. The three final choices are
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:composed}
\mathcal F_2=E+P_S(A,B;r,s),\qquad
\mathcal F_1=E+Q_S(A,B,w),\qquad
\mathcal F_{1,\square}=E+Q_S(A,B,w)^2.
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Complete composed equivalence and ledger]\label{smc:la:thm:composition}
For each choice in \eqref{smc:la:eq:composed}, a positive witness exists exactly when the input is encoded by natural counters $a,b$ satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{smc:la:eq:encoding}
\frac{g_1}{D}=\frac1{20}+\frac1{10}2^{-a},\qquad
\frac{g_3}{D}=\frac1{20}+\frac1{10}2^{-b},
\end{equation}
and $(a+1,b+1)\in U_S$. When $S$ is a program's table, this is the selected by-$T$ or first-exactly-$T$ predicate. The literal ledgers and exact degrees are
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccc@{}}
\toprule
 & $\mathcal F_2$ & $\mathcal F_1$ & $\mathcal F_{1,\square}$\\
\midrule
External positive inputs & $3$ & $3$ & $3$\\
Positive witnesses & $28$ & $27$ & $27$\\
All variables & $31$ & $30$ & $30$\\
Final equations & $1$ & $1$ & $1$\\
Residual-square slots & $17$ & $12$ & $13$\\
Additional block & none & $Q_S$ & none\\
Exact degree & $\max(20,\deg P_S)$ & $\max(20,D_S)$ & $\max(20,2D_S)$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The degree entries involving $D_S$ are for $T\ge1$; every composition has exact degree twenty at $T=0$. For $T\ge1$, the fully distributed $\mathcal F_1$ has $12+3^{n_I}2^{n_E}$ square slots. At $T=0$, its native block is itself a square, so it has thirteen slots there too.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Every summand in \eqref{smc:la:eq:composed} is globally nonnegative. A zero therefore forces every decoding residual and the native block to vanish. Remark~\ref{smc:la:prop:power} gives $p=2^{A-1}$, $q=2^{B-1}$. Equations~\eqref{smc:la:eq:gaps}, positive outputs and positive $D$ force $20g_1-D>0$, $20g_3-D>0$ and, by division by positive quantities, exactly \eqref{smc:la:eq:encoding} with $a=A-1$, $b=B-1$. The native theorem gives acceptance. Conversely any encoded accepted triple supplies $A,B,p,q$, the constructive module witnesses and the unique native witnesses, so every required term vanishes. No promise that an arbitrary triple is encoded has been assumed; unencoded triples have no witnesses.

The counts add the native leaves and slots to the paid 26-witness, twelve-square block. Outputs are already in the module counts. All slots and declared variables remain counted in degenerate cases.

The block $E$ has exact degree twenty, as the independent module monomial \eqref{smc:la:eq:power-top} is absent from the other module, the gap residuals and the native variables. The gap squares have degree four. Finally, a nonzero globally nonnegative polynomial has a nonnegative highest homogeneous part: scale the argument by a positive parameter and pass to the leading limit. Such highest parts cannot cancel in a sum of nonnegative polynomials. Apply this to $E$ and each native block to obtain all stated degree equalities, including the product-block case.
\end{proof}

In particular the uniform degree ceilings at $T\ge1$ are
\[
\max(20,4T),\qquad \max(20,10T^2+8T),\qquad
\max(20,20T^2+16T),
\]
respectively. Calling $\mathcal F_1$ ``thirteen squares'' would incorrectly count a whole product-of-SOS block as one square. The thirteen-square presentation is $\mathcal F_{1,\square}$ and pays the doubled native degree contribution.

\wtag\ [The decoding block~$E$ is source~37's composition with $\ell=12$ (26 positive witnesses and twelve squares, Table~\ref{smc:pp:tab:compositions}); source~37 adds the three witnesses and six squares of source~36's compiler (29 witnesses, 18 squares), source~38 the two witnesses and five squares of its tensor compiler (28 and~17) or the one witness of its product (27). The successive ledgers 57, 29, 28 and~27 all stay valid for their own formulas.]

\subsection{Unique projections, infinite full fibers, and fixed decoding costs}
If a zero exists, the gaps determine
\[
p=\frac{2D}{20g_1-D},\qquad q=\frac{2D}{20g_3-D}.
\]
Injectivity of positive powers of two fixes $A,B$, and the native theorem fixes $(r,s)$ or $w$. Thus $(A,B,p,q,r,s)$ for $\mathcal F_2$, or $(A,B,p,q,w)$ for either one-witness form, is a unique projection. Nevertheless the full 28- or 27-witness fiber is infinite whenever nonempty: vary \eqref{smc:la:eq:progression} in one module while holding its index/output, the other module, the inputs and native witnesses fixed. These composed formulas are neither single-fold nor finite-fold.

Each decoding block has a fixed finite coefficient/support list independent of $T$, with a fixed factored circuit. Adding $E$ increases support by only a $T$-independent constant and coefficient norm by a fixed additive amount. Therefore the native asymptotic expanded-storage, support and factored-description bounds of Section~\ref{smc:la:sec:costs} persist under these compositions. The 30 or 31 total variables do not require a generic dense bound in that many variables. This is a size accounting statement, not a claim of bounded POWER witness height or constant bit-time evaluation.
\section{Context, evidence, and the exact boundary}\label{smc:la:sec:scope}
\subsection{Elementary ingredients and literature context}
The scaled basis in \eqref{smc:la:eq:basis} is ordinary Lagrange interpolation with a common factorial denominator cleared. NIST's \emph{Digital Library of Mathematical Functions}, Section 3.3(i), records the standard nodal formula and basis identities \cite{dlmflagrange}. Tensoring those bases prescribes a Boolean-valued table on a rectangular grid. The underlying finite-grid vanishing principle is classical; Alon's primary paper \cite[Lemma 2.1]{alon1999} gives its familiar degree-bounded finite-set form and an induction proof. The infinite-grid implication used here follows from the same one-variable root argument, proved explicitly in Section~\ref{smc:la:sec:classification}.

Conjunction by a sum of real squares and disjunction by a product of nonnegative factors are elementary algebraic encodings. In the one-witness construction, uniqueness depends additionally on the disjointness of the clipped cells and the positive-integer domain. These contextual observations are not an attribution of the specific formulas or ledgers to the cited works. No exhaustive literature survey, novelty or priority conclusion is offered.

\subsection{What is and is not represented}
The native theorems quantify over all positive inputs and positive integer witnesses, not a finite sample box. Their proofs establish that domain-wide result. For bounded counter programs, clipping transports both by-horizon and exact-first-halt semantics, including loops and initially halted programs. The table itself remains fixed data obtained by finite preprocessing.

In particular $T$ is an index of the family. Writing ``there exists a horizon $T$'' outside the family does not encode its varying acceptance table, factorials or products inside one fixed polynomial. This report supplies no unbounded-halting fixed polynomial or single-fold MRDP result. It gives no global witness minimum, minimum degree, minimum coefficient height, universal-polynomial record, efficient POWER witness-height bound, or new physical simulation theorem. The exact native zero-versus-one classification is the narrower theorem proved in Section~\ref{smc:la:sec:classification}; it does not classify the minimum arity of the gap compositions.

Earlier Reports 66--68 \textup{[sources~36 and~37, and the undelivered Report~68]} retain their own constructions, resource bounds and scopes. The new formulas are replacements available for comparison, not retroactive recounts or corrections to those reports. No claim about arbitrary unencoded physical trajectories, collision horizons or physical resource costs is made here.

The questions the three sources ask themselves are printed in their own sections (Section~\ref{smc:bc:sec:future}, the last paragraphs of Section~\ref{smc:pp:sec:scope} and Section~\ref{smc:la:sec:scope}); the notes there record which of them later sources answer. No claim of the three sources or of the programme's review was found to be wrong. The write rechecked in exact arithmetic the printed counting formulas of source~36 (Theorem~\ref{smc:bc:thm:floor} for all $X<3000$ and at $X=10^6+7$, the shell formula~\eqref{smc:bc:eq:shell} for $X<3000$, the primitive scales~\eqref{smc:bc:eq:dscale} for $a,b<40$, the slope~\eqref{smc:bc:eq:rho} and the four-class constants~\eqref{smc:bc:eq:alphabeta} for $M<40$), the degree and leading coefficient of source~37's Theorem~\ref{smc:pp:thm:interpolants} for $2\leq K\leq7$, and the ledgers of Table~\ref{smc:pp:tab:compositions} and of Theorem~\ref{smc:la:thm:composition}; all agree. These finite checks support, and do not replace, the printed proofs.

\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{smc:xiii:q:gauss} \textbf{Gaussian fluctuations of the encoded-gap deficit (the undelivered Report~68).} \emph{Claim.} For $X$ drawn uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, the deficit $E(X)=\rho X-\mathcal A(X)$ of source~36's Theorem~\ref{smc:bc:thm:countmain} has mean $\tfrac12(\log_2N)^2$ and variance $\tfrac{1637}{5400}(\log_2N)^3$ to leading order and, normalized, a Gaussian limit law; the inverse deviation $D_n-n/\rho$ of Theorem~\ref{smc:bc:thm:inverse}, for $n$ uniform up to $H$, has leading mean $\tfrac{1125}{1486}(\log_2H)^2$, variance $\tfrac{3069375}{4416392}(\log_2H)^3$ and a Gaussian law. \emph{Credit.} Report~68, \emph{Gaussian fluctuations of encoded gap counts and inverse ranks}, 4 October 2026, by the same pipeline; known here only from its delivery README, carried by source~38 and shipped as \path{38-low-arity-qa-pred-tools-README68.md}. \emph{Sketch, as that README describes it.} The digit form~\eqref{smc:bc:eq:exactcount}--\eqref{smc:bc:eq:digit} reduces $E$ to digit sums in bases 2 and~16; the factor $5$ in $X/10$ versus $X/16$ is handled by a five-state multiplication-by-five carry chain, which gives an exact block mean, a rational conditional variance and a martingale decomposition with an $O(m^2)$ variance remainder on complete dyadic blocks; a martingale central limit theorem (cited, with a direct characteristic-function proof for bounded increments) gives the Gaussian law, and prefix mixtures and residue-class moment estimates pass to every cutoff, with variance remainder $O((\log X)^{5/2})$. The inverse statement follows by a common-uniform coupling with uniform short-window bounds, with an $L^2$ comparison error $O((\log\log(H+3))^2)$. \emph{A consistency check by the write.} Since $D_n-n/\rho$ is $E(D_n)/\rho$ up to the bounded terms of~\eqref{smc:bc:eq:inversebound}, and $\log_2D_n=\log_2n+O(1)$, the inverse constants are the forward ones scaled by $1/\rho=1125/743$ and $1/\rho^2$: indeed $\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{1125}{743}=\tfrac{1125}{1486}$ and $\tfrac{1637}{5400}\cdot(\tfrac{1125}{743})^2=\tfrac{3069375}{4416392}$ exactly; and the mean $\tfrac12(\log_2N)^2$ lies, as it must, between the envelopes $\liminf E/(\log_2X)^2=0$ and $\limsup=1$ of~\eqref{smc:bc:eq:sharpE}. \emph{What is missing.} Report~68's article, proofs and audits are not in this batch or in the repository; the constant $1637/5400$, the carry-chain variance and the limit laws are therefore unproved here. Source~36's question on finer error statistics (Section~\ref{smc:bc:sec:future}, item~5) stays open until they are supplied.
\item\label{smc:xiii:q:physical} \textbf{Physical transport.} \emph{Claim.} The certificates of the Part also certify bounded instruction-section reachability of a five-live-signal machine on encoded inputs, with elapsed time strictly between $kD$ and $10kD$ and at most $32k$ binary contacts for first halt at $k>0$ (Sections~\ref{smc:bc:sec:gaps} and~\ref{smc:pp:sec:physical}). \emph{Credit and sketch.} Sources~36 and~37, by composition with source~34's compiler theorem (Theorem~\ref{smc:br:thm:compiler}, Part~XII). \emph{What is missing.} Nothing within this report once Part~XII's theorem is granted; but none of the three sources re-audits it, and the Hilbert's-tenth programme's review of the signal archives read only selected spans of source~34's proof~\cite{reviewnewsignals}. The physical reading stays conditional, as the sources say.
\item\label{smc:xiii:q:pell} \textbf{The all-exponent POWER equivalences.} \emph{Claim.} Every module of the Part represents $o=b^{C-1}$ exactly. \emph{Credit and sketch.} Sources~35--38, through the constructive theorems \texttt{Pell.matiyasevic} and \texttt{Pell.eq\_pow\_of\_pell} of mathlib4 at \texttt{ac77769f}. \emph{What is missing.} The sources read those statements as text and run no Lean; the specialization to the displayed positive-integer residual systems (adapters, natural subtraction, index $C$ versus exponent $C-1$) is proved on paper only. A machine-checked specialization, for instance in the repository's Lean development, would close this.
\end{enumerate}

\appendix
\section{Part~I: a minimal worked use of the compiler}
\label{smc:cg:app:example}

The following code can be run from the archive root. (\wtag\ ``The archive root'' is the delivered layout, with \path{code/signal_certificates.py}; in this report the module is shipped as \path{code/07-collision-geometry-signal_certificates.py}, so the snippet runs in a copy that restores the delivered name (README of this report).) It builds the
first-collision tournament and constructs a complete certificate without
using an external algebra system.
\begin{lstlisting}[language=Python]
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "code")
from signal_certificates import Machine, compile_skeleton

machine = Machine(
    {"A": 2, "B": 0, "C": -1, "H": 0, "R": 0},
    {
        frozenset(("A", "B")): ("H",),
        frozenset(("B", "C")): ("R",),
        frozenset(("A", "B", "C")): ("R",),
    },
)
skeleton = (((0, 1),),)
cert = compile_skeleton(machine, ("A", "B", "C"), skeleton)
gaps = (1, 1)
slacks = cert.witnesses(gaps)
assert cert.evaluate(gaps, slacks) == 0
assert not cert.accepts((3, 1))  # An earlier BC collision.
assert not cert.accepts((2, 1))  # A simultaneous ABC collision.
print(cert.to_dict())
\end{lstlisting}
The order of rows in the exported matrices is lexicographic and need not
match the order used in the displayed mathematical formula. Row order
changes only the order of slack coordinates, not the represented relation
or the uniqueness statement.

\section{Part~II: replay and build guide}\label{smc:sd:app:replay}
The accompanying archive contains this article in editable LaTeX, the compiled PDF, exact Python scripts, expected receipts, example coefficient dictionaries, and a manifest with file hashes. It contains no third-party source PDFs. The scripts require Python 3.10 or later and only the standard library. Assertions must remain enabled; do not run Python with \texttt{-O}.

From the extracted package root run:
\begin{verbatim}
python3 scripts/run_replay.py
\end{verbatim}
The runner copies the executable scripts into a temporary directory, executes the suites there, compares fresh JSON receipts to the stored expectations, and writes a summary under \texttt{replay-output}. The stored expected receipts and packaged examples are not overwritten. Use \texttt{--output DIR} to select a different result directory. The worked-example receipt also contains its concrete witness and explicit rejection reason for the false final-cut schema.


\wtag\ These are the delivered names. In this report the five scripts are shipped as \path{code/11-signal-certificates-*.py}, \path{build.sh} as \path{code/11-signal-certificates-build.sh}, the two example files and the manifest as \path{data/11-signal-certificates-*.json}, and the four expected receipts as \path{data/11-signal-certificates-expected-*_receipt.json}. The runner looks for \path{scripts/}, \path{examples/} and \path{expected_receipts/} in the parent of its own directory and runs the scripts by their delivered names, so it runs only in a copy that restores the delivered layout (see the README); it writes nothing into the shipped files. Of the archive contents listed above, the editable source is printed as this Part rather than shipped separately, and the compiled PDF and the checksum file \path{CHECKSUMS.sha256} are not shipped (the checksum file was verified, 17 of 17 files, at placement); the manifest is shipped, and its payload list still names the delivered paths and the delivered PDF and article source.

The main executable interfaces are:
\begin{itemize}
\item \texttt{signal\_geometry.py}: exact simulator, full-layer compiler, polynomial evaluation and rational Gaussian rank calculation;
\item \texttt{signal\_sparse.py}: event-coordinate and adjacency-lifetime compiler;
\item \texttt{verify\_additional.py}: separately seeded edge cases and sharp height checks;
\item \texttt{verify\_examples.py}: the article's explicit examples and convention checks.
\end{itemize}
The low-level compilers use assertions to reject malformed schema partitions or structurally impossible collision directions. They are reference mathematical implementations, not hardened parsers for untrusted inputs. JSON residual dictionaries use \texttt{@} for the constant term, \texttt{x0}, \texttt{x1}, and so on for input positions, and the listed variable names for natural witnesses. A certificate evaluates to the sum of the squares of those rows. No expanded polynomial is required to replay it.

To rebuild the article run:
\begin{verbatim}
sh build.sh
\end{verbatim}
A working TeX Live installation with \texttt{pdflatex}, Latin Modern fonts, AMS packages, \texttt{geometry}, \texttt{microtype}, \texttt{booktabs}, \texttt{enumitem} and \texttt{hyperref} suffices. The build script uses fixed document metadata and a fixed source-date epoch; exact PDF byte equality across different TeX distributions is not promised. The mathematical replay receipts are exact and version-independent within supported Python semantics.

\section{Part~II: claim and source guide}\label{smc:sd:app:sources}
The source-supported context is limited to the following claims. All certificate theorems and proofs in this article are supplied here rather than attributed to the literature.
\begin{itemize}
\item Durand-Lose 2009: finite configurations in Definition~1; integer inputs in Section~2; speeds in Figure~4; cyclic-tag simulation and halting in Section~5 and Theorem~5. Common-denominator rescaling is our inference, proved in \eqref{smc:sd:eq:normalize}.
\item Durand-Lose 2007: linear-register event simulation in Section~4 of the author version, especially its ninth PDF page; rational models in Section~5. No Diophantine theorem is attributed to it.
\item Durand-Lose 2006: energy and live-population bounds in Definition~3 and the following paragraph; accumulation qualifications in Sections~2.2 and~6.
\item Ginsburg and Spanier 1966: equivalence of Presburger-definable and semilinear subsets of $\NN^n$, Theorem~1.3, pp.~288--289.
\end{itemize}
Primary sources were checked on 2 October 2026. The bibliography links to the papers or their official bibliographic records; copyright-bearing PDFs are not redistributed in this package.


\wtag\ In this report the Durand-Lose 2009 and Ginsburg--Spanier entries are merged with Part~I's entries for the same papers~\cite{durandlose,ginsburgspanier}; the merged entries add source~11's editors and links to Part~I's.

\paragraph{Where the batch-91 addition had to choose.}
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{Placement and order.} All fifteen manuscripts continue Parts of this report or answer its questions, so they are additions to it. Sources~24 and~25 continue Part~VI and form Part~IX; the signal-machine sources follow in the pipeline's order as Parts~X (Reports~56--59), XI (60--63), XII (64--65) and~XIII (66, 67, 69), after Part~VIII and before the appendices. Every result, proof, example, remark, question and limitation of the fifteen sources is printed, except where a restated statement is printed once.
\item \emph{One restatement device.} A statement that a source restates from another is printed once, in the Part that owns its theme; the restatement becomes a numbered remark, marked \wtag, that quotes it, keeps the duplicate's own label and points to the proof printed elsewhere, and references to it say ``Remark''. Genuinely different proofs are kept as marked second routes.
\item \emph{Labels.} Every delivered label of a source carries the sub-prefix of its source (\texttt{smc:rt:}, \texttt{smc:ut:}, \texttt{smc:pm:}, \texttt{smc:fv:}, \texttt{smc:fd:}, \texttt{smc:rf:}, \texttt{smc:pl:}, \texttt{smc:iv:}, \texttt{smc:pj:}, \texttt{smc:hl:}, \texttt{smc:br:}, \texttt{smc:ck:}, \texttt{smc:bc:}, \texttt{smc:pp:}, \texttt{smc:la:}); unlabelled numbered statements are \texttt{smc:<sub>:n<number>}; labels written in the merge carry \texttt{smc:ix:} to \texttt{smc:xiii:} (the front subsections of Parts~X--XIII use \texttt{smc:x:}); the Parts are \texttt{smc:part:reversible}, \texttt{periodic}, \texttt{planar}, \texttt{clocked} and \texttt{nativegap}. \section{Part~III: a small complete quadratic packet}\label{smc:cs:app:example}
Consider the one-dimensional partial-branch presentation of the total map $F(x)=2x$ on $\NN$: branch 0 has guard $x=0$ and update 0; branch 1 has guard $x>0$ and update $2x$. The packet has selectors $b_0,b_1$, copies $z_0,z_1$, and one slack $s$:
\begin{align*}
 P(x,y;b_0,b_1,z_0,z_1,s)
 ={}&(b_0+b_1-1)^2+(x-z_0-z_1)^2+(y-2z_1)^2\\
   &+z_0^2+(z_1-b_1-s)^2+b_1z_0+b_0z_1.
\end{align*}
Here $B=2$, $d=1$, $E=1$, $T=1$, $W=0$, so the ledger gives five variables, five squared residuals, and two products. For $x=0,y=0$ the unique witness is $(1,0,0,0,0)$; for $x>0,y=2x$ it is $(0,1,0,x,x-1)$. Every other input/output pair has no natural witness. The core replay exhaustively checks 100,000 bounded assignments, including every auxiliary tuple in $\{0,\ldots,4\}^5$ for $0\le x<4$, $0\le y<8$.

The generic event-branch compiler also fully enumerates a three-signal transparent test machine with speeds $2,0,-2$. Its 19 branches have $E=20$, $T=84$, $W=0$, yielding 160 auxiliary variables, 111 squared affine residuals, and 19 complementarity products. Both pivot and uniform scalings pass 144 valid-germ tests, including 88 legal steps and two simultaneous steps, with every canonical residual exactly zero.

This example illustrates the exact polynomial mechanics without suggesting that a universal branch family has only two branches. For the signal frontend, the same constructor takes the actual finite label-mode and first-collision branch descriptions.

\section{Part~III: the complete finite mode closure and numeric packet}\label{smc:cs:app:closure}
\subsection{A finite family covering every encoded run}
The naive family of all $114^{18}$ ordered label words is unnecessary. Starting from the literal initial mode, consider each nonempty subset $J$ of eligible adjacent closing pairs. A pair is eligible only when its exact incoming labels have a defined rule and their speeds are in incoming order. Exclude subsets with consecutive edges, since those would constitute an undefined collision of at least three signals. Replace every selected pair atomically by its speed-sorted output pair and add the resulting mode. Repeating to exhaustion gives the least mode-only closure for this syntactic successor operation.

Every legal event of an encoded run uses one of these nonadjacent eligible subsets, by the complete-collision lemma. Induction therefore places every event mode and branch in the closure. Conversely, every retained branch has exactly the original mode, germ, earliest-collision and rule guards, so it introduces no spurious geometric step. Restricting the integer map to this closed mode family preserves every encoded computation.

The closure is an overapproximation of modes numerically reachable from the specified input family: successive graph edges may be realizable at different gap vectors which cannot be spliced into one orbit. No assertion of reachability of every graph node is made. Nevertheless every branch is individually feasible. If $c$ is its speed-difference vector, choose
\[
 h_i=\begin{cases}c_i&i\in J,\\ \max(c_i,0)+1&i\notin J,\end{cases}
 \qquad u=q\sum_i h_i.
\]
All gaps are strictly positive, its next delay is one, exactly $J$ collides, and the output is an admissible germ. The exporter checks this witness for every branch.

The completed enumeration has 49,700 modes and 80,501 branches: 65,557 single-collision branches and 14,944 branches with two simultaneous disjoint collisions. The maximum graph discovery depth is 321. This depth is a graph statistic, not a computation-time bound or a numeric reachability certificate.

Among the modes, 1,728 have no eligible legal pair. Only 36 of those have no closing edge at all and are collision-free; the other 1,692 are blocked by undefined collisions. Of the 36 collision-free modes, six carry an accepting halt label and 30 carry the null label. The fixed final accepting mode in Section~\ref{smc:cs:sec:integer} is the target for encoded runs. Neither all graph sinks nor the union of those six label-bearing modes replaces that target.

\subsection{Exact guard and witness counts}
For each branch the exported guard convention retains one mode equality, $|J|-1$ nonpivot tie equalities, one strict germ guard for each $c_i\ge0$, the strict span guard, the strict pivot-gap guard, and all $17-|J|$ non-$J$ endpoint guards. Some strict guards are redundant; retaining them makes the convention simple and fully reproducible. Nonnegative coordinates are the ambient natural domain, so no weak-gap slacks are introduced.

The resulting exact ledger is
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lr}
\toprule
Quantity & Count\\
\midrule
Branches $B$ & 80,501\\
Equality guards $E$ & 95,445\\
Strict guards $T$ & 2,667,479\\
Weak guards $W$ & 0\\
Auxiliary variables $19B+T$ & 4,196,998\\
All variables including $X,Y$ & 4,197,034\\
Squared affine residuals $37+E+T$ & 2,762,961\\
Complementarity products & 80,501\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Thus the literal one-step polynomial is fully specified, quadratic, nonnegative on natural arguments, and canonical by Theorem~\ref{smc:cs:thm:packet}. For externally fixed $K$ and supplied endpoints, its unrolling has exactly $4{,}197{,}016K-18$ witness variables. This explicit constant is large; the small physical population does not imply a comparably small Diophantine arity.

The untimed affine rows contain 15,323,489 nonzero variable-coefficient entries and one nonzero constant. The maximum absolute affine coefficient has 124 bits. Gap coefficients remain bounded by 24; the larger values arise from finite mode coding. These are sparse affine-circuit statistics, not claims about minimal gate complexity. Adding the optional timestamp coordinate retains the same branch guards and adds one local copy coordinate per branch and two global input/output residuals. Its derived ledger is 4,277,499 auxiliaries and 2,762,963 squared affine residuals per step.

\subsection{What the numeric export contains}
The mode file gives each mode's 18 label indices, speed differences, exact code and graph index. The compact event file records every branch index, source/target index, canonical pivot and bitmask of the complete set $J$. Together with the explicit formulas above, these fixed numbers determine every sparse matrix and guard coefficient. The supplied exporter generates the full numeric branch records, including selector, copy and slack indices. A separate circuit file fixes the global variable order and the polynomial~\eqref{smc:cs:eq:polynomial}. All large codes and generated coefficients are serialized as decimal strings.

The shared selector sum is an expression, not another witness variable. Writing its difference with $b_r$ is exactly $\sum_{h\ne r}b_h$, which is nonnegative on all natural assignments. Keeping this expression factored avoids a quadratic-in-$B$ expansion of the complementarity part. The exporter can regenerate every squared affine residual row or answer individual expanded coefficient queries. The verbose branch and full residual-row files were generated and checked during preparation. They are omitted from the compact archive because they are deterministically regenerable from its complete mode/event data and code.

The supplementary incidence calculation gives 1,059,563,096,023 nonzero terms in the full monomial expansion and a maximum absolute coefficient of 248 bits. Those expansion statistics are derived exactly; no trillion-term monomial file was emitted. The actually generated full affine-residual export was checked independently, including all 15,323,489 nonzero variable-coefficient entries.

This is an explicit coefficient description of one fixed step polynomial and each fixed-horizon family. It does not convert the unknown horizon into a fixed number of natural variables, and it does not assert that the mode graph's finite size bounds the length of a universal run.

\section{Part~VII: canonical timed quartic certificates (source~19)}\label{smc:zd:app:quartic}
The preceding proof supplies more than reachability decidability: it produces exact phase data with a rigid algebraic form. We now apply the constant term lifting compiler already established in Report 13 \textup{[source~18, Section~\ref{smc:tq:sec:compiler}]}. Its one dimensional conclusion is not new here. The finite dimensional extension comes from the proved normal form and a disjoint lexicographic sorting refinement. The complete companion proof and its independent conditional review are included in \file{scientific/timed/}. \wtag\ [Shipped as \path{19-mass-four-zd-timed-PROOF.md} and \path{19-mass-four-zd-timed-REVIEW.md}; with this appendix the fixed-input answer to source~17's Question~\ref{smc:fm:q:quartic} holds in every finite dimension.]

\begin{theorem}[Fixed input timed charts and quartics]\label{smc:zd:thm:quartic}
Fix a CA and input satisfying Theorem~\ref{smc:zd:thm:main}. There is an effective finite family of disjoint charts, each with at most two natural parameters and an integer affine domain, whose time and original frame occupied coordinates are rational polynomials of degree at most two, integer valued on their domains. Occupied sites are strictly lexicographically ordered. The disjoint chart domains map bijectively to the complete timed orbit.

For every fixed tuple $\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$ of nonzero labels, $0\le m\le4$, there is an effectively obtained integer polynomial
\[
 C_{\mathbf a}(t,X_1,\ldots,X_m;w)
\]
of ordinary total degree at most four, with natural witnesses $w$, whose witness fiber is a singleton exactly when $F^t(c)$ has precisely those lexicographically ordered sites and labels, and is empty otherwise. Here $t\in\NN$ and $X_i\in\Z^d$ are external arguments. The witness count depends on the fixed input and rule, not on time or the queried coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{Half open charts own every time exactly once}
\wtag\ [This subsection is source~18's Section~\ref{smc:tq:sec:partition} in the notation of Section~\ref{smc:zd:sec:shuttle} (here $q_\ell$ is source~18's prefix length $b_\ell$, and $C$ is its $B$); new here are the original-frame coordinates in $\Z^d$ and the raw chart count $J$. It is printed because the counts below use it.]
Materialize the finite prefix as one parameter free chart for each $0\le t<T_0$. For a translated periodic or independent tail, extend the prefix through all individual transients and choose one common period $p$. The phase $r$ has the one parameter formula
\[
 t=T_0+r+pn,\qquad 0\le r<p,\quad n\in\NN,
\]
with affine coordinates. Euclidean division determines a unique phase and parameter. The vacuum uses a one clock tail with no occupied coordinates. In the no unit case the same construction already works in the original frame.

For an expanding shuttle, retain the same cycle indexing as in Section~\ref{smc:zd:sec:shuttle}. Let transition $\ell$ have flight length $h_\ell(n)=a_\ell n+b_\ell$ and fixed encounter prefix length $q_\ell\ge0$. The flight length is integral for all natural $n$, so $b_\ell=h_\ell(0)$ and $a_\ell=h_\ell(1)-h_\ell(0)$ are integers. Both $h_\ell(n)>0$ and $a_\ell>0$. The cycle start is
\[
 T(n)=T_0+A\frac{n(n-1)}2+Cn,\qquad A,C\in\Z_{>0},
\]
and transition $\ell$ starts at the quadratic integer valued polynomial
\[
 S_\ell(n)=T(n)+\sum_{h<\ell}(h_h(n)+q_h).
\]
The half open cycle intervals $[T(n),T(n+1))$ partition all times from $T_0$ onward. Each transition owns $[S_\ell(n),S_\ell(n)+h_\ell(n)+q_\ell)$.

If its packet period is $p_\ell$, then for each residue $0\le r<p_\ell$ the flight chart has parameters $n,j\in\NN$, domain and time
\begin{equation}\label{smc:zd:eq:halfopen}
 h_\ell(n)-r-p_\ell j-1\ge0,\qquad
 t=S_\ell(n)+r+p_\ell j.
\end{equation}
It owns only the times strictly before first contact. For $0\le s<q_\ell$, a local prefix chart has parameter $n$ and time $S_\ell(n)+h_\ell(n)+s$. If $q_\ell=0$, contact is the next checkpoint and belongs to the next transition. Thus no boundary is counted twice.

The cycle interval determines $n$, the transition interval determines $\ell$, and division determines the unique flight phase and $j$ or the unique local prefix phase. This proves one chart point per exact time, even if the spatial configuration repeats. Stationary frame coordinates $g_v$ are affine in the chart parameters, and original frame coordinates
\[
 P_v=g_v+\delta t
\]
have degree at most two. If $J$ denotes the raw chart count, the literal construction gives $J=T_0+p$ for an affine tail and $J=T_0+\sum_\ell(p_\ell+q_\ell)$ for a shuttle. These input dependent quantities may be enormous.

\subsection{Disjoint lexicographic sorting and its cost}
For a raw chart with $m$ occupied sites, refine by every permutation $\pi$ and every list of first differing coordinates $k_a\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$ for adjacent sites $v=\pi(a)$, $w=\pi(a+1)$. Require
\[
 g_{w,h}-g_{v,h}=0\quad(h<k_a),\qquad
 g_{w,k_a}-g_{v,k_a}-1\ge0.
\]
The common drift cancels in pair differences, so these conditions are affine. Occupied sites are distinct; hence exactly one order and one first difference list apply at each chart point. Equal labels do not cause multiplicity. Use positive denominator clearing wherever needed.

The sorting factor is $1$ when $m\le1$, and $m!d^{m-1}$ otherwise. Let $B_{\rm ch}$ be the retained chart count after any fixed label tuple filtering, $K$ its total private parameter slots, $M$ its domain inequalities, and $H$ its domain equalities. Then
\begin{equation}\label{smc:zd:eq:chartcounts}
 B_{\rm ch}\le24d^3J,\quad K\le2B_{\rm ch},\quad
 M\le4B_{\rm ch},\quad H\le3(d-1)B_{\rm ch}.
\end{equation}
The notation $B_{\rm ch}$ is separate from the geometric prefix bound $B$ in the main proof. Incompatible label tuples simply retain no charts.

\subsection{The inherited constant term lifting compiler}
A slightly more general interface also covers the pattern consequences below. Chart $i$ has private natural parameters $z_i$, integer polynomial inequalities $A_{ir}(z_i)\ge0$, integer polynomial equalities $H_{is}(z_i)=0$, and rational output vector $P_i(z_i)\in\Q^Q$. All degrees are at most two; outputs are integer valued on the domain. Assume the disjoint domains map injectively to the intended external outputs.

Introduce a natural selector $e_i$, the private parameters, and one natural slack $u_{ir}$ for every inequality. Write
\[
 E=\sum_i e_i,\qquad Z_i=\sum_jz_{ij}+\sum_ru_{ir},\qquad
 \mathcal L_i(f)=f(z_i)-f(0)+f(0)e_i.
\]
Only the literal constant is multiplied by the selector, so no quadratic monomial becomes cubic. For each output coordinate choose a positive common denominator $L_q$ across \emph{all} chart polynomials. Define
\begin{align*}
 R_0&=E-1,&R_{ir}&=\mathcal L_i(A_{ir})-u_{ir},\\
 U_{is}&=\mathcal L_i(H_{is}),&G_i&=(1-e_i)Z_i,\\
 V_q&=L_q\left(y_q-\sum_i\mathcal L_i(P_{iq})\right).
\end{align*}
All residuals have integer coefficients and ordinary degree at most two in the external and witness variables together. Therefore
\begin{equation}\label{smc:zd:eq:sos}
 C(y;w)=R_0^2+\sum_{ir}R_{ir}^2+\sum_{is}U_{is}^2
             +\sum_qV_q^2+\sum_iG_i^2
\end{equation}
is an ordinary quartic sum of squares.

At a natural zero, $E=1$ forces exactly one selector to be $1$. Every inactive gate forces $Z_i=0$, and nonnegativity forces all its parameters and slacks individually to be zero. Its lifted forms vanish. In the selected branch, the remaining equations enforce precisely its domain, its uniquely determined integer slacks, and its output. Conversely an admissible chart point gives that unique zero, with every inactive private variable zero. Thus the natural zeros are in bijection with admissible chart points over the specified output. Half open ownership and disjoint sorting prove Theorem~\ref{smc:zd:thm:quartic}.

\wtag\ [This is the argument of source~18's Proposition~\ref{smc:tq:prop:compiler}, whose residuals~\eqref{smc:tq:eq:domainres}--\eqref{smc:tq:eq:outres} and squared gates~\eqref{smc:tq:eq:sos} appear above as $U_{is}$, $V_q$ and $G_i$; source~19 says itself that the one-dimensional conclusion is not new. The programme has read the shipped companion proof \path{19-mass-four-zd-timed-PROOF.md} in full, in a follow-up (\path{original_frame_first_hit30_fixture.md} with its independent review \path{review_original_frame_first_hit30_fixture.md}, commit \texttt{5b4c091e6})~\cite{reviewfixture}, and found its half-open chart ownership, common clock, first-difference sorting, constant-term lifts, pooled denominators, uniqueness of the inactive natural witnesses and original-frame padding sound as conditional statements; the general normal form stays an inherited hypothesis.]

There are exactly
\begin{equation}\label{smc:zd:eq:witnesscount}
 N_{\rm w}=B_{\rm ch}+K+M\le7B_{\rm ch}\le168d^3J
\end{equation}
natural witnesses, and $1+M+H+Q+B_{\rm ch}$ squared residual slots before deleting identically zero terms. For a fixed $m$ site label tuple, $Q=1+dm$. An empty chart family uses $C=1$ and no witnesses. These counts are deliberately coarse and input dependent.

The polynomial is nonnegative on all real arguments, but its exactness and witness uniqueness are assertions over \emph{natural} witnesses. Replacing them by unrestricted signed difference pairs breaks the inactive branch argument. Pooled denominators are essential: separately scaled branch outputs cannot simply be added without a common scale.

\subsection{Whole configurations and signed external coordinates}
One polynomial can cover varying site counts and labels by encoding
\[
 (t,m,a_1,\ldots,a_4,X_1,\ldots,X_4)
\]
with positive integer nonzero label codes, occupied sites sorted, and all unused label and coordinate slots zero. Append those constants to each chart output; then $Q=6+4d$ and the same witness bound applies. Padded zero coordinates remain literally zero and do not acquire the drift $\delta t$.

For equality up to translation, subtract the first occupied site. The relative coordinates $P_v-P_1=g_v-g_1$ are affine, and time remains quadratic. There is no translation witness. The vacuum is handled separately rather than granting it infinitely many arbitrary translation witnesses.

Signed external integer coordinates are valid polynomial inputs. If all external slots must be natural, replace each scalar $X$ by $X^+-X^-$ and add the squared residual $(X^+X^-)^2$. The accepted pair is uniquely $(\max(X,0),\max(-X,0))$. These are external slots, not extra witnesses. Total degree remains at most four.

\subsection{Fixed patterns including prescribed zeros}
For integer vectors $v,w$, there are $2d+1$ disjoint comparison outcomes: equality, or either sign at their first differing coordinate. Equality uses $d$ coordinate equations; each strict outcome uses earlier coordinate equalities and one inequality with an integer margin of $1$. Comparisons of quadratic outputs therefore introduce only degree two domain conditions, within the compiler interface.

For a fixed anchored pattern on $s$ sites, refine every sorted orbit chart by all comparisons of each occupied site with each window site. The full comparison matrix and fixed labels decide its truth, including zeros. Retain successful matrices and output only $t$. The refinement is disjoint, and the orbit determines a unique chart point at each time, so the quartic has an empty or singleton natural witness fiber. One may take
\[
 B_{\rm anch}\le B_{\rm ch}(2d+1)^{4s},\qquad
 N_{\rm anch}\le(7+4s)B_{\rm anch}.
\]
Here $B_{\rm ch}$ refers to all sorted orbit charts before observation filtering.

For a translated pattern with a nonzero prescribed site $w_*$, every successful placement sends $w_*$ to one of at most four occupied sites carrying the correct label. The candidate shift is $b_i=P_i-w_*$. Refine by the \emph{complete} matrix of comparisons
\[
 P_v-P_i\quad\hbox{against}\quad w-w_*
\]
for all occupied $i,v$ and all pattern sites $w$. The drift cancels and these conditions are affine. The matrix determines the success of every candidate. Retain the matrix once if any candidate succeeds, rather than introducing one branch per success. If a placement is also output, choose the least successful occupied site index. This prevents same time placement multiplicity. Bounds are
\[
 B_{\rm trans}\le B_{\rm ch}(2d+1)^{16s},\qquad
 N_{\rm trans}\le(7+16s)B_{\rm trans}.
\]

A wholly zero translated pattern, including the empty pattern, occurs in every finite support configuration at every time. For occurrence in external natural $t$ alone, the zero polynomial with no witnesses has the single empty witness tuple. There need not be a lexicographically least placement. If a placement is wanted, choose a specified rule that moves its entire window beyond the maximal first support coordinate, with the vacuum handled separately.

These are fixed pattern statements. The chart family and counts may depend on the whole pattern. No uniform arity claim is made for an arbitrary pattern provided as one encoded external input.

\subsection{What time uniqueness does not imply}
Time is external in every single witness claim. If it is existentially quantified instead, the same construction has one zero for \emph{each occurrence time}. A stationary nonempty configuration already gives an infinite fiber. Thus this appendix does not establish untimed finite foldness, a generic single fold MRDP theorem, a uniform bound over input configurations, or exactness for rational or real witnesses. The explicit chart interface, not bare decidability, is what permits the quartic compiler.

The companion finite checks cover 208 drift restored two dimensional shuttle states, 325 lexicographic refinement cases, 1,215 finite witness cube evaluations, and additional selectors, inactive gates, domains, signed pairs, and pattern placements. Their normal and optimized receipts agree. They test the displayed algebra on fixtures; they do not implement a general CA to chart compiler or prove the dynamical normal form by experiment.
